How could it act as a power separately (from where it manifests)?

units.label: Chapter 2 · Verse 54
units.deva:
न कृस्त्न-ब्रह्म-वृत्तिः सा शक्तिः किंत्वेक-देश-भाक्।
घट-शक्तिर् यथा भूमौ स्निग्ध-मृद्येव वर्तते॥
units.translation: This power (of brahman, reality) does not operate everywhere throughout brahman, but rather only occurs in some part (of existence). Just as the power in earth to (materially) produce clay pots only occurs in softened clay, not elsewhere.

gloss.en: the power to make a pot

units.label: Chapter 2 · Verse 55
units.deva:
पादोऽस्य सर्वा भूतानि त्रि-पाद् अस्ति स्वयं-प्रभः।
इत्येक-देश-वृत्तित्वं मायया वदति श्रुतिः॥
units.translation: “Everything (the effects of māyā, manifest to our senses and mind) is only one quarter of this (reality), the other three quarters…” ( (Chāndogya Upaniṣad)) are only this one self-revealing (svayaṃ-prabha, sat). Thus, the scripture reveals māyā as being only a portion (of reality).

gloss.en: this being limited to one part

units.label: Chapter 2 · Verse 56
units.deva:
विष्टभ्याहम् इदं कृत्स्नम् एकांशेन स्थितो जगत्।
इति कृष्णोऽर्जुनायाह जगतस् त्वेक-देशताम्॥
units.translation: “I remain sustaining this entire universe with (just) a fraction (of My self)” ( (Bhagavad Gītā)). Thus, Lord Kṛṣṇa indicates to Arjuna the fractional nature of the universe.

units.label: Chapter 2 · Verse 57
units.deva:
स भूमिं विश्वतो वृत्वा ह्यत्यतिष्ठद् दशाङ्गुलम्।
विकारावर्ति चात्रास्ति श्रुति-सूत्र-कृतोर् वचः॥
units.translation: “This one envelops the entire universe, yet extends beyond by ten fingers” (i.e., innumerably, beyond what is the limit of the perceivable, Ṛg Veda 10.129 & (Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad)); and “(Brahman) is without form (vikāra-avartin, not needing a form) here (beyond the universe of forms)” ( (Brahma Sūtras)) – thus is the declaration made in scripture (śruti) and in the teaching aphorisms (sūtras).

gloss.en: the statement of scripture and aphorist

units.label: Chapter 2 · Verse 58
units.deva:
निरंशेऽप्यंशम् आरोप्य कृत्स्नेंऽशे वेति पृच्छतः।
तद्-भाषयोत्तरं ब्रूते श्रुतिः श्रोतृ-हितैषिणी॥
units.translation: Attributing (āropya) parts even upon the partless (sat), the śruti, for the benefit of the listener (who is still bound up in duality), answers with the same language of the question as to whether (māyā pervades) completely or only part (of reality).

gloss.en: even a part on the partless

units.label: Chapter 2 · Verse 59
units.deva:
सत्-तत्त्वम् आश्रिता शक्तिः कल्पयेत् सति विक्रियाः।
वर्णा भित्ति-गता भित्तौ चित्रं नाना-विधं तथा॥
units.translation: Śakti (this māyā) whose truth is reality (sat-tattva) creates (kalpyayet, conjures as if by magic) differences in reality (the non-dual sat), like paints applied to a wall appear as (if a realistic, 3-D) complex painting on the wall.

units.label: Chapter 2 · Verse 60
units.deva:
आद्यो विकार आकाशः सोऽवकाश-स्वरूपवान्।
आकाशोऽस्तीति सत्-तत्त्वम् आकाशेऽप्यनुगच्छति॥
units.translation: The first modification (the first of the five great elements from māyā) was ākāśa (space). Space is that which gives room (avakāśa, provides dimension). (Being a modification of māyā) its truth also is only (the non-dual) reality (sat-tattva).

gloss.en: that has room as its nature

units.label: Chapter 2 · Verse 61
units.deva:
एक-स्वभावं सत्-तत्त्वम् आकाशो द्वि-स्वभावकः।
नावकाशः सति व्योम्नि स चैषोऽपि द्वयं स्थितम्॥
units.translation: The nature of reality (sat-tattva) is only its own single nature (as existence itself). Space has two natures (as dimension and as existing). In existence itself there is no dimension. In space there is also that (dimension), and thus is dual.

units.label: Chapter 2 · Verse 62
units.deva:
यद्वा प्रतिध्वनिर् व्योम्नो गुणो नासौ सतीक्ष्यते।
व्योम्नि द्वौ सद् ध्वनी तेन सद् एकं द्वि-गुणं वियत्॥
units.translation: Also sound (pratidhvani, perceptible by the sense of hearing) is a quality (guṇa) of space, but this (quality) is not perceived in reality itself. In space there are both sound and existence. So existence is a single (nature) and space is dual natured (dvi-guṇa)*. *(Here, although existence is the very nature of space, it is lumped in as another guṇa based on the common notion of people regarding ‘existence’ that it is merely an attribute which can be there or not be there, as in “the pot ‘is’”, or “the pot ‘is not’”, ).

units.label: Chapter 2 · Verse 63
units.deva:
या शक्तिः कल्पयेद् व्योम सा सद्-व्योम्नोर् अभिन्नताम्।
आपाद्य धर्म-धर्मित्वं व्यत्ययेनावकल्पयेत्॥
units.translation: The same śakti (māyā) that produces space, first produces the notion that existence and space are inseparable (that space exists) and then conjures up the opposite notion that the two are related as a quality and its possessor (dharma-dharmitva, that space has existence or existence has space).

units.label: Chapter 2 · Verse 64
units.deva:
सतो व्योमत्वम् आपन्नं व्योम्नः सत्तां तु लौकिकाः।
तार्किकाश्चावगच्छन्ति मायाया उचितं हि तत्॥
units.translation: It is existence that (initially) appears (by māyā) to have the nature of space (sataḥ vyomatvam, like clay has clay-potness). But logicians (tārkikas), from their worldly perspective (laukikas), then think instead that space has the nature of existence (vyomnaḥ sattām, that ‘space exists’ means space is an independent reality). That indeed would be expected due to māyā (the power of projection, which can conjure up unreal relationships).

units.label: Chapter 2 · Verse 65
units.deva:
यद् यथा वर्तते तस्य तथात्वं भाति मानतः।
अन्यथात्वं भ्रमेणेति न्यायोऽयं सार्व-लौकिकः॥
units.translation: It is common knowledge by a proper means of knowledge (mānataḥ, pratyakṣādi-pramāṇataḥ) that a thing appears as it is (i.e., tasmin tad-buddhiḥ), and to be otherwise (anyathātva) would be by error (bhrama, an illusion).

gloss.en: by a valid means of knowledge

units.label: Chapter 2 · Verse 66
units.deva:
एवं श्रुति-विचारात् प्राग् यथा यद् वस्तु भासते।
विचारेण विपर्येति ततस् तच्-चिन्त्यतां वियत्॥
units.translation: In this way, before inquiry into the scripture (which is here the appropriate means of knowledge, pramāṇa), something appears different afterwards by proper inquiry. Therefore, let us discuss what this space is.

units.label: Chapter 2 · Verse 67
units.deva:
भिन्ने वियत्-सती शब्द-भेदाद् बुद्धेश्च भेदतः।
वाय्वादिष्वनुवृत्तं सन् न तु व्योमेति भेद-धीः॥
units.translation: Space and existence are different because their names (i.e., nāmans) are different and their understandings (i.e., rūpas) are different. Existence encompasses (anuvṛtta) space, but that is not the case for space (which does not encompass existence, i.e., existence was there before the manifestation of space, as well as space is only a ‘part’ of reality). That is their different understanding (bheda-dhī).

gloss.en: and because of difference in understanding
present through wind and the rest

units.label: Chapter 2 · Verse 68
units.deva:
सद् वस्त्वधिक-वृत्तित्वाद् धर्मि व्योम्नस् तु धर्मता।
धिया सतः पृथक्-कारे ब्रूहि व्योम किम् आत्मकं॥
units.translation: Existence, because of being completely inclusive (in time and place) of any entity, is the dharmin (the locus or substance of all entities), whereas space has the nature of being a dharma (a seeming attribute of reality, of this locus). By this understanding (dhiyā), once existence itself is distinguished (is abstracted, from space), then space has what kind of nature (if it is other than reality and is imposed by māyā upon reality)?

units.label: Chapter 2 · Verse 69
units.deva:
अवकाशात्मकं तच् चेद् असत् तद् इति चिन्त्यताम्।
भिन्नं सतोऽसच् च नेति वक्षि चेद् व्याहतिस् तव॥
units.translation: If you say that its nature is (not reality but is) whatever gives dimension (avakāśa-ātmaka), then it should be considered to be a-sat (not-real). If you say (vakṣi) that it (space) exists as other than reality yet it is not not-real (not a-sat), then you contradict yourself.

units.label: Chapter 2 · Verse 70
units.deva:
भातीति चेद् भातु नाम भूषणं मायिकस्य तत्।
यद् असद् भासमानं तन् मिथ्या स्वप्न-गजादिवत्॥
units.translation: If you say (space) is evident (bhāti, to our mind and to the sense of hearing as distance and direction), then (we say) it is only what appears (but is not reality) – and that is the glory of illusion! Whatever is unreal (a-sat) yet appears (to our senses) – that is an illusion (mithyā, a product of universal māyā), similar to a dream elephant, etcetera (which is only a product of our dreaming mind).

gloss.en: like a dream elephant and the rest

units.label: Chapter 2 · Verse 71
units.deva:
जाति-व्यक्ती देहि-देहौ गुण-द्रव्ये यथा पृथक्।
वियत्-सतोस् तथैवास्तु पार्थक्यं कोऽत्र विस्मयः॥
units.translation: Just as there is a distinction between a class and a single member of that class, between a dehin (a jīva, a living subtle body, that assumes a series of innumerable bodies) and its (current) body, and between a substance and a quality of the substance, so too between existence and space.* What is there to wonder? *(They cannot be the same thing, nor in the absence of the former can there be the latter, i.e., there is no member if there is no class, no living body if no subtle body to enliven or perceive it, and no quality if no substance to have it.)

units.label: Chapter 2 · Verse 72
units.deva:
बुद्धोऽपि भेदो नो चित्ते निरूढिं याति चेत् तदा।
अनैकाग्र्यात् संशयाद् वा रूढ्यभावोऽस्य ते वद॥
units.translation: If this (correctly) known difference has not arisen in the mind (through śravaṇa), then tell me, is its lack of staying put due to inattention (an-aikāgrya), or due to some remaining doubt?

gloss.en: the lack of its being established

units.label: Chapter 2 · Verse 73
units.deva:
अप्रमत्तो भव ध्यानाद् आद्येऽन्यस्मिन् विवेचनम्।
कुरु प्रमाण-युक्तिभ्यां ततो रूढतमो भवेत्॥
units.translation: If it is the first (inattention), then be undistracted by gaining a contemplative mind (dhyāna, i.e., by nididhyāsana, ), if the other (doubting) then keep inquiring with a proper means of knowledge (pramāṇa) and its logical application (yukti, i.e., manana, & (Bṛhad-Āraṇyaka Upaniṣad)). In that way may you become most accomplished (rūḍha-tama, i.e., jñāna-yogārūḍha)*. *(Rūḍhi also means ‘common knowledge’ which here applies, in that this teaching now becomes one’s own common knowledge, not a some come-and-go feeling or an academic philosophy.)

gloss.en: in the first or the other case
with means of knowledge and reasoning

units.label: Chapter 2 · Verse 74
units.deva:
ध्यानान् मानाद् युक्तितोऽपि रूढे भेदे वियत्-सतोः।
न कदाचित् वियत् सत्यं सद्-वस्तु च्छिद्रवन् न च॥
units.translation: By (first) thinking over the teaching logically (mananāt yuktitaḥ api) and (then) contemplation (dhyāna, as one first has to have some clear knowledge before contemplation on that knowledge), when this difference between space and (one’s) reality becomes established (rūḍha, common sense), then space can never be taken as reality, nor can the reality (that one is) have the nature of space (i.e., have dimension).

gloss.en: through a valid means of knowledge

units.label: Chapter 2 · Verse 75
units.deva:
ज्ञस्य भाति सदा व्योम निस्-तत्त्वोल्लेख-पूर्ववत्।
सद्-वस्त्वपि विभात्यस्य निच्-छिद्रत्व-पुरःसरम्॥
units.translation: For a knower (of this teaching), space ever only just appears (to one’s thought), just as before the person was unexposed to this teaching of the truth (of space and of reality), yet now for this one (who has been exposed and has assimilated this teaching) the reality (that is the Lord and oneself) vibhāti (shines everywhere, as the shinning consciousness that reveals that space, (Kaṭha Upaniṣad)) unaccompanied by any (limiting) nature of that space (i.e., that space no longer limits me, the limitless conscious-being).

gloss.en: as before the truth was explained
preceded by absence of spatial limits

units.label: Chapter 2 · Verse 76
units.deva:
वासनायं प्रवृद्धायां वियत्-सत्यत्व-वादिनम्।
सन्-मात्र-बोधम् उक्तं च दृष्ट्वा विस्मयते बुधः॥
units.translation: When one’s effortless knowledge (vāsanā, latent tendencies, regarding reality) has matured (i.e., when the knowledge has permeated to the vāsanā level), this wise person (budha) looks on amazed at those who (claim to) know reality while arguing that space is a reality.

gloss.en: the person who argues that space is real

units.label: Chapter 2 · Verse 77
units.deva:
एवम् आकाश-मिथ्यात्वे तत्-सत्यत्वे च वासिते।
न्यायेनानेन वाय्वादेः सद्-वस्तु प्रविविच्यताम्॥
units.translation: Thus, when the unreality of space and the reality of tat (that brahman) are both assimilated (vāsita, ‘both’ because a scholar’s academic knowledge of reality has not corrected their initial childhood vāsanā-based acceptance of the same reality to space), then with that same logic one should distinguish reality (that the Lord and oneself is) from vāyu, etcetera (wind and the other elements, plus everything made from them).

units.label: Chapter 2 · Verse 78
units.deva:
सद्-वस्तुन्येकदेशस्था माया तत्रैक-देश-गम्।
वियत् तत्राप्येक-देश-गतो वायुः प्रकल्पितः॥
units.translation: In reality, māyā pervades only one part (of reality). In that (māyā), space is only one part (of māyā). And in that (space), vāyu (wind or air, the element that expresses as movement) is figured to only be one part (of them).

gloss.en: residing in one part of reality

units.label: Chapter 2 · Verse 79
units.deva:
शोष-स्पर्शौ गतिर् वेगः वायु-धर्मा इमे मताः।
त्रयः स्वभावाः सन्-माया-व्योम्नां ये तेऽपि वायु-गाः॥
units.translation: Dryness, contactability, movement, and force are considered to be the qualities of the (universal) element ‘wind’ (of ‘air’, not to be limited to just the movement of air, but movement however it manifests universally or atomically), and (being within, a part of, the previous three), vāyu also gains (inherits) the three natures of existence, of māyā, and of space (i.e., is not non-reality, but is unreal, and has dimension plus manifests to our senses as sound via space).

units.label: Chapter 2 · Verse 80
units.deva:
वायुर् अस्तीति सद्-भावः सतो वायौ पृथक्-कृते।
निस्तत्व-रूपता माया-स्वभावो व्योम-गो ध्वनिः॥
units.translation: When we say vāyu exists, the existence only belongs to reality itself (sataḥ). If vāyu is taken separately (from sat) then it would lack reality, which (unreality) is the very nature of māyā. And the sound (in wind) properly only belongs to space (not to wind itself).

units.label: Chapter 2 · Verse 81
units.deva:
सतोऽनुवृत्तिः सर्वत्र व्योम्नो नेति पुरेरितम्।
व्योमानुवृत्तिर् अधुना कथं न व्याहतं वचः॥
units.translation: (Objection:) It was stated before that all encompassing (anuvṛtti) belongs to existence, but not to space (). Now (you say) encompassing (over vāyu) belongs to space. How is that statement not a contradiction?

units.label: Chapter 2 · Verse 82
units.deva:
छिद्रानुवृत्तिर् नेतीति पूर्वोक्तिर् अधुना त्वियम्।
शब्दानुवृत्तिर् एवोक्ता वचसो व्याहतिः कुतः॥
units.translation: (Reply:) Previously we said that the all encompassing (of existence) does not belong to space, but here this encompassing (of space over vāyu) belongs only to sound (the sensed attribute, the guṇa of space, not the dimension avakāśa-svarūpa of space, , or perhaps better understood if we take sound as a wave-dimension structure which allows energy, i.e., movement, to manifest, and in this way pervades all movement). From that statement, how could there be a contradiction?* Actually there is only one real sva-rūpa of all these elements, and that is reality itself, .)

units.label: Chapter 2 · Verse 83
units.deva:
ननु सद्-वस्तु-पार्थक्याद् असत्त्वं चेत् तदा कथम्।
अव्यक्त-माया-वैषम्याद् अमायामयताऽपि नो॥
units.translation: Objection (nanu, ‘No indeed’): If, because of being distinct from reality, (an element, such as vāyu) is not real (a-sattva), then why not, because it is distinct (as a product) from unmanifest māyā and thus not being (unreal) māyā, (then it would be real)?

gloss.en: because of being different from reality
because of being different from unmanifest Māyā
not being made of Māyā also

units.label: Chapter 2 · Verse 84
units.deva:
निस्तत्त्व-रूपतैवात्र मायात्वस्य प्रयोजिका।
सा शक्ति-कार्ययोस् तुल्या व्यक्ताव्यक्तत्व-भेदिनोः॥
units.translation: (Reply:) Here (in regard to an element, such as vāyu) it only lacks the nature of reality by partaking (prayojikā) of the (unreal) nature of māyā. That (unreality) is common to both śakti (māyā) and its effect, because both the unmanifest (māyā) and the manifest (elements) are distinct (from reality, tattva).

gloss.en: the state of lacking reality alone here
of those distinguished as manifest and unmanifest

units.label: Chapter 2 · Verse 85
units.deva:
सद्-असत्त्व-विवेकस्य प्रस्तुतत्वात् सा चिन्त्यताम्।
असतोऽवान्तरो भेद आस्तां तच्-चिन्तयात्र किम्॥
units.translation: Because the discernment (viveka, ) of the unreal from the real was introduced as the topic (prastutatva) of this discussion (cintyatā), then what would be the purpose here in bringing up further sub-division from that unreality, and dwelling upon them?

gloss.en: of discernment between real and unreal

units.label: Chapter 2 · Verse 86
units.deva:
सद्-वस्तु ब्रह्म शिष्टोंशो वायुर् मिथ्या यथा वियत्।
वासयित्वा चिरं वायोर् मिथ्यात्वं मरुतं त्यजेत्॥
units.translation: What is real is brahman. Whatever else remains (śiṣṭoṃśa), such as (the element) space or air are just like (unreal) mithyā (from the root mith ‘to mix up’, it is falsely mixing up, mistaking, incompatibles, (Yoga Sūtras)). By making the unreality (mithyātva) of (an element, such as) air a lasting impression (a correcting vāsanā, by proper inquiry and contemplation), then give it up (as being any part of one’s true nature).

units.label: Chapter 2 · Verse 87
units.deva:
चिन्तयेद् वह्निम् अप्येवं मरुतो न्यून-वर्तिनम्।
ब्रह्माण्डावरणेष्वेषा न्यूनाधिक-विचारणा॥
units.translation: In the same way, one should contemplate the element fire also, which has an even more limited extent than air. This inquiry into their limited extent applies in regard also to the rest (the water and earth) of the universe (brahma-aṇḍa).

gloss.en: this inquiry concerning the coverings of the cosmos
inquiry into what is less and greater

units.label: Chapter 2 · Verse 88
units.deva:
वायोर् दशांशतो न्यूनो वह्निर् वायौ प्रकल्पितः।
पुराणोक्तं तारतम्यं दशांशैर् भूत-पञ्चके॥
units.translation: The gradation (tāratamya, of extent) is mentioned in the Purāṇa literature (as well as elsewhere) in regard to manifestation of the elements as being a tenth part (of each prior element), such as fire is formed in air as limited to a tenth part of the air.

units.label: Chapter 2 · Verse 89
units.deva:
वह्निर् उष्णः प्रकाशात्मा पूर्वानुगतिर् अत्र च।
अस्ति वह्निः स निस्तत्वः शब्दवान् स्पर्शवान् अपि॥
units.translation: Heat and light are (the sensed properties) of fire, in addition to the continuance of the prior (properties): fire exists, is unreal, has sound, and has contactability (from reality, māyā, space and air, respectively).

units.label: Chapter 2 · Verse 90
units.deva:
सन्-माया-व्योम-वाय्वंशैर् युक्तस्याग्नेर् निजो गुणः।
रूपं तत्र सतः सर्वम् अन्यद् बुद्ध्या विविच्यताम्॥
units.translation: Along with the (inherited) aspects (qualities) of existence, māyā, space and air, the natural property (nijo guṇaḥ) of fire is form (rūpa, i.e., because of its light we distinguish forms). All these (properties) here are other than reality and should be distinguished (from reality) by the intellect (buddhyā, not by feelings, though that is today’s popular spiritual spin – not that that is more advanced but is more $$$ marketable. Today, renunciation is reduced to vacation).

gloss.en: with the parts of Being, Māyā, space, and wind
of the fire that is joined with them

units.label: Chapter 2 · Verse 91
units.deva:
सतो विवेचिते वह्नौ मिथ्यात्वे सति वासिते।
आपो दशांशतो न्यूनाः कल्पिता इति चिन्तयेत्॥
units.translation: When fire is unreal (mithyātva), apart from reality (which is its logical co-absence), and it exists only when there is reality (its co-presence, ), then water (i.e., liquidity), being a tenth (a fraction, of fire, i.e., liquidity is possible only above absolute zero temperature, and heat is more pervasive than fluids in the universe), one should contemplate that it (water) is confirmed (logically) to be limited (nyuna, and not worth unnecessarily identifying with).

units.label: Chapter 2 · Verse 92
units.deva:
सन्त्यापोऽमूः शून्य-तत्त्वाः स-शब्द-स्पर्श-संयुताः।
रूपवत्योऽन्य-धर्मानुवृत्त्या स्वीयो रसो गुणः॥
units.translation: This water, being existent yet unreal, has perceptibility to the sense of hearing and touch, as well as has visual form (rūpavat) which flow from the qualities of the other (more pervading elements). The quality (guṇa) of having a taste properly only belongs to (water, as the refreshing, neutral taste by which we may judge other tastes).

gloss.en: having form through the presence of other qualities

units.label: Chapter 2 · Verse 93
units.deva:
सतो विवेचितास्वप्सु तन्-मिथ्यात्वे च वासिते।
भूमिर् दशांशतो न्यूना कल्पिताप्स्विति चिन्तयेत्॥
units.translation: When water, apart from reality, has the unreality of that (māyā) and it exists (only when there is reality), then earth (i.e., solidity), being a tenth (a fraction, of the presence of water), one should contemplate that it is confirmed (logically) to be limited (nyuna, and not worth unnecessarily identifying with this packet of carbon and water we call our body).

units.label: Chapter 2 · Verse 94
units.deva:
अस्ति भूस् तत्त्व-शून्याऽस्यां शब्द-स्पर्शौ स-रूपकौ।
रसश्च परतो गन्धो नैजः सत्ता विविच्यताम्॥
units.translation: Earth has existence yet is unreal, has perceptibility to the sense of hearing and touch, and has visual form (rūpaka) and taste, which belong (respectively) to the other (elements). (Only the quality) smell properly belongs to it. Reality should be distinguished (from these elements).

gloss.en: empty of true reality, in this

units.label: Chapter 2 · Verse 95
units.deva:
पृथक्-कृतायां सत्तायां भूमिर् मिथ्याऽवशिष्यते।
भूमेर् दशांशतो न्यूनं ब्रह्माण्डं भूमि-मध्यगम्॥
units.translation: Considered apart from reality, the unreality (mithyā, ‘the falsely taken as real’) of earth remains. As a tenth part (of water) the earth has limitation. This entire universe (brahma-aṇḍa, cosmic egg) has earth in its center (from our perspective).

gloss.en: situated in the middle of earth

units.label: Chapter 2 · Verse 96
units.deva:
ब्रह्माण्ड-मध्ये तिष्ठन्ति भुवनानि चतुर्-दश।
भुवनेषु वसन्त्येषु प्राणि-देहा यथायथम्॥
units.translation: Within this universe, there are fourteen worlds (bhuvanas). In these worlds (six heavens, earth, and seven hells) having life, are the live bodies appropriate (to live there, from most to least sublime).

units.label: Chapter 2 · Verse 97
units.deva:
ब्रह्माण्ड-लोक-देहेषु सद्-वस्तुनि पृथक्-कृते।
असन्तोऽण्डादयो भान्तु तद्-भानेऽपीह का क्षतिः॥
units.translation: When all the worlds and bodies within the universe are apart (from existence, as our analysis has shown), these entities starting from the cosmic egg appear (bhāntu) as unreal. Even if these continue to appear, what loss is there here (in my reality)?

gloss.en: within the cosmic worlds and bodies
unreal, the cosmic egg and the rest

units.label: Chapter 2 · Verse 98
units.deva:
भूत-भौतिक-मायानाम् असत्त्वेऽत्यन्त-वासिते।
सद्-वस्त्वद्वैतम् इत्येषा धीर् विपर्येति न क्वचित्॥
units.translation: When there is a deep impression that the elements and their derivatives are unreal by being distinct from reality (that I am), then the knowledge that (my) reality (as existence-consciousness) is without a second (a-dvaita, non-dual) could nowhere be contradicted (i.e., all these are only appearances within my consciousness, as if inward or outward).

gloss.en: of the elements, their products, and Māyā
when their unreality is deeply impressed

units.label: Chapter 2 · Verse 99
units.deva:
सद्-अद्वैतात् पृथग्-भूते द्वैते भूम्यादि-रूपिणि।
तत्-तद्-अर्थ-क्रिया लोके यथा दृष्टा तथैव सा॥
units.translation: While duality is distinct from the non-dual reality, still the forms of earth onwards retain this or that purposeful activity in this world, as was seen before (this knowledge).

units.label: Chapter 2 · Verse 100
units.deva:
साङ्क्य-काणाद-बौद्धाद्यैर् जगद्-भेदो यथा यथा।
उत्प्रेक्ष्यतेऽनेक-युक्त्या भवत्वेष तथा तथा॥
units.translation: By Sāṅkhyas (the elemental philosophers), Kāṇādas (the atomist philosophers, ), Bauddhas (the various flavors of Buddhism), etc., difference in the universe as being in this or that way is imputed only by their countless logics. Let this be (as long as they are having fun and don't harm, why care).

gloss.en: by Sāṅkhya, Kāṇāda, Buddhist, and other thinkers

units.label: Chapter 2 · Verse 101
units.deva:
अवज्ञातं सद्-अद्वैतं निःशङ्कैर् अन्य-वादिभिः।
एवं का क्षतिर् अस्माकं तद्-द्वैतम् अवजानताम्॥
units.translation: These unhesitating philosophers have disregarded (the means of knowledge regarding) the non-dual reality. (Since they are unable to blunt this means of knowledge, then) in this way, there is no harm for us who (knowledgeably) disregard their duality.

units.label: Chapter 2 · Verse 102
units.deva:
द्वैतावज्ञा सुस्थिता चेद् अद्वैते धीः स्थिरा भवेत्।
स्थैर्ये तस्याः पुमान् एष जीवन्-मुक्त इतीर्यते॥
units.translation: The intellect that can disregard duality can remain established in non-duality. This person who has that steady knowledge is proclaimed to be a jīvan-mukta (freed while living).

units.label: Chapter 2 · Verse 103
units.deva:
एषा ब्राह्मी स्थितिः पार्थ नैनां प्राप्य विमुह्यति।
स्थित्वास्याम् अन्तकालेऽपि ब्रह्म-निर्वाणम् ऋच्छति॥
units.translation: This is being firm in/as reality (brahman, sat), O Arjuna. Attaining this, one is not any longer deluded. Being firm in this, even just at the last moment, one attains liberation in/as brahman ( (Bhagavad Gītā)).

units.label: Chapter 2 · Verse 104
units.deva:
सद्-अद्वैतेऽनृत-द्वैते यद् अन्योन्यैक्य-वीक्षणम्।
तस्यान्त-कालस् तद्-भेद-बुद्धिर् एव न चेतरः॥
units.translation: ‘The last moment’ (anta-kāla) here can mean as clearly seeing the oneness of the mutual (dependent dualities), where the falsity of duality is the reality of oneness. It is the change of mind at that time (tad-bheda-buddhi), not otherwise (see next).

gloss.en: in real nonduality and false duality
seeing the oneness of each with the other

units.label: Chapter 2 · Verse 105
units.deva:
यद्वान्त-कालः प्राणस्य वियोगोऽस्तु प्रसिद्धितः।
तस्मिन् कालेऽपि न भ्रान्तेर् गतायाः पुनर् आगमः॥
units.translation: (…Otherwise, indirectly) ‘the last moment’ means at death, according to common parlance. Even at that time (“attaining liberation” is not due to physical death, since) there is no return of the delusion which had already left (or just then left).* *(Moreover, this emphasizes no rebirth, even though the intellect dissipates. Hence, this alternate interpretation is not lacking purpose).

units.label: Chapter 2 · Verse 106
units.deva:
नी-रोग उपविष्टो वा रुग्णो वा विलुठन् भुवि।
मूर्छितो वा त्यजत्वेष प्राणान् भ्रान्तिर् न सर्वथा॥
units.translation: Whether (one dies) healthy or broken, whether wallowing on the ground or unconscious, having given up the life-energies, this one has no delusion in anyway.

units.label: Chapter 2 · Verse 107
units.deva:
दिने दिने स्वप्न-सुप्त्योर् अधीते विस्मृतेऽप्ययम्।
परे-द्युर् नानधीतः स्यात् तद्वद् विद्या न नश्यति॥
units.translation: What is learned is daily forgotten during dream and deep sleep, yet (remaining in the vāsanā level, in the citta) it does not become unknown the following day. Like that this knowledge (vidyā) is not lost.

units.label: Chapter 2 · Verse 108
units.deva:
प्रमाणोत्पादिता विद्या प्रमाणं प्रबलं विना।
न नश्यति न वेदान्तात् प्रबलं मानम् ईक्ष्यते॥
units.translation: Knowledge attained through a means of knowledge (a pramāṇa, such as perception or logic) does not vanish unless there is a stronger (prabala, non-defective, nirduṣṭa) means of knowledge. There is no stronger means of knowledge (māna) than Vedānta (the Upaniṣads, in regard to the nature of the world and oneself).

gloss.en: produced by a means of knowledge

units.label: Chapter 2 · Verse 109
units.deva:
तस्माद् वेदान्त-संसिद्धिं सद्-अद्वैतं न बाध्यते।
अन्त-कालेऽप्यतो भूत-विवेकान् निर्वृतिः स्थिता॥
units.translation: Therefore, the non-dual reality (knowledge) established by Vedānta does not vanish even at the last moment (in either sense above). Hence, due to this discerning of the elements (as unreal, apart from the reality that one is) this nirvṛti (freedom, loss of transitoriness, the loss of identification with duality) remains.

gloss.en: even at the final moment, therefore

units.label: Chapter 3 · Verse 1
units.deva:
गुहातितं ब्रह्म यत्-तत्-पञ्च-कोश-विवेकतः।
बोद्धुं शक्यं ततः कोश-पञ्चकं प्रविविच्यते॥
units.translation: By discerning the brahman who has entered into the cave (guhā) (as it were) from each of the five kośas (locations where mistakes can be made, which make up the cave), it is possible to gain knowledge (of brahman). Therefore, here the five kośas are investigated.

gloss.en: through discernment of each of the five sheaths

units.label: Chapter 3 · Verse 2
units.deva:
देहाद् अभ्यन्तरः प्राणः प्राणाद् अभ्यन्तरं मनः।
ततः कर्ता ततो भोक्ता गुहा सेयं परम्परा॥
units.translation: Within the (physical) body (deha) is the life energy (prāṇa). Within the prāṇa is the examining mind (manas). Within that (manas) is the doer (kartṛ, the intellect). Within that (kartṛ) is the enjoyer (bhoktṛ). This layering is the cave (guhā, where the light of knowledge is to be brought in).

units.label: Chapter 3 · Verse 3
units.deva:
पितृ-भुक्तान्न-जाद् वीर्याज् जातोऽन्नेनैव वर्धते।
देहः सोऽन्नमयो नात्मा प्राक् चोर्ध्वं तद्-अभावतः॥
units.translation: Arisen from the potency born of the food eaten by the parents, and expanded only by more food, this body is only a modification of food (anna-maya, the first kośa). It is not oneself (ātman), because it (the food-body) does not exist before (its coming together) nor after (its falling apart).

gloss.en: from food eaten by the parents

units.label: Chapter 3 · Verse 4
units.deva:
पूर्व-जन्मन्यसन्न् एतज् जन्म संपादयेत् कथम्।
भावि-जन्मन्यसन् कर्म न भुञ्जीतेह सञ्चितम्॥
units.translation: This (body) was not existing prior to its birth, so how could it produce its birth (i.e., it wasn’t there to manifest itself)? (This body) not existing in any future birth, could then not enjoy its accumulated (sañcita) karma (so the activities of this body are for nothing after the body’s death).

gloss.en: not existing in the previous birth
not existing in a future birth

units.label: Chapter 3 · Verse 5
units.deva:
पूर्णो देहे बलं यच्छन्न् अक्षणां यः प्रवर्तकः।
वायुः प्राणमयो नासावात्मा चैतन्य-वर्जनात्॥
units.translation: Filling this body, giving it strength and energizing the senses, the vital air (vāyu, prāṇa) is called the prāṇa-maya (the second kośa). This also is not oneself (ātman), since it is devoid of consciousness (caitanya, i.e., it cannot be you, the seer).

units.label: Chapter 3 · Verse 6
units.deva:
अहन्तां ममतां देहे गेहादौ च करोति यः।
कामाद्यवस्थया भ्रान्तो नासावात्मा मनोमयः॥
units.translation: The (mind) which forms the ideas of ‘I’ and ‘my’ towards this body, as well as towards house, etc., remains deluded while undergoing various states of desire, etcetera. (Being continually changing) this mano-maya (the third kośa) also is not oneself (ātman).

gloss.en: in the house and the rest

units.label: Chapter 3 · Verse 7
units.deva:
लीना सुप्तौ वपुर् बोधे व्याप्नुयाद् आनखाग्र-गा।
चिच्-छायोपेत-धीर् नात्मा विज्ञानमय-शब्द-भाक्॥
units.translation: The intellect (dhī) endowed with a reflection of consciousness (i.e., it’s a subtle substance that appears conscious, although is not itself consciousness), appears in waking state as pervading the body up to the tips of the fingers, yet vanishes in deep sleep (līnā suptau). It enjoys the name vijñāna-maya (the fourth kośa). It also is not oneself (because it appears and disappears).

gloss.en: going to the tips of the nails
bearing the name made of understanding

units.label: Chapter 3 · Verse 8
units.deva:
कर्तृत्व-करणत्वाभ्यां विक्रियेतान्तरिन्द्रियम्।
विज्ञान-मनसी अन्तर् बहिश् चैते परस्परम्॥
units.translation: The interior organ (i.e., the antaḥ-karaṇa, the whole mind) functions as both the agent and the instrument. It is here divided into the intellect and the mind (the fourth and third kośas). The two operate (for the most part) in the internal and external world, respectively.

units.label: Chapter 3 · Verse 9
units.deva:
काचिद् अन्तर्-मुखा वृत्तिर् आनन्द-प्रतिबिम्ब-भाक्।
पुण्य-भोगे भोग-शान्तौ निद्रा-रूपेण लीयते॥
units.translation: The mental function (vṛti, thought-form) which is only directed inward (antar-mukha) and enjoys just a reflection of ānanda (of the fullness of the ātman, and hence also is not the ānanda-ātman, oneself) is there (in varying degrees) during the experience of (past) puṇya (favorable karma) and when there is a peaceful experience, and abides (quietly unnoticed until waking) in the form of deep sleep. (This ānanda-maya is the fifth kośa.)

units.label: Chapter 3 · Verse 10
units.deva:
कादाचित्कत्वतो नात्मा स्याद् आनन्दमयोऽप्ययम्।
बिम्ब-भूतो य आनन्द आत्माऽसौ सर्वदा स्थितेः॥
units.translation: Because it has the nature of existing only when it appears (kādācitkatva), this ānanda-maya cannot be the ātman. The ānanda (fullness) itself, as the very being of this reflection (of fullness), is the ātman (oneself), since it always remains (in the past, present and future, as well as before time itself comes into being).

gloss.en: this one made of bliss also

units.label: Chapter 3 · Verse 11
units.deva:
ननु देहम् उपक्रम्य निद्रानन्दान्त-वस्तुषु।
मा भूद् आत्मत्वम् अन्यस् तु न कश्चिद् अनुभूयते॥
units.translation: Objection (nanu, ‘No indeed’): Towards all entities from the (waking world) deha to the ānanda in the sleep world (nidrā), nothing else would be left out which could be experienced as oneself (ātmatva).

gloss.en: in things ending with the bliss of sleep

units.label: Chapter 3 · Verse 12
units.deva:
बाढं निद्रादयः सर्वेऽनुभूयन्ते न चेतरः।
तथाप्येतेऽनुभूयन्ते येन तं को निवारयेत्॥
units.translation: (Reply:) Sure (bāḍham). All things from sleep (nidrā) onward (to the body), and nothing else, are experienced (as oneself). But, who can deny that by which all these are in that way experienced?

units.label: Chapter 3 · Verse 13
units.deva:
स्वयम् एवानुभूतित्वाद् विद्यते नानुभाव्यता।
ज्ञातृ-ज्ञानान्तराभावाद् अज्ञेयो न त्वसत्तया॥
units.translation: Since all experience belongs to oneself (svayam) alone, it cannot be something experienced. Because there is no experiencer or experiencing apart from it, then (oneself) cannot be one of the knowables (a-jñeya). But not because it (svam) does not exist (a-sattā).

gloss.en: because there is no other knower or knowledge
but because it does not exist

units.label: Chapter 3 · Verse 14
units.deva:
माधुर्यादि-स्व-भावानाम् अन्यत्र स्व-गुणार्पिणाम्।
स्वस्मिंस् तद्-अर्पणापेक्षा नो न चास्त्यन्यद् अर्पकम्॥
units.translation: Each of the qualities (guṇas, of taste) impart its nature (sva-bhāva), such as sweet, etc., to others, but indeed does not need to impart it to itself (e.g., sugar can make others sweet, but does not require anything else to make itself sweet). Nor can anything else impart it (e.g., salt to sugar, etcetera).

gloss.en: of sweet and the rest, whose nature is their own

units.label: Chapter 3 · Verse 15
units.deva:
अर्पकान्तर-राहित्येऽप्य् अस्त्येषां तत्-स्वभावता।
मा भूत् तथानुभाव्यत्वं बोधात्मा तु न हीत्यते॥
units.translation: Even without another flavorer (arpaka, imparter), these (flavors, i.e., the six rasas: sweet, salty, sour, pungent, astringent and bitter) have their own nature. Similarly, while the nature of knowledge itself (bodha-ātman, caitanya) cannot be a thing to be experienced (by another), still it does not lose this (nature of knowledge, bodha-ātman, by not being an object of the mind, etcetera).

gloss.en: even when another imparter is absent

units.label: Chapter 3 · Verse 16
units.deva:
स्वयं-ज्योतिर् भवत्येष पुरोऽस्माद् भासतेऽखिलात्।
तम् एव भान्तम् अन्वेति तद् भासा भास्यते जगत्॥
units.translation: (The scriptures declares:) This (ātman, puruṣa, while dreaming) is “self-shinning (svayam-jyoti)” ( (Bṛhad-Āraṇyaka Upaniṣad)). It shines before all this (was created). “That (brahma-ātman) alone shines and (everything else) shines after” ( (Kaṭha Upaniṣad)) – by this shine, all that universe which comes after is revealed (bhāsyate).

units.label: Chapter 3 · Verse 17
units.deva:
येनेदं जानते सर्वं तत् केनान्येन जानताम्।
विज्ञातारं केन विद्याच् छक्तं वेद्ये तु साधनम्॥
units.translation: How can that, by which all this (universe) is known, itself be known by anything else? By what can one know the very knower? (Since) an instrument (for knowing, such as the manas or buddhi) is only applicable to what is knowable (vedya, what it can objectify, what it can enclose within its thought form).

units.label: Chapter 3 · Verse 18
units.deva:
स वेत्ति वेद्यं तत्सर्वं नान्यस् तस्यास्ति वेदिता।
विदिताविदिताभ्यां तत् पृथग् बोध-स्वरूपकम्॥
units.translation: The (ātman, self) knows all that is knowable (including the manas and buddhi). Nothing else can be a knower of it. Different from the known and the unknown is that whose very nature is knowledge.

units.label: Chapter 3 · Verse 19
units.deva:
बोधेऽप्यनुभवो यस्य न कथञ्चन जायते।
तं कथं बोधयेच्छास्त्रं लोष्टं नर-समाकृतिम्॥
units.translation: (If denying the existence of consciousness) someone has experience in knowing, yet does not know how (he knows), then in what way could that one be taught the scripture? It’s as if he’s a clod of dirt in the form of a person.

units.label: Chapter 3 · Verse 20
units.deva:
जिह्वा मेऽस्ति न वेत्युक्तिर् लज्जायै केवलं यथा।
न बुध्यते मया बोधो बोद्धव्य इति तादृशी॥
units.translation: Just as it would only amount to an absurdity (lajjā) to say whether or not I have a tongue (since I wouldn’t have to complete the sentence to convey I have one, and I couldn’t say if I didn’t), so it would be to say ‘I do not have knowledge of what knowledge (bodha, caitanya) is, but I need to have it’.

units.label: Chapter 3 · Verse 21
units.deva:
यस्मिन् यस्मिन्न् अस्ति लोके बोधस् तत् तद् उपेक्षणे।
यद् बोध-मात्रं तद् ब्रह्मेत्येवं धीर् ब्रह्म-निश्चयः॥
units.translation: While disregarding everything in the world (i.e., taking them as mithyā, as only nāma-rūpa, not as sat, not as oneself), then bodha (knowledge, consciousness, satyaṃ jñānam) alone exists (remains as the permanent reality, as oneself). This is the pure knowledge which is called brahman (the limitless source and reality of the universe). In this way (not hiding from the world, with eyes wide open) this understanding is clarity in reality (brahman-niścaya).

units.label: Chapter 3 · Verse 22
units.deva:
पञ्च-कोश-परित्यागे साक्षि-बोधावशेषतः।
स्वस्वरूपं स एव स्याच् छून्यत्वं तस्य दुर्घटम्॥
units.translation: While giving up (the claim of reality towards) the five koṣas, since what remains is the knowledge that is the witness (the sākṣin, of them), then that alone would be one’s very nature (sva-sva-rūpa, as pure consciousness-being). It is unnatural (durghaṭa) to attribute non-existence (śūyatva) to it (to one’s very own self).

gloss.en: when the five sheaths are given up

units.label: Chapter 3 · Verse 23
units.deva:
अस्ति तावत् स्वयं नाम विवादाविषयत्वतः।
स्वस्मिन्न् अपि विवादश् चेत् प्रतिवाद्य् अत्र को भवेत्॥
units.translation: Oneself indeed surely exists (asti), since there is no scope here for arguing otherwise. Even if there were an argument regarding the (existence or non-existence of the) self, then who could possibly be the opponent (that argues that he himself is non-existent, and who would pursue a discussion with someone who makes such absurd claims)?

gloss.en: because it is not subject to dispute

units.label: Chapter 3 · Verse 24
units.deva:
स्वासत्त्वं तु न कस्मैचिद् रोचते विभ्रमं विना।
अत एव श्रुतिर् बाधं ब्रूते चासत्त्व-वादिनः॥
units.translation: Aside from delusion, no one seriously entertains the notion that they don’t exist. Thus the scripture exposes the absurdity of one who argues for non-existence.

gloss.en: of the advocate of nonexistence too

units.label: Chapter 3 · Verse 25
units.deva:
असद् ब्रह्मेति चेद् वेद स्वयम् एव भवेद् असत्।
अतोऽस्य मा भूद् वेद्यत्वं स्व-सत्त्वं त्वभ्युपेयताम्॥
units.translation: ‘If anyone thinks that brahman (unlimited existence-knowledge) does not exist, that would only make that one himself or herself non-existent’ ( (Taittirīya Upaniṣad)). Thus, one can accept that while (brahman) would not be an object of knowledge (vedyatva, ), still it is as real as oneself (sva-sattva).

units.label: Chapter 3 · Verse 26
units.deva:
कीदृक् तर्हीति चेत् पृच्छेद् ईदृक्ता नास्ति तत्र हि।
यद् अनीदृग् अतादृक् च तत् स्वरूपं विनिश्चिनु॥
units.translation: If one asks, ‘Then what sort of thing it it?’ Here we say it is not like anything. What is not like a this or that, you should clearly know it only as its own unique nature.

units.label: Chapter 3 · Verse 27
units.deva:
अक्षाणां विषयस् त्वीदृक् परोक्षस् तादृग् उच्यते।
विषयी नाक्ष-विषयः स्वत्वान् नास्य परोक्षता॥
units.translation: Whereas, an object of the senses is said to be ‘like this’, or if beyond the senses is said to be ‘like that’. The one who witnesses objects (the viśayin, sākṣin) cannot be an object of the senses (like ‘this’), and since it is oneself, it cannot have any remoteness (like ‘that’).

gloss.en: not an object of the senses

units.label: Chapter 3 · Verse 28
units.deva:
अवेद्योऽप्यपरोक्षोऽतः स्व-प्रकाशो भवत्ययम्।
सत्यं ज्ञानम् अनन्तं चेत्य् अस्तीह ब्रह्म-लक्षणम्॥
units.translation: Even though it cannot be an object of knowledge (a-vedya), still it is immediate (a-parokṣa, as oneself). So it (brahma-ātman) must be self-shinning (sva-prakāśa, self-revealing). ‘Existence consciousness unlimited’ (satyaṃ jñānam an-antam, (Taittirīya Upaniṣad)), this expression that indicates the nature of brahman is also applicable here (iha, to oneself).

units.label: Chapter 3 · Verse 29
units.deva:
सत्यत्वं बाध-राहित्यं जगद्-बाधैक-साक्षिणः।
बाधः किं साक्षिको ब्रूहि न त्वसाक्षिक इष्यते॥
units.translation: Existence is what can never be negated (bādha-rāhitya). If (at the dissolution of the universe) the one witness of this perishing world itself perishes, then tell me who could be the witnesser (of that)? There would be no witnesser of that.

gloss.en: the sole witness of the world's negation

units.label: Chapter 3 · Verse 30
units.deva:
अपनीतेषु मूर्तेषु ह्यमूर्तं शिष्यते वियत्।
शक्येषु बाधितेष्वन्ते शिष्यते यत् तद् एव तत्॥
units.translation: When all forms are destroyed, then the formless space remains. When all that can be destroyed (including space) ends, that which remains is only that (tad, that reality-brahman).

units.label: Chapter 3 · Verse 31
units.deva:
सर्व-बाधे न किञ्चिच् चेद् यन् न किञ्चित् तद् एव तत्।
भाषा एवात्र भिद्यन्ते निर्बाधं तावद् अस्ति हि॥
units.translation: If you say ‘nothing’ exists upon the dissolution of the entire universe, then isn’t that ‘nothing’ in fact ‘that’ (tad, which is brahman where ‘no other thing is’, a-dvitīya). Only the verbiage differs, in as much as (you say) the dissolution indeed IS.

units.label: Chapter 3 · Verse 32
units.deva:
अत एव श्रुतिर् बाध्यं बाधित्वा शेषयत्यदः।
स एष नेति नेत्यात्मेत्यतद्-व्यावृत्ति-रूपतः॥
units.translation: Because of this alone the scripture makes known that whatever remains after negating the negatable is that (adas, brahman). That very (brahman), which is ‘neti neti’ (‘not this and not that’ name or form, (Bṛhad-Āraṇyaka Upaniṣad)), is ātman (oneself). It is in the form of that (reality) which does not go away (a-vyāvṛtti).

gloss.en: not thus, the Self, whose nature excludes what is not-Self

units.label: Chapter 3 · Verse 33
units.deva:
इदं रूपं तु यद् यावत् तत् त्यक्तुं शक्यतेऽखिलम्।
अशक्यो ह्यनिदं-रूपः स आत्मा बाध-वर्जितः॥
units.translation: Whereas, to which extent every ‘this form’ (every name and form) can be negated, that is not possible for what is not a ‘this form’. That is the ātman (the witness of all ‘this’) left after negation (of all else).

units.label: Chapter 3 · Verse 34
units.deva:
सिद्धं ब्रह्मणि सत्यत्वं ज्ञानत्वं तु पुरेरितम्।
स्वयम् एवानुभूतित्वाद् इत्यादि-वचनैः स्फुटम्॥
units.translation: Here it has been established that in brahman is reality. Now, the fact that its nature is knowledge was clearly told earlier (purā) through the statements ‘svayam eva anubhūtitvāt’ (‘because there is no experiencer or experiencing apart from it’, ), and others (statements, such as ).

gloss.en: and the rest of the statements

units.label: Chapter 3 · Verse 35
units.deva:
न व्यापित्वाद् देशतोऽन्तो नित्यत्वान् नापि कालतः।
न वस्तुतोऽपि सार्वात्म्याद् आनन्त्यं ब्रह्मणि त्रिधा॥
units.translation: Being pervasive (vyāpitva) this (brahma-ātman) is not limited by place (deśataḥ anta). Being persistent (nityatva, before, during and after the universe) it is also not limited by time (kālataḥ). Being the self of all (sārvātmya, the very nature of everything), it is not limited as an object (vastutaḥ). This is the three-fold limitlessness in regard to brahman (namely, deśataḥ, kālataḥ, vastutaḥ).

gloss.en: because it is the Self of all

units.label: Chapter 3 · Verse 36
units.deva:
देश-कालान्य-वस्तूनां कल्पितत्वाच् च मायया।
न देशादि-कृतोऽन्तोऽस्ति ब्रह्मानन्त्यं स्फुटं ततः॥
units.translation: Since place, time, and another object are imposed (by us, by our thinking them as real) due to māyā (the ignorance of the limitless reality and the projection of the cosmic appearance, ), then whatever (limitation) is made from these three (e.g., this separate body here and now) would also not be a limit (to brahma-ātman). Thus the limitlessness of brahman is made clear.

gloss.en: of place, time, and other things
a limit made by place and the rest exists

units.label: Chapter 3 · Verse 37
units.deva:
सत्यं ज्ञानम् अनन्तं यद् ब्रह्म तद् वस्तु तस्य तत्।
ईश्वरत्वं च जीवत्वम् उपाधि-द्वय-कल्पितम्॥
units.translation: This brahman which is unlimited existence-consciousness () is that (only) entity (vastu, and there is not other entity). Its (tasya) Lordship (Īśvaratva) and individuality (jīvatva) are non-intrinsic names and forms (upādhis) dually imposed (by us due to māyā and to a-vidya respectively, ).

units.label: Chapter 3 · Verse 38
units.deva:
शक्तिर् अस्त्य् ऐश्वरी काचित् सर्व-वस्तु-नियामिका।
आनन्दमयम् आरभ्य गूढा सर्वेषु वस्तुषु॥
units.translation: Power (śakti, called māyā), which is attributed to the Lord (Īśvara), is the order (niyāmikā) within everything, beginning from the ānanda-maya (the fifth kośa). This (one unifying power) is hidden within all beings and entities.

units.label: Chapter 3 · Verse 39
units.deva:
वस्तु-धर्मा नियम्येरन् शक्त्या नैव यदा तदा।
अन्योन्य-धर्म-साङ्कर्याद् विप्लवेत जगत् खलु॥
units.translation: If the (peculiar) attributes of entities were not ordered by this power (of the Lord), then due to a commingling of the attributes with each other (as if they each had their own separate minds, and the nature of ‘up’ choose to be ‘blue’ instead of obeying its nature, etc.), the universe would indeed be chaotic.* *(That chaos would be different from sciences’ chaos, which is simply the non-binary nature of entities that are still in obeyance to a subset of possibilities).

gloss.en: because of mixing each other's qualities

units.label: Chapter 3 · Verse 40
units.deva:
चिच्-छायावेशतः शक्तिश् चेतनेव विभाति सा।
तच्-छक्त्युपाधि-संयोगाद् ब्रह्मैवेश्वरतां व्रजेत्॥
units.translation: This power (śakti, māyā as the total sattva of nature, ) by the pervasion of the reflection of consciousness (cit-chāyā-āveśataḥ) appears to be as though it is itself conscious. Due to the association with appearance of the śakti in that (reflection of consciousness), brahman indeed (apparently) gains the nature of being the Lord (i.e., as though gains omniscience).

gloss.en: because of the entry of reflected consciousness
from union with that power-limiting adjunct
Brahman itself, the state of being Lord

units.label: Chapter 3 · Verse 41
units.deva:
कोशोपाधि-विवक्षायां याति ब्रह्मैव जीवताम्।
पिता पितामहश्-चैकः पुत्र-पौत्रौ यथा प्रति॥
units.translation: Brahman gains the status of an individual (jīvatā) when the topic is the association (upādhi) with the kośas (the limiting locations). Just as the very same person gains the status of father or grandfather when in association with his son or grandson.

gloss.en: when the limiting adjunct of the sheaths is being discussed

units.label: Chapter 3 · Verse 42
units.deva:
पुत्रादेर् अविवक्षायां न पिता न पितामहः।
तद्वन्नेशो नापि जीवः शक्ति-कोशाविवक्षणे॥
units.translation: Just as a person is neither a father nor a grandfather when the topic is not his son, etc., so (brahman) is neither the Lord nor the individual, when the topic is not śakti (māyā, the power manifesting the appearance of the universe) nor the kośas (the individual abodes of personification).

gloss.en: of a son and the rest
when power and sheaths are not discussed

units.label: Chapter 3 · Verse 43
units.deva:
य एवं ब्रह्म वेदैष ब्रह्मैव भवति स्वयम्।
ब्रह्मणो नास्ति जन्मातः पुनर् एष न जायते॥
units.translation: The one who knows brahman (reality) in this same way, takes that brahman alone as oneself. Since brahman (reality) has no birth, then this one (oneself) cannot be born again.

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 1
units.deva:
ईश्वरेणापि जीवेन सृष्टं द्वैतं विविच्यते।
विवेके सति जीवेन हेयो बन्धः स्फुटी-भवेत्॥
units.translation: Now is discerned the duality created by the Lord (Īśvara) and also by the individual (jīva). When this discernment is made, then the bondage (bandha) which is to be rejected by the individual is made clear.

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 2
units.deva:
मायां तु प्रकृतिं विद्यान् मायिनं तु महेश्वरम्।
स मायी सृजतीत्याहुः श्वेताश्वतर-शाखिनः॥
units.translation: “One should know māyā as mother nature (prakṛti), and the limitless Lord as having māyā within (māyin))” ( (Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad)), thus declare the adherents to the Śvetāśvatara (Upaniṣad) that the one (the Lord) who wields māyā creates.

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 3
units.deva:
आत्मा वा इदम् अग्रेऽभूत् स ईक्षत सृजा इति।
संकल्पेनासृजल् लोकान् स एतानिति बह्वृचाः॥
units.translation: “Ātman (the self) alone was all this in the beginning… That one envisioned, ‘I now create (sṛjai, sṛje, project the appearance of a world, the universe)’ ” ( (Aitareya Upaniṣad)) – by thought (saṅkalpa) alone He manifested these worlds. So say many such ṛcs (scriptural mantras).

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 4
units.deva:
खं वाय्वग्नि-जलोर्व्योषध्यन्न-देहाः क्रमाद् अमी।
संभूता ब्रह्मणस् तस्माद् एतस्माद् आत्मनोऽखिलाः॥
units.translation: “From this very self (ātman),” ( (Taittirīya Upaniṣad)) from brahman, was manifested all these bodies, in succession, from space, from air, from fire, from water, from earth (urvī), from plants, and from food.

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 5
units.deva:
बहु स्याम् एवातः प्रजायेयेति कामतः।
तपस्-तप्त्वाऽसृजत् सर्वं जगद् इत्याह तित्तिरिः॥
units.translation: From this thought (kāmataḥ), “ ‘Let Me be many. Let Me be born.’ Having thus contemplated, He manifested all this” ( (Taittirīya Upaniṣad)), the universe, says the Tittiri (the Taittirīya Upaniṣad).

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 6
units.deva:
इदम् अग्रे सद् एवासीद् बहुत्वाय तद् ऐक्षत।
तेजोऽबन्नाण्ड-जादीनि ससर्जेति च सामगाः॥
units.translation: “Existence alone was there before all this” ( (Chāndogya Upaniṣad)), thus declare the adherents to the Sāman (the Chāndogya Upaniṣad), and “That (reality) thought (aikṣata) to become many (names and forms), and created energy (tejas), water, food, and those born from eggs, etcetera (wombs, and so on)” ( (Chāndogya Upaniṣad)).

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 7
units.deva:
विस्फुलिङ्गा यथा वह्नेर् जायन्तेऽक्षरतस् तथा।
विविधाश् चिज्-जडा भावा इत्याथर्वणिकी श्रुतिः॥
units.translation: “Just as sparks (visphul-iṅgas, outward expansions)” from (a well-lit) fire (by the thousands) arise “from the imperishable (a-kṣara, puruṣa) the varieties of entities” ( (Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad)) both conscious and unconscious, says the scripture of the Ātharvaṇikas.

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 8
units.deva:
जगद्-अव्याकृतं पूर्वम् आसीद् व्याक्रियताधुना।
दृश्याभ्यां नाम-रूपाभ्यां विराडादिषु ते स्फुटे॥
units.translation: Before (pūrvam, agre, before creation) the universe “was unmanifested (a-vyākṛta) and now (adhunā) is in a state of manifestation (vyākriyatā)” ( (Bṛhad-Āraṇyaka Upaniṣad)). By appearing only as perceptible name and form, these two (nāma-rūpa) manifest (sphuṭa) in everything beginning with Virāṭ (the first manifest cosmic being).

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 9
units.deva:
विराण् मनुर् नरो गावः खराश्वाजादयस् तथा।
पिपीलिकावधि-द्वन्द्वम् इति वाजसनेयिनः॥
units.translation: Virāṭ became each of the manus (the first progenitors), mankind, cows, mules, horses, goats, and so on in that way, as a pair (dvandva, male and female), down to the ants, say the Vājasaneyins (adhering to the Bṛhad-āraṇyaka Upaniṣad).

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 10
units.deva:
कृत्वा रूपान्तरं जैवं देहे प्राविशद् ईश्वरः।
इति ताः श्रुतयः प्राहुर् जीवत्वं प्राण-धारणात्॥
units.translation: The Lord, taking the different forms, entered into every body related to each jīva, say the scriptures (such as (Chāndogya Upaniṣad)). This nature of being a jīva (‘what lives’) is because it holds together (in this body) the life energies (prāṇas, i.e., their seeming multiplicity is due to the appearance of separate packets of prāṇas).

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 11
units.deva:
चैतन्यं यद् अधिष्ठानं लिङ्ग-देहश् च यः पुनः।
चिच्-छाया लिङ्ग-देहस्था तत् संघो जीव उच्यते॥
units.translation: The caitanya (consciousness) which is the abode (adhiṣṭhāna, of everything), plus (as the upādhi, limiting attribute which is) this subtle body (liṅga-deha: consisting of the prāṇa, manas and buddhi kośas, apart from the physical body) and the reflection (the limited presence) of consciousness (cit-chāyā) within that subtle body (which lights it up with knowledge) – that (three-fold) combination is called the jīva, the individual, who can transmigrate through countless bodies).

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 12
units.deva:
माहेश्वरी तु माया या तस्या निर्माण-शक्तिवत्।
विद्यते मोह-शक्तिश् च तं जीवं मोहयत्य् असौ॥
units.translation: Māyā, on the other hand, who belongs to the Lord (māheśvarī), appears to have both the power to manifest (nirmāṇa) and the power to deceive (moha, to hide from everyone their essential nature). It (māyā as moha-śakti) is the one who causes the jīva to be deceived (into thinking it is not limitless consciousness-reality and is only the limited kośa).

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 13
units.deva:
मोहाद् अनीशतां प्राप्य मग्नो वपुषि शोचति।
ईश-सृष्टम् इदं द्वैतं सर्वम् उक्तं समासतः॥
units.translation: Because of this delusion, (the jīva) becomes powerless (an-īśatā, loses its identity with the Lord), takes itself to be this body, and suffers (its limitations). This in brief is said to be the duality (dvaita) manifested by the Lord.

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 14
units.deva:
सप्तान्न-ब्राह्मणे द्वैतं जीव-सृष्टं प्रपञ्चितम्।
अन्नानि सप्त ज्ञानेन कर्मणाऽजनयत् पिता॥
units.translation: In the Saptānna Brāhmaṇa (the 1.5 section of Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad) there is presented the duality manifested by the individual (jīva, see , the individual’s world of experience). Here the father (the jīva, individual) (as though, similar to the Lord Father) creates by its knowledge and activity the seven annas (experiences starting from food, (Bṛhad-Āraṇyaka Upaniṣad)).

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 15
units.deva:
मर्त्यान्नम् एकं देवान्ने द्वे पश्वन्नं चतुर्थकम्।
अन्यत्-त्रितयम् आत्मार्थम् अन्नानां विनियोजनम्॥
units.translation: One food is for humans, two foods are for the deities, the fourth food is for the animals, and the other three are for oneself (ātman, i.e., the jīva). Thus the (seven) foods are allotted.

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 16
units.deva:
व्रीह्यादिकं दर्श-पूर्ण-मासौ क्षीरं तथा मनः।
वाक् प्राणाश् चेति सप्तत्वम् अन्नानाम् अवगम्यताम्॥
units.translation: Cooked rice and other grains (is the food only for humans), the new and full moon sacrifices (are the two foods for the deities), and milk (is the initial food for the animals also) (those are the eaten-foods, by which one is physically satiated), then (the eater-foods, the foods which enjoy other foods, by which one is satiated subtly, are) the mind, speech, and vital-energies (are for oneself the three ‘foods’ for consuming the intermediary world, the terrestrial world and the heavens, respectively). Thus the understanding regarding the seven kinds of foods ( (Bṛhad-Āraṇyaka Upaniṣad)).

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 17
units.deva:
ईशेन यद्यप्येतानि निर्मितानि स्वरूपतः।
तथापि ज्ञान-कर्माभ्यां जीवोऽकार्षीत् तद्-अन्नताम्॥
units.translation: Even though all these are in reality created by the Lord, still the jīva made them his food through his (individual) knowledge and activity (jñāna-karma).

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 18
units.deva:
ईश-कार्यं जीव-भोग्यं जगद् द्वाभ्यां समन्वितम्।
पितृ-जन्या भर्तृ-भोग्या यथा योषित् तथेष्यताम्॥
units.translation: Being created by the Lord but only experienced by the individual, this (one) universe (here, the ‘food’) is understood to accordingly have these two (perspectives: its creator and its enjoyer). Like a young woman (as the māyā universe) is both a daughter to her father (her creator) and a wife to her husband (her enjoyer).

gloss.en: to be enjoyed by the individual
to be enjoyed by a husband

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 19
units.deva:
माया-वृत्त्यात्मको हीश-संकल्पः साधनं जनौ।
मनो-वृत्त्यात्मको जीव-संकल्पो भोग-साधनम्॥
units.translation: In the creation, the thought of the Lord (Īśa-saṅkalpa), which is a modification (vṛtti) of māyā, is the means (sādhana, for creation). Whereas, the thought of the jīva, which is a modification of the mind, is the means of enjoyment (bhoga, of the creation).

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 20
units.deva:
ईश-निर्मित-मण्यादौ वस्तुन्येकविधे स्थिते।
भोक्तृ-धी-वृत्ति-नानात्वात् तद्-भोगो बहुधेष्यते॥
units.translation: Towards a gem (maṇi), etc. created by the Lord, which exists in one way (to the Lord) as an entity, since the experience of that (entity) is through a variety of mental states of the individual experiencer, then it appears variously.

gloss.en: in a gem and so on made by the Lord
in an object of one kind
because of the variety of the experiencer's mental states

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 21
units.deva:
हृष्यत्येको मणिं लब्ध्वा क्रुध्यत्यन्यो ह्यलाभतः।
पश्यत्येव विरक्तोऽत्र न हृष्यति न कुप्यति॥
units.translation: One who gets the gem becomes happy. Another, not getting it, becomes unhappy. Someone else having no interest towards it simply looks on, neither gets happy nor unhappy.

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 22
units.deva:
प्रियोऽप्रिय उपेक्ष्यश् चेत्याकारा मणि-गास् त्रयः।
सृष्टा जीवैर् ईश-सृष्टं रूपं साधारणं त्रिषु॥
units.translation: The jīva creates these three forms of being happy, unhappy, or indifferent, but the Lord created form (of the gem) remains common in those three.

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 23
units.deva:
भार्या स्नुषा ननान्दा च याता मातेत्यनेकधा।
प्रतियोगि-धिया योषिद् भिद्यते न स्वरूपतः॥
units.translation: As a wife, daughter-in-law, husband’s sister, wife of husband's brother, and mother – the same woman appears differently due to contrasting perspectives (dhīs), though she in reality is not herself different.

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 24
units.deva:
ननु ज्ञानानि भिद्यन्ताम् आकारस् तु न भिद्यते।
योषिद्-वपुष्यतिशयो न दृष्टो जीव-निर्मितः॥
units.translation: Objection (nanu): Let these perspectives (of the other individuals) be different, still the form (of the object of these perspectives) does not differ. In regard to the form of the woman, there doesn’t appear to be much created by the (other) individuals.

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 25
units.deva:
मैवं मांसमयी योषित् काचिद् अन्या मनोमयी।
मांसमय्या अभेदेऽपि भिद्यते हि मनोमयी॥
units.translation: (Reply:) No so. As the woman has a physical body, she also has a mental body. Though her physical body may not change, still (due to others’ perspective of her) her own mental frame of mind (her jīva creation) does change (because of others).

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 26
units.deva:
भ्रान्ति-स्वप्न-मनोराज्य-स्मृतिष्वस्तु मनोमयम्।
जाग्रन्मानेन मेयस्य न मनोमयतेति चेत्॥
units.translation: (Objection:) Whereas, in (mental) delusion, dream, fancy and memory, the object is only mental (mano-maya, and is totally affected, completely changed, by the mental state), but as an (external) waking state (mental) object, it is not just the state of the mind (mano-mayatā, since the unchanged external object is also there to affect the state of the mind).

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 27
units.deva:
बाढं माने तु मेयेन योगात् स्याद् विषयाकृतिः।
भाष्य-वार्तिक-काराभ्याम् अयम् अर्थ उदीरितः॥
units.translation: (Reply:) Sure (bāḍham). Due to coming in contact with the object would there be the image of the object (viṣaya-ākṛti) in the mind. This idea is acknowledged by the two teachers, Śaṅkara and Śuresvara.

gloss.en: by the authors of the Commentary and Gloss

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 28
units.deva:
मूषासिक्तं यथा ताम्रं तन्-निभं जायते तथा।
रूपादीन् व्याप्नुवच् चित्तं तन्निभं दृश्यते ध्रुवम्॥
units.translation: Just as copper (tāmra) poured into a crucible, takes on its form (nibha), so too the mind, having reached the external forms, etc. then certainly appears as having their forms (here, the type of mind, like the type of copper, become more a part of that form by taking on the identity of the crucible-like object).

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 29
units.deva:
व्यञ्जको वा यथालोको व्यंग्यस्याकारताम् इयात्।
सर्वार्थ-व्यञ्जकत्वाद् धीर् अर्थाकारा प्रदृश्यते॥
units.translation: Or, just as (at a distance) a revealing light (āloka, from the sun, or lamp) would take on the form of what it reveals, so too the mind, since it reveals all objects, appears as having the forms of its objects (here, the light being uniform and less identified with its object, manifests more the varied features of the object than of itself).

gloss.en: of what is revealed, its form

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 30
units.deva:
मातुर् मानाभिनिष्पत्तिः निष्पन्नं मेयम् एति तत्।
मेयाभिसङ्गतं तच् च मेयाभत्वं प्रपद्यते॥
units.translation: From the cognizer (mātṛ, the jīva) the cognition (māna, a thought) is produced. Having been produced, it reaches out to its object (meya). Having come together with its object, it assumes the form of the object ( (Yoga Sūtras)).

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 31
units.deva:
सत्येवं विषयौ द्वौ स्तो घटौ मृण्मय-धीमयौ।
मृण्मयो मानमेयः स्यात् साक्षि-भास्यस्तु धीमयः॥
units.translation: In this manner, there are two existent objects (viṣayas), such as a pot (ghaṭa) consisting of this clay (mṛd-maya, the clay in a certain form in this place and time) and the pot consisting of the understanding of it (dhī-maya). The material form (mṛd-maya) itself consists of the (material) form being encompassed by the mind (māna-maya)*. The understanding form (dhī-maya)** is that which is illumined by the witness (the sākṣin, the jīva-ātman, internally ). ** (The buddhi-maya, , is the understanding of that being a ‘pot’ at that place and time, which remains after the initial perception, about which one has purposes, desires, etcetera).

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 32
units.deva:
अन्वय-व्यतिरेकाभ्यां धीमयो जीव-बन्धकृत्।
सत्यस्मिन् सुख-दुःखे स्तस् तस्मिन्न् असति न द्वयम्॥
units.translation: By the logic of co-presence and co-absence (anvaya-vyatireka, ), the understanding form (dhī-maya, how one understands the world and oneself) is what brings about the bondage (the limitation) of the jīva. Only when there is this (dhī-maya, and its understandings) is there these joys and sorrows, and when it is not there then this duality (dvaya, pairs of joys and sorrows, etcetera) is as well not there.

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 33
units.deva:
असत्यपि च बाह्यार्थे स्वप्नादौ बध्यते नरः।
समाधि-सुप्ति-मूर्च्छासु सत्यप्यस्मिन् न बध्यते॥
units.translation: Even in the absence of external objects (bāhya-arthas) during dream, etc. (svapna-ādi, dreams, fancies, etc.), a person feels bound (limited). During samādhi (where one temporarily has no ideation, or if it is there, it is understood as being nothing other than one’s limitless self and thus non-binding), deep sleep or unconsciousness, at those times one is not feeling bound.

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 34
units.deva:
दूर-देशं गते पुत्रे जीवत्येवात्र तत्-पिता।
विप्रलंभक-वाक्येन मृतं मत्वा प्ररोदिति॥
units.translation: Towards a son who had gone to a distant land and remains living there, his father, by a lie from a deceiver, thinks him dead and wails.

gloss.en: by the words of a deceiver

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 35
units.deva:
मृतेऽपि तस्मिन् वार्तायम् अश्रुतायां न रोदिति।
अतः सर्वस्य जीवस्य बन्धकृन् मानसं जगत्॥
units.translation: Even if while living there (the son) had died, (his father) having not yet heard this news would not be wailing. Therefore, the cause of bondage for every jīva is only the mental world (the personal world of one’s understanding).* *(“Mana eva manuṣyāṇāṃ kāraṇaṃ bandha-mokṣayoḥ, Mind alone is man’s cause for bondage and freedom” AmBU.2 (Amṛta-bindu Upaniṣad). “Cittam eva hi saṃsāraḥ tad praytnena śodhayet, yad-cittaḥ tad-mayaḥ bhavati guhyam etad sanātanam, The mind alone is one’s transient existence. One should make effort to clean it up. In whatever way one thinks, that one becomes. This is an eternal mystery” MaitU.1.9 (Maitrāyaṇi Upaniṣad).)

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 36
units.deva:
विज्ञान-वादो बाह्यार्थ-वैयर्थ्यात् स्याद् इहेति चेत्।
न हृद्याकारम् आधातुं बाह्यस्यापेक्षितत्वतः॥
units.translation: (Objection:) Doesn’t this amount to an idealist philosophy (vijñāna-vāda), since it deprives external objects of any utility? (Reply:) No, because we accept that the form in the mind (hṛd, the buddhi) is dependent upon an external world.

gloss.en: because of the uselessness of external objects

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 37
units.deva:
वैयर्थ्यम् अस्तु वा बाह्यं न वारयितुम् ईश्महे।
प्रयोजनम् अपेक्षन्ते न मानानीति हि स्थितिः॥
units.translation: Or, on the other hand, one can accept that the external world has no utility (at least in terms of one being completely free from bondage), still we are not able to do away with it (as we at least need a teaching and a teacher to gain freedom). Any means of knowledge (mānas, pramāṇa, of the external world) is not concerned with its usage (prayojana, the desired purpose, etc. of the object), but only with revealing what is there (sthīti).* *(Or, This means of knowledge, our teachings here, are not concerned with how to make use of the world, the topic of the prior portion of the Vedas, but rather its reality, the topic of the Vedāntas, the Upaniṣads).

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 38
units.deva:
बन्धश् चेन् मानस-द्वैतं तन्-निरोधेन शाम्यति।
अभ्यसेद् योगम् एवातो ब्रह्म-ज्ञानेन किं वद॥
units.translation: (Objection:) If bondage is the mental world (mānasa-dvaita), then peace is by withdrawing (nirodha) it (the mind from the world, (Yoga Sūtras)). Therefore, only yoga should be practiced. What use is there to talk about knowledge of brahman?

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 39
units.deva:
तात्कालिक-द्वैत-शान्ताव् अप्यागामि-जनि-क्षयः।
ब्रह्म-ज्ञानं विना न स्याद् इति वेदान्त-डिण्डिमः॥
units.translation: (Reply:) In simply stilling the appearance of the world for a time, there is (temporarily) the stopping of creating new karma (āgāmin). But (eliminating all karma: sañcita accumulated, prārabdha fructifying, and āgāmin new) cannot be without brahma-jñāna (knowing oneself as the limitless reality that is naturally free of all karma, and thus free from birth and death). This is the ‘drumbeat’ (teaching) of Vedānta.

gloss.en: in the temporary calming of duality

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 40
units.deva:
अनिवृत्तेऽपीश-सृष्टे द्वैते तस्य मृषात्मताम्।
बुद्ध्वा ब्रह्माद्वयं बोद्धुं शक्यं वस्त्वैक्य-वादिनः॥
units.translation: Even while the duality world manifested by the Lord (Īśa-śṛṣṭa) is not averted, still by knowing the unreal nature of that world, the non-dualist (vastu-aikya-vādin) is able to know the non-dual brahman (reality).

gloss.en: even when the Lord's creation is not ceased
by the one who teaches the unity of reality

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 41
units.deva:
प्रलये तन्-निवृत्तौ तु गुरु-शास्त्राद्यभावतः।
विरोधि-द्वैताभावेऽपि न श्क्यं बोद्धुम् अद्वयम्॥
units.translation: Even when that (universe) disappears at the dissolution (pralāya) and there is the absence of an opposing duality, still one cannot know non-duality, since there is no teacher or scripture (guru-śāstra, the means of knowledge and a guide), etc. (namely, one’s mind, to learn, is not there).

gloss.en: because of the absence of teacher-scripture and so on
even when opposing duality is absent

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 42
units.deva:
अबाधकं साधकं च द्वैतम् ईश्वर-निर्मितम्।
अपनेतुम् अशक्यं चेत्यास्तां तद् द्विष्यते कुतः॥
units.translation: The duality manifested by the Lord (Īśvara-nirmita) is a help (sādhaka, a means in the form of a guru, etc.) instead of a hindrance (a-bādhaka, an obstacle). Moreover, no one (even if a great Yogī) is able to banish it. May it indeed remain. What reason is there to hate it (or even be sad, see commentary on ) (Yoga Sūtras)?

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 43
units.deva:
जीव-द्वैतं तु शास्त्रीयम् अशास्त्रीयम् इति द्विधा।
उपाददीत शास्त्रियम् आ तत्त्वस्यावबोधनात्॥
units.translation: However, the duality created by the jīva (the individual) is of two kinds: in keeping with śāstra (the scriptural means of knowledge for ultimate reality), or not. One should take up the śāstrīya (the scriptural perspective of one’s dvaita) until the ultimate reality (tattva, taught in the scripture) is known (as oneself).

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 44
units.deva:
आत्म-ब्रह्म-विचाराख्यं शास्त्रीयं मानसं जगत्।
बुद्धे तत्त्वे तच् च हेयम् इति श्रुत्यनुशासनम्॥
units.translation: The mental world according to scripture (śāstrīyaṃ mānasaṃ jagat) is known as inquiry into both oneself and brahman. Finally, the scripture teaches that even this (the śāstrīyaṃ mānasaṃ jagat) is given up when the truth is known.

gloss.en: called inquiry into Self and Brahman

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 45
units.deva:
शास्त्राण्यधीत्य मेधावी अभ्यस्य च पुनः पुनः।
परमं ब्रह्म विज्ञाय उल्कावत् तान्यधोत्सृजेत्॥
units.translation: “Having studied the scriptures, the informed person (medhāvin) should repeat (i.e., analyze and contemplate) it again and again, and, having assimilated the knowledge of the ultimate brahman (as ātman, oneself), then (adha) one would (naturally) give up (the notion that there is more to study or gain), like one gives up a torch (having reached one’s destination)” (AmNU.01 (Amṛta-nāda Upaniṣad)).

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 46
units.deva:
ग्रन्थम् अभ्यस्य मेधावी ज्ञान-विज्ञान-तत्परः।
पलालम् इव धान्यार्थी त्यजेद् ग्रन्थम् अशेषतः॥
units.translation: “Having studied the books (grantha), the informed person (medhāvin), having the assimilation of this knowledge (jñāna-vijñāna) as the ultimate (tat-para), would give up the (need for the) books completely, like one gives up the straw after extracting their grains” (AmBU.18 (Amṛta-bindu Upaniṣad)).

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 47
units.deva:
तम् एव धीरो विज्ञाय प्रज्ञां कुर्वीत ब्राह्मणः।
नानुध्यायेद् बहूञ् शब्दान् वाचो विग्लापनं हि तत्॥
units.translation: “The wise (dhīra) and learned person (brāhmaṇa), having assimilated the knowledge of that very one and gained this knowledge (prajñā), would not dwell on even more (and other) texts, since that would simply be an (unnecessary) waste of words (vāc)” ( (Bṛhad-Āraṇyaka Upaniṣad)).

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 48
units.deva:
तम् एवैकं विजानीथ ह्यन्या वाचो विमुञ्चथ।
यच् चेद् वाङ् मनसी प्राज्ञ इत्याद्याः श्रुतयः स्फुटाः॥
units.translation: “May you know that non-dual (eka, to be oneself). Any words (or ideas) that differ, give them up,” (Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad). “The discerning person (prājña) should (resolve, reposition one’s identity from) speech (and the other organs) into the mind (manas)…,” (etcetera: the mind into the intellect, the intellect into that Lord, and that into the one’s peaceful self, (Kaṭha Upaniṣad)). Thus there are many such open statements in the scriptures.

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 49
units.deva:
अशास्त्रीयम् अपि द्वैतं तीव्रं मन्दम् इति द्विथा।
काम-क्रोधादिकं तीव्रं मनो-राज्यं तथेतरत्॥
units.translation: Moreover, the duality (created by the jīva) that is not in keeping with śāstra (the scriptural means of knowledge for ultimate reality) is of two kinds: tīvra (intense, i.e., having excessive rajas guṇa) or manda (lazy or dull, i.e., having excessive tamas guṇa). The intense has the nature of craving for, anger against, etc.; and the other (the lazy or dull) is a world of fantasy (mano-rājya).

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 50
units.deva:
उभयं तत्त्व-बोधात् प्राक् निवार्यं बोध-सिद्धये।
शमः समाहितत्वं च साधनेषु श्रुतं यतः॥
units.translation: One needs to give up both these (tīvra and manda strivings, as one’s tat-para, the most important in one’s life) at the start of this study of ultimate reality (which will show one why and how to get away from these two) in order to complete this knowledge (bodha-siddhi). Therefore, śama (composure) and samāhitatva (attentiveness, respectively) are indicated in the scripture among the sādhanas (the preparations for gaining this knowledge).

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 51
units.deva:
बोधाद् ऊर्ध्वं च तद्धेयं जीवन्-मुक्ति-प्रसिद्धये।
कामादि-क्लेश-बन्धेन युक्तस्य न हि मुक्तता॥
units.translation: And after attaining knowledge, in order to remain accomplished while living free (jīvan-mukti), that (tad a-śāstrīya, lifestyle contrary to the teaching) ought to be avoided (heya). For the one habituated by the hindering (kleśa) bonds of desire, etc. ( (Yoga Sūtras)), the freedom (through knowledge) is not appreciated (i.e., life remains as troublesome as before, at least for others around, even though one has the liberating knowledge, such as for sage Dur-vāsas).

gloss.en: by the bonds of afflictions beginning with desire

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 52
units.deva:
जीवन्-मुक्तिर् इयं मा भूज् जन्माभावे त्वहं कृती।
तर्हि जन्मापि तेऽस्त्वेव स्वर्ग-मात्रात् कृती भवान्॥
units.translation: (If one says) ‘Let there be no living free (after knowledge). I would be satisfied (kṛtin) in just not having another rebirth.’ In that case, still you will have a rebirth. (Because from the knowledge you have gained) you sir would be satisfied only by a stay in heaven (i.e., if your knowledge has not penetrated your unconscious, then that unconscious, the vāsanās, will bring you rebirth).

gloss.en: for you, let it indeed be

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 53
units.deva:
क्षयातिशय-दोषेण स्वर्गो हेयो यदा तदा।
स्वयं दोषतम् आत्मायं कामादिः किं न हीयते॥
units.translation: (And if heaven is thought to be okay:) Since heaven ought to be given up as being defective with gradations (kṣaya-atiśaya, downs and ups, of pleasures), then, (heaven) itself being defective, why not give up all that which has this kind of nature built from desires, onwards?

gloss.en: because of the flaw of loss and increase

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 54
units.deva:
तत्त्वं बुद्ध्वापि कामादीन् निःशेषं न जहासि चेत्।
यथेष्टाचरणं ते स्यात् कर्म-शास्त्रातिलङ्घिनः॥
units.translation: Even though knowing the reality, if you cannot completely give up (hindering) desires, etc., then your behavior will be ruled by your whims, and will transgress the (common) rule of laws (which will offend others and bring trouble to yourself).

gloss.en: one who transgresses the rule of action

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 55
units.deva:
बुद्धाद्वैत-स्वतत्त्वस्य यथेष्टाचरणं यदि।
शुनां तत्त्व-दृशां चैव को भेदोऽशुचि-भक्षणे॥
units.translation: For one who effortlessly (sva-tattva, nija-svarūpam, without much sādhana) has come to know the non-dual, and then lives (as before) according to one’s whim, then what is the difference between a dog and this seer of the truth in that they both only enjoy an unclean life (a-śuci-bhakṣaṇa)?

gloss.en: of one who knows the nondual Self as truth

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 56
units.deva:
बोधात् पुरा मनो-दोषमात्रात् क्लिश्यस्य् अथाधुना।
अशेष-लोक-निन्दा चेत्यहो ते बोध-वैभवम्॥
units.translation: Before this (spiritual) knowledge, simply from the defects of the mind you continue to live a troubled life (kliśyasi), but now (having gained knowledge) you also suffer censure of the entire world (i.e., now you also become a hypocrite in everyone’s eyes). Alas, what a greatness from knowledge you have gained!

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 57
units.deva:
विड्-वराहादि-तुल्यत्वं मा कांक्षीस् तत्त्व-विद् भवान्।
सर्व-धी-दोष-संत्यागाल् लोकैः पूज्यश् च देववत्॥
units.translation: You sir, a knower of truth, should not seek the level of a pig in its own excrement, etc. By completely freeing yourself from all the defects of the mind, the people will honor (you) like a deity (which would be an encouragement to others and a non-hindrance to you, a win-win).

gloss.en: equality with pigs and so on
from abandoning all defects of mind

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 58
units.deva:
काम्यादि-दोष-दृष्ट्याद्याः कामादि-त्याग-हेतवः।
प्रसिद्धा मोक्ष-शास्त्रेषु तान् अन्विष्य सुखी भव॥
units.translation: Well-known in the teachings meant for freedom (mokṣa-śāstras) are the means for freeing oneself from desires, etc. by the practices of seeing the defects of following desires, etc. ( (Yoga Sūtras)). Adhering to these (teachings), may you have a pleasant life (with this knowledge, while jīvan-mukta).

gloss.en: seeing flaws in desired actions and so on
causes for abandoning desire and so on

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 59
units.deva:
त्यज्यताम् एष कामादिर् मनो-राज्ये तु का क्षतिः।
अशेष-दोष-बीजत्वात् क्षतिर् भगवतेरिता॥
units.translation: (Objection:) Let the (acting upon) desires, etc. be given up, but, what’s the harm in just fantasizing (mano-rājya, upon them)? (Reply:) The harm is because it (fantasizing) is the seed for the rest of the defects. This was indicated by Lord (Kṛṣṇa).

gloss.en: because it is the seed of all defects

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 60
units.deva:
ध्यायतो विषयान् पुंसः संगस् तेषूपजायते।
संगात् संजायते कामः कामात् क्रोधोऽभिजायते॥
units.translation: “For a person who mentally dwells on objects, attachment (saṅga) to them arises; from attachment (allowed to flame up) arises binding desire (kāma, requirements in order to be happy and anticipations of their fruition); from (thwarted) anticipations arises anger (krodha)” (Bhagavad Gītā)).

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 61
units.deva:
शक्यं जेतुं मनो-राज्यं निर्विकल्प-समाधितः।
सुसंपादः क्रमात् सोऽपि स-विकल्प-समाधिना॥
units.translation: This mano-rājya (fanciful thinking, where the manas, not the intellect, is given the keys to one’s kingdom, so to speak) can be overcome by contemplation (samādhi, with this teaching) on the attributeless reality (nirvikalpa, the nirguṇa brahman). Further, that can be eased into (susaṃpāda-kramāt) by contemplation on the attributed reality (vikalpa, the sa-guṇa brahman, Īśvara, the Lord, even though the attributes are unreal, , & , and (Yoga Sūtras)).

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 62
units.deva:
बुद्ध-तत्त्वेन धी-दोष-शून्येनैकान्त-वासिना।
दीर्घं प्रणवम् उच्चार्य मनो-राज्यं विजीयते॥
units.translation: With the reality being known (enough to contemplate it), freed from the defects in thinking (that the unreal is real), and abiding long enough alone (without interruption), while contemplating praṇava (Om, (Yoga Sūtras)) one overcomes mano-rājya, being ruled by the mind).

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 63
units.deva:
जिते तस्मिन् वृत्ति-शून्यं मनस् तिष्ठति मूकवत्।
एतत् पदं वसिष्ठेन रामाय बहुधेरितम्॥
