units.translation: When that (mano-rājya) is overcome (and its chattering has calmed down), thinking may cease (for a time) and the mind remains like a mute. This state was variously described by Vasiṣṭha to Rāma (in the Yoga-Vasiṣṭha).

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 64
units.deva:
दृश्यं नास्तीति बोधेन मनसो दृश्य-मार्जनम्।
संपन्नं चेत् तद् उत्पन्ना परा निर्वाण-निर्वृतिः॥
units.translation: With the knowledge that the phenomenal (dṛśya universe) is unreal (na asti, is only its appearance and nothing more, ), clearing the appearances of the mind (as defining, limiting, oneself), if that (clarity) remains, then there is a profound (para) tranquility (from problems) called nirvāṇa (freedom, mokṣa).

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 65
units.deva:
विचारितम् अलं शास्त्रं चिरम् उद्ग्राहितं मिथः।
संत्यक्त-वासनान् मौनाद् ऋते नास्त्युत्तमं पदम्॥
units.translation: Having thoroughly studied scripture for a sufficient time together (mithas, with a teacher) to make it understood, still without mauna (quietude, the practice of the ascetics, munis) by having completely freed oneself from (without identity with) the vāsanas (the unconscious binding fetters) the ultimate goal (as oneself unlimited by the conscious and unconscious mind’s fetters) is not in hand.

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 66
units.deva:
विक्षिप्यते कदाचिद् धीः कर्मणा भोग-दायिना।
पुनः समाहिता सा स्यात् तथैवाभ्यास-पाटवात्॥
units.translation: The mind (dhī, intellect) sometimes is thrown off (from its śāstriya perspective) due to karma bestowed from (past) experience (waiting as a vāsana to arise). (In that case) by the skillful practice (of attentive contemplation) again one should samāhita (gather back, the contemplative intellect, from the tamas of fancies back to satva, ).

gloss.en: in that same way, by skill in practice

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 67
units.deva:
विक्षेपो यस्य नास्त्यस्य ब्रह्मवित्त्वं न मन्यते।
ब्रह्मैवायम् इति प्राहुर् मुनयः पार-दर्शिनः॥
units.translation: The one whose (intellect) is not thrown off track (from knowing oneself as limitless) is considered not just a knower of brahman, but is brahman itself, thus say the far-seeing munis (ascetics, manana-śīlas, those who have mastered their mind).

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 68
units.deva:
दर्शनादर्शने हित्वा स्वयं केल्वल-रूपतः।
यस् तिष्ठति स तु ब्रह्मन् ब्रह्म न ब्रह्मवित् स्वयम्॥
units.translation: Freed from sometimes seeing and sometimes not seeing (the truth), who remains oneself alone as one’s unitary nature, O Brahman, that one is self-evident (svayam) brahman, not merely a knower OF brahman.

units.label: Chapter 4 · Verse 69
units.deva:
जीवन्-मुक्तेः परा-काष्ठा जीव-द्वैत-विवर्जनात्।
लभ्यतेऽसावतोऽत्रेदम् ईश-द्वैताद् विवेचितम्॥
units.translation: The far measure (parā-kāṣṭhā) of living liberated (jīvan-mukti) starts from getting free from jīva-dvaita (the limited, binding world perspective of the individual, & ). When that is attained, then this becomes the discernment of the Lord’s world (Īśvara-dvaita, the common factual world only as it appears, and living in this world as brahman alone).

units.label: Chapter 5 · Verse 1
units.deva:
येनेक्षते शृणोतीदं जिघ्रति व्याकरोति च।
स्वाद्वस्वादू विजानाति तत् प्रज्ञानम् उदीरितम्॥
units.translation: (The first mahā-vākya:) That by which one sees all this, hears, smells, speaks, and distinguishes sweet and non-sweet is called ‘prajñānam (consciousness)’, (in “prajñānaṃ brahma,” ‘Consciousness is brahman’, (Aitareya Upaniṣad)).

units.label: Chapter 5 · Verse 2
units.deva:
चतुर्-मुखेन्द्र-देवेषु मनुष्याश्व-गवादिषु।
चैतन्यम् एकं ब्रह्मातः प्रज्ञानं ब्रह्म मय्यपि॥
units.translation: The one consciousness in Lord Brahma (the Lord with four faces), Indra, and all deities, as well as in humans, horses, cows, etcetera – is brahman (reality). Therefore, prajñāna brahman is in me also.

gloss.en: among four-faced Brahmā, Indra, and the gods
among people, horses, cows, and so on

units.label: Chapter 5 · Verse 3
units.deva:
परिपूर्णः परात्माऽस्मिन् देहे विद्याधिकारिणि।
बुद्धेः साक्षितया स्थित्वा स्फुरन्न् अहम् इतीर्यते॥
units.translation: In this body fit (adhikārin) for that knowledge is the full (paripūrṇa), ultimate ātman (self). Existing as the witness of the intellect, it reveals (itself), proclaimed as ‘I’.

units.label: Chapter 5 · Verse 4
units.deva:
स्वतः पूर्णः परात्माऽत्र ब्रह्म-शब्देन वर्णितः।
अस्मीत्यैक्य-परामर्शस् तेन ब्रह्म भवाम्यहम्॥
units.translation: (The second mahā-vākya:) The natural fullness (pūrṇa) that is the ultimate self is encompassed here by the word ‘brahman’. The word ‘asmi (I am)’ (in “ahaṃ brahma asmi,” ‘I am brahman’, (Bṛhad-Āraṇyaka Upaniṣad)) indicates the identity with that brahman which I am.

units.label: Chapter 5 · Verse 5
units.deva:
एकम् एवाद्वितीयं सन् नाम-रूप-विवर्जितम्।
सृष्टेः पुराऽधुनाप्यस्य तादृक्त्वं तद् इतीर्यते॥
units.translation: (The third mahā-vākya:) Existing alone, one non-dual, devoid of name or form (nāma-rūpa) before the manifestation, and now still existing as that very same. This is indicated by the word ‘tad (that)’ (in “tat tvam asi,” ‘That (brahman) you are’, (Chāndogya Upaniṣad)).

units.label: Chapter 5 · Verse 6
units.deva:
श्रोतुर् देहेन्द्रियातीतं वस्त्वत्र त्वं-पदेरितम्।
एकता ग्राह्यतेऽसीति तद् ऐक्यम् अनुभूयताम्॥
units.translation: Transcending the body and senses of the one listening (to this teaching) is the vastu (entity) here indicated by the word ‘tvam (you)’. The word ‘asi (are)’ indicates the identity. That identity is to be intimately assimilated (anubhūyatām).

units.label: Chapter 5 · Verse 7
units.deva:
स्वप्रकाशापरोक्षत्वम् अयम् इत्युक्तितो मतम्।
अहं-कारादि-देहान्तात् प्रत्यग् आत्मेति गीयते॥
units.translation: (The fourth mahā-vākya:) Its self-revealing, non-remoteness is understood by the word, ‘ayam (this, (Sanskrit Grammar))’. The word ‘ātman (self)’ announces the one interior to this, beginning with the notion of ‘I’ and ending with this body (in “ayam ātmā brahma,” ‘This self is brahman’, (Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad)).

units.label: Chapter 5 · Verse 8
units.deva:
दृश्यमानस्य सर्वस्य जगतस् तत्त्वम् ईर्यते।
ब्रह्म-शब्देन तद् ब्रह्म स्वप्रकाशात्म-रूपकम्॥
units.translation: The very nature (tattva) of the entire apparent universe is indicated by the word, ‘brahman (limitless reality)’. That brahman has the nature of the self-revealing ātman (oneself).

gloss.en: whose form is the self-luminous Self

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 1
units.deva:
यथा चित्र-पटे दृष्टम् अवस्थानां चतुष्टयम्।
परमात्मनि विज्ञेयं तथाऽवस्था-चतुष्टयम्॥
units.translation: Like on a picture canvas are seen four stages of manifestation (avasthā), similarly upon the ultimate reality (parama-ātman) are known to be four stages of manifestation (of the world).
units.iast:
yathā citra-paṭe dṛṣṭam avasthānāṃ catuṣṭayam|
paramātmani vijñeyaṃ tathā’vasthā-catuṣṭayam||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 2
units.deva:
यथा धौतो घट्टितश् च लाञ्छितो रञ्जितः पटः।
चिद् अन्तर्-यामी सूत्रात्मा विराड्-आत्मा तथेर्यते॥
units.translation: Like a canvas (paṭa) is at first clean (dhauta), then prepared (stiffened with starch), then outlined, and finally colored in, similarly there is consciousness (cit, which is one only without a second), then (upon this is imposed) a Lord (antar-yāmin, the inner controller, which provides order everywhere), a subtle nature (sūtra-ātman, Hiraṇya-garbha, subtility manifestable to a mind), and finally a gross nature (Virāṭ-ātman, physicality manifestable to the subtle senses).
units.iast:
yathā dhauto ghaṭṭitaś ca lāñchito rañjitaḥ paṭaḥ|
cid antar-yāmī sūtrātmā virāḍ-ātmā tatheryate||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 3
units.deva:
स्वतः शुभ्रोऽत्र धौतः स्याद् घट्टितोऽन्न-विलेपनात्।
मष्याकारैर् लाञ्छितः स्याद् रञ्जितो वर्ण-पूरणात्॥
units.translation: Here the ‘cleaned’ (dhauta) would be a naturally clear (canvas), the ‘prepared’ would be from covering with food-starch, the ‘outlined’ would be by the penciled forms, and the ‘colored’ would be by filling in with colors.
units.iast:
svataḥ śubhro’tra dhautaḥ syād ghaṭṭito’nna-vilepanāt|
maṣyākārair lāñchitaḥ syād rañjito varṇa-pūraṇāt||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 4
units.deva:
स्वतश् चिद् अन्तर्-यामी तु मायावी सूक्ष्म-सृष्टितः।
सूत्रात्मा स्थूल-सृष्ट्यैव विराड् इत्युच्यते परः॥
units.translation: Consciousness (cit) is naturally (pure, without a second), whereas, when with māyā (the power of hiding the one and projecting the many) it is the Lord (antar-yāmin, the inner controller), which when manifested subtly it is called the subtle nature (sūtra-ātman), and when further manifested grossly (to the senses) it is called Virāṭ (the Lord manifested physically). This is the totality (para, which is brahman).
units.iast:
svataś cid antar-yāmī tu māyāvī sūkṣma-sṛṣṭitaḥ|
sūtrātmā sthūla-sṛṣṭyaiva virāḍ ityucyate paraḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 5
units.deva:
ब्रह्माद्याः स्तम्ब-पर्यन्ताः प्राणिनोऽत्र जडा अपि।
उत्तमाधम-भावेन वर्तन्ते पट-चित्रवत्॥
units.translation: On this (para brahman) are all the living beings (prāṇins) starting with Lord Brahmā to a tuft of grass, as well as all the inanimate objects (jaḍas). They appear as being superior and inferior (to each other), like the painted images (citra) on a canvas.
units.iast:
brahmādyāḥ stamba-paryantāḥ prāṇino’tra jaḍā api|
uttamādhama-bhāvena vartante paṭa-citravat||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 6
units.deva:
चित्रार्पित-मनुष्याणां वस्त्राभासाः पृथक् पृथक्।
चित्राधारेण वस्त्रेण सदृशा इव कल्पिताः॥
units.translation: People are imposed (arpita, by us) upon the painted images and they separately appear (ābhāsa) to have clothing. With their clothing these (prātibhāsika* appearances on the canvas imposed by our mind) are imagined as seemingly not different from (the vyāvahārika factual reality of) the painted canvas. *(The terms ‘imposed’, ‘imagined’, etc., indicate we are talking about levels of reality, which has two levels: unreal and real. In regard to our everyday life, here as the painting example, these appear as imaginary, prātibhāsika, and as factual, vyāvahārika. In regard to the goal of this teaching, here as they apply to the individual and to the one reality, these are the imaginary plus the factual as the unreal and the consciousness as the real, pāramārthika, see (Yoga Sūtras))

gloss.en: of people placed in a picture

units.iast:
citrārpita-manuṣyāṇāṃ vastrābhāsāḥ pṛthak pṛthak|
citrādhāreṇa vastreṇa sadṛśā iva kalpitāḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 7
units.deva:
पृथक् पृथक् चिद्-आभासाश् चैतन्याध्यस्त-देहिनाम्।
कल्प्यन्ते जीव-नामानो बहुधा संसरन्त्यमी॥
units.translation: (Similarly) the (vyāvahārika, visual) appearances in (pāramārthika, real) consciousness of separate embodied people as if having their own separate consciousness (caitanya) are imagined by us as entities called jīvas (individual living being). They are imagined as being many and undergo coming and going (saṃsāra, transmigration through a succession of moments of time and births).

gloss.en: of embodied beings superimposed on consciousness

units.iast:
pṛthak pṛthak cid-ābhāsāś caitanyādhyasta-dehinām|
kalpyante jīva-nāmāno bahudhā saṃsarantyamī||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 8
units.deva:
वस्त्राभास-स्थितान् वर्णान् यद्वद् आधार-वस्त्र-गान्।
वदन्त्यज्ञास् तथा जीव-संसारं चिद्-गतं विदुः॥
units.translation: The unknowing talk like the (vyāvahārika) paints exist as the (prātibhāsika) appearances of clothes, etcetera, as if they have become (vyāvahārika) clothes stuck on the (vyāvahārika) surface (canvas). In that way, they think the (vyāvahārika) transmigration of the jīvas is there for the (pāramārthika) consciousness also.
units.iast:
vastrābhāsa-sthitān varṇān yadvad ādhāra-vastra-gān|
vadantyajñās tathā jīva-saṃsāraṃ cid-gataṃ viduḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 9
units.deva:
चित्र-स्थ-पर्वतादीनां वस्त्राभासो न लिख्यते।
सृष्टि-स्थ-मृत्तिकादीनां चिदाभासस् तथा न हि॥
units.translation: The mountains, etcetera, represented in the painting are not drawn as having the appearance of clothing. Thus here, the earth, etcetera, present in creation indeed do not appear to us as having consciousness.

gloss.en: of mountains and so on in a picture
of earth and so on in creation

units.iast:
citra-stha-parvatādīnāṃ vastrābhāso na likhyate|
sṛṣṭi-stha-mṛttikādīnāṃ cidābhāsas tathā na hi||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 10
units.deva:
संसारः परमार्थोऽयं संलग्नः स्वात्म-वस्तुनि।
इति भ्रान्तिर् अविद्या स्याद् विद्ययैषा निवर्तते॥
units.translation: The delusion (bhrānti) that this transient life (saṃsāra) as absolutely real (paramārtha) is what I am stuck with (saṃlagna) in my reality (sva-ātma-vastu) would be the a-vidyā (ignorance), which this vidyā (in the form of the teaching here) removes.

gloss.en: in the reality of one's Self

units.iast:
saṃsāraḥ paramārtho’yaṃ saṃlagnaḥ svātma-vastuni|
iti bhrāntir avidyā syād vidyayaiṣā nivartate||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 11
units.deva:
आत्माभासस्य जीवस्य संसारो नात्म-वस्तुनः।
इति बोधो भवेद् विद्या लभ्यतेऽसौ विचारणात्॥
units.translation: Saṃsāra belongs to the jīva which is only a semblance of the self (ātma-ābhāsa, the appearance of consciousness limited to the mind within this body), not to the (unlimited) reality of the self (ātma-vastu) – this understanding would here be the vidyā. This is attained through discerning inquiry (vicāraṇa).

gloss.en: of the appearance of the Self

units.iast:
ātmābhāsasya jīvasya saṃsāro nātma-vastunaḥ|
iti bodho bhaved vidyā labhyate’sau vicāraṇāt||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 12
units.deva:
सदा विचारयेत् तस्माज् जगज्-जीव-परात्मनः।
जीव-भाव-जगद्-भाव-बाधे स्वात्मैव शिष्यते॥
units.translation: Therefore, one should continually inquire into the absolute nature (para-ātman) of the universe and the individual. When the (limited) nature of the individual and of the universe is negated (bādha, ), one’s self alone remains.

gloss.en: of the universe, individual, and supreme Self
when the individual-state and world-state are negated

units.iast:
sadā vicārayet tasmāj jagaj-jīva-parātmanaḥ|
jīva-bhāva-jagad-bhāva-bādhe svātmaiva śiṣyate||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 13
units.deva:
नाप्रतीतिस् तयोर् बाधः किन्तु मिथ्यात्व-निश्चयः।
नो चेत् सुषुप्ति-मूर्च्छादौ मुच्येतायत्नतो जनः॥
units.translation: The negation is not their disappearance (a-pratīti, to the senses), but rather the clear understanding of their mithyātva (unreality, not being absolutely as real as oneself). If otherwise (their simply disappearing), then a person would effortlessly gain freedom after they go to deep sleep or go unconscious.
units.iast:
nāpratītis tayor bādhaḥ kintu mithyātva-niścayaḥ|
no cet suṣupti-mūrcchādau mucyetāyatnato janaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 14
units.deva:
परमात्मावशेषोऽपि तत्-सत्यत्व-विनिश्चयः।
न जगद् विस्मृतिर् नो चेज् जीवन्-मुक्तिर् न संभवेत्॥
units.translation: Moreover (besides the unreality of the individual and the universe), that one’s absolute nature alone remains () indicates the discernment of the real nature of this (ātman), not simply disregarding (vismṛti) the universe. Otherwise, jīvan-mukti (living while liberated) would not be possible.

gloss.en: even though only the supreme Self remains

units.iast:
paramātmāvaśeṣo’pi tat-satyatva-viniścayaḥ|
na jagad vismṛtir no cej jīvan-muktir na saṃbhavet||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 15
units.deva:
परोक्षा चापरोक्षेति विद्या द्वेधा विचार-जा।
तत्रापरोक्ष-विद्याप्तौ विचारोऽयं समाप्यते॥
units.translation: The knowledge (vidyā) arising from inquiry is of two kinds: indirect (parokṣa) and direct (a-parokṣa, ‘not indirect’). Between these two, when knowledge is direct, then the inquiry has completed.
units.iast:
parokṣā cāparokṣeti vidyā dvedhā vicāra-jā|
tatrāparokṣa-vidyāptau vicāro’yaṃ samāpyate||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 16
units.deva:
अस्ति ब्रह्मेति चेद् वेद परोक्ष-ज्ञानम् एव तत्।
अहं ब्रह्मेति चेद् वेद साक्षात्-कारः स उच्यते॥
units.translation: If one knows ‘brahman exists’, that is only an indirect knowledge (an acknowledgment that there is something limitless that is called ‘brahman’). If one knows ‘I am brahman (the limitless reality)’, that is direct appreciation (sākṣāt-kāra).
units.iast:
asti brahmeti ced veda parokṣa-jñānam eva tat|
ahaṃ brahmeti ced veda sākṣāt-kāraḥ sa ucyate||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 17
units.deva:
तत्-साक्षात्-कार-सिद्ध्यर्थम् आत्म-तत्त्वं विविच्यते।
येनायं सर्व-संसारात् सद्य एव विमुच्यते॥
units.translation: In order to establish the direct appreciation of the nature of oneself, it is here discerned as that by which one is immediately (sadya) freed from all of saṃsāra (notions of bondage, i.e., it is okay that there is a limitless brahman, but how does that help me, unless I am that same limitless).
units.iast:
tat-sākṣāt-kāra-siddhyartham ātma-tattvaṃ vivicyate|
yenāyaṃ sarva-saṃsārāt sadya eva vimucyate||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 18
units.deva:
कूटस्थो ब्रह्म जीवेशाव् इत्येवं चित् चतुर्-विधा।
घटाकाश-महाकाशौ जलाकाशाभ्र-खे यथा॥
units.translation: The consciousness (cit) can be indicated in four ways: the kūṭa-stha (what remains unchanging in the changing, (Bhagavad Gītā)) and brahman (the limitless reality), or the jīva (the nature of myself) and Īśvara (the nature of the Lord). In the same way respectively, (space) can be indicated as pot-space or limitless-space (as an example of kūṭa-stha and brahman), or as the sky (reflecting) in a (pot of) water or sky (reflecting) in (the moisture of) a cloud (as an example of jīva and Īśvara).
units.iast:
kūṭastho brahma jīveśāv ityevaṃ cit catur-vidhā|
ghaṭākāśa-mahākāśau jalākāśābhra-khe yathā||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 19
units.deva:
घटावच्छिन्न-खे नीरं यत् तत्र प्रतिबिम्बितः।
साभ्र-नक्षत्र आकाशो जलाकाश उदीरितः॥
units.translation: The sky in a pot (jala-ākāśa) is explained as what is reflected (pratibimbita) in the water inside the space limited (avacchinna) in a pot, which is the sky along with the clouds (in the day) and stars (in the night).
units.iast:
ghaṭāvacchinna-khe nīraṃ yat tatra pratibimbitaḥ|
sābhra-nakṣatra ākāśo jalākāśa udīritaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 20
units.deva:
महाकाशस्य मध्ये यन् मेघ-मण्डलम् ईक्ष्यते।
प्रतिबिंबतया तत्र मेघाकाशो जले स्थितः॥
units.translation: The sky in a cloud (megha-ākāśa) is explained as what is reflected in the water that is a body of water (megha-maṇḍala) in the vast space.
units.iast:
mahākāśasya madhye yan megha-maṇḍalam īkṣyate|
pratibiṃbatayā tatra meghākāśo jale sthitaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 21
units.deva:
मेघांश-रूपम् उदकं तुषाराकार-संस्थितम्।
तत्र ख-प्रतिबिंबोऽयं नीरत्वाद् अनुमीयते॥
units.translation: The water in the form of the cloud particles are present in the form of mist (tuṣāra), in that, due its nature of being water (that can reflect), one could infer that there would be the reflection (pratibimba) of the vast sky (in all directions).

gloss.en: situated in the form of mist

units.iast:
meghāṃśa-rūpam udakaṃ tuṣārākāra-saṃsthitam|
tatra kha-pratibiṃbo’yaṃ nīratvād anumīyate||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 22
units.deva:
अधिष्ठानतया देह-द्वयावच्छिन्न-चेतनः।
कूटवन् निर्विकारेण स्थितः कूटस्थ उच्यते॥
units.translation: The kūṭa-stha is said to be what remains unchanging like a mountain peak (kūṭavat, or a hardened iron hammer or anvil). It is the consciousness (cetana) limited (avacchinna) in both the (physical and subtle) bodies, as their (unchanging) substantive reality (adhiṣṭānatā).

gloss.en: consciousness limited by the two bodies

units.iast:
adhiṣṭhānatayā deha-dvayāvacchinna-cetanaḥ|
kūṭavan nirvikāreṇa sthitaḥ kūṭastha ucyate||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 23
units.deva:
कूतस्थे कल्पिता बुद्धिस् तत्र चित्-प्रतिबिंबकः।
प्राणानां धारणाज् जीवः संसारेण स युज्यते॥
units.translation: On the kuṭa-stha is imposed (kalpita) the intellect (buddhi). Reflected in the consciousness, in that (buddhi), is the (notion of) the jīva (the individual) due to the support of the life-forces (prāṇas). That one (the jīva) is subject to saṃsāra (migration in time and births).
units.iast:
kūtasthe kalpitā buddhis tatra cit-pratibiṃbakaḥ|
prāṇānāṃ dhāraṇāj jīvaḥ saṃsāreṇa sa yujyate||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 24
units.deva:
जल-व्योम्ना घटाकाशो यथा सर्वस् तिरोहितः।
तथा जीवेन कूटस्थः सोऽन्योन्याध्यास उच्यते॥
units.translation: Just as the entirety the space within the pot is hidden (tirohita) by the (reflected) sky on the surface of water (in the pot), similarly, the (entirely of) kūṭa-stha* (consciousness present in the mind, and everywhere) is hidden by the jīva (the notion of individuality reflecting in the intellect). That is called mutual imposition (anyonya-adhyāsa, where the uninformed mind imposes limited individuality on oneself and that individual imposes the limitation of its reflection of the universe on the totality of space, of consciousness). Then, he combines this understanding of the unchanging reality of the individual with the changing notion of ‘I’ as the individual exampled by the changing reflecting surface of water in the very same pot, which is the surface that masks the changeless depth of one’s reality, the kūṭa-stha.)
units.iast:
jala-vyomnā ghaṭākāśo yathā sarvas tirohitaḥ|
tathā jīvena kūṭasthaḥ so’nyonyādhyāsa ucyate||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 25
units.deva:
अयं जीवो न कूटस्थं विविनक्ति कदाचन।
अनादिर् अविवेकोऽयं मूलाऽविद्येति गम्यताम्॥
units.translation: (By this mutual imposition) the jīva (on its own) will not ever discern the (totality of) kūṭa-stha (unchanging consciousness, as its real nature). This lack of discernment is beginningless (as is the nature of any kind of ignorance, such as it makes no sense to say that my ignorance of Chinese language started at some particular time). This (lack of discernment) is to be understood as the root ignorance (mūlā a-vidyā, from which all other problems of limitation evolve).
units.iast:
ayaṃ jīvo na kūṭasthaṃ vivinakti kadācana|
anādir aviveko’yaṃ mūlā’vidyeti gamyatām||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 26
units.deva:
विक्षेपावृति-रूपाभ्यां द्विधाऽविद्या व्यवस्थिता।
न भाति नास्ति कूटस्थ इत्यापादनम् आवृतिः॥
units.translation: This ignorance appears in two forms as concealment (āvṛti) and projection (vikṣepa). The concealment (myself as limitless consciousness being unknown) is the material basis (āpādana) for (the projection, & ) ‘Consciousness (kūṭa-stha) is not seen so it does not exist’ (hence, I am only my body and mind that I can see, nothing else).

gloss.en: by the forms of projection and concealment

units.iast:
vikṣepāvṛti-rūpābhyāṃ dvidhā’vidyā vyavasthitā|
na bhāti nāsti kūṭastha ityāpādanam āvṛtiḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 27
units.deva:
अज्ञानी विदुषा पृष्टः कूटस्थं न प्रबुध्यते।
न भाति नास्ति कूटस्थ इति बुध्वा वदत्यपि॥
units.translation: If a wise person asks someone who does not know about the kūṭa-stha, (the reply would be) “It is not known. It is not seen. The kūṭa-stha does not exist.” In this way that one would think and also admit.
units.iast:
ajñānī viduṣā pṛṣṭaḥ kūṭasthaṃ na prabudhyate|
na bhāti nāsti kūṭastha iti budhvā vadatyapi||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 28
units.deva:
स्वप्रकाशे कुतोऽविद्या तां विना कथम् आवृतिः।
इत्यादि-तर्क-जालानि स्वानुभूतिर् ग्रसत्यसौ॥
units.translation: From where could this ignorance (a-vidyā) come into one’s consciousness (sva-prakāśa, kūṭa-stha)? Without that (ignorance) how could there be concealment (āvṛti)? – Such are the webs of logic which one’s own experience swallows (i.e., it is useless to question what is already an obvious fact, namely, that this ignorance is already here, much like ignorance of Chinese language).
units.iast:
svaprakāśe kuto’vidyā tāṃ vinā katham āvṛtiḥ|
ityādi-tarka-jālāni svānubhūtir grasatyasau||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 29
units.deva:
स्वानुभूतावविश्वासे तर्कस्याप्यनवस्थितेः।
कथं वा तार्किकं-मन्यस् तत्त्व-निश्चयम् आप्नुयात्॥
units.translation: When one does not trust one’s own experience yet has (the trust) of a logic that can have no finality (that can be factually verified), then how could such a one, thinking he is a logician, gain any clarity in truth?

gloss.en: when distrust of one's own experience
because even reasoning has no firm ground
one who thinks himself a logician

units.iast:
svānubhūtāvaviśvāse tarkasyāpyanavasthiteḥ|
kathaṃ vā tārkikaṃ-manyas tattva-niścayam āpnuyāt||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 30
units.deva:
बुद्ध्यारोहाय तर्कश् चेद् अपेक्षेत तथा सति।
स्वानुभूत्यनुसारेण तर्क्यतां मा कु-तर्क्यताम्॥
units.translation: If logic (tarka) is meant for firming up the intellect, then, in that case, one should expect it to be like that. One should employ logic in keeping with one’s experience, not employ illogic (which confounds the intellect).
units.iast:
buddhyārohāya tarkaś ced apekṣeta tathā sati|
svānubhūtyanusāreṇa tarkyatāṃ mā ku-tarkyatām||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 31
units.deva:
स्वानुभूतिर् अविद्यायाम् आवृतौ च प्रदर्शिता।
अतः कूटस्थ-चैतन्यम् अविरोधीति तर्क्यताम्॥
units.translation: One’s experience regarding ignorance and its power of concealment was clearly shown (). Therefore, one should employ logic based on this experience that the unchanging consciousness (kūṭa-stha-caitanya) is not opposed (to ignorance, i.e., we are aware of what we know, and also are aware of our ignorance regarding what we do not know).
units.iast:
svānubhūtir avidyāyām āvṛtau ca pradarśitā|
ataḥ kūṭastha-caitanyam avirodhīti tarkyatām||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 32
units.deva:
तच् चेद् विरोधि केनेयम् आवृतिर् ह्यनुभूयताम्।
विवेकस् तु विरोध्यस्यास् तत्त्व-ज्ञानिनि दृश्यताम्॥
units.translation: If that (unchanging consciousness) is opposed to the concealing (by ignorance), then the latter is experienced by whom? Whereas, it is discerning knowledge (viveka, a form of vṛtti-jñāna, not svarūpa-jñāna) that is opposed to this (concealing, i.e., whenever knowledge of something comes then its ignorance goes, because they are opposing, while awareness witnesses the presence of both ignorance and its absence). This fact is seen in regard to a knower of the truth.
units.iast:
tac ced virodhi keneyam āvṛtir hyanubhūyatām|
vivekas tu virodhyasyās tattva-jñānini dṛśyatām||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 33
units.deva:
अविद्यावृत-कूटस्थे देह-द्वय-युता चितिः।
शुक्तौ रूप्यवद् अध्यस्ता विक्षेपाध्यास एव हि॥
units.translation: When the kūṭa-stha (limitless consciousness present within) is obscured (from our intellect) by ignorance, this consciousness is then (seemingly) endowed with the two bodies (the physical and the mental), imposed like (an imagined piece of) silver on a mother of pearl shell. This indeed is the erroneous predication (adhyāsa) called vikṣepa (projection, the example of silver on a shell is one of projecting a desirable piece of silver on an otherwise useless shell).

gloss.en: in the unchanging basis covered by ignorance

units.iast:
avidyāvṛta-kūṭasthe deha-dvaya-yutā citiḥ|
śuktau rūpyavad adhyastā vikṣepādhyāsa eva hi||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 34
units.deva:
इदम्-अंशश् च सत्यत्वं शुक्तिगं रूप्य ईक्ष्यते।
स्वयंत्वं वस्तुताचैवं विक्षेपे वीक्ष्यतेऽन्यगम्॥
units.translation: (In the example, “This is silver”) The ‘this’ is factual reality, but ‘silver’ placed on the shinny surface of the shell is (alone) seen. In the same way (in the delusion “this body and mind is real and it is me”) my-ness is the reality, but when projection occurs, it is placed on what is other (anya-ga, than oneself).

gloss.en: is seen as belonging to another

units.iast:
idam-aṃśaś ca satyatvaṃ śuktigaṃ rūpya īkṣyate|
svayaṃtvaṃ vastutācaivaṃ vikṣepe vīkṣyate’nyagam||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 35
units.deva:
नील-पृष्ठ-त्रिकोणत्वं यथा शुक्तौ तिरोहितम्।
असङ्गानन्दताद्येवं कूटस्थेऽपि तिरोहितम्॥
units.translation: Just as the iridescent (nīla, blue) surface and triangular shape on the shell are obscured (tirohita), so too the absence of associations (a-saṅga) and fullness (ānandatā) within oneself (kūṭa-stha, the one who always remains the same) are obscured.
units.iast:
nīla-pṛṣṭha-trikoṇatvaṃ yathā śuktau tirohitam|
asaṅgānandatādyevaṃ kūṭasthe’pi tirohitam||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 36
units.deva:
आरोपितस्य दृष्टान्ते रूप्यं नाम यथा तथा।
कूटस्थाध्यस्त-विक्षेप-नामाहम् इति निश्चयः॥
units.translation: In the illustration (dṛṣṭānta), what is imposed has the (valued reality notion and) name ‘silver’. Similarly, is the certain notion that it is (an individual) with the name ‘I’ (aham) projected and imposed upon the consciousness within (the kūṭa-stha).

gloss.en: the notion “I” projected on the unchanging basis

units.iast:
āropitasya dṛṣṭānte rūpyaṃ nāma yathā tathā|
kūṭasthādhyasta-vikṣepa-nāmāham iti niścayaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 37
units.deva:
इदम्-अंशं स्वतः पश्यन् रूप्यम् इत्यभिमन्यते।
तथा स्वं च स्वतः पश्यन्न् अहम् इत्यभिमन्यते॥
units.translation: Naturally seeing the ‘this’ (here and now) aspect (only of the shell), yet one identifies it to be ‘silver’. Similarly, naturally seeing oneself (svam, the inherent nature of oneself and all entities), one identifies it as (an individual) ‘I’.
units.iast:
idam-aṃśaṃ svataḥ paśyan rūpyam ityabhimanyate|
tathā svaṃ ca svataḥ paśyann aham ityabhimanyate||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 38
units.deva:
इदन्त्व-रूप्यते भिन्ने स्वत्वाहन्ते तथेष्यताम्।
सामान्यं च विशेषश् च ह्युभयत्रापि गम्यते॥
units.translation: Both the natures of (perceptible) ‘this’ and (notional) ‘silver’ are different (as the first being common to everyone and the latter being peculiar to some), similarly is different the (obvious) self and the (notional) ‘I’. In both there is indeed a commonality (sāmānya) and peculiarity (viśeṣa).
units.iast:
idantva-rūpyate bhinne svatvāhante tatheṣyatām|
sāmānyaṃ ca viśeṣaś ca hyubhayatrāpi gamyate||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 39
units.deva:
देव-दत्तः स्वयं गच्छेत् त्वं वीक्षस्व स्वयं तथा।
अहं स्वयं न शक्नोमीत्येवं लोके प्रयुज्यते॥
units.translation: One sees such common expressions as, ‘Deva-datta himself (svam) may go’, ‘You yourself (svam) see’, similarly, ‘I myself (svam) am not able’.
units.iast:
deva-dattaḥ svayaṃ gacchet tvaṃ vīkṣasva svayaṃ tathā|
ahaṃ svayaṃ na śaknomītyevaṃ loke prayujyate||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 40
units.deva:
इदं रूप्यम् इदं वस्त्रम् इति यद्वद् इदं तथा।
असौ त्वम् अहम् इत्येषु स्वयम् इत्यभिमन्यते॥
units.translation: Just as (the demonstrative pronoun) ‘this’ is (common) in the expressions, ‘This silver’ and ‘This cloth’, similarly, (the reflexive pronoun) ‘self’ (svam) is identified (as common) in regard to the pronouns ‘he’, ‘you’, and ‘I’ (as himself, yourself, and myself).
units.iast:
idaṃ rūpyam idaṃ vastram iti yadvad idaṃ tathā|
asau tvam aham ityeṣu svayam ityabhimanyate||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 41
units.deva:
अहन्त्वाद् भिद्यतां स्वत्वं कूटस्थे तेन किं तव।
स्वयं-शब्दार्थ एवैष कूटस्थ इति मे भवेत्॥
units.translation: (Doubt:) (The common) self (svam) is different from (the concept of the peculiar) ‘I’, but what has this to do in regard to the kūṭa-stha for you? (Reply:) The meaning of the word ‘self’ (svam) indeed is this ‘kūṭa-stha’ for me.
units.iast:
ahantvād bhidyatāṃ svatvaṃ kūṭasthe tena kiṃ tava|
svayaṃ-śabdārtha evaiṣa kūṭastha iti me bhavet||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 42
units.deva:
अन्यत्व-वारकं स्वत्वम् इति चेद् अन्य-वारणम्।
कूटस्थस्यात्मतां वक्तुर् इष्टम् एव हि तद् भवेत्॥
units.translation: (Doubt:) Doesn’t the word ‘self’ (svam) just exclude otherness (exclude not-self, not just indicate oneself). (Reply:) Excluding other is the very nature (ātmatā) of (the one and only) ‘kūṭa-stha’. That (understanding) would indeed be acceptable (iṣṭa, to us).

gloss.en: the self-nature of the unchanging basis

units.iast:
anyatva-vārakaṃ svatvam iti ced anya-vāraṇam|
kūṭasthasyātmatāṃ vaktur iṣṭam eva hi tad bhavet||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 43
units.deva:
स्वयम् आत्मेति पर्यायौ तेन लोके तयोः सह।
प्रयोगो नास्त्यतः स्वत्वम् आत्मत्वं चान्य-वारकम्॥
units.translation: Svayam (oneself) and ātman (the self) are alternative words (paryāya, synonyms), so in common parlance both these are not used together. Therefore, ‘oneself’ and the ‘self’ both exclude any other thing.
units.iast:
svayam ātmeti paryāyau tena loke tayoḥ saha|
prayogo nāstyataḥ svatvam ātmatvaṃ cānya-vārakam||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 44
units.deva:
घटः स्वयं न जानातीत्येवं स्वत्वं घटादिषु।
अचेतनेषु दृष्टं चेद् दृश्यताम् आत्म-सत्त्वतः॥
units.translation: (Doubt:) But (the reflexive pronoun) ‘svam’ (self) is seen to apply to objects that lack consciousness such as a pot, etcetera, as in the expression ‘the pot itself (svayam) does not know’. (Reply:) Such usage is seen because of the reality (sattva) basis of the innate nature (ātman, of all entities, even the inanimate).
units.iast:
ghaṭaḥ svayaṃ na jānātītyevaṃ svatvaṃ ghaṭādiṣu|
acetaneṣu dṛṣṭaṃ ced dṛśyatām ātma-sattvataḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 45
units.deva:
चेतनाचेतन-भिदा कूटस्थात्म-कृता न हि।
किन्तु बुद्धि-कृताभास-कृतैवेत्यवगम्यताम्॥
units.translation: The difference between animate and inanimate is indeed not due to the kūṭa-stha or the ātman. Rather, (the difference) is only made by the reflection (ābhāsa, of consciousness) itself due to the mind (buddhi, a subtle entity present only in the animate that becomes conscious by the presence of consciousness) – this is how it is to be understood.

gloss.en: made by the mind-made reflection; so let it be understood

units.iast:
cetanācetana-bhidā kūṭasthātma-kṛtā na hi|
kintu buddhi-kṛtābhāsa-kṛtaivetyavagamyatām||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 46
units.deva:
यथा चेतन आभासः कूटस्थे भ्रान्ति-कल्पितः।
अचेतनो घटादिश् च तथा तत्रैव कल्पितः॥
units.translation: Just as the conscious reflection (limited to the mind) itself is an erroneous notion within the kūṭa-stha, so the unconscious pot, etcetera is a notion within that (the kūṭa-stha) alone.
units.iast:
yathā cetana ābhāsaḥ kūṭasthe bhrānti-kalpitaḥ|
acetano ghaṭādiś ca tathā tatraiva kalpitaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 47
units.deva:
तत्तेदन्ते अपि स्वत्वम् इव त्वम्-अहम्-आदिषु।
सर्वत्रानुगते तेन तयोर् अप्यात्मतेति चेत्॥
units.translation: (Doubt:) Even ‘that’ (tad) and ‘this’ (idam, pronouns), like ‘svam’ (it/your/one…self), can be applied everywhere to you, I, etc. (all three grammatical persons), therefore both (‘that’ and ‘this’) also are meaning ‘ātman’ (the self).

gloss.en: among you, I, and so on

units.iast:
tattedante api svatvam iva tvam-aham-ādiṣu|
sarvatrānugate tena tayor apyātmateti cet||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 48
units.deva:
ते आत्मत्वेऽप्यनुगते तत्तेदन्ते ततस् तयोः।
आत्मत्वं नैव संभाव्यं सम्यक्त्वादेर् यथा तथा॥
units.translation: (Reply:) Even though both these pronouns, ‘that’ and ‘this’, can refer to the self (as ‘that self’ and ‘this self’), apart from that usage these two cannot refer only to the self, the same as the (general adjectives) ‘correct’, etc. (can refer to a noun, but cannot be limited to only refer to just one noun).

gloss.en: such as correctness and so on

units.iast:
te ātmatve’pyanugate tattedante tatas tayoḥ|
ātmatvaṃ naiva saṃbhāvyaṃ samyaktvāder yathā tathā||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 49
units.deva:
तत्तेदन्ते स्वतान्यत्वे त्वन्ताहन्ते परस्परम्।
प्रतिद्वन्द्वितया लोके प्रसिद्धे नास्ति संशयः॥
units.translation: The pair of words ‘that’ and ‘this’, ‘itself’ and ‘other’, as well as ‘you’ and ‘I’ are well-know in common parlance as being mutually exclusive (of each other). No one doubts this.
units.iast:
tattedante svatānyatve tvantāhante parasparam|
pratidvandvitayā loke prasiddhe nāsti saṃśayaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 50
units.deva:
अन्यतायाः प्रतिद्वन्द्वी स्वयं कूटस्थ इष्यताम्।
त्वन्तायाः प्रतियोग्येषोऽहम् इत्यात्मनि कल्पितः॥
units.translation: The opposite of ‘other’ (anya) is oneself (svayam), which is recognized as the kūṭa-stha (one’s conscious being). The opposite of ‘you’ (tvam) is the ‘I’ (aham), which is imposed on oneself (on kūṭa-stha).
units.iast:
anyatāyāḥ pratidvandvī svayaṃ kūṭastha iṣyatām|
tvantāyāḥ pratiyogyeṣo’ham ityātmani kalpitaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 51
units.deva:
अहन्तास्वत्वयोर् भेदे रूप्यतेदन्तयोर् इव।
स्पष्टेऽपि मोहम् आपन्ना एकत्वं प्रतिपेदिरे॥
units.translation: Like between ‘silver’ and ‘this’ (of the shell) is the distinction between ‘I’ (the notion of individuality) and ‘self’ (the consciousness being, kūṭa-stha). Even though clear, those who are overcome with delusion (moha, of a-vidyā) take them as identical.
units.iast:
ahantāsvatvayor bhede rūpyatedantayor iva|
spaṣṭe’pi moham āpannā ekatvaṃ pratipedire||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 52
units.deva:
तादात्म्याध्यास एवात्र पूर्वोक्ताविद्यया कृतः।
अविद्यायां निवृत्तायां तत्कार्यं विनिवर्तते॥
units.translation: This identity imposition (tād-ātmya-adhyāsa, between the ‘other’ and myself, ) is brought about by a-vidyā, beginningless ignorance of one’s limitless nature) which was explained before (). When this ignorance is negated (by assimilated knowledge of oneself), its effects are discounted (as being mere temporary appearances, not touching upon the limitless consciousness self).
units.iast:
tādātmyādhyāsa evātra pūrvoktāvidyayā kṛtaḥ|
avidyāyāṃ nivṛttāyāṃ tatkāryaṃ vinivartate||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 53
units.deva:
अविद्यावृति-तादात्म्ये विद्ययैव विनश्यतः।
विक्षेपस्य स्वरूपस् तु प्रारब्ध-क्षयम् ईक्षते॥
units.translation: The concealing and identification due to ignorance are both removed by knowledge alone. But, the essence of the projections (i.e., māyā, the appearances of the world, ) is continued to be experienced until the end of one’s prārabdha (life-term karma, the fructifying karma that brought and keeps this body and mind here during this time).

gloss.en: until the exhaustion of past karma

units.iast:
avidyāvṛti-tādātmye vidyayaiva vinaśyataḥ|
vikṣepasya svarūpas tu prārabdha-kṣayam īkṣate||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 54
units.deva:
उपादाने विनष्टेऽपि क्षणं कार्यं प्रतीक्षते।
इत्याहुस् तार्किकास् तद्वद् अस्माकं किं न संभवेत्॥
units.translation: Even the logicians say that when the material cause of something is destroyed its (subsequent) effect is seen the next moment. So why not for us (Vedāntins) this (continuation of the body and mind after destruction of a-vidyā)?
units.iast:
upādāne vinaṣṭe’pi kṣaṇaṃ kāryaṃ pratīkṣate|
ityāhus tārkikās tadvad asmākaṃ kiṃ na saṃbhavet||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 55
units.deva:
तन्तूनां दिन-सङ्ख्यानां तैस् तादृक् क्षण ईरितः।
भ्रमस्यासङ्ख्य-कल्पस्य योग्यः क्षण इहेष्यताम्॥
units.translation: Those (logicians) even believe that (at least subtly the form of the cloth, which is an effect of its material cause, the threads) lasts the same amount of time as the last number of days of its threads. Similarly here for us, the innumerable effects of delusion may have their appropriate moments of survival.
units.iast:
tantūnāṃ dina-saṅkhyānāṃ tais tādṛk kṣaṇa īritaḥ|
bhramasyāsaṅkhya-kalpasya yogyaḥ kṣaṇa iheṣyatām||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 56
units.deva:
विना क्षोद-क्षमं मानं तैर् वृथा परिकल्प्यते।
श्रुति-युक्त्यनुभूतिभ्यो वदतां किं नु दुःशकम्॥
units.translation: Without any evidence (māna, pramāṇa) that can withstand a pounding (a questioning), they (the logicians) uselessly propose (this theory that an effect can survive a few moments beyond the destruction of its material cause). However, being based upon scripture, logic and experience, how could this (survival of the fructifying karma of an individual even after discerning unreality of this very universe itself) be impractical?

gloss.en: a proof able to withstand scrutiny

units.iast:
vinā kṣoda-kṣamaṃ mānaṃ tair vṛthā parikalpyate|
śruti-yuktyanubhūtibhyo vadatāṃ kiṃ nu duḥśakam||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 57
units.deva:
आस्तां दुस्तार्किकैः साकं विवादं प्रकृतं ब्रुवे।
स्वाऽहमोः सिद्धम् एकत्वं कूटस्थ-परिणामिनोः॥
units.translation: Me talking about this current topic (prakṛta) with unreasonable logicians (who do not accept the scriptures as a means of knowledge here) would be continuing an unending dispute (vi-vāda). The fact (siddha, from scripture, which is evidenced by us and is logical) is that oneself and ‘I’ is a (false) identification of the kūṭa-stha (the permanent consciousness) and the changing (pariṇāmin, body-mind complex), respectively.
units.iast:
āstāṃ dustārkikaiḥ sākaṃ vivādaṃ prakṛtaṃ bruve|
svā’hamoḥ siddham ekatvaṃ kūṭastha-pariṇāminoḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 58
units.deva:
भ्राम्यन्ते पण्डितं-मन्याः सर्वे लौकिक-तैर्थिकाः।
अनादृत्या श्रुतिं मौर्ख्यात् केवलं युक्तिम् आश्रिताः॥
units.translation: All those who consider themselves learned and are world-bound logicians, without regard to the prominence of the scripture (as the pramāṇa, essential authority, in this topic) and dependent solely on logic, they only make themselves (and others) confused.
units.iast:
bhrāmyante paṇḍitaṃ-manyāḥ sarve laukika-tairthikāḥ|
anādṛtyā śrutiṃ maurkhyāt kevalaṃ yuktim āśritāḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 59
units.deva:
पूर्वापर-परामर्श-विकलास् तत्र केचन।
वाक्याभासान् स्वस्व-पक्षे योजयन्त्यप्यलज्जया॥
units.translation: Among them, some (who accept some authority of the scripture) lacking reflexion on the context (pūrva-apara, on what what said before and after) unembarrassedly employ semblances of scriptures in arguing their own viewpoint alone (not the scripture’s).

gloss.en: lacking consideration of what came before and after

units.iast:
pūrvāpara-parāmarśa-vikalās tatra kecana|
vākyābhāsān svasva-pakṣe yojayantyapyalajjayā||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 60
units.deva:
कूटस्थादि-शरीरान्त-सङ्घातस्यात्मतां जगुः।
लोकायताः पामराश् च प्रत्यक्षाभासम् आश्रिताः॥
units.translation: Materialists (lokāyatas) and simple people (pāmara), dependent on a semblance (limitation, misremembrance and perversion) of their own experiences (pratyakṣa-ābhāsa), become themselves identified with this complex (saṅghāta) beginning with their conscious being to the gross body.

gloss.en: of the aggregate from the unchanging basis to the body

units.iast:
kūṭasthādi-śarīrānta-saṅghātasyātmatāṃ jaguḥ|
lokāyatāḥ pāmarāś ca pratyakṣābhāsam āśritāḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 61
units.deva:
श्रौती-कर्तुं स्वपक्षं ते कोशम् अन्नमयं तथा।
विरोचनस्य सिद्धान्तं प्रमाणं प्रतिजज्ञिरे॥
units.translation: Similarly there are those who recognize as a means of knowledge the conclusion of Virocana ( (Chāndogya Upaniṣad)) as their own opinion and treat it as if it was scripture that the only treasure (kośa) is this food body (anna-maya, ).
units.iast:
śrautī-kartuṃ svapakṣaṃ te kośam annamayaṃ tathā|
virocanasya siddhāntaṃ pramāṇaṃ pratijajñire||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 62
units.deva:
जीवात्म-निर्गमे देह-मरणस्यात्र दर्शनात्।
देहातिरिक्त एवात्मेत्याहुर् लोकायताः परे॥
units.translation: Other materialists (lokāyatas) say that since the death of the body here is seen when the essence (ātman) of the individual leaves it, then the self must be something other than the body.

gloss.en: at the departure of the individual self
only the self, thus they say

units.iast:
jīvātma-nirgame deha-maraṇasyātra darśanāt|
dehātirikta evātmetyāhur lokāyatāḥ pare||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 63
units.deva:
प्रत्यक्षत्वेनाभिमताऽहं-धीर् देहातिरेकिणम्।
गमयेद् इन्द्रियात्मानं वच्मीत्यादि-प्रयोगतः॥
units.translation: From the expressions ‘I speak’ (vacmi), etcetera, as the notion of ‘I’ is recognized through the nature of sensing, another would conjecture the self to be these powers (indriyas, the organs of sensing and acting) separate from the body.

gloss.en: the “I” thought regarded as direct perception

units.iast:
pratyakṣatvenābhimatā’haṃ-dhīr dehātirekiṇam|
gamayed indriyātmānaṃ vacmītyādi-prayogataḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 64
units.deva:
वागादीनाम् इन्द्रियाणां कलहः श्रुतिषु श्रुतः।
तेन चैतन्यम् एतेषाम् आत्मत्वं तत एव हि॥
units.translation: Heard in the scriptures is the quarreling among speech, etc. indriyas ( (Chāndogya Upaniṣad), (Bṛhad-Āraṇyaka Upaniṣad)). By that, each must have consciousness (have an ātman). But apart from them (the prāṇa, the life-force was seen to be superior) so it must be the (superior) ātman.
units.iast:
vāgādīnām indriyāṇāṃ kalahaḥ śrutiṣu śrutaḥ|
tena caitanyam eteṣām ātmatvaṃ tata eva hi||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 65
units.deva:
हैरण्य-गर्भाः प्राणात्म-वादिनस् त्वेवम् ऊचिरे।
चक्षुराद्यक्ष-लोपेऽपि प्राण-सत्त्वे तु जीवति॥
units.translation: But the followers of Hiraṇya-garbha argue that (from the same scripture above) the prāṇa alone is ātman. They say that even when each of the senses, starting from sight, fail, nevertheless one survives as long as the prāṇa remains.

gloss.en: even when the senses beginning with sight fail

units.iast:
hairaṇya-garbhāḥ prāṇātma-vādinas tvevam ūcire|
cakṣurādyakṣa-lope’pi prāṇa-sattve tu jīvati||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 66
units.deva:
प्राणो जागर्ति सुप्तेऽपि प्राण-श्रैष्ठ्यादिकं श्रुतम्।
कोशः प्राणमयः सम्यग् विस्तरेण प्रपञ्चितः॥
units.translation: The prāṇa remains awake even when one is deep asleep. Prāṇa’s superiority, etc. is indicated in the scriptures. The prāṇa-maya kośa is widely discussed in detail (elsewhere too).

gloss.en: the superiority of life-breath and so on

units.iast:
prāṇo jāgarti supte’pi prāṇa-śraiṣṭhyādikaṃ śrutam|
kośaḥ prāṇamayaḥ samyag vistareṇa prapañcitaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 67
units.deva:
मन आत्मेति मन्यन्त उपासन-परा जनाः।
प्राणस्याभोक्तृता स्पष्टा भोक्तृत्वं मनसस् ततः॥
units.translation: Other people holding meditation (upāsana) as the ultimate consider the mind (manas) to be the ātman. The prāṇa clearly has no enjoyership, while this mind does have enjoyership (bhoktṛtva).
units.iast:
mana ātmeti manyanta upāsana-parā janāḥ|
prāṇasyābhoktṛtā spaṣṭā bhoktṛtvaṃ manasas tataḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 68
units.deva:
मन एव मनुष्याणां कारणं बन्ध-मोक्षयोः।
श्रुतो मनोमयः कोशस् तेनात्मेतीरितं मनः॥
units.translation: The scripture says, “Mind alone is mans’ cause for bondage and freedom” (), and (thus) it discusses the mano-maya kośa. Therefore, (for these people) the mind is considered ātman.
units.iast:
mana eva manuṣyāṇāṃ kāraṇaṃ bandha-mokṣayoḥ|
śruto manomayaḥ kośas tenātmetīritaṃ manaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 69
units.deva:
विज्ञानम् आत्मेति पर आहुः क्षणिक-वादिनः।
यतो विज्ञान-मूलत्वं मनसो गम्यते स्फुटम्॥
units.translation: Others (some Buddhists) clearly believe that vijñāna (intellect) is the ātman. They are (called) kṣaṇika-vādins (proclaimers that reality is momentary), because the mind (manas) is based on (momentary) thought (vijñāna, a distinct unit of knowledge).
units.iast:
vijñānam ātmeti para āhuḥ kṣaṇika-vādinaḥ|
yato vijñāna-mūlatvaṃ manaso gamyate sphuṭam||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 70
units.deva:
अहं-वृत्तिर् इदं-वृत्तिर् इत्यन्तःकरणं द्विधा।
विज्ञानं स्याद् अहं-वृत्तिर् इदं-वृत्तिर् मनो भवेत्॥
units.translation: The internal organ (antaḥ-karaṇa, the mind in general) is of two modes: an ‘I’-thought (any thought connected to the sense of I, ownership, etc.) and a ‘this’-thought (any thought connected to the sense of this that is other than I). The ‘I’-thought is (called) the vijñāna (intellect, such as ‘I know this’) and the ‘this’-thought is the manas.* *(Manas is a technical name for any thought that is not an intellect thought, such as a thought that directs the senses to their objects or cognizes internal sensations, such as ‘this sadness’, apart from the intellection that ‘I am sad’, etcetera. In other words, the manas is the figuring-out or work-in-process mind and the vijñāna or buddhi is the settled, determined mind).
units.iast:
ahaṃ-vṛttir idaṃ-vṛttir ityantaḥkaraṇaṃ dvidhā|
vijñānaṃ syād ahaṃ-vṛttir idaṃ-vṛttir mano bhavet||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 71
units.deva:
अहं-प्रत्यय-बीजत्वम् इदं-वृत्तेर् इति स्फुटम्।
अविदित्वा स्वम् आत्मानं बाह्यं वेत्ति न तु क्वचित्॥
units.translation: Clearly, a 'this’-thought has its origin from the ‘I’-thought (i.e., the idea of ‘other’ comes from the idea of a ‘me’). Without my self, there can never be an idea of an external (outside of my self).
units.iast:
ahaṃ-pratyaya-bījatvam idaṃ-vṛtter iti sphuṭam|
aviditvā svam ātmānaṃ bāhyaṃ vetti na tu kvacit||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 72
units.deva:
क्षणे क्षणे जन्म-नाशावहं-वृत्तेर् मितौ यतः।
विज्ञानं क्षणिकं तेन स्वप्रकाशं स्वतो मितेः॥
units.translation: Because the ‘I’-thought has a limit (mita) as moment by moment born-gone (and not a continuity), then vijñāna (the intellect) is momentary, and this intellect (miti) is self-luminous (not requiring another thought to illumine it).

gloss.en: of the I-thought's birth and death

units.iast:
kṣaṇe kṣaṇe janma-nāśāvahaṃ-vṛtter mitau yataḥ|
vijñānaṃ kṣaṇikaṃ tena svaprakāśaṃ svato miteḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 73
units.deva:
विज्ञानमय-कोशोऽयं जीव इत्यागमा जगुः।
सर्व-संसार एतस्य जन्म-नाश-सुखादिकः॥
units.translation: Even the ancient texts ( (Taittirīya Upaniṣad)) claim that the vijñāna-maya kośa is the jīva. For this one alone is the entire saṃsāra (phenomenal appearance) consisting of births and deaths, and in between sorrows, etcetera.
units.iast:
vijñānamaya-kośo’yaṃ jīva ityāgamā jaguḥ|
sarva-saṃsāra etasya janma-nāśa-sukhādikaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 74
units.deva:
विज्ञानं क्षणिकं नात्मा विद्युद्-अभ्र-निमेषवत्।
अन्यस्यानुपलब्धत्वाच् छून्यं माध्यमिका जगुः॥
units.translation: The Mādhyamika (Buddhists) claim that vijñāna cannot be the (permanent) ātman as it is momentary, like lightning flashes in a cloud, or the blink of the eye, and since there is seen nothing other than these, then (the permanent) is nothing (śūnya, the void).

gloss.en: because of the non-perception of anything else

units.iast:
vijñānaṃ kṣaṇikaṃ nātmā vidyud-abhra-nimeṣavat|
anyasyānupalabdhatvāc chūnyaṃ mādhyamikā jaguḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 75
units.deva:
असद् एवेदम् इत्यादाव् इदम् एव श्रुतं ततः।
ज्ञान-ज्ञेयात्मकं सर्वं जगद् भ्रान्ति-प्रकल्पितम्॥
units.translation: Even (your) scripture talks about this (śūnya), starting with, “(In the beginning) there was only this non-existence (a-sat)”, etc. ( (Chāndogya Upaniṣad)). Therefore, this entire jagat (impermanent phenomenal world) consisting of knowing and known is but an erroneous illusion (imagined permanence connecting the momentary).
units.iast:
asad evedam ityādāv idam eva śrutaṃ tataḥ|
jñāna-jñeyātmakaṃ sarvaṃ jagad bhrānti-prakalpitam||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 76
units.deva:
निरधिष्ठान-विभ्रान्तेर् अभावाद् आत्मनोऽस्तिता।
शून्यस्यापि ससाक्षित्वाद् अन्यधा नोक्तिर् अस्य ते॥
units.translation: (Reply:) (Logically:) Since there can be no illusion (no effect) without a substratum (adhiṣṭhāna, a substantive cause, such as a mirage water illusion requires a distant surface over which a layer of air reflects the blue sky above), the ātman (oneself) must have that nature of being the (substantive) reality (of even an illusion of permanency amongst the transitory). Moreover, since any (claim of) śūnya (nothingness, as the substratum of the phenomenal) requires a witness (to this fact), those (Śūnya-vādins) have no one (other than śūnya) to claim this (śūnya, and if śūnya itself is self-aware, then śūnya is simply another name for existent consciousness).
units.iast:
niradhiṣṭhāna-vibhrānter abhāvād ātmano’stitā|
śūnyasyāpi sasākṣitvād anyadhā noktir asya te||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 77
units.deva:
अन्यो विज्ञानमयत आनन्दमय आन्तरः।
अस्तीत्येवोपलब्धव्य इति वैदिक-दर्शनम्॥
units.translation: (Scripturally:) Internal to the vijñāna-maya is another (kośa) called ānanda-maya (the sense of fullness, which is there even in the nothingness of deep sleep, , (Taittirīya Upaniṣad)). And it (ānanda-maya) indeed does experientially exist, per the scriptural perspective.

gloss.en: exists, thus alone to be experienced

units.iast:
anyo vijñānamayata ānandamaya āntaraḥ|
astītyevopalabdhavya iti vaidika-darśanam||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 78
units.deva:
अणुर् महान् मध्यमो वेत्येवं तत्रापि वादिनः।
बहुधा विवदन्ते हि श्रुति-युक्ति-समाश्रयात्॥
units.translation: Other disputants regarding this topic argue variously from scripture and logic that (ātman) is tiny, pervasive, or medium in size.
units.iast:
aṇur mahān madhyamo vetyevaṃ tatrāpi vādinaḥ|
bahudhā vivadante hi śruti-yukti-samāśrayāt||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 79
units.deva:
अणुं वदन्त्यान्तर्-आलाः सूक्ष्म-नाडी-प्रचारतः।
रोम्णः सहस्र-भागेन तुल्यासु प्रचरत्ययम्॥
units.translation: The Antar-ālas (the ‘Inside’ proponents) argue this (ātman) is tiny aṇu, since it abides and moves within the subtle nāḍīs (the prāṇa pathways inside the body), which are equal to a thousandth the width of a hair.

gloss.en: because of movement through subtle channels

units.iast:
aṇuṃ vadantyāntar-ālāḥ sūkṣma-nāḍī-pracārataḥ|
romṇaḥ sahasra-bhāgena tulyāsu pracaratyayam||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 80
units.deva:
अणोर् अणीयान् एषोऽणुः सूक्ष्मात् सूक्ष्मतरं त्विति।
अणुत्वम् आहुः श्रुतयः शतशोऽध सहस्रशः॥
units.translation: (Ātman) is “smaller than the small” ( (Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad)), “This is tiny” ( (Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad)), “Subtler than the subtle” ( (Kaivalya Upaniṣad)) – hundreds and thousands of scripture quotes they recite to show its tiny nature.
units.iast:
aṇor aṇīyān eṣo’ṇuḥ sūkṣmāt sūkṣmataraṃ tviti|
aṇutvam āhuḥ śrutayaḥ śataśo’dha sahasraśaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 81
units.deva:
बालाग्र-शत-भागस्य शतधा कल्पितस्य च।
भागो जीवः स विज्ञेय इति चाहापरा श्रुतिः॥
units.translation: And another scripture text says, “The individual (jīva, ātman) is to be known as (the size of) a fraction (bhāga) of a hundredth part of the tip of a hair (bāla = vāla) divided a hundred (more) times” ( (Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad)).

gloss.en: of a hundredth part of a hair-tip

units.iast:
bālāgra-śata-bhāgasya śatadhā kalpitasya ca|
bhāgo jīvaḥ sa vijñeya iti cāhāparā śrutiḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 82
units.deva:
दिगम्बरा मध्यमत्वम् आहुर् आ-पाद-मस्तकम्।
चैतन्य-व्याप्ति-संदृष्टेर् आ-नखाग्र-श्रुतेर् अपि॥
units.translation: The Dig-ambaras say it is a medium size from the foot to the head, because it is clearly seen to be pervaded by consciousness, and also the because of the scripture, “Up to the tips of the nails” ( (Bṛhad-Āraṇyaka Upaniṣad)).

gloss.en: because of the clear sight of consciousness pervading
because of the scripture up to the nail-tips

units.iast:
digambarā madhyamatvam āhur ā-pāda-mastakam|
caitanya-vyāpti-saṃdṛṣṭer ā-nakhāgra-śruter api||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 83
units.deva:
सूक्ष्म-नाडी-प्रचारस् तु सूक्ष्माद् अवयवैर् भवेत्।
स्थूल-देहस्य हस्ताभ्यां कञ्चुक-प्रतिमोकवत्॥
units.translation: Also, it abides within the subtle nāḍīs since it is subtle, and exists within each of the limbs (avayavas), like the hands of a large person can slip into (the sleeves of) a coat.

gloss.en: because of movement in subtle channels

units.iast:
sūkṣma-nāḍī-pracāras tu sūkṣmād avayavair bhavet|
sthūla-dehasya hastābhyāṃ kañcuka-pratimokavat||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 84
units.deva:
न्यूनाधिक-शरीरेषु प्रवेशोऽपि गमागमैः।
आत्मांशानां भवेत् तेन मध्यमत्वं विनिश्चितम्॥
units.translation: Even though determined to be medium sized (madhyamatva), it enters into small and large bodies through this coming and going, and accommodates itself to the parts of each of the bodies.

gloss.en: of the parts of the Self

units.iast:
nyūnādhika-śarīreṣu praveśo’pi gamāgamaiḥ|
ātmāṃśānāṃ bhavet tena madhyamatvaṃ viniścitam||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 85
units.deva:
सांशस्य घटवन् नाशो भवत्येव तथा सति।
कृत-नाशाऽकृताभ्यागमयोः को वारको भवेत्॥
units.translation: For what has parts, like a (constructed) pot, there would be a destruction (a deconstruction). So it is in this case (when the body, like the pot, is destroyed, the ātman likewise comes and goes) there would be the defect of the loss of what was earned (kṛta, the loss of the individual’s accumulated karma) and thus the arrival of what was not earned (i.e., the accumulated karma being lost, then one’s birth could not be the result of one’s prior accumulated karma).* *(Amusingly, this is an obvious defect here to these thinkers, but is the common belief in the West, where there seemingly is a low sense of universal justice. In which case, God or pure chance is to be cursed for why one is born in one’s situation.)

gloss.en: of loss of what was done and arrival of what was not done

units.iast:
sāṃśasya ghaṭavan nāśo bhavatyeva tathā sati|
kṛta-nāśā’kṛtābhyāgamayoḥ ko vārako bhavet||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 86
units.deva:
तस्माद् आत्मा महान् एव नैवाणुर् नापि मध्यमः।
आकाशवत् सर्व-गतो निरंशः श्रुति-संमतः॥
units.translation: Therefore, the ātman (the self) is neither large, small, nor medium. It is all pervasive, like space, and hence without parts (nir-aṃśa, shapeless). This is the well-discerned position of the scriptures.
units.iast:
tasmād ātmā mahān eva naivāṇur nāpi madhyamaḥ|
ākāśavat sarva-gato niraṃśaḥ śruti-saṃmataḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 87
units.deva:
इत्युक्त्वा तद्-विशेषे तु बहुधा कलहं ययुः।
अचिद्-रूपोऽथ चिद्-रूपश् चिद्-अचिद्-रूप इत्यपि॥
units.translation: Thus has been told the various ways they have come to quarrel (as to the location or size of the self). Now, as to whether it (ātman) is unconscious (a-cit) or conscious (cit), or even a compound of both.
units.iast:
ityuktvā tad-viśeṣe tu bahudhā kalahaṃ yayuḥ|
acid-rūpo’tha cid-rūpaś cid-acid-rūpa ityapi||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 88
units.deva:
प्राभाकरास् तार्किकाश् च प्राहुर् अस्याचिद्-आत्मताम्।
आकाशवद् द्रव्यम् आत्मा शब्दवत् तद्-गुणश् चितिः॥
units.translation: The followers of Prabhākara (himself a Mīmāṃsaka, Veda textual scholar) and the Logicians (Tārkikas) say that it (ātman) is by nature unconscious. Ātman is a substance (dravya) and (is pervasive) like space, and consciousness is its quality (guṇa), like sound (is considered a quality of space).
units.iast:
prābhākarās tārkikāś ca prāhur asyācid-ātmatām|
ākāśavad dravyam ātmā śabdavat tad-guṇaś citiḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 89
units.deva:
इच्छा-द्वेष-प्रयत्नाश् च धर्माधर्मौ सुखासुखे।
तत्-संस्काराश् च तस्यैते गुणाश् चितिवद् ईरिताः॥
units.translation: They proclaim that, similar to having consciousness, it has other qualities, such as desire, aversion effort, virtue, vice, pleasure, pain, and other saṃskāras (latent tendencies) that belong to it.
units.iast:
icchā-dveṣa-prayatnāś ca dharmādharmau sukhāsukhe|
tat-saṃskārāś ca tasyaite guṇāś citivad īritāḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 90
units.deva:
आत्मनो मनसा योगे स्वादृष्ट-वशतो गुणाः।
जायन्तेऽथ प्रलीयन्ते सुषुप्तेऽदृष्ट-संक्षयात्॥
units.translation: When such an ātman (with its consciousness, desire, etc.) joins with a mind (manas), in accordance with its past karma (a-dṛṣṭa, from prior lives) those qualities are (accordingly) manifest. Then, due the depletion (of that day’s worth) of past karma (a-dṛṣṭa), then these (qualities) become unmanifest (pralīyante) during deep sleep state (suṣupta).* *(Our author here describes a daily level concern for a Pūrva-Mīmāṃsaka follower knowledgeable in jyotiṣa, astrology.)

gloss.en: in deep sleep from the exhaustion of unseen karma

units.iast:
ātmano manasā yoge svādṛṣṭa-vaśato guṇāḥ|
jāyante’tha pralīyante suṣupte’dṛṣṭa-saṃkṣayāt||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 91
units.deva:
चितिमत्वाच् चेतनोऽयम् इच्छा-द्वेष-प्रयत्नवान्।
स्याद् धर्माधर्मयोः कर्ता भोक्ता दुःखादिमत्त्वतः॥
units.translation: This (ātman) is conscious (cetana) because it possesses the quality of consciousness (citi), and (thus) has desire, aversion, effort (etcetera). It would then be the doer (kartṛ) of supportive and unsupportive acts (dharma-adharma, supportive of getting more pleasant births in heaven and in rebirths here), and would be the experiencer (bhoktṛ), because of thus gaining the sorrows, etc. (reactions of the mind to the results of one’s actions).

gloss.en: because it has sorrow and so on

units.iast:
citimatvāc cetano’yam icchā-dveṣa-prayatnavān|
syād dharmādharmayoḥ kartā bhoktā duḥkhādimattvataḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 92
units.deva:
यथाऽत्र कर्म-वशतः कादाचित् कं सुखादिकम्।
तथा लोकान्तरे देहे कर्मणेच्छादि जन्यते॥
units.translation: Just as in this life, in accordance with one’s (past) karma, sometimes there is some joy, etc., so too upon gaining a body in another world, (in accordance with one’s karma) there arises desires, etc. (to keep getting more of those moments of joy).

gloss.en: by karma, desire and so on

units.iast:
yathā’tra karma-vaśataḥ kādācit kaṃ sukhādikam|
tathā lokāntare dehe karmaṇecchādi janyate||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 93
units.deva:
एवं च सर्वगस्यापि संभवेतां गमागमौ।
कर्म-काण्डः समग्रोऽत्र प्रमाणम् इति ते ब्रुवन्॥
units.translation: In this way, a coming and going would be possible (for ātman) despite (contradictorily) it being all pervasive (sarva-ga, like space). These (Pūrva-Mīmāṃsakas) claim here that the entirely of the karma-kāṇḍa (the Veda dealing specifically with ritual life and rites, which they take to be the purport of the entire Veda, including its Upaniṣads) is the means of knowledge (pramāṇa) here (regarding ātman).* *(Whereas Vedāntins, called Uttara-Mīmāṃsakas, limit the pramāṇa regarding ātman to just the latter part of the Veda consisting of the Upaniṣads, alone having this unique topic of the ultimate nature of ātman.)

gloss.en: the ritual portion of the Veda

units.iast:
evaṃ ca sarvagasyāpi saṃbhavetāṃ gamāgamau|
karma-kāṇḍaḥ samagro’tra pramāṇam iti te bruvan||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 94
units.deva:
आनन्दमय-कोशो यः सुषुप्तौ परिशिष्यते।
अस्पष्ट-चित् स आत्मैषां पूर्व-कोशोऽस्य ते गुणाः॥
units.translation: What remains even into deep sleep and is called the ānanda-maya kośa (conscious of joy) yet (at that time) is not conscious of anything else (a-spaṣṭa-cit) is for them (the Prābhākara school of Mīmāṃsakas) the very ātman. And it is one’s original condition (pūrva-kośa, the causal body) for manifesting (upon awaking and upon a rebirth) the other qualities (guṇas, retained in unmanifest form, ).
units.iast:
ānandamaya-kośo yaḥ suṣuptau pariśiṣyate|
aspaṣṭa-cit sa ātmaiṣāṃ pūrva-kośo’sya te guṇāḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 95
units.deva:
गूढं चैतन्यम् उत्प्रेक्ष्य जड-बोध-स्वरूपताम्।
आत्मनो ब्रुवते भाट्टाश् चिद्-उत्प्रेक्षोत्थित-स्मृतेः॥
units.translation: The Bhāṭṭas (followers of Kumārila-Bhaṭṭa, another Mīmāṃsaka), accepting that consciousness, caitanya, can be hidden, say the ātman has the nature of being both unconscious and conscious (jaḍa-bodha), because of one’s memory later upon waking (that at the previous time I was aware of being unconscious) one must accept that consciousness (as being unconscious too at that time).

gloss.en: because of the memory arising from imagining consciousness

units.iast:
gūḍhaṃ caitanyam utprekṣya jaḍa-bodha-svarūpatām|
ātmano bruvate bhāṭṭāś cid-utprekṣotthita-smṛteḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 96
units.deva:
जडो भूत्व तदाऽस्वाप्सम् इति जाड्य-स्मृतिस् तदा।
विना जाड्यानुभूतिं न कथञ्चिद् उपपद्यते॥
units.translation: “I became unconscious and then slept,” is our remembrance of being jaḍa at that time. Yet without something to experience this unconscious state, how could there be such (a memory, hence one must be able to be conscious and unconscious at the same time).
units.iast:
jaḍo bhūtva tadā’svāpsam iti jāḍya-smṛtis tadā|
vinā jāḍyānubhūtiṃ na kathañcid upapadyate||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 97
units.deva:
द्रष्टुर् दृष्टेर् अलोपश् च श्रुतः सुप्तौ ततस् स्वयम्।
अप्रकाश-प्रकाशाभ्याम् आत्मा खद्योतवद् युतः॥
units.translation: In sleep “for the seer (draṣṭṛ) there is no cessation of seeing,” says the scripture ( (Bṛhad-Āraṇyaka Upaniṣad)). Thus ātman oneself has both a dark and light nature, like a fire-fly.
units.iast:
draṣṭur dṛṣṭer alopaś ca śrutaḥ suptau tatas svayam|
aprakāśa-prakāśābhyām ātmā khadyotavad yutaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 98
units.deva:
निरंशस्योभयात्मत्वं न कथञ्चिद् घटिष्यते।
तेन चिद्-रूप एवात्मेत्याहुः साङ्ख्य-विवेकिनः॥
units.translation: The Sāṅkhyas who discern (a distinction between the conscious puruṣa and unconscious prakṛti) say that the part-less (nir-aṃśa, i.e., the ātman) cannot in any way have a dual nature (ubhaya-ātmatva), and by that the ātman can only be in the form of consciousness (cit-rūpa).

gloss.en: the state of having two natures for the partless

units.iast:
niraṃśasyobhayātmatvaṃ na kathañcid ghaṭiṣyate|
tena cid-rūpa evātmetyāhuḥ sāṅkhya-vivekinaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 99
units.deva:
जाड्यांशः प्रकृते रूपं विकारिस् त्रि-गुणं च तत्।
चितो भोगापवर्गार्थं प्रकृतिः सा प्रवर्तते॥
units.translation: Prakṛti has a form consisting of parts that are unconscious (jāḍya-aṃśa), and that form has modifications, which consists of (variations of) the three guṇas. This prakṛti exists for the sake of the conscious being’s experiences and release (apavarga, from the cycle of experiences).
units.iast:
jāḍyāṃśaḥ prakṛte rūpaṃ vikāris tri-guṇaṃ ca tat|
cito bhogāpavargārthaṃ prakṛtiḥ sā pravartate||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 100
units.deva:
असंगायाश् चितेर् बन्ध-मोक्षौ भेदाग्रहान् मतौ।
बन्ध-मुक्ति-व्यवस्थार्थं पूर्वेषाम् इव चिद्-भिदा॥
units.translation: The consciousness (citi, puruṣa) which by nature cannot interact (a-saṅga) is considered bound and then freed because of not grasping the difference (between that prakṛti and oneself, the puruṣa). Like for the preceding (philosophers), in order for there to be different states of being bound and freed, (there must be multiple puruṣas due to) a difference between these conscious beings.
units.iast:
asaṃgāyāś citer bandha-mokṣau bhedāgrahān matau|
bandha-mukti-vyavasthārthaṃ pūrveṣām iva cid-bhidā||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 101
units.deva:
महतः परम् अव्यक्तम् इति प्रकृतिर् उच्यते।
श्रुतावसङ्गता तद्वद् असङ्गो हीत्यतिस्फुटा॥
units.translation: Scripture says, “Beyond the great [principle] is the unmanifest”; thus [it] is called Prakṛti. Likewise, scripture makes non-attachment very clear with the words, “unattached indeed.”
units.iast:
mahataḥ param avyaktam iti prakṛtir ucyate|
śrutāvasaṅgatā tadvad asaṅgo hītyatisphuṭā||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 102
units.deva:
चित्-सन्निधौ प्रवृत्तायाः प्रकृतेर् हि नियामकम्।
ईश्वरं ब्रुवते योगाः स जीवेभ्यः परः श्रुतः॥
units.translation: The Yogins call Īśvara the controller of Prakṛti when it acts in the presence of consciousness; scripture says that He is beyond the jīvas.

gloss.en: is heard / is stated in scripture

units.iast:
cit-sannidhau pravṛttāyāḥ prakṛter hi niyāmakam|
īśvaraṃ bruvate yogāḥ sa jīvebhyaḥ paraḥ śrutaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 103
units.deva:
प्रधान-क्षेत्रज्ञ-पतिर् गुणेश इति हि श्रुतिः।
आरण्यकेऽसंभ्रमेण ह्यन्तर्-याम्युपपादितः॥
units.translation: Scripture indeed says, “[He is] lord of Pradhāna and the knower of the field, lord of the guṇas.” In the Āraṇyaka, the Inner Ruler is clearly established.
units.iast:
pradhāna-kṣetrajña-patir guṇeśa iti hi śrutiḥ|
āraṇyake’saṃbhrameṇa hyantar-yāmyupapāditaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 104
units.deva:
अत्रापि कलहायन्ते वादिनः स्वस्व-युक्तिभिः।
वाक्यान्यपि यथा-प्रज्ञं दार्ढ्यायोदाहरन्ति हि॥
units.translation: Here too the debaters argue with their respective reasoning. They also cite scriptural passages, according to their understanding, to strengthen their views.
units.iast:
atrāpi kalahāyante vādinaḥ svasva-yuktibhiḥ|
vākyānyapi yathā-prajñaṃ dārḍhyāyodāharanti hi||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 105
units.deva:
क्लेश-कर्म-विपाकैस् तद् आशयैर् अप्यसंयुतः।
पुं-विशेषो भवेद् ईशो जीववत् सोऽप्यसङ्ग-चित्॥
units.translation: Īśvara is a special Puruṣa, unconnected with afflictions, actions, their results, and their latent traces. He too, like a jīva, is unattached consciousness.
units.iast:
kleśa-karma-vipākais tad āśayair apyasaṃyutaḥ|
puṃ-viśeṣo bhaved īśo jīvavat so’pyasaṅga-cit||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 106
units.deva:
तथापि पुं-विशेषत्वाद् घटतेऽस्य नियन्तृता।
अव्यवस्थौ बन्ध-मोक्षावापतेतामिहान्यथा॥
units.translation: Even so, because He is a special Puruṣa, His role as controller is fitting. Otherwise, bondage and liberation would fall into disorder here.

gloss.en: because of being a special Puruṣa

units.iast:
tathāpi puṃ-viśeṣatvād ghaṭate’sya niyantṛtā|
avyavasthau bandha-mokṣāvāpatetāmihānyathā||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 107
units.deva:
भीषाऽस्माद् इत्येवम् आदाव् असङ्गस्य परात्मनः।
श्रुतं तद्-युक्तम् अप्यस्य क्लेश-कर्माद्यसङ्गमात्॥
units.translation: Scripture says, “Out of fear of Him,” and so on, of the unattached Supreme Self. That too is fitting, since He is unconnected with afflictions, actions, and the like.

gloss.en: is heard / is stated in scripture
because of non-connection with afflictions, actions, and the like

units.iast:
bhīṣā’smād ityevam ādāv asaṅgasya parātmanaḥ|
śrutaṃ tad-yuktam apyasya kleśa-karmādyasaṅgamāt||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 108
units.deva:
जीवानाम् अप्यसङ्गत्वात् क्लेशादिर् न ह्यथापि च।
विवेकाग्रहतः क्लेश-कर्मादि प्राग् उदीरितम्॥
units.translation: Jīvas too are unattached, so afflictions and the like do not truly belong to them. Yet because discrimination is not grasped, afflictions, action, and the rest were described earlier [as appearing to belong to them].
units.iast:
jīvānām apyasaṅgatvāt kleśādir na hyathāpi ca|
vivekāgrahataḥ kleśa-karmādi prāg udīritam||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 109
units.deva:
नित्य-ज्ञान-प्रयत्नेच्छा-गुणान् ईशस्य मन्वते।
असङ्गस्य नियन्तृत्वम् अयुक्तम् इति तार्किकाः॥
units.translation: The logicians think that Īśvara has the qualities of eternal knowledge, effort, and desire; they say that being a controller is unfitting for one who is unattached.
units.iast:
nitya-jñāna-prayatnecchā-guṇān īśasya manvate|
asaṅgasya niyantṛtvam ayuktam iti tārkikāḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 110
units.deva:
पुं-विशेषत्वम् अप्यस्य गुणैर् एव न चान्यथा।
सत्य-कामः सत्य-सङ्कल्प इत्यादि-श्रुतिर् जगौ॥
units.translation: His status as a special Puruṣa is due to those qualities alone, and not otherwise. Scripture declares, “true in desire, true in resolve,” and the like.

gloss.en: the status of a special Puruṣa

units.iast:
puṃ-viśeṣatvam apyasya guṇair eva na cānyathā|
satya-kāmaḥ satya-saṅkalpa ityādi-śrutir jagau||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 111
units.deva:
नित्य-ज्ञानादिमत्त्वेऽस्य सृष्टिर् एव सदा भवेत्।
हिरण्य-गर्भ ईशोऽतो लिङ्ग-देहेन संयुतः॥
units.translation: If He has eternal knowledge and the like, creation would continue forever. Īśvara would therefore be Hiraṇyagarbha, endowed with a subtle body.

gloss.en: when possessing eternal knowledge and the like

units.iast:
nitya-jñānādimattve’sya sṛṣṭir eva sadā bhavet|
hiraṇya-garbha īśo’to liṅga-dehena saṃyutaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 112
units.deva:
उद्गीथ-ब्राह्मणे तस्य माहात्म्यम् अतिविस्तृतम्।
लिङ्ग-सत्त्वेऽपि जीवत्वं नास्य कर्माद्यभावतः॥
units.translation: His greatness is described at great length in the Udgītha Brāhmaṇa. Although a subtle body is present, He is not a jīva, because He has no karma and the like.

gloss.en: when a subtle body is present
because karma and the like are absent

units.iast:
udgītha-brāhmaṇe tasya māhātmyam ativistṛtam|
liṅga-sattve’pi jīvatvaṃ nāsya karmādyabhāvataḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 113
units.deva:
स्थूल-देहं विना लिङ्ग-देहो न क्वापि दृश्यते।
वैराजो देह ईशोऽतः सर्वतो मस्तकादिमान्॥
units.translation: A subtle body is nowhere seen without a gross body. Therefore [they say], the Virāj body is Īśvara, having a head and the rest everywhere.

gloss.en: having a head and the rest

units.iast:
sthūla-dehaṃ vinā liṅga-deho na kvāpi dṛśyate|
vairājo deha īśo’taḥ sarvato mastakādimān||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 114
units.deva:
सहस्र-शीर्षेत्येवं च विश्वतश् चक्षुर् इत्यपि।
श्रुतिम् इत्याहुर् अनिशं विश्व-रूपस्य चिन्तकाः॥
units.translation: Those who contemplate the cosmic form continually cite the scriptural expressions “thousand-headed” and “with eyes everywhere.”
units.iast:
sahasra-śīrṣetyevaṃ ca viśvataś cakṣur ityapi|
śrutim ityāhur aniśaṃ viśva-rūpasya cintakāḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 115
units.deva:
सर्वतः पाणि-पादत्वे कृम्यादेर् अपीशता।
ततश् चतुर्-मुखो देव एवेशो नेतरः पुमान्॥
units.translation: If [He] has hands and feet everywhere, even a worm and the like would have lordship. Therefore the four-faced deity alone is Īśvara, and no other person.

gloss.en: in the condition of having hands and feet
even a worm and the like

units.iast:
sarvataḥ pāṇi-pādatve kṛmyāder apīśatā|
tataś catur-mukho deva eveśo netaraḥ pumān||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 116
units.deva:
पुत्रार्थं तम् उपासीना एवम् आहुः प्रजा-पतिः।
प्रजा असृजतेत्यादि श्रुतिं चोदाहरन्त्यमी॥
units.translation: Those who worship Him for the sake of a son say, “[He is] Prajāpati,” and cite scriptural statements such as, “Prajāpati created the creatures.”

gloss.en: for the sake of a son

units.iast:
putrārthaṃ tam upāsīnā evam āhuḥ prajā-patiḥ|
prajā asṛjatetyādi śrutiṃ codāharantyamī||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 117
units.deva:
विष्णोर् नाभेः समुद्भूतः वेधाः कमल-जस् ततः।
विष्णुर् एवेश इत्याहुर् लोके भागवता जनाः॥
units.translation: Brahmā, the lotus-born, arose from Viṣṇu’s navel; therefore the Bhagavata devotees in the world say, “Viṣṇu alone is the Lord.”
units.iast:
viṣṇor nābheḥ samudbhūtaḥ vedhāḥ kamala-jas tataḥ|
viṣṇur eveśa ityāhur loke bhāgavatā janāḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 118
units.deva:
शिवस्य पादौ अन्वेष्टुम् शार्ङ्गी अशक्तः ततः शिवः।
ईशो न विष्णुर् इत्याहुः शैवा आगम-मानिनः॥
units.translation: Because Śārṅgin [Viṣṇu] could not find Śiva’s feet, the Śaivas who accept the Āgamas say, “Śiva is the Lord, not Viṣṇu.”

gloss.en: Śārṅgin (Viṣṇu, bearer of the Śārṅga bow)

units.iast:
śivasya pādau anveṣṭum śārṅgī aśaktaḥ tataḥ śivaḥ|
īśo na viṣṇur ityāhuḥ śaivā āgama-māninaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 119
units.deva:
पुर-त्रयं साधयितुं विघ्नेशं सोऽप्यपूजयत्।
विनायकं प्राहुर् ईशम् गाण-पत्यमते रताः॥
units.translation: He too worshipped Vighneśa to bring down the three cities. Those devoted to the Gaṇapatya view say that Vināyaka is the Lord.
units.iast:
pura-trayaṃ sādhayituṃ vighneśaṃ so’pyapūjayat|
vināyakaṃ prāhur īśam gāṇa-patyamate ratāḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 120
units.deva:
एवम् अन्ये स्वस्व-पक्षाभिमानेनान्यथाऽन्यथा।
मन्त्रार्थ-वाद-कल्पादीन् आश्रित्य प्रतिपेदिरे॥
units.translation: Likewise, others, proud of their respective positions, maintain different views, relying on mantras, explanatory passages, ritual traditions, and the like.

gloss.en: through pride in their respective positions

units.iast:
evam anye svasva-pakṣābhimānenānyathā’nyathā|
mantrārtha-vāda-kalpādīn āśritya pratipedire||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 121
units.deva:
अन्तर्-यामिणम् आरभ्य स्थावरान्तेश-वादिनः।
सन्त्य् अश्वत्थार्क-वंशादेः कुल-दैवत-दर्शनात्॥
units.translation: There are those who speak of Īśvara from the Inner Ruler all the way to immovable things; they do so because the aśvattha, arka, bamboo, and the like are regarded as family deities.

gloss.en: those who hold Īśvara to extend to immovable things

units.iast:
antar-yāmiṇam ārabhya sthāvarānteśa-vādinaḥ|
santy aśvatthārka-vaṃśādeḥ kula-daivata-darśanāt||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 122
units.deva:
तत्त्व-निश्चय-कामेन न्यायागम-विचारिणाम्।
एकैव प्रतिपत्तिः स्यात् साऽप्यत्र स्फुटम् उच्यते॥
units.translation: For those who seek certainty about reality and examine reasoning and scripture, there should be one conclusion; that conclusion is clearly stated here.

gloss.en: by one who desires certainty about reality
for those who examine reasoning and scripture

units.iast:
tattva-niścaya-kāmena nyāyāgama-vicāriṇām|
ekaiva pratipattiḥ syāt sā’pyatra sphuṭam ucyate||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 123
units.deva:
मायां तु प्रकृतिं विद्यान् मायिनं तु महेश्वरम्।
अस्यावयव-भूतैस् तु व्याप्तं सर्वम् इदं जगत्॥
units.translation: Know Māyā as Prakṛti, and the wielder of Māyā as the Great Lord. The whole universe is pervaded by beings that are His parts.

gloss.en: by those that have become His parts

units.iast:
māyāṃ tu prakṛtiṃ vidyān māyinaṃ tu maheśvaram|
asyāvayava-bhūtais tu vyāptaṃ sarvam idaṃ jagat||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 124
units.deva:
इति श्रुत्यनुसारेण न्याय्यो निर्णय ईश्वरे।
तथा सत्य-विरोधः स्यात् स्थावरान्तेश-वादिनाम्॥
units.translation: This is the reasonable conclusion about Īśvara in accordance with scripture. If so, it does not conflict with those who hold Īśvara to extend to immovable things.

gloss.en: for those who hold Īśvara to extend to immovable things

units.iast:
iti śrutyanusāreṇa nyāyyo nirṇaya īśvare|
tathā satya-virodhaḥ syāt sthāvarānteśa-vādinām||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 125
units.deva:
माया चेयं तमो-रूपा तापनीये तद्-ईरणात्।
अनुभूतिं तत्र मानं प्रतिजज्ञे श्रुतिः स्वयम्॥
units.translation: The Tapanīya [Upaniṣad] says that this Māyā is of the nature of darkness. Scripture itself declares experience to be evidence for it.
units.iast:
māyā ceyaṃ tamo-rūpā tāpanīye tad-īraṇāt|
anubhūtiṃ tatra mānaṃ pratijajñe śrutiḥ svayam||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 126
units.deva:
जडं मोहात्मकं तच् चेत्यनुभावयति श्रुतिः।
आ-बाल-गोपं स्पष्टत्वाद् आनन्त्यं तस्य साऽब्रवीत्॥
units.translation: Scripture makes us recognize Māyā as inert and delusive. Because its extent is plainly evident even to children and cowherds, scripture declares it boundless.

gloss.en: makes known / causes to be experienced

units.iast:
jaḍaṃ mohātmakaṃ tac cetyanubhāvayati śrutiḥ|
ā-bāla-gopaṃ spaṣṭatvād ānantyaṃ tasya sā’bravīt||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 127
units.deva:
अचिद्-आत्म-घटादीनां यत् स्वरूपं जडं हि तत्।
यत्र कुण्ठी-भवेद् बुद्धिः स मोह इति लौकिकाः॥
units.translation: The nature of pots and the like, which are insentient, is indeed inert. Where the intellect becomes dull, ordinary people call that delusion.

gloss.en: of pots and the like, which are insentient

units.iast:
acid-ātma-ghaṭādīnāṃ yat svarūpaṃ jaḍaṃ hi tat|
yatra kuṇṭhī-bhaved buddhiḥ sa moha iti laukikāḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 128
units.deva:
इत्थं लौकिक-दृष्ट्यैतत् सर्वैर् अप्यनुभूयते।
युक्ति-दृष्ट्या त्वनिर्वाच्यं नासद् आसीद् इति श्रुतेः॥
units.translation: Everyone experiences this in ordinary perception. From the standpoint of reasoning, however, it is indefinable, as scripture says, “It was not non-being.”
units.iast:
itthaṃ laukika-dṛṣṭyaitat sarvair apyanubhūyate|
yukti-dṛṣṭyā tvanirvācyaṃ nāsad āsīd iti śruteḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 129
units.deva:
नासद् आसीद् विभातत्वान् नो सदासीच् च बाधनात्।
विद्या-दृष्ट्या श्रुतं तुच्छं तस्य नित्य-निर्वृत्तितः॥
units.translation: It was not non-existent, because it appears; nor was it existent, because it is sublated. From the standpoint of knowledge, scripture calls it insubstantial, since it is permanently negated.
units.iast:
nāsad āsīd vibhātatvān no sadāsīc ca bādhanāt|
vidyā-dṛṣṭyā śrutaṃ tucchaṃ tasya nitya-nirvṛttitaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 130
units.deva:
तुच्छाऽनिर्वचनीया च वास्तवी चेत्यसौ त्रिधा।
ज्ञेया माया त्रिभिर् बोधैः श्रौत-यौक्तिक-लौकिकैः॥
units.translation: By three standpoints—scriptural, reasoned, and ordinary—Māyā is to be understood in three ways: as insubstantial, indefinable, and real.
units.iast:
tucchā’nirvacanīyā ca vāstavī cetyasau tridhā|
jñeyā māyā tribhir bodhaiḥ śrauta-yauktika-laukikaiḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 131
units.deva:
अस्य सत्त्वम् असत्त्वं च जगतो दर्शयत्यसौ।
प्रसारणाच् च सङ्कोचाद् यथा चित्र-पटस् तथा॥
units.translation: Māyā shows the world as present and absent, like a painted cloth when it is spread out and drawn together.
units.iast:
asya sattvam asattvaṃ ca jagato darśayatyasau|
prasāraṇāc ca saṅkocād yathā citra-paṭas tathā||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 132
units.deva:
अस्वतन्त्रा हि माया स्याद् अप्रतीतेर् विना चितिम्।
स्वतन्त्राऽपि तथैव स्याद् असङ्गस्यान्यथा-कृतेः॥
units.translation: Māyā would be dependent, since it is not perceived without consciousness. Yet it would also be independent, since it makes the unattached [Self] appear otherwise.
units.iast:
asvatantrā hi māyā syād apratīter vinā citim|
svatantrā’pi tathaiva syād asaṅgasyānyathā-kṛteḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 133
units.deva:
कूटस्थासङ्गम् आत्मानं जगत्त्वेन करोति सा।
चिद्-आभास-स्वरूपेण जीवेशावपि निर्ममे॥
units.translation: Māyā makes the immutable, unattached Self into the world. In the form of reflected consciousness, she also creates the jīva and Īśvara.

gloss.en: in the form of reflected consciousness

units.iast:
kūṭasthāsaṅgam ātmānaṃ jagattvena karoti sā|
cid-ābhāsa-svarūpeṇa jīveśāvapi nirmame||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 134
units.deva:
