कूटस्थम् अनुपद्रुत्य करोति जगदादिकम्।
दुर्घटैक-विधायिन्यां मायायां का चमत्-कृतिः॥
units.translation: Without disturbing the immutable [Self], Māyā makes the world and the rest. What wonder is there in Māyā, which uniquely brings about the impossible?

gloss.en: in the one uniquely bringing about the impossible

units.iast:
kūṭastham anupadrutya karoti jagadādikam|
durghaṭaika-vidhāyinyāṃ māyāyāṃ kā camat-kṛtiḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 135
units.deva:
द्रवत्वम् उदके वह्नाव् औष्ण्यं काठिन्यम् अश्मनि।
मायाया दुर्घटत्वं च स्वतः सिद्ध्यति नान्यतः॥
units.translation: Fluidity is in water, heat in fire, and hardness in stone; likewise, Māyā’s capacity to bring about the impossible is established by itself, not by anything else.

gloss.en: the capacity to bring about the impossible

units.iast:
dravatvam udake vahnāv auṣṇyaṃ kāṭhinyam aśmani|
māyāyā durghaṭatvaṃ ca svataḥ siddhyati nānyataḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 136
units.deva:
न वेत्ति लोको यावत् ताम् साक्षात् तावच् चमत्-कृतिम्।
धत्ते मनसि पश्चात् तु मायैषेत्युपशाम्यति॥
units.translation: As long as a person does not directly know Māyā, astonishment occupies the mind. But afterward, when one thinks, “This is Māyā,” it subsides.
units.iast:
na vetti loko yāvat tām sākṣāt tāvac camat-kṛtim|
dhatte manasi paścāt tu māyaiṣetyupaśāmyati||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 137
units.deva:
प्रसरन्ति हि चोद्यानि जगद्-वस्तुत्व-वादिषु।
न चोदनीयं मायायां तस्याश् चोद्यैक-रूपतः॥
units.translation: Objections multiply among those who argue that the world is real. Māyā itself need not be questioned, since its very nature is a question.

gloss.en: among those who argue that the world is real
because its very nature is a question

units.iast:
prasaranti hi codyāni jagad-vastutva-vādiṣu|
na codanīyaṃ māyāyāṃ tasyāś codyaika-rūpataḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 138
units.deva:
चोद्येऽपि यदि चोद्यं स्यात् त्वच्-चोद्ये चोद्यते मया।
परिहार्यं ततश् चोद्यं न पुनः प्रतिचोद्यताम्॥
units.translation: If a question itself can be questioned, I question your question. Therefore, the question should be set aside and not raised again.

gloss.en: let it be questioned in reply

units.iast:
codye’pi yadi codyaṃ syāt tvac-codye codyate mayā|
parihāryaṃ tataś codyaṃ na punaḥ praticodyatām||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 139
units.deva:
विस्मयैक-शरीराया मायायाश् चोद्य-रूपतः।
अन्वेष्यः परिहारोऽस्या बुद्धिमद्भिः प्रयत्नतः॥
units.translation: Because Māyā is an embodiment of wonder and has the nature of a question, the wise should diligently seek a way to resolve it.
units.iast:
vismayaika-śarīrāyā māyāyāś codya-rūpataḥ|
anveṣyaḥ parihāro’syā buddhimadbhiḥ prayatnataḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 140
units.deva:
मायात्वम् एव निश्चेयम् इति चेत् तर्हि निश्चिनु।
लोक-प्रसिद्ध-मायाया लक्षणं यत् तद् ईक्ष्यताम्॥
units.translation: If you say that Māyā’s very nature must be determined, then determine it: consider the well-known definition of Māyā.

gloss.en: of Māyā well known in the world

units.iast:
māyātvam eva niśceyam iti cet tarhi niścinu|
loka-prasiddha-māyāyā lakṣaṇaṃ yat tad īkṣyatām||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 141
units.deva:
न निरूपयितुं शक्या विस्पष्टं भासते च या।
सा मायेतीन्द्र-जालादौ लोकाः संप्रतिपेदिरे॥
units.translation: People accept as Māyā, as in magic and the like, whatever clearly appears but cannot be defined.
units.iast:
na nirūpayituṃ śakyā vispaṣṭaṃ bhāsate ca yā|
sā māyetīndra-jālādau lokāḥ saṃpratipedire||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 142
units.deva:
स्पष्टं भाति जगच् चेदम् अशक्यं तन्-निरूपणम्।
मायामयं जगत् तस्माद् ईक्षस्वापक्षपाततः॥
units.translation: This world clearly appears, but its nature cannot be determined. Therefore, look upon the world as Māyā-made, without bias.
units.iast:
spaṣṭaṃ bhāti jagac cedam aśakyaṃ tan-nirūpaṇam|
māyāmayaṃ jagat tasmād īkṣasvāpakṣapātataḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 143
units.deva:
निरूपयितुम् आरब्धे निखिलैर् अपि पण्डितैः।
अज्ञानं पुरतस् तेषां भाति कक्षासु कासुचित्॥
units.translation: When all the scholars begin to define it, ignorance appears before them at some stage.
units.iast:
nirūpayitum ārabdhe nikhilair api paṇḍitaiḥ|
ajñānaṃ puratas teṣāṃ bhāti kakṣāsu kāsucit||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 144
units.deva:
देहेन्द्रियादयो भावा वीर्येणोत्पादिताः कथम्।
कथं वा तत्र चैतन्यम् इत्युक्ते ते किम् उत्तरम्॥
units.translation: How are the body, senses, and the rest produced from seed? Or how does consciousness arise in them? When asked, what answer can they give?
units.iast:
dehendriyādayo bhāvā vīryeṇotpāditāḥ katham|
kathaṃ vā tatra caitanyam ityukte te kim uttaram||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 145
units.deva:
वीर्यस्यैष स्वभावश् चेत् कथं तद्-विदितं त्वया।
अन्वय-व्यतिरेकौ यौ भग्नौ तौ वन्ध्य-वीर्यतः॥
units.translation: If this is the seed’s nature, how do you know that? The two methods of agreement and difference fail in the case of an infertile seed.
units.iast:
vīryasyaiṣa svabhāvaś cet kathaṃ tad-viditaṃ tvayā|
anvaya-vyatirekau yau bhagnau tau vandhya-vīryataḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 146
units.deva:
न जानामि किम् अप्येतद् इत्यन्ते शरणं तव।
अत एव महान्तोऽस्य प्रवदन्तीन्द्र-जालताम्॥
units.translation: In the end, your recourse is, “I do not know any of this.” For that very reason, the wise call it a magic show.

gloss.en: the state of being a magic show

units.iast:
na jānāmi kim apyetad ityante śaraṇaṃ tava|
ata eva mahānto’sya pravadantīndra-jālatām||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 147
units.deva:
एतस्मात् किम् इवेन्द्र-जालम् अपरं यद् गर्भ-वास-स्थितम्।
रेतश् चेतति हस्त-मस्तक-पद-प्रोद्भूत-नानाङ्कुरम्।
पर्यायेण शिशुत्व-यौवन-जरा-वेषैर् अनेकैर् वृतम्।
पश्यत्यत्ति शृणोति जिघ्रति तथा गच्छत्यथागच्छति॥
units.translation: What is more magical than this: seed resting in the womb becomes conscious, sprouts hands, head, and feet, and is surrounded in turn by the many forms of childhood, youth, and old age; it sees, eats, hears, smells, goes, and comes.
units.iast:
etasmāt kim ivendra-jālam aparaṃ yad garbha-vāsa-sthitam|
retaś cetati hasta-mastaka-pada-prodbhūta-nānāṅkuram|
paryāyeṇa śiśutva-yauvana-jarā-veṣair anekair vṛtam|
paśyatyatti śṛṇoti jighrati tathā gacchatyathāgacchati||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 148
units.deva:
देहवद् वट-धानादौ सुविचार्य विलोक्यतम्।
क्व धानाः कुत्र वा वृक्षस् तस्मान् मायेति निश्चिनु॥
units.translation: As with the body, carefully examine a banyan seed and the like: where is the seed, and where is the tree? Therefore, understand this as Māyā.

gloss.en: as with the body / like a body
in a banyan seed and the like

units.iast:
dehavad vaṭa-dhānādau suvicārya vilokyatam|
kva dhānāḥ kutra vā vṛkṣas tasmān māyeti niścinu||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 149
units.deva:
निरुक्तावभिमानं ये दधते तार्किकादयः।
हर्ष-मिश्रादिभिस् ते तु खण्डनादौ सुशिक्षिताः॥
units.translation: Logicians and others who pride themselves on their explanations have, in turn, been well trained by Harṣa Miśra and others in works of refutation such as the Khaṇḍana.

gloss.en: in Khaṇḍana and the like (works of refutation)

units.iast:
niruktāvabhimānaṃ ye dadhate tārkikādayaḥ|
harṣa-miśrādibhis te tu khaṇḍanādau suśikṣitāḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 150
units.deva:
अचिन्त्याः खलु ये भावा न तांस् तर्केषु योजयेत्।
अचिन्त्य-रचना-रूपं मनसाऽपि जगत् खलु॥
units.translation: One should not subject truly inconceivable things to logical argument. The world itself is a formation inconceivable even to the mind.

gloss.en: of the nature of an inconceivable formation

units.iast:
acintyāḥ khalu ye bhāvā na tāṃs tarkeṣu yojayet|
acintya-racanā-rūpaṃ manasā’pi jagat khalu||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 151
units.deva:
अचिन्त्य-रचना-शक्ति-बीजं मायेति निश्चिनु।
माया-बीजं तद् एवैकं सुषुप्तावनुभूयते॥
units.translation: Know Māyā as the seed of the power to create the inconceivable. That very one seed of Māyā is experienced in deep sleep.
units.iast:
acintya-racanā-śakti-bījaṃ māyeti niścinu|
māyā-bījaṃ tad evaikaṃ suṣuptāvanubhūyate||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 152
units.deva:
जाग्रत्-स्वप्न-जगत् तत्र लीनं बीज इव द्रुमः।
तस्माद् अशेष-जगतो वासनास् तत्र संस्थिताः॥
units.translation: The waking and dream worlds are latent there, like a tree in its seed. Therefore, the latent impressions of the whole world remain there.
units.iast:
jāgrat-svapna-jagat tatra līnaṃ bīja iva drumaḥ|
tasmād aśeṣa-jagato vāsanās tatra saṃsthitāḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 153
units.deva:
या बुद्धि-वासनास् तासु चैतन्यं प्रतिबिम्बति।
मेघाकाशवद् अस्पष्ट-चिदाभासोऽनुमीयताम्॥
units.translation: In those latent impressions of the intellect, consciousness is reflected. Like the sky appearing faintly in a cloud, an indistinct reflection of consciousness should be inferred.

gloss.en: like the sky in a cloud

units.iast:
yā buddhi-vāsanās tāsu caitanyaṃ pratibimbati|
meghākāśavad aspaṣṭa-cidābhāso’numīyatām||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 154
units.deva:
साभासम् एव तद्-बीजं धी-रूपेण प्ररोहति।
अतो बुद्धौ चिदाभासो विस्पष्टं प्रतिभासते॥
units.translation: That seed, together with its reflection, sprouts in the form of intellect. Therefore, the reflection of consciousness appears distinctly in the intellect.
units.iast:
sābhāsam eva tad-bījaṃ dhī-rūpeṇa prarohati|
ato buddhau cidābhāso vispaṣṭaṃ pratibhāsate||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 155
units.deva:
मायाभासेन जीवेशौ करोतीति श्रुतौ श्रुतम्।
मेघाकाश-जलाकाशाविव तौ सुव्यवस्थितौ॥
units.translation: Scripture says that Māyā creates the jīva and Īśvara through her appearance. Those two are set out like space in a cloud and space in water.

gloss.en: through the appearance / reflection of Māyā

units.iast:
māyābhāsena jīveśau karotīti śrutau śrutam|
meghākāśa-jalākāśāviva tau suvyavasthitau||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 156
units.deva:
मेघवद् वर्तते माया मेघ-स्थित-तुषारवत्।
धी-वासनाश् चिदाभासस् तुषारस्थ-खवत् स्थितः॥
units.translation: Māyā operates like a cloud; the latent impressions of the intellect are like mist within a cloud, and the reflected consciousness is like the sky within that mist.

gloss.en: like mist situated in a cloud
like the sky situated in mist

units.iast:
meghavad vartate māyā megha-sthita-tuṣāravat|
dhī-vāsanāś cidābhāsas tuṣārastha-khavat sthitaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 157
units.deva:
मायाऽधीनश् चिदाभासः श्रुतौ मायी महेश्वरः।
अन्तर्-यामि च सर्वज्ञो जगद्-योनिः स एव हि॥
units.translation: The reflection of consciousness depends on Māyā; scripture says the Great Lord is the wielder of Māyā. He alone is the Inner Ruler, all-knowing, and the source of the universe.

gloss.en: the source / womb of the universe

units.iast:
māyā’dhīnaś cidābhāsaḥ śrutau māyī maheśvaraḥ|
antar-yāmi ca sarvajño jagad-yoniḥ sa eva hi||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 158
units.deva:
सौषुप्तम् आनन्दमयं प्रक्रम्यैवं श्रुतिर् जगौ।
एष सर्वेश्वर इति सोऽयं वेदोक्त ईश्वरः॥
units.translation: Having begun with “the one in deep sleep is full of bliss,” scripture says, “This is the Lord of all.” That one is the Īśvara taught in the Veda.
units.iast:
sauṣuptam ānandamayaṃ prakramyaivaṃ śrutir jagau|
eṣa sarveśvara iti so’yaṃ vedokta īśvaraḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 159
units.deva:
सर्वज्ञत्वादिके तस्य नैव विप्रतिपद्यताम्।
श्रौतार्थस्यावितर्क्यत्वान् मायायां सर्व-संभवात्॥
units.translation: One should not dispute His omniscience and the like: the meaning of scripture is beyond reasoning, and anything is possible in Māyā.
units.iast:
sarvajñatvādike tasya naiva vipratipadyatām|
śrautārthasyāvitarkyatvān māyāyāṃ sarva-saṃbhavāt||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 160
units.deva:
अयं यत् सृजते विश्वं तद् अन्यथयितुं पुमान्।
न कोऽपि शक्तस् तेनायं सर्वेश्वर इतीरितः॥
units.translation: Whatever this [Lord] creates, no person can change. Therefore, He is called the Lord of all.
units.iast:
ayaṃ yat sṛjate viśvaṃ tad anyathayituṃ pumān|
na ko’pi śaktas tenāyaṃ sarveśvara itīritaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 161
units.deva:
अशेष-प्राणि-बुद्धीनां वासनास् तत्र संस्थीताः।
ताभिः क्रोडी-कृतं सर्वं तेन सर्वज्ञ ईरितः॥
units.translation: The latent impressions in the minds of all living beings are there; through them everything is contained. Therefore He is called all-knowing.
units.iast:
aśeṣa-prāṇi-buddhīnāṃ vāsanās tatra saṃsthītāḥ|
tābhiḥ kroḍī-kṛtaṃ sarvaṃ tena sarvajña īritaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 162
units.deva:
वासनानां परोक्षत्वात् सर्वज्ञत्वं न हीक्ष्यते।
सर्व-बुद्धिषु तद् दृष्ट्वा वासनास्वनुमीयताम्॥
units.translation: Because latent impressions are not directly perceived, omniscience is not evident. Seeing Him in every intellect, one should infer His knowledge of those impressions.
units.iast:
vāsanānāṃ parokṣatvāt sarvajñatvaṃ na hīkṣyate|
sarva-buddhiṣu tad dṛṣṭvā vāsanāsvanumīyatām||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 163
units.deva:
विज्ञानमय-मुख्येषु कोशेष्वन्यत्र चैव हि।
अन्तस् तिष्ठन् यमयति तेनान्तर्-यामितां व्रजेत्॥
units.translation: Standing within the sheaths, beginning with the intellect sheath, and elsewhere too, He directs them. Therefore He is called the Inner Controller.

gloss.en: among those beginning with the intellect sheath
the state of being the Inner Controller

units.iast:
vijñānamaya-mukhyeṣu kośeṣvanyatra caiva hi|
antas tiṣṭhan yamayati tenāntar-yāmitāṃ vrajet||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 164
units.deva:
बुद्धौ तिष्ठन्नान्तरोऽस्या धियाऽनीक्ष्यश् च धी-वपुः।
धियम् अन्तर्-यमयतीत्येवं वेदेन घोषितम्॥
units.translation: Standing within the intellect, He is internal to it but cannot be known by the intellect, whose body He is. He controls the intellect from within—so the Veda declares.
units.iast:
buddhau tiṣṭhannāntaro’syā dhiyā’nīkṣyaś ca dhī-vapuḥ|
dhiyam antar-yamayatītyevaṃ vedena ghoṣitam||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 165
units.deva:
तन्तुः पटे स्थितो यद्वद् उपादानतया तथा।
सर्वोपादान-रूपत्वात् सर्वत्रायम् अवस्थितः॥
units.translation: Just as the thread is present in the cloth as its material cause, so this [Lord] is present everywhere, being the material cause of all.

gloss.en: because of being the material cause of all

units.iast:
tantuḥ paṭe sthito yadvad upādānatayā tathā|
sarvopādāna-rūpatvāt sarvatrāyam avasthitaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 166
units.deva:
पटाद् अप्यान्तरस् तन्तुः तन्तोर् अप्यंशुर् आन्तरः।
आन्तरत्वस्य विश्रान्तिर् यत्रासावनुमीयताम्॥
units.translation: Thread is more internal than cloth, and fiber is more internal than thread. One should infer where this inwardness comes to rest.
units.iast:
paṭād apyāntaras tantuḥ tantor apyaṃśur āntaraḥ|
āntaratvasya viśrāntir yatrāsāvanumīyatām||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 167
units.deva:
द्वित्रान्तरत्वकक्षाणां दर्शनेऽप्ययम् आन्तरः।
न वीक्ष्यते ततो युक्ति-श्रुतिभ्याम् एव निर्णयः॥
units.translation: Even when one examines two or three levels of what lies within, this innermost [principle] is not seen. Therefore the conclusion rests on reasoning and scripture alone.
units.iast:
dvitrāntaratvakakṣāṇāṃ darśane’pyayam āntaraḥ|
na vīkṣyate tato yukti-śrutibhyām eva nirṇayaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 168
units.deva:
पट-रूपेण संस्थानात् पटस् तन्तोर् वपुर् यथा।
सर्व-रूपेण संस्थानात् सर्वम् अस्य वपुस् तथा॥
units.translation: Just as the cloth is the body of the thread, since the thread is arranged in the form of cloth, so everything is His body, since He is arranged in every form.
units.iast:
paṭa-rūpeṇa saṃsthānāt paṭas tantor vapur yathā|
sarva-rūpeṇa saṃsthānāt sarvam asya vapus tathā||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 169
units.deva:
तन्तोः सङ्कोच-विस्तार-चलनादौ पटस् तथा।
अवश्यम् एव भवति न स्वातन्त्र्यं पटे मनाक्॥
units.translation: When the thread contracts, expands, or moves, the cloth does likewise; the cloth has no independence at all.
units.iast:
tantoḥ saṅkoca-vistāra-calanādau paṭas tathā|
avaśyam eva bhavati na svātantryaṃ paṭe manāk||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 170
units.deva:
तथाऽन्तर्-याम्ययं यत्र यया वासनया यथा।
विक्रियेत तथाऽवश्यं भवत्येव न संशयः॥
units.translation: Likewise, whatever change occurs under the Inner Controller, wherever and through whatever latent tendency, occurs necessarily in that way; there is no doubt.
units.iast:
tathā’ntar-yāmyayaṃ yatra yayā vāsanayā yathā|
vikriyeta tathā’vaśyaṃ bhavatyeva na saṃśayaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 171
units.deva:
ईश्वरः सर्व-भूतानां हृद्-देशेऽर्जुन तिष्ठति।
भ्रामयन् सर्व-भूतानि यन्त्रारूढानि मायया॥
units.translation: The Lord dwells in the heart-region of all beings, O Arjuna, causing all beings mounted on a machine to revolve by Māyā.
units.iast:
īśvaraḥ sarva-bhūtānāṃ hṛd-deśe’rjuna tiṣṭhati|
bhrāmayan sarva-bhūtāni yantrārūḍhāni māyayā||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 172
units.deva:
सर्व-भूतानि विज्ञानमयास् ते हृदये स्थिताः।
तदुपादान-भूतेशस् तत्र विक्रियते खलु॥
units.translation: “All beings” means the intellect-sheaths situated in the heart. The Lord, who is their material cause, indeed appears to undergo change there.

gloss.en: the Lord who is their material cause

units.iast:
sarva-bhūtāni vijñānamayās te hṛdaye sthitāḥ|
tadupādāna-bhūteśas tatra vikriyate khalu||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 173
units.deva:
देहादि-पञ्जरं यन्त्रं तदारोहोऽभिमानिता।
विहित-प्रतिषिद्धेषु प्रवृत्तिर् भ्रमणं भवेत्॥
units.translation: The cage of the body and so on is the machine; being mounted on it means identifying with it. Activity in prescribed and forbidden acts is what “revolving” means.

gloss.en: the cage of the body and so on

units.iast:
dehādi-pañjaraṃ yantraṃ tadāroho’bhimānitā|
vihita-pratiṣiddheṣu pravṛttir bhramaṇaṃ bhavet||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 174
units.deva:
विज्ञानमय-रूपेण तत्-प्रवृत्ति-स्वरूपतः।
स्वशक्त्येशो विक्रियते मायया भ्रामणं हि तत्॥
units.translation: The Lord, by His own power, appears to undergo change through Māyā in the form of the intellect-sheath, according to its activity. That indeed is “causing to revolve.”

gloss.en: in the form of the intellect-sheath
according to the nature of its activity

units.iast:
vijñānamaya-rūpeṇa tat-pravṛtti-svarūpataḥ|
svaśaktyeśo vikriyate māyayā bhrāmaṇaṃ hi tat||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 175
units.deva:
अन्तर्-यमयतीत्युक्त्याऽयम् एवार्थः श्रुतौ श्रुतः।
पृथिव्यादिषु सर्वत्र न्यायोऽयं योज्यतां धिया॥
units.translation: This very meaning is heard in the Śruti through the statement, “He controls from within.” Apply this reasoning thoughtfully everywhere, from the earth onward.

gloss.en: in the earth and the rest

units.iast:
antar-yamayatītyuktyā’yam evārthaḥ śrutau śrutaḥ|
pṛthivyādiṣu sarvatra nyāyo’yaṃ yojyatāṃ dhiyā||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 176
units.deva:
जानामि धर्मं न च मे प्रवृत्तिर् जानाम्यधर्मं न च मे निवृत्तिः।
केनापि देवेन हृदि स्थितेन यथा नियुक्तोऽस्मि तथा करोमि॥
units.translation: “I know what is right, yet I have no inclination to act; I know what is wrong, yet I have no inclination to refrain. As I am directed by some deity seated in my heart, so I act.”
units.iast:
jānāmi dharmaṃ na ca me pravṛttir jānāmyadharmaṃ na ca me nivṛttiḥ|
kenāpi devena hṛdi sthitena yathā niyukto’smi tathā karomi||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 177
units.deva:
नार्थः पुरुष-कारेणेत्येव मा शङ्क्यतां यतः।
ईशः पुरुष-कार-स्वरूपेणापि विवर्तते॥
units.translation: Do not think, therefore, that human effort has no effect. For the Lord also manifests in the very form of human effort.

gloss.en: in the very form of human effort

units.iast:
nārthaḥ puruṣa-kāreṇetyeva mā śaṅkyatāṃ yataḥ|
īśaḥ puruṣa-kāra-svarūpeṇāpi vivartate||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 178
units.deva:
ईदृग्-बोधेनेश्वरस्य प्रवृत्तिर् मैव वार्यताम्।
तथापीशस्य बोधेन स्वात्मासङ्गत्व-धी-जनिः॥
units.translation: Let it not be thought that this kind of understanding rules out the Lord’s activity. Even so, knowledge of the Lord gives rise to the understanding that one’s own Self is unattached.

gloss.en: let it be prevented / ruled out
arising of the understanding that one’s own Self is unattached

units.iast:
īdṛg-bodheneśvarasya pravṛttir maiva vāryatām|
tathāpīśasya bodhena svātmāsaṅgatva-dhī-janiḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 179
units.deva:
तावता मुक्तिर् इत्याहुः श्रुतयः स्मृतयस् तथा।
श्रुति-स्मृती ममैवाज्ञे इत्यपीश्वर-भाषितम्॥
units.translation: By that alone, they say, there is liberation—the Śrutis and Smṛtis say so. The Lord too has declared, “Śruti and Smṛti are indeed My commands.”
units.iast:
tāvatā muktir ityāhuḥ śrutayaḥ smṛtayas tathā|
śruti-smṛtī mamaivājñe ityapīśvara-bhāṣitam||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 180
units.deva:
आज्ञाया भीति-हेतुत्वं भीषाऽस्माद् इति हि श्रुतम्।
सर्वेश्वरत्वम् एतत् स्याद् अन्तर्-यामित्वतः पृथक्॥
units.translation: Scripture indeed says, “Out of fear of Him …” This would mean lordship over all, distinct from being the Inner Controller.
units.iast:
ājñāyā bhīti-hetutvaṃ bhīṣā’smād iti hi śrutam|
sarveśvaratvam etat syād antar-yāmitvataḥ pṛthak||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 181
units.deva:
एतस्य वा अक्षरस्य प्रशासन इति श्रुतिः।
अन्तः प्रविष्टः शास्ताऽयं जनानाम् इति च श्रुतिः॥
units.translation: The Śruti says, “By the command of this imperishable one …”; and it also says, “Having entered within, this one is the ruler of people.”
units.iast:
etasya vā akṣarasya praśāsana iti śrutiḥ|
antaḥ praviṣṭaḥ śāstā’yaṃ janānām iti ca śrutiḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 182
units.deva:
जगद्-योनिर् भवेद् एष प्रभवाप्यय-कृत्त्वतः।
आविर्-भाव-तिरो-भावाव् उत्पत्ति-प्रलयौ मतौ॥
units.translation: This is the source of the universe because it brings about its arising and dissolution. “Arising” and “dissolution” are understood as manifestation and disappearance.

gloss.en: because it brings about arising and dissolution

units.iast:
jagad-yonir bhaved eṣa prabhavāpyaya-kṛttvataḥ|
āvir-bhāva-tiro-bhāvāv utpatti-pralayau matau||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 183
units.deva:
आविर्-भावयति स्वस्मिन् विलीनं सकलं जगत्।
प्राणि-कर्म-वशाद् एष पटो यद्वत् प्रसारितः॥
units.translation: This [Lord] manifests in itself the entire universe that had been dissolved, according to the karma of living beings, just as a cloth is spread out.

gloss.en: according to the karma of living beings

units.iast:
āvir-bhāvayati svasmin vilīnaṃ sakalaṃ jagat|
prāṇi-karma-vaśād eṣa paṭo yadvat prasāritaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 184
units.deva:
पुनस् तिरो-भावयति स्वात्मन्येवाखिलं जगत्।
प्राणि-कर्म-क्षय-वशात् सङ्कोचित-पटो यथा॥
units.translation: Again, it makes the entire universe disappear into itself when the karma of living beings is exhausted, just as a cloth is rolled up.

gloss.en: because the karma of living beings is exhausted

units.iast:
punas tiro-bhāvayati svātmanyevākhilaṃ jagat|
prāṇi-karma-kṣaya-vaśāt saṅkocita-paṭo yathā||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 185
units.deva:
रात्रि-घस्रौ सुप्ति-बोधावुन्मीलन-निमीलने।
तूष्णीं-भाव-मनो-राज्ये इव सृष्टि-लयाविमौ॥
units.translation: These two, creation and dissolution, are like night and day, sleep and waking, the closing and opening of the eyes, and quietness and the mind’s imaginings.
units.iast:
rātri-ghasrau supti-bodhāvunmīlana-nimīlane|
tūṣṇīṃ-bhāva-mano-rājye iva sṛṣṭi-layāvimau||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 186
units.deva:
आविर्-भाव-तिरो-भाव-शक्तिमत्त्वेन हेतुना।
आरम्भ-परिणामादि-चोद्यानां नात्र संभवः॥
units.translation: Because it possesses the power to manifest and make disappear, there can be no objection here concerning a beginning, transformation, and so on.

gloss.en: through possessing the power to manifest and make disappear

units.iast:
āvir-bhāva-tiro-bhāva-śaktimattvena hetunā|
ārambha-pariṇāmādi-codyānāṃ nātra saṃbhavaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 187
units.deva:
अचेतनानां हेतुः स्याज् जाड्यांशेनेश्वरस् तथा।
चिदाभासांशतस् त्वेष जीवानां कारणं भवेत्॥
units.translation: The Lord is the cause of insentient things through the inert aspect; but this same [Lord] is the cause of living beings through the aspect of reflected consciousness.

gloss.en: through the aspect of reflected consciousness

units.iast:
acetanānāṃ hetuḥ syāj jāḍyāṃśeneśvaras tathā|
cidābhāsāṃśatas tveṣa jīvānāṃ kāraṇaṃ bhavet||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 188
units.deva:
तमः-प्रधानः क्षेत्राणां चित्-प्रधानश् चिदात्मनाम्।
परः कारणताम् एति भावना-ज्ञान-कर्मभिः॥
units.translation: The Supreme assumes causal status for bodies through the predominance of tamas, and for conscious selves through the predominance of consciousness, by means of impressions, knowledge, and action.
units.iast:
tamaḥ-pradhānaḥ kṣetrāṇāṃ cit-pradhānaś cidātmanām|
paraḥ kāraṇatām eti bhāvanā-jñāna-karmabhiḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 189
units.deva:
इति वार्तिक-कारेण जड-चेतन-हेतुता।
परमात्मन एवोक्ता नेश्वरस्येति चेच् छृणु॥
units.translation: Thus the Vārtika author stated that being the cause of the inert and the conscious belongs to the Supreme Self alone, not to Īśvara. If you raise that objection, listen.

gloss.en: being the cause of the inert and the conscious

units.iast:
iti vārtika-kāreṇa jaḍa-cetana-hetutā|
paramātmana evoktā neśvarasyeti cec chṛṇu||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 190
units.deva:
अन्योन्याध्यासम् अत्रापि जीव-कूटस्थयोर् इव।
ईश्वर-ब्रह्मणोः सिद्धं कृत्वा ब्रूते सुरेश्वरः॥
units.translation: Sureśvara speaks here after taking the mutual superimposition of Īśvara and Brahman as established, as in the case of the jīva and Kūṭastha.
units.iast:
anyonyādhyāsam atrāpi jīva-kūṭasthayor iva|
īśvara-brahmaṇoḥ siddhaṃ kṛtvā brūte sureśvaraḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 191
units.deva:
सत्यं ज्ञानम् अनन्तं यद् ब्रह्म तस्मात् समुत्थिताः।
खं वाय्वग्नि-जलोर्व्योषद्ध्यन्न-देहा इति श्रुतिः॥
units.translation: The Śruti says: “That which is truth, knowledge, and limitless is Brahman.” From it arose space, air, fire, water, earth, plants, food, and bodies.
units.iast:
satyaṃ jñānam anantaṃ yad brahma tasmāt samutthitāḥ|
khaṃ vāyvagni-jalorvyoṣaddhyanna-dehā iti śrutiḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 192
units.deva:
आपात-दृष्टितस् तत्र ब्रह्मणो भाति हेतुता।
हेतोश् च सत्यता तस्माद् अन्योन्याध्यास इष्यते॥
units.translation: At first glance, in that passage, Brahman appears to be a cause, and the cause appears real. Therefore, mutual superimposition is understood.
units.iast:
āpāta-dṛṣṭitas tatra brahmaṇo bhāti hetutā|
hetoś ca satyatā tasmād anyonyādhyāsa iṣyate||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 193
units.deva:
अन्योन्याध्यास-रूपोऽसावन्न-लिप्त-पटो यथा।
घट्टितेनैकताम् एति तद्वद् भ्रान्त्यैकतां गतः॥
units.translation: This mutual superimposition is like cloth treated with rice paste: by being stiffened, the two seem to become one. Likewise, through error, [Brahman and Īśvara] are taken as one.

gloss.en: having the form of mutual superimposition

units.iast:
anyonyādhyāsa-rūpo’sāvanna-lipta-paṭo yathā|
ghaṭṭitenaikatām eti tadvad bhrāntyaikatāṃ gataḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 194
units.deva:
मेघाकाश-महा-काशौ विविच्येते न पामरैः।
तद्वद् ब्रह्मेशयोर् ऐक्यं पश्यन्त्यापात-दर्शिनः॥
units.translation: Ordinary people do not distinguish the space in a cloud from the vast space. Likewise, those who see only at first glance perceive identity between Brahman and the Lord.

gloss.en: those who see at first glance

units.iast:
meghākāśa-mahā-kāśau vivicyete na pāmaraiḥ|
tadvad brahmeśayor aikyaṃ paśyantyāpāta-darśinaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 195
units.deva:
उपक्रमादिभिर् लिङ्गैस् तात्पर्यस्य विचारणात्।
असङ्गं ब्रह्म मायावी सृजत्येष महेश्वरः॥
units.translation: By examining the purport through textual indicators such as the opening, one understands: Brahman is unattached; this Great Lord, the wielder of Māyā, creates.

gloss.en: through the opening and other indicators

units.iast:
upakramādibhir liṅgais tātparyasya vicāraṇāt|
asaṅgaṃ brahma māyāvī sṛjatyeṣa maheśvaraḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 196
units.deva:
सत्यं ज्ञानम् अनन्तं चेत्युपक्रम्योपसंहृतम्।
यतो वाचो निवर्तन्त इत्यसङ्गत्व-निर्णयः॥
units.translation: Having begun with “truth, knowledge, limitless,” the passage concludes with “from which speech turns back.” Thus Brahman’s non-attachment is established.
units.iast:
satyaṃ jñānam anantaṃ cetyupakramyopasaṃhṛtam|
yato vāco nivartanta ityasaṅgatva-nirṇayaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 197
units.deva:
मायी सृजति विश्वं सन्निरुद्धस् तत्र मायया।
अन्य इत्यपरा ब्रूते श्रुतिस् तेनेश्वरः सृजेत्॥
units.translation: Another Śruti says, “The wielder of Māyā creates the universe”; the other one there is bound by Māyā. Therefore, the Lord is the creator.
units.iast:
māyī sṛjati viśvaṃ sanniruddhas tatra māyayā|
anya ityaparā brūte śrutis teneśvaraḥ sṛjet||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 198
units.deva:
आनन्दमय ईशोऽयं बहु स्याम् इत्यवैक्षत।
हिरण्य-गर्भ-रूपोऽभूत् सुप्तिः स्वप्नो यथा भवेत्॥
units.translation: This blissful Lord thought, “May I become many”; He became Hiraṇyagarbha, as deep sleep becomes a dream.
units.iast:
ānandamaya īśo’yaṃ bahu syām ityavaikṣata|
hiraṇya-garbha-rūpo’bhūt suptiḥ svapno yathā bhavet||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 199
units.deva:
क्रमेण युग-पद् वैषा सृष्टिर् ज्ञेया यथा-श्रुति।
द्वि-विध-श्रुति-सद्भावाद् द्वि-विध-स्वप्न-दर्शनात्॥
units.translation: According to the Śruti, this creation is to be understood as occurring either in sequence or all at once, since scripture speaks in two ways and two kinds of dreams are seen.

gloss.en: because two kinds of scriptural statements exist
because two kinds of dreams are seen

units.iast:
krameṇa yuga-pad vaiṣā sṛṣṭir jñeyā yathā-śruti|
dvi-vidha-śruti-sadbhāvād dvi-vidha-svapna-darśanāt||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 200
units.deva:
सूत्रात्मा सूक्ष्म-देहाख्यः सर्व-जीव-घनात्मकः।
सर्वाहंमान-धारित्वात् क्रिया-ज्ञानादि-शक्तिमान्॥
units.translation: Sūtrātman, called the subtle body, is the aggregate of all living beings. Because it bears all the “I” notions, it has the powers of action, knowledge, and so on.

gloss.en: whose nature is the aggregate of all living beings
because it bears all the “I” notions
possessing the powers of action, knowledge, and so on

units.iast:
sūtrātmā sūkṣma-dehākhyaḥ sarva-jīva-ghanātmakaḥ|
sarvāhaṃmāna-dhāritvāt kriyā-jñānādi-śaktimān||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 201
units.deva:
प्रत्यूषे वा प्रदोषे वा मग्नो मन्दे तमस्ययम्।
लोको भाति यथा तद्वद् अस्पष्टं जगद् ईक्ष्यते॥
units.translation: Just as the world appears immersed in dim darkness at dawn or dusk, so the universe is seen indistinctly.
units.iast:
pratyūṣe vā pradoṣe vā magno mande tamasyayam|
loko bhāti yathā tadvad aspaṣṭaṃ jagad īkṣyate||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 202
units.deva:
सर्वतो लाञ्छितो मष्या यथा स्याद् घट्टितः पटः।
सूक्ष्माकारैस् तथेशस्य वपुः सर्वत्र लाञ्छितः॥
units.translation: Just as a prepared cloth is marked everywhere with ink, so the Lord’s body is marked everywhere by subtle forms.
units.iast:
sarvato lāñchito maṣyā yathā syād ghaṭṭitaḥ paṭaḥ|
sūkṣmākārais tatheśasya vapuḥ sarvatra lāñchitaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 203
units.deva:
सस्यं वा शाक-जातं वा सर्वतोऽङ्कुरितं यथा।
कोमलं तद्वद् एवैष पेलवो जगद्-अङ्कुरः॥
units.translation: Just as a crop or a plant shoot sprouts everywhere, tender and delicate, so is this sprout of the universe.
units.iast:
sasyaṃ vā śāka-jātaṃ vā sarvato’ṅkuritaṃ yathā|
komalaṃ tadvad evaiṣa pelavo jagad-aṅkuraḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 204
units.deva:
आतपाभात-लोको वा पटो वा वर्ण-पूरितः।
सस्यं वा फलितं यद्वत् तथा स्पष्ट-वपुर् विराट्॥
units.translation: Just as the world shines in sunlight, a cloth is filled with color, or a crop ripens, so Virāj’s form is clear.
units.iast:
ātapābhāta-loko vā paṭo vā varṇa-pūritaḥ|
sasyaṃ vā phalitaṃ yadvat tathā spaṣṭa-vapur virāṭ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 205
units.deva:
विश्व-रूपाध्याय एष उक्तः सूक्तेऽपि पौरुषे।
धात्रादि-स्तम्ब-पर्यन्तान् एतस्यावयवान् विदुः॥
units.translation: This [Virāj] is described in the chapter on the Cosmic Form and also in the Puruṣa Sūkta. They know the parts of this [form] from the Creator down to a clump of grass.

gloss.en: in the chapter on the Cosmic Form
ending with a clump of grass

units.iast:
viśva-rūpādhyāya eṣa uktaḥ sūkte’pi pauruṣe|
dhātrādi-stamba-paryantān etasyāvayavān viduḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 206
units.deva:
ईश-सूत्र-विराड्-वेधो-विष्णु-रुद्र-इन्द्र-वह्नयः।
विघ्न-भैरव-मैराल-मारिका-यक्ष-राक्षसाः॥
units.translation: Īśa, Sūtra, Virāj, Vedhas, Viṣṇu, Rudra, Indra, and Vahni; Vighna, Bhairava, Mairāla, Mārikā, Yakṣas, and Rākṣasas.
units.iast:
īśa-sūtra-virāḍ-vedho-viṣṇu-rudra-indra-vahnayaḥ|
vighna-bhairava-mairāla-mārikā-yakṣa-rākṣasāḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 207
units.deva:
विप्र-क्षत्रिय-विट्-शूद्रा गवाश्व-मृग-पक्षिणः।
अश्वत्थ-वट-चूताद्या यव-व्रीहि-तृणादयः॥
units.translation: Brahmins, Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas, and Śūdras; cows, horses, deer, and birds; fig, banyan, and mango trees; barley, rice, grasses, and the like.
units.iast:
vipra-kṣatriya-viṭ-śūdrā gavāśva-mṛga-pakṣiṇaḥ|
aśvattha-vaṭa-cūtādyā yava-vrīhi-tṛṇādayaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 208
units.deva:
जल-पाषाण-मृत्-काष्ठ-वास्या-कुद्दालकादयः।
ईश्वराः सर्व एवैते पूजिताः फल-दायिनः॥
units.translation: Water, stone, soil, wood, adzes, spades, and the like: all these are forms of the Lord; when worshipped, they bestow results.
units.iast:
jala-pāṣāṇa-mṛt-kāṣṭha-vāsyā-kuddālakādayaḥ|
īśvarāḥ sarva evaite pūjitāḥ phala-dāyinaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 209
units.deva:
यथा यथोपासते तं फलम् ईयुस् तथा तथा।
फलोत्कर्षापकर्षौ तु पूज्य-पूजानुसारतः॥
units.translation: As they worship Him, so they attain the result; the result is higher or lower according to the worship offered to the object of worship.

gloss.en: according to the worship of the one worshipped

units.iast:
yathā yathopāsate taṃ phalam īyus tathā tathā|
phalotkarṣāpakarṣau tu pūjya-pūjānusārataḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 210
units.deva:
मुक्तिस् तु ब्रह्म-तत्त्वस्य ज्ञानाद् एव न चान्यथा।
स्वप्न-बोधं विना नैव स्व-स्वप्नो हीयते यथा॥
units.translation: Liberation comes only from knowledge of Brahman’s reality, and not otherwise—just as one’s own dream does not end without waking from it.
units.iast:
muktis tu brahma-tattvasya jñānād eva na cānyathā|
svapna-bodhaṃ vinā naiva sva-svapno hīyate yathā||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 211
units.deva:
अद्वितीय-ब्रह्म-तत्त्वे स्वप्नोऽयम् अखिलं जगत्।
ईश-जीवादि-रूपेण चेतनाचेतनात्मकम्॥
units.translation: Within the nondual reality of Brahman, this whole world is a dream, consisting of conscious and insentient things in the forms of Īśa, jīva, and so on.

gloss.en: in the nondual reality of Brahman
in the forms of Īśa, jīva, and so on
consisting of conscious and insentient things

units.iast:
advitīya-brahma-tattve svapno’yam akhilaṃ jagat|
īśa-jīvādi-rūpeṇa cetanācetanātmakam||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 212
units.deva:
आनन्दमय-विज्ञानमयाव् ईश्वर-जीवकौ।
मायया कल्पितावेतौ ताभ्यां सर्वं प्रकल्पितम्॥
units.translation: The Lord and the jīva are the bliss-sheath and the intellect-sheath; these two are projected by Māyā, and everything is projected from them.
units.iast:
ānandamaya-vijñānamayāv īśvara-jīvakau|
māyayā kalpitāvetau tābhyāṃ sarvaṃ prakalpitam||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 213
units.deva:
ईक्षणादि-प्रवेशान्ता सृष्टिर् ईशेन कल्पिता।
जाग्रदादि-विमोक्षान्तः संसारो जीव-कल्पितः॥
units.translation: Creation, from the first act of seeing through entry into all things, is projected by Īśa. Saṃsāra, from waking onward through liberation, is projected by the jīva.
units.iast:
īkṣaṇādi-praveśāntā sṛṣṭir īśena kalpitā|
jāgradādi-vimokṣāntaḥ saṃsāro jīva-kalpitaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 214
units.deva:
अद्वितीयं ब्रह्म-तत्त्वम् असङ्गं तन् न जानते।
जीवेशयोर् मायिकयोर् वृथैव कलहं ययुः॥
units.translation: They do not know the nondual reality of Brahman as unattached; they engage in a pointless quarrel about the illusory jīva and Īśvara.
units.iast:
advitīyaṃ brahma-tattvam asaṅgaṃ tan na jānate|
jīveśayor māyikayor vṛthaiva kalahaṃ yayuḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 215
units.deva:
ज्ञात्वा सदा तत्त्व-निष्ठान् अनुमोदामहे वयम्।
अनुशोचाम एवान्यान् न भ्रान्तैर् विवदामहे॥
units.translation: Having known those who are always steadfast in truth, we rejoice; we grieve for the others and do not argue with the deluded.
units.iast:
jñātvā sadā tattva-niṣṭhān anumodāmahe vayam|
anuśocāma evānyān na bhrāntair vivadāmahe||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 216
units.deva:
तृणार्चकादि-योगान्ता ईश्वरे भ्रान्तिम् आश्रिताः।
लोकायतादि-साङ्ख्यान्ता जीवे विभ्रान्तिम् आश्रिताः॥
units.translation: Those from grass-worshippers up to yogins resort to delusion about Īśvara; those from materialists to Sāṅkhyas resort to confusion about the jīva.
units.iast:
tṛṇārcakādi-yogāntā īśvare bhrāntim āśritāḥ|
lokāyatādi-sāṅkhyāntā jīve vibhrāntim āśritāḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 217
units.deva:
अद्वितीय-ब्रह्म-तत्त्वं न जानन्ति यदा तदा।
भ्रान्ता एवाखिलास् तेषां क्व मुक्तिः क्वेह वा सुखम्॥
units.translation: As long as they do not know the nondual reality of Brahman, all of them remain deluded. Where is liberation for them, or happiness here?
units.iast:
advitīya-brahma-tattvaṃ na jānanti yadā tadā|
bhrāntā evākhilās teṣāṃ kva muktiḥ kveha vā sukham||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 218
units.deva:
उत्तमाधम-भावश् चेत् तेषां स्याद् अस्तु तेन किम्।
स्वप्नस्थ-राज्य-भिक्षाभ्यां न बुद्धः स्पृश्यते खलु॥
units.translation: If they have higher or lower status, so what? One who is awake is not affected by being king or beggar in a dream.

gloss.en: by kingship and beggary in a dream

units.iast:
uttamādhama-bhāvaś cet teṣāṃ syād astu tena kim|
svapnastha-rājya-bhikṣābhyāṃ na buddhaḥ spṛśyate khalu||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 219
units.deva:
तस्मान् मुमुक्षुभिर् नैव मतिर् जीवेश-वादयोः।
कार्या किन्तु ब्रह्म-तत्त्वं विचार्यं बुध्यतां च तत्॥
units.translation: Therefore, seekers of liberation should not direct their thought to theories about the jīva and Īśvara. Instead, Brahman’s reality should be examined and known.

gloss.en: in theories about the jīva and Īśvara

units.iast:
tasmān mumukṣubhir naiva matir jīveśa-vādayoḥ|
kāryā kintu brahma-tattvaṃ vicāryaṃ budhyatāṃ ca tat||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 220
units.deva:
पूर्व-पक्षतया तौ चेत् तत्त्व-निश्चय-हेतुताम्।
प्राप्नुतोऽस्तु निमज्जस्व तयोर् नैतावताऽवशः॥
units.translation: If those two, treated as preliminary arguments, serve to establish the truth, so be it; immerse yourself in them, but do not become helpless under their sway.

gloss.en: the state of being a means to establish the truth

units.iast:
pūrva-pakṣatayā tau cet tattva-niścaya-hetutām|
prāpnuto’stu nimajjasva tayor naitāvatā’vaśaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 221
units.deva:
असङ्ग-चिद् विभुर् जीवः साङ्ख्योक्तस् तादृग् ईश्वरः।
योगोक्तस् तत्-त्वमोर् अर्थौ शुद्धौ ताविति चेच् छृणु॥
units.translation: If you say, “The jīva is unattached consciousness and all-pervasive, as in Sāṅkhya; Īśvara is the same; Yoga says the two meanings of ‘That’ and ‘you’ are pure”—then listen.
units.iast:
asaṅga-cid vibhur jīvaḥ sāṅkhyoktas tādṛg īśvaraḥ|
yogoktas tat-tvamor arthau śuddhau tāviti cec chṛṇu||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 222
units.deva:
न तत्-त्वमोर् उभावर्थावस्मत् सिद्धान्ततां गतौ।
अद्वैत-बोधनायैव सा कक्षा काचिद् इष्यते॥
units.translation: Those two meanings of “That” and “you” are not our final conclusion. That framework is accepted only as a means to teach nonduality.

gloss.en: the status of a final conclusion

units.iast:
na tat-tvamor ubhāvarthāvasmat siddhāntatāṃ gatau|
advaita-bodhanāyaiva sā kakṣā kācid iṣyate||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 223
units.deva:
अनादि-मायया भ्रान्ता जीवेशौ सुविलक्षणौ।
मन्यन्ते तद्-व्युदासाय केवलं शोधनं तयोः॥
units.translation: Deluded by beginningless Māyā, people consider the jīva and Īśvara to be very different. To remove that mistake, those two need to be properly examined.
units.iast:
anādi-māyayā bhrāntā jīveśau suvilakṣaṇau|
manyante tad-vyudāsāya kevalaṃ śodhanaṃ tayoḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 224
units.deva:
अत एवात्र दृष्टान्तो योग्यः प्राक् सम्यग् ईरितः।
घटाकाश-महाकाश-जलाकाशाभ्र-खात्मकः॥
units.translation: Therefore, the earlier example is apt here: pot-space and great space, and the sky reflected in water and in a cloud.
units.iast:
ata evātra dṛṣṭānto yogyaḥ prāk samyag īritaḥ|
ghaṭākāśa-mahākāśa-jalākāśābhra-khātmakaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 225
units.deva:
जलाभ्रोपाध्य-धीने ते जलाकाशाभ्र-खे तयोः।
आधारौ तु घटाकाश-महाकाशौ सुनिर्मलौ॥
units.translation: The water-space and cloud-space depend on the limiting conditions of water and cloud. But the bases of pot-space and great space are completely pure.

gloss.en: dependent on the limiting conditions of water and cloud

units.iast:
jalābhropādhya-dhīne te jalākāśābhra-khe tayoḥ|
ādhārau tu ghaṭākāśa-mahākāśau sunirmalau||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 226
units.deva:
एवम् आनन्द-विज्ञानमयौ माया-धियोर् वशौ।
तद्-अधिष्ठान-कूटस्थ-ब्रह्मणी तु सुनिर्मले॥
units.translation: Thus the bliss-sheath and intellect-sheath are under the power of Māyā and the intellect, respectively. But their two bases, Kūṭastha and Brahman, are completely pure.
units.iast:
evam ānanda-vijñānamayau māyā-dhiyor vaśau|
tad-adhiṣṭhāna-kūṭastha-brahmaṇī tu sunirmale||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 227
units.deva:
एतत्-कक्षोपयोगेन साङ्ख्य-योगौ मतौ यदि।
देहोऽन्नमय-कक्षत्वाद् आत्मत्वेनाभ्युपेयताम्॥
units.translation: If Sāṅkhya and Yoga use this kind of argument, then—since the body is a food-sheath—let the body itself be accepted as the Self.
units.iast:
etat-kakṣopayogena sāṅkhya-yogau matau yadi|
deho’nnamaya-kakṣatvād ātmatvenābhyupeyatām||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 228
units.deva:
आत्म-भेदो जगत् सत्यम् ईशोऽन्य इति चेत् त्रयम्।
त्यज्यते तैस् तदा साङ्ख्य-योग-वेदान्त-सम्मतिः॥
units.translation: If they give up these three views—that selves are different, the world is real, and the Lord is separate—then Sāṅkhya, Yoga, and Vedānta agree.

gloss.en: agreement among Sāṅkhya, Yoga, and Vedānta

units.iast:
ātma-bhedo jagat satyam īśo’nya iti cet trayam|
tyajyate tais tadā sāṅkhya-yoga-vedānta-sammatiḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 229
units.deva:
जीवोऽसङ्गत्व-मात्रेण कृतार्थ इति चेत् तदा।
स्रक्-चन्दनादि-नित्यत्व-मात्रेणापि कृतार्थता॥
units.translation: If one says the jīva is fulfilled merely by being unattached, then, by the same reasoning, flowers, sandalwood, and the like would be fulfilled merely by being eternal.
units.iast:
jīvo’saṅgatva-mātreṇa kṛtārtha iti cet tadā|
srak-candanādi-nityatva-mātreṇāpi kṛtārthatā||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 230
units.deva:
यथा स्रगादि-नित्यत्वं दुः-संपाद्यं तथात्मनः।
असङ्गत्वं न संभाव्यं जीवतोर् जगद्-ईशयोः॥
units.translation: Just as the eternality of a garland and the like is hard to establish, so the Self’s non-attachment is inconceivable while the jīva, the world, and the Lord are held to exist separately.
units.iast:
yathā sragādi-nityatvaṃ duḥ-saṃpādyaṃ tathātmanaḥ|
asaṅgatvaṃ na saṃbhāvyaṃ jīvator jagad-īśayoḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 231
units.deva:
अवश्यं प्रकृतिः सङ्गं पुरेवापादयेत् तदा।
नियच्छत्येतम् ईशोऽपि कोऽस्य मोक्षस् तथा सति॥
units.translation: If Prakṛti necessarily continues to cause attachment as before, and the Lord also controls him, then what liberation does he have?
units.iast:
avaśyaṃ prakṛtiḥ saṅgaṃ purevāpādayet tadā|
niyacchatyetam īśo’pi ko’sya mokṣas tathā sati||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 232
units.deva:
अविवेक-कृतः सङ्गः नियमश् चेति चेत् तदा।
बलाद् आपतितो माया-वादः साङ्ख्यस्य दुर्मतेः॥
units.translation: If you say attachment and control are caused by lack of discernment, you are forced to accept the Māyā doctrine, which contradicts Sāṅkhya.
units.iast:
aviveka-kṛtaḥ saṅgaḥ niyamaś ceti cet tadā|
balād āpatito māyā-vādaḥ sāṅkhyasya durmateḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 233
units.deva:
बन्ध-मोक्ष-व्यवस्थार्थम् आत्म-नानात्वम् इष्यताम्।
इति चेन् न यतो माया व्यवस्थापयितुं क्षमा॥
units.translation: If one says that plurality of selves must be accepted to account for bondage and liberation, no—Māyā can account for that arrangement.
units.iast:
bandha-mokṣa-vyavasthārtham ātma-nānātvam iṣyatām|
iti cen na yato māyā vyavasthāpayituṃ kṣamā||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 234
units.deva:
दुर्घटं घट-यामीति विरुद्धं किम् न पश्यसि।
वास्तवौ बन्ध-मोक्षौ तु श्रुतिर् न सहतेतराम्॥
units.translation: Do you not see the contradiction in saying, “I make the impossible possible”? Scripture does not at all accept bondage and liberation as ultimately real.
units.iast:
durghaṭaṃ ghaṭa-yāmīti viruddhaṃ kim na paśyasi|
vāstavau bandha-mokṣau tu śrutir na sahatetarām||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 235
units.deva:
न निरोधो न चोत्पत्तिर् न बद्धो न च साधकः।
न मुमुक्षुर् न वै मुक्तः इत्येषा परमार्थता॥
units.translation: This is the highest truth: there is no cessation and no arising, no bound person and no practitioner, no seeker of liberation and indeed no liberated person.
units.iast:
na nirodho na cotpattir na baddho na ca sādhakaḥ|
na mumukṣur na vai muktaḥ ityeṣā paramārthatā||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 236
units.deva:
मायाख्यायाः काम-धेनोर् वत्सौ जीवेश्वरावुभौ।
यथेच्छं पिबतां द्वैतं तत्त्वं त्वद्वैतम् एव हि॥
units.translation: The jīva and Īśvara are both calves of the wish-fulfilling cow called Māyā; let them drink duality as they please. The truth, however, is only nonduality.
units.iast:
māyākhyāyāḥ kāma-dhenor vatsau jīveśvarāvubhau|
yathecchaṃ pibatāṃ dvaitaṃ tattvaṃ tvadvaitam eva hi||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 237
units.deva:
कूटस्थ-ब्रह्मणोर् भेदो नाम-मात्राद् ऋते न हि।
घटाकाश-महाकाशौ वियुज्येते न हि क्वचित्॥
units.translation: There is no difference between Kūṭastha and Brahman apart from the name. Just as the space in a pot is never separated from the vast space.
units.iast:
kūṭastha-brahmaṇor bhedo nāma-mātrād ṛte na hi|
ghaṭākāśa-mahākāśau viyujyete na hi kvacit||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 238
units.deva:
यद् अद्वैतं श्रुतं सृष्टेः प्राक् तद् एवाद्य चोपरि।
मुक्तावपि वृथा माया भ्रामयत्यखिलान् जनान्॥
units.translation: The nonduality declared in scripture before creation is the same now and thereafter, even in liberation. Māyā needlessly deludes all people.
units.iast:
yad advaitaṃ śrutaṃ sṛṣṭeḥ prāk tad evādya copari|
muktāvapi vṛthā māyā bhrāmayatyakhilān janān||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 239
units.deva:
ये वदन्तीत्थम् एतेऽपि भ्राम्यन्ते विद्ययात्र किम्।
न यथा पूर्वम् एतेषाम् अत्र भ्रान्तेर् अदर्शनात्॥
units.translation: If one objects that even those who speak this way still seem to wander, what use is their knowledge? No: they are not deluded as before, for their delusion is no longer present.

gloss.en: because it is not seen / is absent

units.iast:
ye vadantīttham ete’pi bhrāmyante vidyayātra kim|
na yathā pūrvam eteṣām atra bhrānter adarśanāt||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 240
units.deva:
ऐहिकामुष्मिकः सर्वः संसारो वास्तवस् ततः।
न भाति नास्ति चाद्वैतम् इत्यज्ञानि-विनिश्चयः॥
units.translation: The ignorant conclude that all saṃsāra, here and hereafter, is real, and that nonduality neither appears nor exists.

gloss.en: pertaining to this world and the next

units.iast:
aihikāmuṣmikaḥ sarvaḥ saṃsāro vāstavas tataḥ|
na bhāti nāsti cādvaitam ityajñāni-viniścayaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 241
units.deva:
ज्ञानिनो विपरीतोऽस्मान् निश्चयः सम्यग् ईक्ष्यते।
स्वस्व-निश्चयतो बद्धो मुक्तोऽहं चेति मन्यते॥
units.translation: The conviction of the wise is seen to be the opposite of ours. According to one’s own conviction, one thinks, “I am bound” or “I am free.”
units.iast:
jñānino viparīto’smān niścayaḥ samyag īkṣyate|
svasva-niścayato baddho mukto’haṃ ceti manyate||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 242
units.deva:
नाद्वैतम् अपरोक्षं चेन् न चिद्-रूपेण भासनात्।
अशेषेण न भातं चेत् द्वैतं किं भासते तव॥
units.translation: (Objection:) If nonduality is not directly known—(Reply:) No, because it shines as consciousness. (Objection:) If it does not shine completely, then how does duality appear completely to you?
units.iast:
nādvaitam aparokṣaṃ cen na cid-rūpeṇa bhāsanāt|
aśeṣeṇa na bhātaṃ cet dvaitaṃ kiṃ bhāsate tava||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 243
units.deva:
दिङ्-मात्रेण विभानं तु द्वयोर् अपि समं खलु।
द्वैत-सिद्धिवद् अद्वैत-सिद्धिस् ते तावता न किम्॥
units.translation: Both are equally known only in outline. If duality can be established, why not establish nonduality to the same extent?

gloss.en: only in outline / by a mere indication
as with the establishment of duality

units.iast:
diṅ-mātreṇa vibhānaṃ tu dvayor api samaṃ khalu|
dvaita-siddhivad advaita-siddhis te tāvatā na kim||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 244
units.deva:
द्वैतेन हीनम् अद्वैतं द्वैत-ज्ञाने कथं त्विदम्।
चिद्-भानं त्वविरोध्यस्य द्वैतस्यातोऽसमे उभे॥
units.translation: (Objection:) If nonduality is devoid of duality, how can it be present when duality is known? (Reply:) The awareness of consciousness does not conflict with this duality; therefore, the two are not incompatible opposites.
units.iast:
dvaitena hīnam advaitaṃ dvaita-jñāne kathaṃ tvidam|
cid-bhānaṃ tvavirodhyasya dvaitasyāto’same ubhe||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 245
units.deva:
एवं तर्हि शृणु द्वैतम् असन् मायामयत्वतः।
तेन वास्तवम् अद्वैतं परिशेषाद् विभासते॥
units.translation: So listen: duality is unreal because it consists of Māyā. Therefore, nonduality alone shines as real, since it remains when the rest is set aside.
units.iast:
evaṃ tarhi śṛṇu dvaitam asan māyāmayatvataḥ|
tena vāstavam advaitaṃ pariśeṣād vibhāsate||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 246
units.deva:
अचिन्त्य-रचना-रूपं मायैव सकलं जगत्।
इति निश्चित्य वस्तुत्वम् अद्वैते परिशेष्यताम्॥
units.translation: The entire universe is Māyā alone, in the form of an inconceivable construction. Having understood this, let reality be recognized as what remains in nonduality.

gloss.en: in the form of an inconceivable construction
let it remain / be recognized as what remains

units.iast:
acintya-racanā-rūpaṃ māyaiva sakalaṃ jagat|
iti niścitya vastutvam advaite pariśeṣyatām||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 247
units.deva:
पुनर् द्वैतस्य वस्तुत्वं भाति चेत् त्वं तथा पुनः।
परिशीलय को वात्र प्रयासस् तेन ते वद॥
units.translation: If the reality of duality appears again, examine it carefully again. What effort is there in that? Tell me.
units.iast:
punar dvaitasya vastutvaṃ bhāti cet tvaṃ tathā punaḥ|
pariśīlaya ko vātra prayāsas tena te vada||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 248
units.deva:
कियन्तं कालम् इति चेत् खेदोऽयं द्वैत इष्यताम्।
अद्वैते तु न युक्तोऽयं सर्वानर्थ-निवारणात्॥
units.translation: If you ask, “For how long?”, let this weariness belong to duality. In nonduality it is not reasonable, since all troubles are removed.
units.iast:
kiyantaṃ kālam iti cet khedo’yaṃ dvaita iṣyatām|
advaite tu na yukto’yaṃ sarvānartha-nivāraṇāt||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 249
units.deva:
क्षुत्-पिपासादयो दृष्टा यथा-पूर्वं मयीति चेत्।
मच्-छब्द-वाच्येऽहङ्कारे दृश्यन्तां नेति को वदेत्॥
units.translation: If you say, “Hunger, thirst, and the rest are seen in me as before,” let them be seen in the ego denoted by the word “me”—who would deny it?

gloss.en: in what is denoted by the word “me”

units.iast:
kṣut-pipāsādayo dṛṣṭā yathā-pūrvaṃ mayīti cet|
mac-chabda-vācye’haṅkāre dṛśyantāṃ neti ko vadet||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 250
units.deva:
चिद्-रूपेऽपि प्रसज्येरंस् तादात्म्याध्यासतो यदि।
मा ध्यानं कुरु किन्तु त्वं विवेकं कुरु सर्वदा॥
units.translation: Even if they seem to attach to consciousness through superimposed identity, do not meditate on that; instead, practice discrimination at all times.
units.iast:
cid-rūpe’pi prasajyeraṃs tādātmyādhyāsato yadi|
mā dhyānaṃ kuru kintu tvaṃ vivekaṃ kuru sarvadā||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 251
units.deva:
झटित्यध्यास आयाति दृढ-वासनयेति चेत्।
आवर्तयेद् विवेकं च दृढं वासयितुं सदा॥
units.translation: If superimposition arises suddenly because of strong latent tendencies, repeat discrimination continually to establish it firmly.

gloss.en: because of a strong latent tendency
one should repeat / turn back to

units.iast:
jhaṭityadhyāsa āyāti dṛḍha-vāsanayeti cet|
āvartayed vivekaṃ ca dṛḍhaṃ vāsayituṃ sadā||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 252
units.deva:
विवेके द्वैत-मिथ्यात्वं युक्त्यैवेति न भण्यताम्।
अचिन्त्य-रचनात्वस्यानुभूतिर् हि स्व-साक्षिकी॥
units.translation: While discerning, do not say that duality’s unreality is established by logic alone; one’s own experience witnesses its being an inconceivable construction.

gloss.en: of its being an inconceivable construction

units.iast:
viveke dvaita-mithyātvaṃ yuktyaiveti na bhaṇyatām|
acintya-racanātvasyānubhūtir hi sva-sākṣikī||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 253
units.deva:
चिद् अप्यचिन्त्य-रचना यदि तर्ह्यस्तु नो वयम्।
चितिं सुचिन्त्य-रचनां ब्रूमो नित्यत्व-कारणात्॥
units.translation: If consciousness too is an inconceivable construction, let that be. We call consciousness a well-considered construction because it is eternal.
units.iast:
cid apyacintya-racanā yadi tarhyastu no vayam|
citiṃ sucintya-racanāṃ brūmo nityatva-kāraṇāt||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 254
units.deva:
प्राग्-अभावो नानुभूतश् चितेर् नित्या ततश् चितिः।
द्वैतस्य प्राग्-अभावस् तु चैतन्येनानुभूयते॥
units.translation: The prior nonexistence of consciousness is not experienced; therefore, consciousness is eternal. But the prior nonexistence of duality is experienced through consciousness.
units.iast:
prāg-abhāvo nānubhūtaś citer nityā tataś citiḥ|
dvaitasya prāg-abhāvas tu caitanyenānubhūyate||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 255
units.deva:
प्राग्-अभाव-युतं द्वैतं रच्यते हि घटादिवत्।
तथापि रचनाऽचिन्त्या मिथ्या तेनेन्द्र-जालवत्॥
units.translation: Duality, which had not existed before, is indeed constructed like a pot and the like. Yet its construction is inconceivable and therefore unreal, like a magic show.

gloss.en: like a pot and the like

units.iast:
prāg-abhāva-yutaṃ dvaitaṃ racyate hi ghaṭādivat|
tathāpi racanā’cintyā mithyā tenendra-jālavat||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 256
units.deva:
चित् प्रत्यक्षा ततोऽन्यस्य मिथ्यात्वं चानुभूयते।
नाद्वैतम् अपरोक्षं चेत्येतन्न व्याहतं कथम्॥
units.translation: Consciousness is directly present, and the unreality of what is other is experienced. How is it not contradictory to say that nonduality is not directly known?
units.iast:
cit pratyakṣā tato’nyasya mithyātvaṃ cānubhūyate|
nādvaitam aparokṣaṃ cetyetanna vyāhataṃ katham||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 257
units.deva:
इत्थं ज्ञात्वाऽप्यसन्तुष्टाः केचित् कुत इतीर्यताम्।
चार्वाकादेः प्रबुद्धस्यात्मा देहः कुतो वद॥
units.translation: If some remain dissatisfied even after understanding this, explain why: tell me, why does the learned Cārvāka say the body is the Self?
units.iast:
itthaṃ jñātvā’pyasantuṣṭāḥ kecit kuta itīryatām|
cārvākādeḥ prabuddhasyātmā dehaḥ kuto vada||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 258
units.deva:
सम्यग् विचारो नास्त्यस्य धी-दोषाद् इति चेत् तथा।
असन्तुष्टास् तु शास्त्रार्थं न त्वैक्षन्त विशेषतः॥
units.translation: If you say he lacks proper inquiry because of a defect in the intellect, then likewise the dissatisfied have not clearly understood the meaning of scripture.

gloss.en: because of a defect in the intellect

units.iast:
samyag vicāro nāstyasya dhī-doṣād iti cet tathā|
asantuṣṭās tu śāstrārthaṃ na tvaikṣanta viśeṣataḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 259
units.deva:
यदा सर्वे प्रमुच्यन्ते कामा येऽस्य हृदि श्रिताः।
इति श्रौतं फलं दृष्टं नेति चेद् दृष्टम् एव तत्॥
units.translation: The scriptural result is seen in the words, “When all the desires lodged in his heart are released.” If you say it is not seen, that result is indeed seen.
units.iast:
yadā sarve pramucyante kāmā ye’sya hṛdi śritāḥ|
iti śrautaṃ phalaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ neti ced dṛṣṭam eva tat||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 260
units.deva:
यदा सर्वे प्रभिद्यन्ते हृदय-ग्रन्थयस्त्विति।
कामा ग्रन्थि-स्वरूपेण व्याख्याता वाक्य-शेषतः॥
units.translation: In the phrase, “When all the knots of the heart are broken,” desires are explained as having the nature of knots by the rest of the passage.

gloss.en: as having the nature of knots
by the rest of the passage

units.iast:
yadā sarve prabhidyante hṛdaya-granthayastviti|
kāmā granthi-svarūpeṇa vyākhyātā vākya-śeṣataḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 261
units.deva:
अहङ्कार-चिदात्मानाव् एकी-कृत्याविवेकतः।
इदं मे स्याद् इदं मे स्याद् इतीच्छाः काम-शब्दिताः॥
units.translation: By failing to distinguish the ego from the conscious Self, one thinks, “May this be mine; may that be mine.” Such desires are called kāma.

gloss.en: the ego and the conscious Self

units.iast:
ahaṅkāra-cidātmānāv ekī-kṛtyāvivekataḥ|
idaṃ me syād idaṃ me syād itīcchāḥ kāma-śabditāḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 262
units.deva:
अप्रवेश्य चिदात्मानं पृथक् पश्यन्न् अहङ्-कृतिम्।
इच्छंस् तु कोटि-वस्तूनि न बाधो ग्रन्थि-भेदतः॥
units.translation: Without superimposing the conscious Self on the ego, one sees the ego as separate. One may then desire countless things; after the knot is severed, there is no conflict.
units.iast:
apraveśya cidātmānaṃ pṛthak paśyann ahaṅ-kṛtim|
icchaṃs tu koṭi-vastūni na bādho granthi-bhedataḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 263
units.deva:
ग्रन्थि-भेदेऽपि संभाव्या इच्छाः प्रारब्ध-दोषतः।
बुद्ध्वापि पाप-बाहुल्याद् असन्तोषो यथा तव॥
units.translation: Desires can arise even after the knot is severed, owing to defects of prārabdha. Even with understanding, dissatisfaction may remain because of accumulated wrongdoing, as in your case.

gloss.en: because of an abundance of wrongdoing

units.iast:
granthi-bhede’pi saṃbhāvyā icchāḥ prārabdha-doṣataḥ|
buddhvāpi pāpa-bāhulyād asantoṣo yathā tava||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 264
units.deva:
अहंकार-गतेच्छाद्यैर् देह-व्याध्यादिभिस् तदा।
वृक्षादि-जन्म-नाशैर् वा चिद्-रूपात्मनि किं भवेत्॥
units.translation: What do desires located in the ego, bodily illnesses, or the arising and passing of trees have to do with the Self, whose nature is consciousness?

gloss.en: by desires and the rest located in the ego
by bodily illness and the rest
in the Self whose nature is consciousness

units.iast:
ahaṃkāra-gatecchādyair deha-vyādhyādibhis tadā|
vṛkṣādi-janma-nāśair vā cid-rūpātmani kiṃ bhavet||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 265
units.deva:
ग्रन्थि-भेदात् पुराप्येवम् इति चेत् तन् न विस्मर।
अयम् एव ग्रन्थि-भेदस् तव तेन कृती-भवान्॥
units.translation: If you say this was so even before the knot was severed, do not forget: this very understanding is the severing of the knot. Through it, you become fulfilled.
units.iast:
granthi-bhedāt purāpyevam iti cet tan na vismara|
ayam eva granthi-bhedas tava tena kṛtī-bhavān||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 266
units.deva:
नैवं जानन्ति मूढाश् चेत् सोऽयं ग्रन्थिर् न चापरः।
ग्रन्थि-तद्-भेद-मात्रेण वैषम्यं मूढ-बुद्धयोः॥
units.translation: If the deluded do not know this, that itself is the knot, nothing else. The only difference between the deluded and the wise is that knot and its severance.

gloss.en: only by that knot and its severance
between the deluded and the wise

units.iast:
naivaṃ jānanti mūḍhāś cet so’yaṃ granthir na cāparaḥ|
granthi-tad-bheda-mātreṇa vaiṣamyaṃ mūḍha-buddhayoḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 267
units.deva:
प्रवृत्तौ वा निवृत्तौ वा देहेन्द्रिय-मनो-धियाम्।
न किञ्चिद् अपि वैषम्यम् अस्त्यज्ञानि-विबुद्धयोः॥
units.translation: In the activity or withdrawal of the body, senses, mind, and intellect, there is no difference at all between the ignorant and the awakened.

gloss.en: of body, senses, mind, and intellect
between the ignorant and the awakened

units.iast:
pravṛttau vā nivṛttau vā dehendriya-mano-dhiyām|
na kiñcid api vaiṣamyam astyajñāni-vibuddhayoḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 268
units.deva:
व्रात्य-श्रोत्रिययोर् वेद-पाठापाठ-कृता भिदा।
नाहारादाव् अस्ति भेदः सोऽयं न्यायोऽत्र योग्यताम्॥
units.translation: The difference between an uninitiated person and a Vedic scholar comes from studying or not studying the Veda; in food and the like there is no difference. Apply the same reasoning here.

gloss.en: between an uninitiated person and a Vedic scholar
caused by studying or not studying the Veda

units.iast:
vrātya-śrotriyayor veda-pāṭhāpāṭha-kṛtā bhidā|
nāhārādāv asti bhedaḥ so’yaṃ nyāyo’tra yogyatām||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 269
units.deva:
न द्वेष्टि संप्रवृत्तानि न निवृत्तानि काङ्क्षति।
उदासीनवद् आसीन इति ग्रन्थि-भिदोच्यते॥
units.translation: “He does not dislike what has arisen, nor long for what has ceased; he remains as if indifferent.” Such a person is said to have severed the knot.

gloss.en: one who has severed the knot

units.iast:
na dveṣṭi saṃpravṛttāni na nivṛttāni kāṅkṣati|
udāsīnavad āsīna iti granthi-bhidocyate||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 270
units.deva:
औदासीन्यं विधेयं चेद् वच्छब्दव्यर्थता तदा।
न शक्ता अस्य देहाद्या इति चेद् रोग एव सः॥
units.translation: If indifference were enjoined, the suffix “-vat” (“as if”) would be pointless. If his body and the rest are unable to function, that is simply illness.
units.iast:
audāsīnyaṃ vidheyaṃ ced vacchabdavyarthatā tadā|
na śaktā asya dehādyā iti ced roga eva saḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 271
units.deva:
तत्त्व-बोधं क्षयं व्याधिं मन्यन्ते ये महा-धियः।
तेषां प्रज्ञाऽतिविशदा किं तेषां दुःशकं वद॥
units.translation: Those great intellects who call knowledge of truth a disease of consumption: tell me, what is difficult for them?
units.iast:
tattva-bodhaṃ kṣayaṃ vyādhiṃ manyante ye mahā-dhiyaḥ|
teṣāṃ prajñā’tiviśadā kiṃ teṣāṃ duḥśakaṃ vada||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 272
units.deva:
भरतादेर् अप्रवृत्तिः पुराणोक्तेति चेत् तदा।
जक्षन् क्रीडन् रतिं विन्दन्न् इत्यश्रौषीर् न किं श्रुतिम्॥
units.translation: If you say that the withdrawal of Bharata and the others is stated in the Purāṇas, then have you not heard the Śruti, “Eating, playing, finding delight …”?
units.iast:
bharatāder apravṛttiḥ purāṇokteti cet tadā|
jakṣan krīḍan ratiṃ vindann ityaśrauṣīr na kiṃ śrutim||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 273
units.deva:
न ह्याहारादि सन्त्यज्य भरताद्याः स्थिताः क्वचित्।
काष्ठ-पाषाणवत् किन्तु सङ्ग-भीता उदासते॥
units.translation: Bharata and the others did not remain anywhere after giving up food and the like, like wood and stone. Rather, fearing attachment, they remained indifferent.
units.iast:
na hyāhārādi santyajya bharatādyāḥ sthitāḥ kvacit|
kāṣṭha-pāṣāṇavat kintu saṅga-bhītā udāsate||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 274
units.deva:
सङ्गी हि बाध्यते लोके निःसङ्गः सुखम् अश्नुते।
तेन सङ्गः परित्याज्यः सर्वदा सुखम् इच्छता॥
units.translation: The attached person is indeed afflicted in the world; the unattached enjoys happiness. Therefore, one who always desires happiness should abandon attachment.
units.iast:
saṅgī hi bādhyate loke niḥsaṅgaḥ sukham aśnute|
tena saṅgaḥ parityājyaḥ sarvadā sukham icchatā||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 275
units.deva:
अज्ञात्वा शास्त्र-हृदयं मूढो वक्त्यन्यथाऽन्यथा।
मूर्खाणां निर्णयस्त्वास्ताम् अस्मत् सिद्धान्त उच्यते॥
units.translation: Not knowing the heart of scripture, a fool speaks in one way and then another. Let the judgment of fools stand; now our conclusion is stated.
units.iast:
ajñātvā śāstra-hṛdayaṃ mūḍho vaktyanyathā’nyathā|
mūrkhāṇāṃ nirṇayastvāstām asmat siddhānta ucyate||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 276
units.deva:
वैराग्य-बोधोपरमाः सहायास् ते परस्परम्।
प्रायेण सह वर्तन्ते वियुज्यन्ते क्वचित् क्वचित्॥
units.translation: Dispassion, knowledge, and withdrawal help one another. They are generally found together, though they are sometimes separated.
units.iast:
vairāgya-bodhoparamāḥ sahāyās te parasparam|
prāyeṇa saha vartante viyujyante kvacit kvacit||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 277
units.deva:
हेतु-स्वरूप-कार्याणि भिन्नान्येषाम् असङ्करः।
यथावद्-अवगन्तव्यः शास्त्रार्थं प्रविविच्यता॥
units.translation: Their causes, natures, and results are distinct. This lack of confusion among them should be understood properly by carefully discerning the meaning of scripture.
units.iast:
hetu-svarūpa-kāryāṇi bhinnānyeṣām asaṅkaraḥ|
yathāvad-avagantavyaḥ śāstrārthaṃ pravivicyatā||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 278
units.deva:
दोष-दृष्टिर् जिहासा च पुनर् भोगेष्वदीनता।
असाधारण-हेत्वाद्या वैराग्यस्य त्रयोऽप्यमी॥
units.translation: Seeing the flaws in enjoyments, wanting to give them up, and not depending on them: these are the three distinctive features of dispassion, corresponding to its cause, nature, and result.

gloss.en: the distinctive cause and the rest

units.iast:
doṣa-dṛṣṭir jihāsā ca punar bhogeṣvadīnatā|
asādhāraṇa-hetvādyā vairāgyasya trayo’pyamī||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 279
units.deva:
श्रवणादि-त्रयं तद्वत् तत्त्व-मिथ्या-विवेचनम्।
पुनर् ग्रन्थेर् अनुदयो बोधस्यैते त्रयो मताः॥
units.translation: For knowledge, the three are listening and the rest, discerning the real from the unreal, and the non-arising of the knot.

gloss.en: discerning the real from the unreal

units.iast:
śravaṇādi-trayaṃ tadvat tattva-mithyā-vivecanam|
punar granther anudayo bodhasyaite trayo matāḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 280
units.deva:
यमादिर् धी-निरोधश् च व्यवहारस्य सङ्क्षयः।
स्युर् हेत्वाद्या उपरतेर् इत्यसङ्कर ईरितः॥
units.translation: Yama and the rest, restraint of the mind, and the cessation of ordinary activity are, respectively, the cause, nature, and result of withdrawal. Thus their distinction is stated.
units.iast:
yamādir dhī-nirodhaś ca vyavahārasya saṅkṣayaḥ|
syur hetvādyā uparater ityasaṅkara īritaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 281
units.deva:
तत्त्व-बोधः प्रधानं स्यात् साक्षान् मोक्ष-प्रदत्वतः।
बोधोपकारिणावेतौ वैराग्योपरमावुभौ॥
units.translation: Knowledge of truth is primary because it directly gives liberation; dispassion and withdrawal are both aids to that knowledge.
units.iast:
tattva-bodhaḥ pradhānaṃ syāt sākṣān mokṣa-pradatvataḥ|
bodhopakāriṇāvetau vairāgyoparamāvubhau||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 282
units.deva:
त्रयोऽप्यत्यन्त-पक्वाश् चेन् महतस् तपसः फलम्।
दुरितेन क्वचित् किञ्चित् कदाचित् प्रतिबध्यते॥
units.translation: If all three are fully matured, they are the fruit of great discipline. They may be obstructed by some fault, in some respect, at some time.
units.iast:
trayo’pyatyanta-pakvāś cen mahatas tapasaḥ phalam|
duritena kvacit kiñcit kadācit pratibadhyate||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 283
units.deva:
वैराग्योपरती पूर्णे बोधस् तु प्रतिबध्यते।
यस्य तस्य न मोक्षोऽस्ति पुण्य-लोकस् तपो-बलात्॥
units.translation: If dispassion and withdrawal are complete but knowledge is obstructed, that person does not gain liberation; through the power of discipline, [he gains] a world of merit.
units.iast:
vairāgyoparatī pūrṇe bodhas tu pratibadhyate|
yasya tasya na mokṣo’sti puṇya-lokas tapo-balāt||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 284
units.deva:
पूर्णे बोधे तदन्यौ द्वौ प्रतिबद्धौ यदा तदा।
मोक्षो विनिश्चितः किन्तु दृष्ट-दुःखं न नश्यति॥
units.translation: When knowledge is complete but the other two are obstructed, liberation is certain; nevertheless, visible suffering does not disappear.
units.iast:
pūrṇe bodhe tadanyau dvau pratibaddhau yadā tadā|
mokṣo viniścitaḥ kintu dṛṣṭa-duḥkhaṃ na naśyati||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 285
units.deva:
ब्रह्म-लोक-तृणीकारो वैराग्यस्यावधिर् मतः।
देहात्मवत् परात्मत्व-दार्ढ्ये बोधः समाप्यते॥
units.translation: Dispassion is complete when even Brahma-loka is treated like straw. Knowledge is complete when conviction in the supreme Self is as firm as the former conviction that the body is the Self.

gloss.en: as firmly as the body as Self
the nature of the supreme Self

units.iast:
brahma-loka-tṛṇīkāro vairāgyasyāvadhir mataḥ|
dehātmavat parātmatva-dārḍhye bodhaḥ samāpyate||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 286
units.deva:
सुप्तिवद् विस्मृतिः सीमा भवेद् उपरमस्य हि।
दिशाऽनया विनिश्चेयं तारतम्यम् अवान्तरम्॥
units.translation: The limit of withdrawal is forgetfulness like deep sleep. By this indication, its intermediate degrees should be determined.
units.iast:
suptivad vismṛtiḥ sīmā bhaved uparamasya hi|
diśā’nayā viniśceyaṃ tāratamyam avāntaram||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 287
units.deva:
आरब्ध-कर्म-नानात्वाद् बुद्धानाम् अन्यथाऽन्यथा।
वर्तनं तेन शास्त्रार्थे भ्रमितव्यं न पण्डितैः॥
units.translation: Because the wise have different prārabdha, their conduct varies. Scholars should not be confused about the meaning of scripture because of that.

gloss.en: because of differences in prārabdha karma

units.iast:
ārabdha-karma-nānātvād buddhānām anyathā’nyathā|
vartanaṃ tena śāstrārthe bhramitavyaṃ na paṇḍitaiḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 288
units.deva:
स्वस्व-कर्मानुसारेण वर्तन्तां ते यथा तथा।
अविशिष्टः सर्व-बोधः समा मुक्तिर् इति स्थितिः॥
units.translation: Let them act according to their own karma, however they do. Knowledge is the same in all, and liberation is the same: that is the settled conclusion.
units.iast:
svasva-karmānusāreṇa vartantāṃ te yathā tathā|
aviśiṣṭaḥ sarva-bodhaḥ samā muktir iti sthitiḥ||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 289
units.deva:
जगच्-चित्रं स्व-चैतन्ये पटे चित्रम् इवार्पितम्।
मायया तद्-उपेक्ष्यैव चैतन्यं परिशेष्यताम्॥
units.translation: The picture of the world is superimposed by Māyā on one’s own consciousness, like a picture on cloth. By setting that aside, let consciousness alone remain.

gloss.en: let it remain as what is left

units.iast:
jagac-citraṃ sva-caitanye paṭe citram ivārpitam|
māyayā tad-upekṣyaiva caitanyaṃ pariśeṣyatām||

units.label: Chapter 6 · Verse 290
units.deva:
चित्र-दीपम् इमं नित्यं येऽनुसन्दधते बुधाः।
पश्यन्तोऽपि जगच्-चित्रं ते मुह्यन्ति न पूर्ववत्॥
units.translation: Wise people who regularly reflect on this Citra-dīpa, even while seeing the picture of the world, are no longer deluded as before.
units.iast:
citra-dīpam imaṃ nityaṃ ye’nusandadhate budhāḥ|
paśyanto’pi jagac-citraṃ te muhyanti na pūrvavat||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 1
units.deva:
आत्मानं चेद् विजानीयाद् अयम् अस्मीति पूरुषः।
किमिच्छन् कस्य कामाय शरीरम् अनुसंज्वरेत्॥
units.translation: If a person were to know the Self as “I am this,” what would they desire, and for whose sake would they grieve over the body?

gloss.en: would grieve over / be tormented by

units.iast:
ātmānaṃ ced vijānīyād ayam asmīti pūruṣaḥ|
kimicchan kasya kāmāya śarīram anusaṃjvaret||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 2
units.deva:
अस्याः श्रुतेरभिप्रायः सम्यग् अत्र विचार्यते।
जीवन्मुक्तस्य या तृप्तिः सा तेन विशदायते॥
units.translation: Here the purport of this Śruti is examined fully; through this, the contentment of one liberated while living is made clear.
units.iast:
asyāḥ śruterabhiprāyaḥ samyag atra vicāryate|
jīvanmuktasya yā tṛptiḥ sā tena viśadāyate||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 3
units.deva:
मायाभासेन जीवेशौ करोतीति श्रुतत्वतः।
कल्पितावेव जीवेशौ ताभ्यां सर्वं प्रकल्पितम्॥
units.translation: Scripture says that Māyā produces the individual and the Lord through its appearance. The two are themselves projected; through them, everything is projected.
units.iast:
māyābhāsena jīveśau karotīti śrutatvataḥ|
kalpitāveva jīveśau tābhyāṃ sarvaṃ prakalpitam||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 4
units.deva:
ईक्षणादि-प्रवेशान्ता सृष्टिरीशेन कल्पिता।
जाग्रदादि-विमोक्षान्तः संसारो जीव-कल्पितः॥
units.translation: Creation, beginning with seeing and ending with entry, is projected by the Lord. Saṃsāra, beginning with waking and ending with liberation, is projected by the individual.
units.iast:
īkṣaṇādi-praveśāntā sṛṣṭirīśena kalpitā|
jāgradādi-vimokṣāntaḥ saṃsāro jīva-kalpitaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 5
units.deva:
भ्रमाधिष्ठान-भूतात्मा कूटस्थासङ्ग-चिद्वपुः।
अन्योन्याध्यासतोऽसङ्ग-धीस्थ-जीवोऽत्र पूरुषः॥
units.translation: The person here is the jīva appearing in the intellect through mutual superimposition; the Self that underlies the error is immutable, unattached consciousness.

gloss.en: the Self that is the basis of error
whose nature is immutable, unattached consciousness
the jīva appearing in the intellect as the unattached Self

units.iast:
bhramādhiṣṭhāna-bhūtātmā kūṭasthāsaṅga-cidvapuḥ|
anyonyādhyāsato’saṅga-dhīstha-jīvo’tra pūruṣaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 6
units.deva:
साधिष्ठानो विमोक्षादौ जीवोऽधिक्रियते न तु।
केवलो निरधिष्ठान-विभ्रान्तेः क्वाप्यसिद्धितः॥
units.translation: With a substratum, the individual is qualified for liberation and the like, but not by itself, since an unsupported illusion is never established.

gloss.en: because of an illusion without a substratum

units.iast:
sādhiṣṭhāno vimokṣādau jīvo’dhikriyate na tu|
kevalo niradhiṣṭhāna-vibhrānteḥ kvāpyasiddhitaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 7
units.deva:
अधिष्ठानांश-संयुक्तं भ्रमांशम् अवलम्बते।
यदा तदाहं संसारीत्येवं जीवोऽतिमन्यते॥
units.translation: When the individual clings to the illusory aspect joined with the substratum, it assumes, “I am caught in saṃsāra.”
units.iast:
adhiṣṭhānāṃśa-saṃyuktaṃ bhramāṃśam avalambate|
yadā tadāhaṃ saṃsārītyevaṃ jīvo’timanyate||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 8
units.deva:
भ्रमांशस्य तिरस्काराद् अधिष्ठान-प्रधानता।
यदा तदा चिदात्माहम् असङ्गोऽस्मीति बुद्ध्यते॥
units.translation: When the illusory aspect is set aside and the substratum becomes predominant, one understands, “I am the Self as consciousness; I am unattached.”
units.iast:
bhramāṃśasya tiraskārād adhiṣṭhāna-pradhānatā|
yadā tadā cidātmāham asaṅgo’smīti buddhyate||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 9
units.deva:
नासङ्गेऽहंकृतिर्युक्ता कथम् अस्मीति चेच्छृणु।
एको मुख्यो द्वावमुख्यावित्यर्थस्त्रिविधोऽहमः॥
units.translation: If you ask, “How can an ‘I’ notion be fitting in the unattached Self?” listen: the word “I” has three senses, one primary and two secondary.
units.iast:
nāsaṅge’haṃkṛtiryuktā katham asmīti cecchṛṇu|
eko mukhyo dvāvamukhyāvityarthastrividho’hamaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 10
units.deva:
अन्योन्याध्यास-रूपेण कूटस्थाभासयोर्वपुः।
एकीभूय भवेन्मुख्यस्तत्र मूढैः प्रयुज्यते॥
units.translation: When the changeless Self and its reflection are treated as one through mutual superimposition, the primary “I” sense arises; the deluded use it that way.

gloss.en: of the changeless Self and its reflection

units.iast:
anyonyādhyāsa-rūpeṇa kūṭasthābhāsayorvapuḥ|
ekībhūya bhavenmukhyastatra mūḍhaiḥ prayujyate||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 11
units.deva:
पृथग् आभास-कूटस्थावमुख्यौ तत्र तत्त्ववित्।
पर्यायेण प्रयुङ्क्तेऽहं-शब्दं लोके च वैदिके॥
units.translation: The knower of truth uses these two secondary senses—the ābhāsa and the kūṭastha—separately, applying the word “I” in turn in ordinary and Vedic usage.

gloss.en: the reflection and the changeless Self

units.iast:
pṛthag ābhāsa-kūṭasthāvamukhyau tatra tattvavit|
paryāyeṇa prayuṅkte’haṃ-śabdaṃ loke ca vaidike||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 12
units.deva:
लौकिक-व्यवहारेऽहं गच्छामीत्यादिके बुधः।
विविच्यैव चिदाभासं कूटस्थात् तं विवक्षति॥
units.translation: In ordinary speech, when a wise person says “I go” and the like, they mean the reflection of consciousness, distinguished from the changeless Self.
units.iast:
laukika-vyavahāre’haṃ gacchāmītyādike budhaḥ|
vivicyaiva cidābhāsaṃ kūṭasthāt taṃ vivakṣati||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 13
units.deva:
असङ्गोऽहं चिदात्माहम् इति शास्त्रीय-दृष्टितः।
अहं-शब्दं प्रयुङ्क्तेयं कूटस्थे केवले बुधः॥
units.translation: From the scriptural standpoint, the wise person uses “I” for the changeless Self alone: “I am unattached; I am consciousness itself.”
units.iast:
asaṅgo’haṃ cidātmāham iti śāstrīya-dṛṣṭitaḥ|
ahaṃ-śabdaṃ prayuṅkteyaṃ kūṭasthe kevale budhaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 14
units.deva:
ज्ञानिताज्ञानिते त्वात्माभासस्यैव न चात्मनः।
तथा च कथम् आभासः कूटस्थोऽस्मीति बुध्यताम्॥
units.translation: Knowing and not-knowing belong to the reflection of the Self alone, not to the Self itself. How, then, can the reflection understand, “I am the changeless Self”?

gloss.en: of the reflection of the Self

units.iast:
jñānitājñānite tvātmābhāsasyaiva na cātmanaḥ|
tathā ca katham ābhāsaḥ kūṭastho’smīti budhyatām||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 15
units.deva:
नायं दोषश्चिदाभासः कूटस्थैक-स्वभाववान्।
आभासत्वस्य मिथ्यात्वात् कूटस्थत्वावशेषणात्॥
units.translation: There is no defect here: the reflection of consciousness has the changeless Self as its sole nature. The reflection is not independently real, so only the changeless Self remains.

gloss.en: having the changeless Self as its sole nature
of the state of being a reflection
because it is not independently real
because only the changeless Self remains

units.iast:
nāyaṃ doṣaścidābhāsaḥ kūṭasthaika-svabhāvavān|
ābhāsatvasya mithyātvāt kūṭasthatvāvaśeṣaṇāt||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 16
units.deva:
कूटस्थोऽस्मीति बोधोऽपि मिथ्या चेन्नेति को वदेत्।
न हि सत्यतयाभीष्टं रज्जु-सर्प-विसर्पणम्॥
units.translation: If even the thought “I am the changeless Self” is unreal, who would dispute that? The slithering of a snake imagined on a rope is not accepted as real.

gloss.en: the slithering of a snake imagined on a rope

units.iast:
kūṭastho’smīti bodho’pi mithyā cenneti ko vadet|
na hi satyatayābhīṣṭaṃ rajju-sarpa-visarpaṇam||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 17
units.deva:
तादृशेनापि बोधेन संसारो विनिवर्तते।
यक्षानुरूपो हि बलिरित्याहुर्लौकिका जनाः॥
units.translation: Even such knowledge ends saṃsāra. Ordinary people say, “The offering should suit the yakṣa.”
units.iast:
tādṛśenāpi bodhena saṃsāro vinivartate|
yakṣānurūpo hi balirityāhurlaukikā janāḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 18
units.deva:
तस्माद् आभास-पुरुषः स-कूटस्थो विविच्य तम्।
कूटस्थोऽस्मीति विज्ञातुम् अर्हतीत्यभ्यधाच्श्रुतिः॥
units.translation: Therefore, the person associated with the reflection and the changeless Self can distinguish that Self and know, “I am the changeless Self,” as the Śruti declares.

gloss.en: the person appearing as a reflection

units.iast:
tasmād ābhāsa-puruṣaḥ sa-kūṭastho vivicya tam|
kūṭastho’smīti vijñātum arhatītyabhyadhācśrutiḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 19
units.deva:
असंदिग्धाविपर्यस्त-बोधो देहात्मनीक्ष्यते।
तद्वद् अत्रेति निर्णेतुम् अयम् इत्यभिधीयते॥
units.translation: A doubt-free, unconfused cognition that the body is the Self is observed. Likewise, here the word “this” is used to establish [that certainty].

gloss.en: in identifying the body as the Self

units.iast:
asaṃdigdhāviparyasta-bodho dehātmanīkṣyate|
tadvad atreti nirṇetum ayam ityabhidhīyate||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 20
units.deva:
देहात्म-ज्ञानवज्ज्ञानं देहात्म-ज्ञान-बाधकम्।
आत्मन्येव भवेद् यस्य स नेच्छन्नपि मुच्यते॥
units.translation: When knowledge that cancels body-identification is as firm as the notion “I am the body” and is established in the Self, that person is freed even without desiring liberation.

gloss.en: like the knowledge “I am the body”

units.iast:
dehātma-jñānavajjñānaṃ dehātma-jñāna-bādhakam|
ātmanyeva bhaved yasya sa necchannapi mucyate||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 21
units.deva:
अयम् इत्यपरोक्षत्वम् उच्यते चेत् तद् उच्यताम्।
स्वयं-प्रकाश-चैतन्यम् अपरोक्षं सदा यतः॥
units.translation: If it is said that “this” denotes immediacy, let it be so, since self-luminous consciousness is always immediately present.
units.iast:
ayam ityaparokṣatvam ucyate cet tad ucyatām|
svayaṃ-prakāśa-caitanyam aparokṣaṃ sadā yataḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 22
units.deva:
परोक्षम् अपरोक्षं च ज्ञानम् अज्ञानम् इत्यदः।
नित्यापरोक्ष-रूपेऽपि द्वयं स्याद् दशमे यथा॥
units.translation: Though the Self is always immediate, it can be spoken of in terms of indirect and direct knowledge, and of knowledge and ignorance—as in the tenth-man example.
units.iast:
parokṣam aparokṣaṃ ca jñānam ajñānam ityadaḥ|
nityāparokṣa-rūpe’pi dvayaṃ syād daśame yathā||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 23
units.deva:
नव-संख्याहृत-ज्ञानो दशमो विभ्रमात् तदा।
न वेत्ति दशमोऽस्मीति वीक्ष्यमाणोऽपि तान् नव॥
units.translation: Through a mistaken count of nine, the tenth man does not know “I am the tenth,” even while looking at those nine.
units.iast:
nava-saṃkhyāhṛta-jñāno daśamo vibhramāt tadā|
na vetti daśamo’smīti vīkṣyamāṇo’pi tān nava||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 24
units.deva:
न भाति नास्ति दशम इति स्वं दशमं तदा।
मत्वा वक्ति तद् अज्ञान-कृतम् आवरणं विदुः॥
units.translation: Then, thinking of himself as the tenth, he says, “The tenth is not seen; he is not here.” The wise call this concealment caused by ignorance.
units.iast:
na bhāti nāsti daśama iti svaṃ daśamaṃ tadā|
matvā vakti tad ajñāna-kṛtam āvaraṇaṃ viduḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 25
units.deva:
नद्यां ममार दशम इति शोचन् प्ररोदिति।
अज्ञान-कृत-विक्षेपं रोदनादिं विदुर्बुधः॥
units.translation: Grieving, “The tenth man died in the river,” he weeps. The wise know such weeping and the like as projection caused by ignorance.
units.iast:
nadyāṃ mamāra daśama iti śocan praroditi|
ajñāna-kṛta-vikṣepaṃ rodanādiṃ vidurbudhaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 26
units.deva:
न मृतो दशमोऽस्तीति श्रुत्वाप्त-वचनं तदा।
परोक्षत्वेन दशमं वेत्ति स्वर्गादि-लोकवत्॥
units.translation: Then, hearing a reliable person say, “The tenth man is not dead,” he knows the tenth indirectly, as one knows heaven and other distant worlds.

gloss.en: the words of a trustworthy person

units.iast:
na mṛto daśamo’stīti śrutvāpta-vacanaṃ tadā|
