parokṣatvena daśamaṃ vetti svargādi-lokavat||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 27
units.deva:
त्वम् एव दशमोऽसीति गणयित्वा प्रदर्शितः।
अपरोक्षतया ज्ञात्वा हृष्यत्येव न रोदिति॥
units.translation: After he is shown by counting, “You are indeed the tenth,” he knows it directly, rejoices, and no longer weeps.
units.iast:
tvam eva daśamo’sīti gaṇayitvā pradarśitaḥ|
aparokṣatayā jñātvā hṛṣyatyeva na roditi||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 28
units.deva:
अज्ञानावृति-विक्षेप-द्विविधा-ज्ञान-तृप्तयः।
शोकापगम इत्येते योजनीयाश्चिदात्मनि॥
units.translation: Ignorance, concealment, projection, the two kinds of knowledge, contentment, and the ending of grief—all these are to be applied to the Self as consciousness.
units.iast:
ajñānāvṛti-vikṣepa-dvividhā-jñāna-tṛptayaḥ|
śokāpagama ityete yojanīyāścidātmani||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 29
units.deva:
संसारासक्त-चित्तः संश्चिदाभासः कदाचन।
स्वयं-प्रकाश-कूटस्थं स्वतत्त्वं नैव वेत्त्ययम्॥
units.translation: The reflection of consciousness, with its mind attached to saṃsāra, never knows its own nature as the self-luminous, changeless Self.

gloss.en: whose mind is attached to saṃsāra

units.iast:
saṃsārāsakta-cittaḥ saṃścidābhāsaḥ kadācana|
svayaṃ-prakāśa-kūṭasthaṃ svatattvaṃ naiva vettyayam||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 30
units.deva:
न भाति नास्ति कूटस्थ इति वक्ति प्रसङ्गतः।
कर्ता भोक्ताहम् अस्मीति विक्षेपं प्रतिपद्यते॥
units.translation: One says, “The changeless Self does not appear; it does not exist,” and consequently falls into projection: “I am the doer and enjoyer.”
units.iast:
na bhāti nāsti kūṭastha iti vakti prasaṅgataḥ|
kartā bhoktāham asmīti vikṣepaṃ pratipadyate||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 31
units.deva:
अस्ति कूटस्थ इत्यादौ परोक्षं वेत्ति वार्त्तया।
पश्चात् कूटस्थ एवास्मीत्येवं वेत्ति विचारतः॥
units.translation: Through a teacher, one learns indirectly that the changeless Self exists; later, through inquiry, one knows, “I alone am the changeless Self.”
units.iast:
asti kūṭastha ityādau parokṣaṃ vetti vārttayā|
paścāt kūṭastha evāsmītyevaṃ vetti vicārataḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 32
units.deva:
कर्ता भोक्तेत्येवम् आदि-शोक-जातं प्रमुञ्चति।
कृतं कृत्यं प्रापणीयं प्राप्तम् इत्येव तुष्यति॥
units.translation: One is freed from all suffering beginning with “I am the doer and enjoyer,” and is content: “What had to be done is done; what had to be attained is attained.”
units.iast:
kartā bhoktetyevam ādi-śoka-jātaṃ pramuñcati|
kṛtaṃ kṛtyaṃ prāpaṇīyaṃ prāptam ityeva tuṣyati||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 33
units.deva:
अज्ञानम् आवृतिस्तद्वद्-विक्षेपश्च परोक्ष-धीः।
अपरोक्ष-मतिः शोक-मोक्षस्तृप्तिर्निरङ्कुशा॥
units.translation: Ignorance, concealment, projection, indirect knowledge, direct knowledge, the ending of grief, and unbounded contentment [are the seven states].
units.iast:
ajñānam āvṛtistadvad-vikṣepaśca parokṣa-dhīḥ|
aparokṣa-matiḥ śoka-mokṣastṛptirniraṅkuśā||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 34
units.deva:
सप्तावस्था इमाः सन्ति चिदाभासस्य तास्विमौ।
बन्ध-मोक्षौ स्थितौ तत्र तिस्रो बन्ध-कृतः स्मृताः॥
units.translation: These are the seven states of the reflection of consciousness. Bondage and liberation occur among them; the first three are said to cause bondage.
units.iast:
saptāvasthā imāḥ santi cidābhāsasya tāsvimau|
bandha-mokṣau sthitau tatra tisro bandha-kṛtaḥ smṛtāḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 35
units.deva:
न जानामीत्युदासीन-व्यवहारस्य कारणम्।
विचार-प्रागभावेन युक्तम् अज्ञानम् ईरितम्॥
units.translation: Ignorance, linked to the absence of prior inquiry, is said to cause the indifferent stance, “I do not know.”

gloss.en: by the prior absence of inquiry

units.iast:
na jānāmītyudāsīna-vyavahārasya kāraṇam|
vicāra-prāgabhāvena yuktam ajñānam īritam||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 36
units.deva:
अमार्गेण विचार्याथ नास्ति नो भाति चेत्यसौ।
विपरीत-व्यवहृतिरावृतेः कार्यम् इष्यते॥
units.translation: After reasoning by an improper method, one concludes, “It does not exist; it does not appear.” This mistaken view is said to be the effect of concealment.
units.iast:
amārgeṇa vicāryātha nāsti no bhāti cetyasau|
viparīta-vyavahṛtirāvṛteḥ kāryam iṣyate||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 37
units.deva:
देह-द्वय-चिदाभास-रूपो विक्षेप ईरितः।
कर्तृत्वाद्यखिलः शोकः संसाराख्योऽस्य बन्धकः॥
units.translation: Projection is the reflection of consciousness appearing through the two bodies; all suffering beginning with doership is the bondage called saṃsāra.

gloss.en: in the form of the reflection of consciousness

units.iast:
deha-dvaya-cidābhāsa-rūpo vikṣepa īritaḥ|
kartṛtvādyakhilaḥ śokaḥ saṃsārākhyo’sya bandhakaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 38
units.deva:
अज्ञानमावृतिश्चैते विक्षेपात् प्राक् प्रसिद्ध्यतः।
यद्यप्यथाप्यवस्थे ते विक्षेपस्यैव नात्मनः॥
units.translation: Though ignorance and concealment appear before projection, those two states belong to projection alone, not to the Self.
units.iast:
ajñānamāvṛtiścaite vikṣepāt prāk prasiddhyataḥ|
yadyapyathāpyavasthe te vikṣepasyaiva nātmanaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 39
units.deva:
विक्षेपोत्पत्तितः पूर्वम् अपि विक्षेप-संस्कृतिः।
अस्त्येव तदवस्थात्वम् अविरुद्धं ततस्तयोः॥
units.translation: Even before a projection arises, its latent impression exists; therefore, it is consistent to treat those two earlier states as states of projection.

gloss.en: the state of belonging to that

units.iast:
vikṣepotpattitaḥ pūrvam api vikṣepa-saṃskṛtiḥ|
astyeva tadavasthātvam aviruddhaṃ tatastayoḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 40
units.deva:
ब्रह्मण्यारोपितत्वेन ब्रह्मावस्थे इमे इति।
न शङ्कनीयं सर्वासां ब्रह्मण्येवाधिरोपणात्॥
units.translation: Do not conclude that these are states of Brahman merely because they are superimposed on Brahman; all states are superimposed on Brahman alone.
units.iast:
brahmaṇyāropitatvena brahmāvasthe ime iti|
na śaṅkanīyaṃ sarvāsāṃ brahmaṇyevādhiropaṇāt||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verses 41–42
units.deva:
संसार्यहं विबुद्धोऽहं निःशोकस्तुष्ट इत्यपि।
जीवगा उत्तरावस्था भान्ति न ब्रह्मगा यदि॥
तर्ह्यज्ञोऽहं ब्रह्म-सत्त्व-भाने मद्-दृष्टितो न हि।
इति पूर्वे अवस्थे च भासेते जीवगे खलु॥
units.translation: If the later states—“I am bound in saṃsāra,” “I am awakened,” “I am free from grief,” and “I am content”—appear in the jīva and not in Brahman, then surely the earlier states—“I am ignorant” and “Brahman’s reality does not appear to me”—also appear in the jīva.
units.iast:
saṃsāryahaṃ vibuddho’haṃ niḥśokastuṣṭa ityapi|
jīvagā uttarāvasthā bhānti na brahmagā yadi||
tarhyajño’haṃ brahma-sattva-bhāne mad-dṛṣṭito na hi|
iti pūrve avasthe ca bhāsete jīvage khalu||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 43
units.deva:
अज्ञानस्याश्रयो ब्रह्मेत्यधिष्ठानतया जगुः।
जीवावस्थात्वम् अज्ञानाभिमानित्वाद् अवादिषम्॥
units.translation: The teachers said that Brahman is the substratum and support of ignorance. I have said that it is a state of the jīva because of identification with ignorance.

gloss.en: being a state of the jīva

units.iast:
ajñānasyāśrayo brahmetyadhiṣṭhānatayā jaguḥ|
jīvāvasthātvam ajñānābhimānitvād avādiṣam||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 44
units.deva:
ज्ञान-द्वयेन नष्टेऽस्मिन्नज्ञाने तत्कृतावृतिः।
न भाति नास्ति चेत्येषा द्विविधापि विनश्यति॥
units.translation: When this ignorance is destroyed by the two kinds of knowledge, its twofold concealment—“It does not appear” and “It does not exist”—also disappears.

gloss.en: by the two kinds of knowledge

units.iast:
jñāna-dvayena naṣṭe’sminnajñāne tatkṛtāvṛtiḥ|
na bhāti nāsti cetyeṣā dvividhāpi vinaśyati||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 45
units.deva:
परोक्ष-ज्ञानतो नश्येद् असत्त्वावृत्ति-हेतुता।
अपरोक्ष-ज्ञान-नाश्या ह्यभानावृत्ति-हेतुता॥
units.translation: Indirect knowledge removes the cause of the concealment “It does not exist”; direct knowledge removes the cause of the concealment “It does not appear.”

gloss.en: the cause of concealment as nonexistence
to be destroyed by direct knowledge
the cause of concealment as nonappearance

units.iast:
parokṣa-jñānato naśyed asattvāvṛtti-hetutā|
aparokṣa-jñāna-nāśyā hyabhānāvṛtti-hetutā||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 46
units.deva:
अभानावरणे नष्टे जीवत्वारोप-संक्षयात्।
कर्तृत्वाद्यखिलः शोकः संसाराख्यः निवर्तते॥
units.translation: When the concealment of nonappearance is destroyed, the imposition of jīva-hood ends; all suffering beginning with doership—the bondage called saṃsāra—ceases.

gloss.en: because the imposition of jīva-hood ends

units.iast:
abhānāvaraṇe naṣṭe jīvatvāropa-saṃkṣayāt|
kartṛtvādyakhilaḥ śokaḥ saṃsārākhyaḥ nivartate||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 47
units.deva:
निवृत्ते सर्व-संसारे नित्य-मुक्तत्व-भासनात्।
निरङ्कुशा भवेत् तृप्तिः पुनः शोकासमुद्भवात्॥
units.translation: When all saṃsāra has ceased, the ever-free nature shines; with grief no longer arising, unbounded contentment follows.
units.iast:
nivṛtte sarva-saṃsāre nitya-muktatva-bhāsanāt|
niraṅkuśā bhavet tṛptiḥ punaḥ śokāsamudbhavāt||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 48
units.deva:
अपरोक्ष-ज्ञान-शोक-निवृत्त्याख्ये उभे इमे।
अवस्थे जीवगे ब्रूते आत्मानं चेदिति श्रुतिः॥
units.translation: The Śruti says that the passage “If one knows the Self…” presents these two states in the jīva: direct knowledge and the removal of grief.
units.iast:
aparokṣa-jñāna-śoka-nivṛttyākhye ubhe ime|
avasthe jīvage brūte ātmānaṃ cediti śrutiḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 49
units.deva:
अयम् इत्यपरोक्षत्वम् उक्तं तद् द्विविधं भवेत्।
विषय-स्वप्रकाशत्वाद् धियाऽप्येवं तदीक्षणात्॥
units.translation: The word “this” is said to indicate immediacy, which is twofold: the object’s self-luminosity and its being seen by the intellect.
units.iast:
ayam ityaparokṣatvam uktaṃ tad dvividhaṃ bhavet|
viṣaya-svaprakāśatvād dhiyā’pyevaṃ tadīkṣaṇāt||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 50
units.deva:
परोक्ष-ज्ञान-कालेऽपि विषय-स्वप्रकाशता।
समा ब्रह्म स्वप्रकाशम् अस्तीत्येवं विबोधनात्॥
units.translation: Even during indirect knowledge, the object’s self-luminosity is the same, because it is taught that Brahman is self-luminous.
units.iast:
parokṣa-jñāna-kāle’pi viṣaya-svaprakāśatā|
samā brahma svaprakāśam astītyevaṃ vibodhanāt||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 51
units.deva:
अहं ब्रह्मेत्यनुल्लिख्य ब्रह्मास्तीत्येवम् उल्लिखेत्।
परोक्ष-ज्ञानम् एतं न भ्रान्तं बाधानिरूपणात्॥
units.translation: Rather than stating “I am Brahman,” one should first state “Brahman exists.” This indirect knowledge is not erroneous, since it is not contradicted.
units.iast:
ahaṃ brahmetyanullikhya brahmāstītyevam ullikhet|
parokṣa-jñānam etaṃ na bhrāntaṃ bādhānirūpaṇāt||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 52
units.deva:
ब्रह्म नास्तीति मानं चेत् स्याद् बाध्येत तदा ध्रुवम्।
न चैवं प्रबलं मानं पश्यामोऽतो न बाध्यते॥
units.translation: If there were valid evidence that Brahman does not exist, [the knowledge that Brahman exists] would certainly be contradicted. But we see no such strong evidence; therefore it is not contradicted.
units.iast:
brahma nāstīti mānaṃ cet syād bādhyeta tadā dhruvam|
na caivaṃ prabalaṃ mānaṃ paśyāmo’to na bādhyate||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 53
units.deva:
व्यक्त्यनुल्लेखमात्रेण भ्रमत्वे स्वर्गधीरपि।
भ्रान्तिः स्याद् व्यक्त्यनुल्लेखात् सामान्योल्लेख-दर्शनात्॥
units.translation: If [the knowledge] is considered false merely because it does not state the particular identity, then belief in heaven would also be false, since scripture presents it generally without that specific statement.

gloss.en: merely by not stating the particular
because the particular is not stated
because a general statement is seen

units.iast:
vyaktyanullekhamātreṇa bhramatve svargadhīrapi|
bhrāntiḥ syād vyaktyanullekhāt sāmānyollekha-darśanāt||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 54
units.deva:
अपरोक्षत्व-योग्यस्य न परोक्षमतिर्भ्रमः।
परोक्षम् इत्यनुल्लेखाद् अर्थात् पारोक्ष्य-सम्भवात्॥
units.translation: Indirect knowledge of what is fit to be known directly is not erroneous: being known indirectly does not mean it is only indirectly knowable.

gloss.en: of what is fit to be known directly

units.iast:
aparokṣatva-yogyasya na parokṣamatirbhramaḥ|
parokṣam ityanullekhād arthāt pārokṣya-sambhavāt||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 55
units.deva:
अंशागृहीतिर्भ्रान्तिश्चेद् घट-ज्ञानं भ्रमो भवेत्।
निरंशस्यापि सांशत्वं व्यावर्त्यांश-विभेदतः॥
units.translation: If failing to grasp one part makes knowledge erroneous, then knowing a pot would also be erroneous. Even the partless can appear divided, because apparent parts are distinguished and set aside.

gloss.en: because apparent parts are distinguished and excluded

units.iast:
aṃśāgṛhītirbhrāntiśced ghaṭa-jñānaṃ bhramo bhavet|
niraṃśasyāpi sāṃśatvaṃ vyāvartyāṃśa-vibhedataḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 56
units.deva:
असत्त्वांशो निवर्तेत परोक्ष-ज्ञानतस्तथा।
अभानांश-निवृत्तिः स्याद् अपरोक्ष-धिया कृता॥
units.translation: Indirect knowledge removes the belief that Brahman does not exist; direct understanding removes the belief that Brahman does not appear.

gloss.en: the removal of the aspect of nonappearance

units.iast:
asattvāṃśo nivarteta parokṣa-jñānatastathā|
abhānāṃśa-nivṛttiḥ syād aparokṣa-dhiyā kṛtā||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 57
units.deva:
दशमोऽस्तीत्यविभ्रान्तं परोक्ष-ज्ञानम् ईक्ष्यते।
ब्रह्मास्तीत्यपि तद्वत् स्याद् अज्ञानावरणं समम्॥
units.translation: “The tenth man exists” is recognized as valid indirect knowledge. Likewise, “Brahman exists” can be valid; in both cases the veil of ignorance is the same.
units.iast:
daśamo’stītyavibhrāntaṃ parokṣa-jñānam īkṣyate|
brahmāstītyapi tadvat syād ajñānāvaraṇaṃ samam||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 58
units.deva:
आत्मा ब्रह्मेति वाक्यार्थे निःशेषेण विचारिते।
व्यक्तिरुल्लिख्यते यद्वद् दशमस्त्वम् असीत्यतः॥
units.translation: When the meaning of the sentence “Ātman is Brahman” has been fully examined, its particular application is stated, as in “You are the tenth.”

gloss.en: in the meaning of the sentence

units.iast:
ātmā brahmeti vākyārthe niḥśeṣeṇa vicārite|
vyaktirullikhyate yadvad daśamastvam asītyataḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 59
units.deva:
दशमः क इति प्रश्ने त्वम् एवेति निराकृते।
गणयित्वा स्वेन सह स्वम् एव दशमं स्मरेत्॥
units.translation: When asked, “Who is the tenth?” and told, “You alone,” he counts himself with the others and recognizes himself as the tenth.
units.iast:
daśamaḥ ka iti praśne tvam eveti nirākṛte|
gaṇayitvā svena saha svam eva daśamaṃ smaret||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 60
units.deva:
दशमोऽस्मीति वाक्योत्था न धीरस्य विहन्यते।
आदि-मध्यावसानेषु न नवत्वस्य संशयः॥
units.translation: The knowledge arising from the statement “I am the tenth” is never contradicted; at the beginning, middle, or end, the nine others are not in doubt.
units.iast:
daśamo’smīti vākyotthā na dhīrasya vihanyate|
ādi-madhyāvasāneṣu na navatvasya saṃśayaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 61
units.deva:
सदेवेत्यादि-वाक्येन ब्रह्म-सत्त्वं परोक्षतः।
गृहीत्वा तत्त्वमस्यादि-वाक्याद् व्यक्तिं समुल्लिखेत्॥
units.translation: Having indirectly grasped Brahman’s existence from statements such as “Being alone [was this],” one should state the direct identity through statements such as “You are That.”

gloss.en: from a statement beginning “You are That”

units.iast:
sadevetyādi-vākyena brahma-sattvaṃ parokṣataḥ|
gṛhītvā tattvamasyādi-vākyād vyaktiṃ samullikhet||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 62
units.deva:
आदि-मध्यावसानेषु स्वस्य ब्रह्मत्व-धीरियम्।
नैव व्यभिचरेत् तस्माद् आपरोक्ष्यं प्रतिष्ठितम्॥
units.translation: This knowledge of one’s identity as Brahman does not deviate at the beginning, middle, or end; therefore its immediacy is established.

gloss.en: at the beginning, middle, and end

units.iast:
ādi-madhyāvasāneṣu svasya brahmatva-dhīriyam|
naiva vyabhicaret tasmād āparokṣyaṃ pratiṣṭhitam||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 63
units.deva:
जन्मादि-कारणत्वाख्य-लक्षणेन भृगुः पुरा।
परोक्षेण गृहीत्वाथ विचारात् व्यक्तिम् ऐक्षत॥
units.translation: Long ago, Bhṛgu indirectly grasped Brahman through the mark of being the cause of creation and the like; then, through inquiry, he saw it directly.
units.iast:
janmādi-kāraṇatvākhya-lakṣaṇena bhṛguḥ purā|
parokṣeṇa gṛhītvātha vicārāt vyaktim aikṣata||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 64
units.deva:
यद्यपि त्वमसीत्यत्र वाक्यं नोचे भृगोः पिता।
तथाप्यन्नं प्राणम् इति विचार्यस्थलम् उक्तवान्॥
units.translation: Though Bhṛgu’s father did not use the statement “You are That,” he nonetheless set out the method by discussing food, prāṇa, and the like.
units.iast:
yadyapi tvamasītyatra vākyaṃ noce bhṛgoḥ pitā|
tathāpyannaṃ prāṇam iti vicāryasthalam uktavān||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 65
units.deva:
अन्न-प्राणादि-कोषेषु सुविचार्य पुनः पुनः।
आनन्द-व्यक्तिम् ईक्षित्वा ब्रह्म-लक्ष्माप्ययूयुजत्॥
units.translation: After carefully examining the sheaths beginning with food and prāṇa again and again, he saw the direct manifestation of bliss and took it as the mark of Brahman.

gloss.en: in the sheaths beginning with food and prāṇa

units.iast:
anna-prāṇādi-koṣeṣu suvicārya punaḥ punaḥ|
ānanda-vyaktim īkṣitvā brahma-lakṣmāpyayūyujat||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 66
units.deva:
सत्यं ज्ञानम् अनन्तं चेत्येवं ब्रह्म-स्वलक्षणम्।
उक्त्वा गुहाहितत्वेन कोशेष्वेतत् प्रदर्शितम्॥
units.translation: After stating Brahman’s own nature as reality, knowledge, and the limitless, the teaching presents it as lodged in the cave within the sheaths.
units.iast:
satyaṃ jñānam anantaṃ cetyevaṃ brahma-svalakṣaṇam|
uktvā guhāhitatvena kośeṣvetat pradarśitam||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 67
units.deva:
पारोक्ष्येण विबुध्येन्द्रो य आत्मेयादि-लक्षणात्।
अपरोक्षी-कर्तुम् इच्छंश्चतुर्वारं गुरुं ययौ॥
units.translation: Indra learned indirectly from the definition beginning “the Self which…”. Wishing to know the Self directly, he went to his teacher four times.
units.iast:
pārokṣyeṇa vibudhyendro ya ātmeyādi-lakṣaṇāt|
aparokṣī-kartum icchaṃścaturvāraṃ guruṃ yayau||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 68
units.deva:
आत्मा वा इदमित्यादौ परोक्षं ब्रह्म-लक्षितम्।
अध्यारोपापवादाभ्यां प्रज्ञानं ब्रह्म दर्शितम्॥
units.translation: At the beginning, the statement “The Self alone was this” indirectly indicates Brahman; through superimposition and retraction, it reveals “Consciousness is Brahman.”
units.iast:
ātmā vā idamityādau parokṣaṃ brahma-lakṣitam|
adhyāropāpavādābhyāṃ prajñānaṃ brahma darśitam||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 69
units.deva:
अवान्तरेण वाक्येन परोक्ष-ब्रह्म-धीर्भवेत्।
सर्वत्रैव महा-वाक्य-विचारात् त्वपरोक्ष-धीः॥
units.translation: An indirect understanding of Brahman may arise from an intermediate statement; direct understanding comes through inquiry into the mahāvākyas.
units.iast:
avāntareṇa vākyena parokṣa-brahma-dhīrbhavet|
sarvatraiva mahā-vākya-vicārāt tvaparokṣa-dhīḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 70
units.deva:
ब्रह्मापारोक्ष्य-सिद्ध्यर्थं महा-वाक्यमितीरितम्।
वाक्यवृत्तावतो ब्रह्मापरोक्ष्ये विमतिर्नहि॥
units.translation: The mahāvākya is stated to establish Brahman’s direct knowledge. Therefore, Vākyavṛtti has no doubt about the direct knowledge of Brahman.

gloss.en: to establish direct knowledge of Brahman
in the direct knowledge of Brahman

units.iast:
brahmāpārokṣya-siddhyarthaṃ mahā-vākyamitīritam|
vākyavṛttāvato brahmāparokṣye vimatirnahi||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 71
units.deva:
आलम्बनतया भाति योऽस्मत्-प्रत्यय-शब्दयोः।
अन्तःकरण-सम्भिन्न-बोधः स त्वम्-पदाभिधः॥
units.translation: The awareness that appears as the basis of the thought and word “I,” conditioned by the inner instrument, is what the word “you” denotes.

gloss.en: awareness conditioned by the inner instrument

units.iast:
ālambanatayā bhāti yo’smat-pratyaya-śabdayoḥ|
antaḥkaraṇa-sambhinna-bodhaḥ sa tvam-padābhidhaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 72
units.deva:
मायोपाधिर्जगद्-योनिः सर्वज्ञत्वादि-लक्षणः।
पारोक्ष्य-शबलः सत्याद्यात्मकस्तत्पदाभिधः॥
units.translation: The word “That” denotes Brahman as the source of the world, associated with Māyā as an adjunct, marked by omniscience, and known indirectly through existence and the like.

gloss.en: marked by omniscience and the like
of the nature of existence and the like

units.iast:
māyopādhirjagad-yoniḥ sarvajñatvādi-lakṣaṇaḥ|
pārokṣya-śabalaḥ satyādyātmakastatpadābhidhaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 73
units.deva:
प्रत्यक्-परोक्षतैकस्य स-द्वितीयत्व-पूर्णता।
विरुद्ध्येते यतस्तस्माल्लक्षणा सम्प्रवर्तते॥
units.translation: Because inwardness and remoteness, and having a second and being complete, conflict in one and the same reality, an implied meaning is used.
units.iast:
pratyak-parokṣataikasya sa-dvitīyatva-pūrṇatā|
viruddhyete yatastasmāllakṣaṇā sampravartate||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 74
units.deva:
तत्त्वमस्यादि-वाक्येषु लक्षणा भाग-लक्षणा।
सोऽयमित्यादि-वाक्यस्थ-पदयोरिव नापरा॥
units.translation: In statements such as “You are That,” the implied meaning is partial indication, as in the two words of “That is this”; no other kind is intended.

gloss.en: in statements such as “You are That”
in a statement such as “That is this”

units.iast:
tattvamasyādi-vākyeṣu lakṣaṇā bhāga-lakṣaṇā|
so’yamityādi-vākyastha-padayoriva nāparā||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 75
units.deva:
संसर्गो वा विशिष्टो वा वाक्यार्थो नात्र संमतः।
अखण्डैक-रसत्वेन वाक्यार्थो विदुषां मतः॥
units.translation: The sentence is not taken here to mean connection or qualified difference. The wise take its meaning as indivisible oneness.
units.iast:
saṃsargo vā viśiṣṭo vā vākyārtho nātra saṃmataḥ|
akhaṇḍaika-rasatvena vākyārtho viduṣāṃ mataḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 76
units.deva:
प्रत्यग्-बोधो य आभाति सोऽद्वयानन्द-लक्षणः।
अद्वयानन्द-रूपश्च प्रत्यग्-बोधैक-लक्षणः॥
units.translation: The awareness within that shines is marked by nondual fullness; nondual fullness itself is marked by the awareness within.

gloss.en: of the nature of nondual fullness

units.iast:
pratyag-bodho ya ābhāti so’dvayānanda-lakṣaṇaḥ|
advayānanda-rūpaśca pratyag-bodhaika-lakṣaṇaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verses 77–78
units.deva:
इत्थम् अन्योऽन्य-तादात्म्य-प्रतिपत्तिर्यदा भवेत्।
अब्रह्मत्वं त्वमर्थस्य व्यवर्त्येत तदैव हि॥
तदर्थस्य च पारोक्ष्यं यद्येवं किं ततः शृणु।
पूर्णानन्दैक-रूपेण प्रत्यग्-बोधोऽवशिष्यते॥
units.translation: When mutual identity is understood in this way, the “not Brahman” status of the meaning of “you” is removed, and the remoteness of the meaning of “That” is removed as well. What follows? Listen: inward awareness remains, of the nature of complete nondual fullness.

gloss.en: the status of not being Brahman
of the nature of complete nondual fullness

units.iast:
ittham anyo’nya-tādātmya-pratipattiryadā bhavet|
abrahmatvaṃ tvamarthasya vyavartyeta tadaiva hi||
tadarthasya ca pārokṣyaṃ yadyevaṃ kiṃ tataḥ śṛṇu|
pūrṇānandaika-rūpeṇa pratyag-bodho’vaśiṣyate||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 79
units.deva:
एवं सति महा-वाक्यात् परोक्ष-ज्ञानम् ईर्यते।
यैस्तेषां शास्त्र-सिद्धान्त-विज्ञानं शोभतेतराम्॥
units.translation: If one says that the mahāvākya gives only indirect knowledge, then that person’s grasp of the scripture’s conclusion is truly “brilliant.”
units.iast:
evaṃ sati mahā-vākyāt parokṣa-jñānam īryate|
yaisteṣāṃ śāstra-siddhānta-vijñānaṃ śobhatetarām||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 80
units.deva:
आस्तां शास्त्रस्य सिद्धान्तो युक्त्या वाक्यात् परोक्ष-धीः।
स्वर्गादि-वाक्यवन्नेवं दशमे व्यभिचारतः॥
units.translation: Leave aside the scripture’s conclusion: reasoning says a statement gives only indirect knowledge, as with statements about heaven and the like. But the tenth-man example shows that this is not always so.

gloss.en: like statements about heaven and the like

units.iast:
āstāṃ śāstrasya siddhānto yuktyā vākyāt parokṣa-dhīḥ|
svargādi-vākyavannevaṃ daśame vyabhicārataḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 81
units.deva:
स्वतोऽपरोक्ष-जीवस्य ब्रह्मत्वम् अभिवांछतः।
नश्येत् सिद्धापरोक्षत्वम् इति युक्तिर्महत्यहो॥
units.translation: To claim that the already direct self-knowledge of the jīva would disappear when it seeks identity with Brahman—what great reasoning, indeed!
units.iast:
svato’parokṣa-jīvasya brahmatvam abhivāṃchataḥ|
naśyet siddhāparokṣatvam iti yuktirmahatyaho||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 82
units.deva:
वृद्धिम् इष्टवतो मूलम् अपि नष्टम् इतीरितम्।
लौकिकं वचनं सार्थं सम्पन्नं त्वत्-प्रसादतः॥
units.translation: By your grace, a worldly saying has come true: “One who seeks profit may lose even the principal.”
units.iast:
vṛddhim iṣṭavato mūlam api naṣṭam itīritam|
laukikaṃ vacanaṃ sārthaṃ sampannaṃ tvat-prasādataḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 83
units.deva:
अन्तःकरण-संभिन्न-बोधो जीवोऽपरोक्षताम्।
अर्हत्युपाधि-सद्-भावान्न तु ब्रह्मानुपाधितः॥
units.translation: The individual awareness associated with the mind can be directly known because its limiting adjunct is present; Brahman without an adjunct cannot.
units.iast:
antaḥkaraṇa-saṃbhinna-bodho jīvo’parokṣatām|
arhatyupādhi-sad-bhāvānna tu brahmānupādhitaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 84
units.deva:
नैवं ब्रह्मत्व-बोधस्य सोपाधि-विषयत्वतः।
यावद् विदेह-कैवल्यम् उपाधेरनिवारणात्॥
units.translation: Not so: knowledge of Brahmanhood has an adjunct as its object, since the adjunct cannot be removed until final liberation beyond embodiment.

gloss.en: because its object is associated with an adjunct

units.iast:
naivaṃ brahmatva-bodhasya sopādhi-viṣayatvataḥ|
yāvad videha-kaivalyam upādheranivāraṇāt||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 85
units.deva:
अन्तःकरण-साहित्य-राहित्याभ्यां विशिष्यते।
उपाधिर्जीव-भावस्य ब्रह्मतायाश्च नान्यथा॥
units.translation: The limiting adjunct distinguishes the state of the jīva from Brahman by the presence or absence of the inner instrument; otherwise, there is no difference.

gloss.en: by the presence and absence of the inner instrument
of the state of the jīva

units.iast:
antaḥkaraṇa-sāhitya-rāhityābhyāṃ viśiṣyate|
upādhirjīva-bhāvasya brahmatāyāśca nānyathā||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 86
units.deva:
यथा विधिरुपाधिः स्यात् प्रतिषेधस्तथा न किम्।
सुवर्ण-लौह-भेदेन शृङ्खलात्वं न भिद्यते॥
units.translation: If affirmation can be a limiting adjunct, why can negation not be one too? A chain is a chain whether made of gold or iron.

gloss.en: the state of being a chain

units.iast:
yathā vidhirupādhiḥ syāt pratiṣedhastathā na kim|
suvarṇa-lauha-bhedena śṛṅkhalātvaṃ na bhidyate||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 87
units.deva:
अतद्व्यावृत्ति-रूपेण साक्षाद्-विधि-मुखेन च।
वेदान्तानां प्रवृत्तिः स्याद् द्विधेत्याचार्य-भाषितम्॥
units.translation: The teachers say that Vedānta proceeds in two ways: by excluding what is not That and by direct affirmation.

gloss.en: in the form of excluding what is not That

units.iast:
atadvyāvṛtti-rūpeṇa sākṣād-vidhi-mukhena ca|
vedāntānāṃ pravṛttiḥ syād dvidhetyācārya-bhāṣitam||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 88
units.deva:
अहमर्थ-परित्यागाद् अहं ब्रह्मेति धीः कुतः।
नैवम् अंशस्य हि त्यागो भाग-लक्षणयोदितः॥
units.translation: If the meaning of “I” were entirely abandoned, how could the understanding “I am Brahman” arise? Not so: partial indication gives up only one aspect.
units.iast:
ahamartha-parityāgād ahaṃ brahmeti dhīḥ kutaḥ|
naivam aṃśasya hi tyāgo bhāga-lakṣaṇayoditaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 89
units.deva:
अन्तःकरण-सन्त्यागाद् अवशिष्टे चिदात्मनि।
अहं ब्रह्मेति वाक्येन ब्रह्मत्वं साक्षिणीक्ष्यते॥
units.translation: When the inner instrument is set aside and the Self as consciousness remains, the sentence “I am Brahman” reveals Brahmanhood in the witness.

gloss.en: when the inner instrument is set aside

units.iast:
antaḥkaraṇa-santyāgād avaśiṣṭe cidātmani|
ahaṃ brahmeti vākyena brahmatvaṃ sākṣiṇīkṣyate||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 90
units.deva:
स्व-प्रकाशोऽपि साक्ष्येष धी-वृत्त्या व्याप्यतेऽन्यवत्।
फल-व्याप्यत्वम् एवास्य शास्त्र-कृद्भिर्निवारितम्॥
units.translation: Even the self-luminous witness is grasped by a mental state, as other objects are; scripture teachers deny that it must be made known by the result of cognition.

gloss.en: being encompassed by the result of cognition

units.iast:
sva-prakāśo’pi sākṣyeṣa dhī-vṛttyā vyāpyate’nyavat|
phala-vyāpyatvam evāsya śāstra-kṛdbhirnivāritam||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 91
units.deva:
बुद्धि-तत्-स्थ-चिदाभासौ द्वावपि व्याप्नुतो घटम्।
तत्राज्ञानं धिया नश्येद् आभासेन घटः स्फुरेत्॥
units.translation: Both the intellect and the reflection of consciousness reach the pot. There, the intellect removes ignorance, and the reflection reveals the pot.

gloss.en: the intellect and the reflection of consciousness located in it

units.iast:
buddhi-tat-stha-cidābhāsau dvāvapi vyāpnuto ghaṭam|
tatrājñānaṃ dhiyā naśyed ābhāsena ghaṭaḥ sphuret||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 92
units.deva:
ब्रह्मण्यज्ञान-नाशाय वृत्ति-व्याप्तिरपेक्षिता।
स्वयं-स्फुरण-रूपत्वान्नाभास उपयुज्यते॥
units.translation: To remove ignorance about Brahman, a mental cognition is needed. Because Brahman is self-luminous, the reflection of consciousness is not needed to reveal it.
units.iast:
brahmaṇyajñāna-nāśāya vṛtti-vyāptirapekṣitā|
svayaṃ-sphuraṇa-rūpatvānnābhāsa upayujyate||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 93
units.deva:
चक्षुर्दीपावपेक्ष्येते घटादेर्दर्शने तथा।
न दीप-दर्शने किन्तु चक्षुरेकम् अपेक्ष्यते॥
units.translation: To see a pot and the like, both the eye and a lamp are needed; to see the lamp itself, only the eye is needed.

gloss.en: of a pot and the like

units.iast:
cakṣurdīpāvapekṣyete ghaṭāderdarśane tathā|
na dīpa-darśane kintu cakṣurekam apekṣyate||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 94
units.deva:
स्थितोऽप्यसौ चिदाभासो ब्रह्मण्येकीभवेत् परम्।
न तु ब्रह्मण्यतिशयं फलं कुर्याद् घटादिवत्॥
units.translation: Though it exists, the reflection of consciousness is ultimately one with Brahman; it does not reveal anything new about Brahman as it does about a pot.

gloss.en: as with a pot and the like

units.iast:
sthito’pyasau cidābhāso brahmaṇyekībhavet param|
na tu brahmaṇyatiśayaṃ phalaṃ kuryād ghaṭādivat||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 95
units.deva:
अप्रमेयम् अनादिं चेत्यत्र श्रुत्येदमीरितम्।
मनसैवेदम् आप्तव्यम् इति धी-व्याप्यता श्रुता॥
units.translation: Śruti says that Brahman is immeasurable and beginningless; it also says that this is to be attained by the mind. Thus cognition by the mind is taught.
units.iast:
aprameyam anādiṃ cetyatra śrutyedamīritam|
manasaivedam āptavyam iti dhī-vyāpyatā śrutā||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 96
units.deva:
आत्मानं चेद् विजानीयाद् अयम् अस्मीति वाक्यतः।
ब्रह्मात्म-व्यक्तिम् उल्लिख्य यो बोधः सोऽभिधीयते॥
units.translation: The knowledge that states the direct identity of Brahman and the Self is called [direct knowledge], arising from the sentence “If one knows the Self, ‘I am this.’”

gloss.en: the direct identity of Brahman and the Self

units.iast:
ātmānaṃ ced vijānīyād ayam asmīti vākyataḥ|
brahmātma-vyaktim ullikhya yo bodhaḥ so’bhidhīyate||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 97
units.deva:
अस्तु बोधोऽपरोक्षोऽत्र महा-वाक्यात् तथाप्यसौ।
न दृढः श्रवणादीनाम् आचार्यैः पुनरीरणात्॥
units.translation: Direct knowledge may arise here from a mahāvākya; nevertheless, it may not be firm. Therefore, the teachers prescribe repeated listening and the like.
units.iast:
astu bodho’parokṣo’tra mahā-vākyāt tathāpyasau|
na dṛḍhaḥ śravaṇādīnām ācāryaiḥ punarīraṇāt||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 98
units.deva:
अहं ब्रह्मेति वाक्यार्थ-बोधो यावद् दृढीभवेत्।
शमादि-सहितस्तावद् अभ्यसेच्छ्रवणादिकम्॥
units.translation: Until the understanding of “I am Brahman” becomes firm, one should continue listening and the like, together with composure and other disciplines.

gloss.en: together with composure and the like

units.iast:
ahaṃ brahmeti vākyārtha-bodho yāvad dṛḍhībhavet|
śamādi-sahitastāvad abhyasecchravaṇādikam||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 99
units.deva:
बाधं सन्ति ह्यदार्ढ्यस्य हेतवः श्रुत्यनेकता।
असम्भाव्यत्वम् अर्थस्य विपरीता च भावना॥
units.translation: The causes of an unsteady understanding are conflicting scriptural statements, the apparent impossibility of the meaning, and contrary habitual thinking.
units.iast:
bādhaṃ santi hyadārḍhyasya hetavaḥ śrutyanekatā|
asambhāvyatvam arthasya viparītā ca bhāvanā||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 100
units.deva:
शाखाभेदात् कामभेदाच्छ्रुतं कर्माण्यथान्यथा।
एवम् अत्रापि मा शङ्कीत्यतः श्रवणम् आचरेत्॥
units.translation: Different Vedic branches and differing aims teach different ritual actions; do not let that create doubt here. Therefore, one should undertake listening.
units.iast:
śākhābhedāt kāmabhedācchrutaṃ karmāṇyathānyathā|
evam atrāpi mā śaṅkītyataḥ śravaṇam ācaret||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 101
units.deva:
वेदान्तानाम् अशेषाणाम् आदि-मध्यावसानतः।
ब्रह्मात्मन्येव तात्पर्यम् इति धीः श्रवणं भवेत्॥
units.translation: Listening consists in understanding that all Vedānta, from beginning to middle to end, has its purport in Brahman as the Self.
units.iast:
vedāntānām aśeṣāṇām ādi-madhyāvasānataḥ|
brahmātmanyeva tātparyam iti dhīḥ śravaṇaṃ bhavet||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 102
units.deva:
समन्वयाध्याय एतत् सूक्तं धी-स्वास्थ्य-कारिभिः।
तर्कैः सम्भावनार्थस्य द्वितीयाध्यायः ईरिता॥
units.translation: The chapter on harmonization states this well, as explained by those who clarify understanding; the second chapter sets out reasoning to establish the plausibility of its meaning.

gloss.en: by those who bring clarity to understanding
for establishing the plausibility of the meaning

units.iast:
samanvayādhyāya etat sūktaṃ dhī-svāsthya-kāribhiḥ|
tarkaiḥ sambhāvanārthasya dvitīyādhyāyaḥ īritā||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 103
units.deva:
बहु-जन्म-दृढाभ्यासाद् देहादिष्वात्मधीः क्षणात्।
पुनः पुनरुदेत्येवं जगत्-सत्यत्व-धीरपि॥
units.translation: Because of strong conditioning from many births, the thought “I am the body” and the like, and the belief that the world is real, keep arising moment after moment.

gloss.en: in the body and the like
the belief that the world is real

units.iast:
bahu-janma-dṛḍhābhyāsād dehādiṣvātmadhīḥ kṣaṇāt|
punaḥ punarudetyevaṃ jagat-satyatva-dhīrapi||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 104
units.deva:
विपरीता भावनेयम् ऐकाग्र्यात् सा निवर्तते।
तत्त्वोपदेशात् प्राग् एव भवत्येतदुपासनात्॥
units.translation: This contrary habit of thought is removed by one-pointedness; that one-pointedness is developed through worship, even before instruction in truth.
units.iast:
viparītā bhāvaneyam aikāgryāt sā nivartate|
tattvopadeśāt prāg eva bhavatyetadupāsanāt||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 105
units.deva:
उपास्तयोऽत एवात्र ब्रह्म-शास्त्रेऽपि चिन्तिताः।
प्रागनभ्यासिनः पश्चाद् ब्रह्माभ्यासेन तद् भवेत्॥
units.translation: Therefore, worship practices are also discussed here in the teaching of Brahman. For those who did not practice earlier, one-pointedness later arises through contemplation of Brahman.
units.iast:
upāstayo’ta evātra brahma-śāstre’pi cintitāḥ|
prāganabhyāsinaḥ paścād brahmābhyāsena tad bhavet||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 106
units.deva:
तच्-चिन्तनं तत्-कथनम् अन्योन्यं तत्-प्रबोधनम्।
एतद्-एक-परत्वं च ब्रह्माभ्यासं विदुर्बुधाः॥
units.translation: The wise call contemplation of Brahman: thinking of it, speaking of it, teaching one another about it, and keeping it as the sole aim.
units.iast:
tac-cintanaṃ tat-kathanam anyonyaṃ tat-prabodhanam|
etad-eka-paratvaṃ ca brahmābhyāsaṃ vidurbudhāḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 107
units.deva:
तम् एव धीरो विज्ञाय प्रज्ञां कुर्वीत ब्राह्मणः।
नानुध्यायाद् बहुञ्छब्दान् वाचो विग्लापनं हि तत्॥
units.translation: A wise brāhmaṇa, knowing that alone, should cultivate understanding and not dwell on many words; that only wears out speech.
units.iast:
tam eva dhīro vijñāya prajñāṃ kurvīta brāhmaṇaḥ|
nānudhyāyād bahuñchabdān vāco viglāpanaṃ hi tat||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 108
units.deva:
अनन्याश्चिन्तयन्तो मां ये जनाः पर्युपासते।
तेषां नित्याभियुक्तानां योगक्षेमं वहाम्यहम्॥
units.translation: Those who worship Me, thinking of Me as nonseparate and always remaining united with Me—I secure what they lack and protect what they have.
units.iast:
ananyāścintayanto māṃ ye janāḥ paryupāsate|
teṣāṃ nityābhiyuktānāṃ yogakṣemaṃ vahāmyaham||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 109
units.deva:
इति श्रुति-स्मृती नित्यम् आत्मन्येकाग्रतां धियः।
विधत्त विपरीताया भावनायाः क्षयाय हि॥
units.translation: Thus Śruti and Smṛti continually prescribe one-pointed attention on the Self to wear away contrary habit of thought.
units.iast:
iti śruti-smṛtī nityam ātmanyekāgratāṃ dhiyaḥ|
vidhatta viparītāyā bhāvanāyāḥ kṣayāya hi||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 110
units.deva:
यद् यथा वर्तते तस्य तत्त्वं हित्वान्यथात्व-धीः।
विपरीत-भावना स्यात् पित्रादावरि-धीर्यथा॥
units.translation: To set aside what something truly is and think of it as otherwise is contrary thinking, as when one regards a father and the like as an enemy.

gloss.en: the thought that it is otherwise
in one’s father and the like

units.iast:
yad yathā vartate tasya tattvaṃ hitvānyathātva-dhīḥ|
viparīta-bhāvanā syāt pitrādāvari-dhīryathā||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 111
units.deva:
आत्मा देहादि-भिन्नोऽयं मिथ्या चेदं जगत् तयोः।
देहाद्यात्मत्व-सत्यत्व-धीर्विपर्यय-भावना॥
units.translation: The Self is distinct from the body and the like, and this world is unreal. Contrary thinking is the belief that the body is the Self and the world is real.

gloss.en: distinct from the body and the like
the body and the like as the Self

units.iast:
ātmā dehādi-bhinno’yaṃ mithyā cedaṃ jagat tayoḥ|
dehādyātmatva-satyatva-dhīrviparyaya-bhāvanā||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 112
units.deva:
तत्त्व-भावनया नश्येत् सातो देहातिरिक्तताम्।
आत्मनो भावयेत् तद्वन् मिथ्यात्वं जगतोऽनिशम्॥
units.translation: That contrary thought should perish through contemplation of truth. Therefore, one should contemplate the Self’s distinctness from the body and, likewise, the world’s unreality continually.
units.iast:
tattva-bhāvanayā naśyet sāto dehātiriktatām|
ātmano bhāvayet tadvan mithyātvaṃ jagato’niśam||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 113
units.deva:
किं मन्त्र-जपवन् मूर्ति-ध्यानवच् चात्म-भेद-धीः।
जगन्मिथ्यात्व-धीश्चात्र व्यावर्त्या स्यादु तान्यथा॥
units.translation: Should one cultivate the understanding that the Self is distinct [from the body] and the world is unreal by mantra repetition or image meditation, or in some other way?

gloss.en: the understanding that the Self is distinct
the understanding that the world is unreal

units.iast:
kiṃ mantra-japavan mūrti-dhyānavac cātma-bheda-dhīḥ|
jaganmithyātva-dhīścātra vyāvartyā syādu tānyathā||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 114
units.deva:
अन्यथेति विजानीहि दृष्टार्थत्वेन भुक्तिवत्।
बुभुक्षुर्जपवद् भुङ्क्ते न कश्चिन्नियतः क्वचित्॥
units.translation: Understand the other method as having a result seen here and now, like eating: a hungry person eats without a fixed procedure prescribed for them.

gloss.en: as having a result seen directly

units.iast:
anyatheti vijānīhi dṛṣṭārthatvena bhuktivat|
bubhukṣurjapavad bhuṅkte na kaścinniyataḥ kvacit||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 115
units.deva:
अश्नाति वा न वाश्नाति भुङ्क्ते वा स्वेच्छयान्यथा।
येन केन प्रकारेण क्षुधाम् अपनिनीषति॥
units.translation: Whether one eats, fasts, or does something else by choice, one seeks by whatever means to remove hunger.
units.iast:
aśnāti vā na vāśnāti bhuṅkte vā svecchayānyathā|
yena kena prakāreṇa kṣudhām apaninīṣati||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 116
units.deva:
नियमेन जपं कुर्याद् अकृतौ प्रत्यवायतः।
अन्यथा-करणेऽनर्थः स्वर-वर्ण-विपर्ययात्॥
units.translation: Mantra repetition must follow rules, because failing to do so brings an adverse result. Done improperly, it can become meaningless through altered accent or mispronounced sounds.

gloss.en: because of altered accent or sound

units.iast:
niyamena japaṃ kuryād akṛtau pratyavāyataḥ|
anyathā-karaṇe’narthaḥ svara-varṇa-viparyayāt||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 117
units.deva:
क्षुधेव दृष्ट-बाधाकृद् विपरीता च भावना।
जेया केनाप्युपायेन नास्त्यत्रानुष्ठितेः क्रमः॥
units.translation: Like hunger, contrary thinking causes visible distress; it should be conquered by any means, with no fixed ritual procedure here.
units.iast:
kṣudheva dṛṣṭa-bādhākṛd viparītā ca bhāvanā|
jeyā kenāpyupāyena nāstyatrānuṣṭhiteḥ kramaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 118
units.deva:
उपायः पूर्वम् एवोक्तस्तच्-चिन्ता-कथनादिकः।
एतद् एक-परत्वेऽपि निर्बन्धो ध्यानवन् न हि॥
units.translation: The method was already stated: contemplating it, discussing it, and the like. Even when giving this one’s full attention, there is no rigid rule as in formal meditation.

gloss.en: consisting of contemplating, discussing it, and the like
in giving this one’s full attention

units.iast:
upāyaḥ pūrvam evoktastac-cintā-kathanādikaḥ|
etad eka-paratve’pi nirbandho dhyānavan na hi||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 119
units.deva:
मूर्ति-प्रत्यय-सान्तत्यम् अन्यानन्तरितं धियः।
ध्यानं तत्रातिनिर्बन्धो मनसश्चञ्चलात्मनः॥
units.translation: Meditation on an image is a continuous stream of that image-thought, uninterrupted by other thoughts; this requires strict restraint of the naturally restless mind.

gloss.en: a continuous stream of the image-thought

units.iast:
mūrti-pratyaya-sāntatyam anyānantaritaṃ dhiyaḥ|
dhyānaṃ tatrātinirbandho manasaścañcalātmanaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 120
units.deva:
चञ्चलं हि मनः कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवद् दृढम्।
तस्याहं निग्रहं मन्ये वायोरिव सुदुष्करम्॥
units.translation: The mind is restless, turbulent, strong, and stubborn, O Kṛṣṇa; I think it is as hard to restrain as the wind.
units.iast:
cañcalaṃ hi manaḥ kṛṣṇa pramāthi balavad dṛḍham|
tasyāhaṃ nigrahaṃ manye vāyoriva suduṣkaram||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 121
units.deva:
अप्यब्धि-पानान् महतः सुमेरून्मूलनाद् अपि।
अपि वह्न्यशनात् साधो विषमश्चित्तनिग्रहः॥
units.translation: O good one, restraining the mind is harder than drinking the ocean, uprooting Mount Sumeru, or eating fire.
units.iast:
apyabdhi-pānān mahataḥ sumerūnmūlanād api|
api vahnyaśanāt sādho viṣamaścittanigrahaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 122
units.deva:
कथनादौ न निर्बन्धः शृङ्खला-बद्ध-देहवत्।
किन्त्वनन्तेतिहासाद्यैर्विनोदो नाट्यवद् धियः॥
units.translation: There is no compulsion about discussion and the like as if one’s body were chained. Rather, epics and the like engage the mind as a play does.

gloss.en: like a body bound by chains
through countless epics and the like

units.iast:
kathanādau na nirbandhaḥ śṛṅkhalā-baddha-dehavat|
kintvanantetihāsādyairvinodo nāṭyavad dhiyaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 123
units.deva:
चिद् एवात्मा जगन् मिथ्येत्यत्र पर्यवसानतः।
निदिध्यासन-विक्षेपो नेतिहासादिभिर्भवेत्॥
units.translation: Since the conclusion here is “Consciousness alone is the Self; the world is unreal,” epics and the like do not distract from contemplation.
units.iast:
cid evātmā jagan mithyetyatra paryavasānataḥ|
nididhyāsana-vikṣepo netihāsādibhirbhavet||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 124
units.deva:
कृषि-वाणिज्य-सेवादौ काव्य-तर्कादिकेषु च।
विक्षिप्यते प्रवृत्ता धीस्तैस्तत्त्व-स्मृत्यसम्भवात्॥
units.translation: A mind engaged in farming, commerce, service, poetry, argument, and the like becomes distracted, because remembering the truth is then difficult.

gloss.en: in farming, commerce, service, and the like
in poetry, argument, and the like
because remembering the truth is difficult

units.iast:
kṛṣi-vāṇijya-sevādau kāvya-tarkādikeṣu ca|
vikṣipyate pravṛttā dhīstaistattva-smṛtyasambhavāt||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 125
units.deva:
अनुसन्दधतैवात्र भोजनादौ प्रवर्तितुम्।
शक्यतेऽत्यन्त-विक्षेपाभावाद् आशु पुनः स्मृतेः॥
units.translation: By keeping the teaching in view, one can engage in eating and the like; there is no prolonged distraction because recollection returns quickly.
units.iast:
anusandadhataivātra bhojanādau pravartitum|
śakyate’tyanta-vikṣepābhāvād āśu punaḥ smṛteḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 126
units.deva:
तत्त्व-विस्मृतिमात्रान् नानर्थः किन्तु विपर्ययात्।
विपर्येतुं न कालोऽस्ति झटिति स्मरतः क्वचित्॥
units.translation: Mere forgetting of the truth is not harmful; error comes from thinking wrongly. For one who remembers quickly, there is no time for a mistaken view to take hold.

gloss.en: from mere forgetting of the truth

units.iast:
tattva-vismṛtimātrān nānarthaḥ kintu viparyayāt|
viparyetuṃ na kālo’sti jhaṭiti smarataḥ kvacit||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 127
units.deva:
तत्त्व-स्मृतेरवसरो नास्त्यन्याभ्यास-शालिनः।
प्रत्युताभ्यास-घातित्वाद् बलात् तत्त्वम् उपेक्ष्यते॥
units.translation: One habitually absorbed in other pursuits leaves no opening to recall the truth; those habits instead overpower and suppress it.

gloss.en: for one habituated to other pursuits
because of the obstructive force of habit

units.iast:
tattva-smṛteravasaro nāstyanyābhyāsa-śālinaḥ|
pratyutābhyāsa-ghātitvād balāt tattvam upekṣyate||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 128
units.deva:
तम् एवैकं विजानीत ह्यन्या वाचो विमुञ्चथ।
इति श्रुतं तथान्यत्र वाचो विग्लापनं त्विति॥
units.translation: “Know that One alone; give up all other words.” Thus Śruti declares, and elsewhere says, “Words are only a weariness of speech.”
units.iast:
tam evaikaṃ vijānīta hyanyā vāco vimuñcatha|
iti śrutaṃ tathānyatra vāco viglāpanaṃ tviti||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 129
units.deva:
आहारादि-त्यजन् नैव जीवेच् छास्त्रान्तरं त्यजन्।
किं न जीवसि येनैवं करोष्यत्र दुराग्रहम्॥
units.translation: You would not live if you gave up food and the like; but would giving up other treatises make you unable to live? Why cling to them so stubbornly?
units.iast:
āhārādi-tyajan naiva jīvec chāstrāntaraṃ tyajan|
kiṃ na jīvasi yenaivaṃ karoṣyatra durāgraham||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 130
units.deva:
जनकादेः कथं राज्यम् इति चेद् दृढ-बोधतः।
तथा तवापि चेत् तर्कं पठ यद्वा कृषिं कुरु॥
units.translation: If you ask how Janaka and the others could rule a kingdom, it was because their knowledge was firm. If yours is just as firm, study logic or farm as you please.
units.iast:
janakādeḥ kathaṃ rājyam iti ced dṛḍha-bodhataḥ|
tathā tavāpi cet tarkaṃ paṭha yadvā kṛṣiṃ kuru||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 131
units.deva:
मिथ्यात्व-वासनादार्ढ्ये प्रारब्ध-क्षय-काङ्क्षया।
अक्लिश्यन्तः प्रवर्तन्ते स्वस्व-कर्मानुसारतः॥
units.translation: When conviction in the world’s unreality is firm, one acts according to one’s own karma without distress, while awaiting the exhaustion of prārabdha.

gloss.en: when conviction of unreality is firm
with the wish for prārabdha to be exhausted
according to each one’s own karma

units.iast:
mithyātva-vāsanādārḍhye prārabdha-kṣaya-kāṅkṣayā|
akliśyantaḥ pravartante svasva-karmānusārataḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 132
units.deva:
अतिप्रसङ्गो मा शक्यः स्व-कर्म-वश-वर्तिनाम्।
अस्तु वा कः अत्र शक्येत कर्म वारयितुं वद॥
units.translation: No overextension is involved for those governed by their own karma. Or, be that as it may, who here could prevent karma? Tell me.

gloss.en: for those governed by their own karma

units.iast:
atiprasaṅgo mā śakyaḥ sva-karma-vaśa-vartinām|
astu vā kaḥ atra śakyeta karma vārayituṃ vada||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 133
units.deva:
ज्ञानिनोऽज्ञानिनश् चात्र समेऽप्यारब्ध-कर्मणि।
न क्लेशो ज्ञानिनो धैर्यान् मूढः क्लिश्यत्यधैर्यतः॥
units.translation: Though prārabdha karma is the same for the wise and the unwise, the wise have no distress because of steadiness; the unwise suffer because they lack it.
units.iast:
jñānino’jñāninaś cātra same’pyārabdha-karmaṇi|
na kleśo jñānino dhairyān mūḍhaḥ kliśyatyadhairyataḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 134
units.deva:
मार्गे गन्त्रोर्द्वयोः श्रान्तौ समायाम् अप्यदूरताम्।
जानन् धैर्याद् द्रुतं गच्छेद् अन्यस्तिष्ठति दीन-धीः॥
units.translation: Two travelers may be equally tired on a road. One who knows the destination is near goes quickly with confidence, while the other, discouraged, stays put.
units.iast:
mārge gantrordvayoḥ śrāntau samāyām apyadūratām|
jānan dhairyād drutaṃ gacched anyastiṣṭhati dīna-dhīḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 135
units.deva:
साक्षात्-कृतात्म-धीः सम्यग् अविपर्यय-बाधितः।
किम् इच्छन् कस्य कामाय शरीरम् अनुसंज्वरेत्॥
units.translation: One whose understanding of the Self is direct and free from error—what would they desire, and for whose sake would they suffer along with the body?

gloss.en: one whose understanding of the Self is direct

units.iast:
sākṣāt-kṛtātma-dhīḥ samyag aviparyaya-bādhitaḥ|
kim icchan kasya kāmāya śarīram anusaṃjvaret||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 136
units.deva:
जगन्-मिथ्यात्व-धी-भावाद् आक्षिप्तौ काम्य-कामुकौ।
तयोरभावे सन्तापः शाम्येन् निःस्नेह-दीपवत्॥
units.translation: With the understanding that the world is unreal, both desired objects and the desirer are set aside; without them, distress subsides like a lamp without oil.

gloss.en: the desired object and the desirer

units.iast:
jagan-mithyātva-dhī-bhāvād ākṣiptau kāmya-kāmukau|
tayorabhāve santāpaḥ śāmyen niḥsneha-dīpavat||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 137
units.deva:
गन्धर्व-पत्तने किंचिन् नैन्द्रजालिक-निर्मितम्।
जानन् कामयते किन्तु जिहासति हसन्निदम्॥
units.translation: Knowing that a city of Gandharvas is a magician’s creation, one does not desire anything there; laughing, one lets it go.
units.iast:
gandharva-pattane kiṃcin naindrajālika-nirmitam|
jānan kāmayate kintu jihāsati hasannidam||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 138
units.deva:
आपात-रमणीयेषु भोगेष्वेवं विचारवान्।
नानुरज्जति किन्त्वेतान् दोष-दृष्ट्या जिहासति॥
units.translation: Likewise, one who has inquired does not cling to pleasures attractive at first glance, but abandons them after seeing their defects.
units.iast:
āpāta-ramaṇīyeṣu bhogeṣvevaṃ vicāravān|
nānurajjati kintvetān doṣa-dṛṣṭyā jihāsati||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 139
units.deva:
अर्थानाम् अर्जने क्लेशस्तथैव परिरक्षणे।
नाशे दुःखं व्यये दुःखं धिग् अर्थान् क्लेश-कारिणः॥
units.translation: There is trouble in gaining possessions and in keeping them, grief when they are lost and grief when they are spent. Fie on possessions that bring such trouble.
units.iast:
arthānām arjane kleśastathaiva parirakṣaṇe|
nāśe duḥkhaṃ vyaye duḥkhaṃ dhig arthān kleśa-kāriṇaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 140
units.deva:
मांस-पाञ्चालिकायास्तु यन्त्र-लोलेऽङ्ग-पञ्जरे।
स्नाय्वस्थिग्रन्थिशालिन्याः स्त्रियाः किम् इव शोभनम्॥
units.translation: What is beautiful in a woman, a flesh-doll in a moving frame of limbs, held together by sinews, bones, and joints?
units.iast:
māṃsa-pāñcālikāyāstu yantra-lole’ṅga-pañjare|
snāyvasthigranthiśālinyāḥ striyāḥ kim iva śobhanam||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 141
units.deva:
एवमादिषु शास्त्रेषु दोषाः सम्यक्प्रपञ्चिताः।
विमृशन् अनिशं तानि कथं दुःखेषु मज्जति॥
units.translation: The scriptures set out such faults in detail. Reflecting on them constantly, how could one sink into sorrow?
units.iast:
evamādiṣu śāstreṣu doṣāḥ samyakprapañcitāḥ|
vimṛśan aniśaṃ tāni kathaṃ duḥkheṣu majjati||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 142
units.deva:
क्षुधया पीड्यमानोऽपि न विषं ह्यत्तुमिच्छति।
मिष्टान्नध्वस्ततृड्जानन्नामूढस्तज्जिघत्सति॥
units.translation: Even when tormented by hunger, one does not want to eat poison. A discerning person, knowing that sweet food satisfies craving, wants that [food].

gloss.en: one whose craving is quenched by sweet food

units.iast:
kṣudhayā pīḍyamāno’pi na viṣaṃ hyattumicchati|
miṣṭānnadhvastatṛḍjānannāmūḍhastajjighatsati||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 143
units.deva:
प्रारब्धकर्मप्राबल्याद्भोगेष्विच्छा भवेद्यदि।
क्लिश्यनेव तदाप्येष भुङ्क्ते विष्टिगृहीतवत्॥
units.translation: If desire for pleasures arises because of the force of past karma, this person still suffers while enjoying them, like someone seized for forced labor.

gloss.en: because of the force of already-started karma
like one seized for forced labor

units.iast:
prārabdhakarmaprābalyādbhogeṣvicchā bhavedyadi|
kliśyaneva tadāpyeṣa bhuṅkte viṣṭigṛhītavat||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 144
units.deva:
भुञ्जानास्तानपि बुधाः श्रद्धावन्तः कुटुम्बिनः।
नाद्यापि कर्म नश्छिन्नमिति क्लिश्यन्ति सन्ततम्॥
units.translation: Even while enjoying those things, faithful wise householders continually grieve, thinking, “Our karma has not yet been cut off.”
units.iast:
bhuñjānāstānapi budhāḥ śraddhāvantaḥ kuṭumbinaḥ|
nādyāpi karma naśchinnamiti kliśyanti santatam||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 145
units.deva:
नायं क्लेशोऽत्र संसारतापः किन्तु विरक्तता।
भ्रान्तिज्ञाननिदानो हि तापः सांसारिकः स्मृतः॥
units.translation: This distress is not worldly anguish; it is dispassion. Worldly anguish, they say, is caused by mistaken understanding.

gloss.en: the burning pain of worldly life
having mistaken knowledge as its cause

units.iast:
nāyaṃ kleśo’tra saṃsāratāpaḥ kintu viraktatā|
bhrāntijñānanidāno hi tāpaḥ sāṃsārikaḥ smṛtaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 146
units.deva:
विवेकेन परिक्लिश्यन्नल्पभोगेन तृप्यति।
अन्यथानन्तभोगेऽपि नैव तृप्यति कर्हिचित्॥
units.translation: One who becomes disenchanted through discernment is content with little enjoyment. Otherwise, one is never content, even with endless enjoyment.
units.iast:
vivekena parikliśyannalpabhogena tṛpyati|
anyathānantabhoge’pi naiva tṛpyati karhicit||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 147
units.deva:
न जातु कामः कामानामुपभोगेन शाम्यति।
हविषा कृष्णवर्त्मेव भूय एव अभिवर्धते॥
units.translation: Desire is never quieted by enjoying desired things; like fire fed with ghee, it only grows further.
units.iast:
na jātu kāmaḥ kāmānāmupabhogena śāmyati|
haviṣā kṛṣṇavartmeva bhūya eva abhivardhate||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 148
units.deva:
परिज्ञायोपभुक्तो हि भोगो भवति तुष्टये।
विज्ञाय सेवितश्चौरी मैत्रीमेति न चौरताम्॥
units.translation: Enjoyment taken with full understanding brings contentment. A thief knowingly put to work becomes a friend, not a thief.
units.iast:
parijñāyopabhukto hi bhogo bhavati tuṣṭaye|
vijñāya sevitaścaurī maitrīmeti na cauratām||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 149
units.deva:
मनसो निगृहीतस्य लीलाभोगोऽल्पकोऽपि यः।
तमेवालब्धविस्तारं क्लिष्टत्वाद्बहु मन्यते॥
units.translation: A person whose mind is restrained regards even a little casual enjoyment as abundant, because pursuing it further brings trouble.

gloss.en: for one whose mind is restrained

units.iast:
manaso nigṛhītasya līlābhogo’lpako’pi yaḥ|
tamevālabdhavistāraṃ kliṣṭatvādbahu manyate||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 150
units.deva:
बद्धमुक्तो महीपालो ग्राममात्रेण तुष्यति।
परैर्न बद्धो नाक्रान्तो न राष्ट्रं बहु मन्यते॥
units.translation: A king freed from captivity is content with just a village. One who has never been captured or overrun by enemies does not value a kingdom highly.
units.iast:
baddhamukto mahīpālo grāmamātreṇa tuṣyati|
parairna baddho nākrānto na rāṣṭraṃ bahu manyate||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 151
units.deva:
विवेके जाग्रति सति दोषदर्शनलक्षणे।
कथमारब्धकर्मापि भोगेच्छां जनयिष्यति॥
units.translation: (Question:) When discernment, marked by seeing the faults of pleasures, is awake, how could past karma produce a desire for enjoyment?
units.iast:
viveke jāgrati sati doṣadarśanalakṣaṇe|
kathamārabdhakarmāpi bhogecchāṃ janayiṣyati||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 152
units.deva:
नैष दोषो यतोऽनेकविधं प्रारब्धमीक्ष्यते।
इच्छानिच्छा परेच्छा च प्रारब्धं त्रिविधं स्मृतम्॥
units.translation: (Reply:) There is no inconsistency, because past karma is understood to be of many kinds. It is threefold: with desire, without desire, and through another’s desire.
units.iast:
naiṣa doṣo yato’nekavidhaṃ prārabdhamīkṣyate|
icchānicchā parecchā ca prārabdhaṃ trividhaṃ smṛtam||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 153
units.deva:
अपथ्यसेविन्श्चौरा राजदाररता अपि।
जानन्त एव स्वानर्थमिच्छन्त्यारब्धकर्मतः॥
units.translation: People who consume harmful food, thieves, and those involved with a king’s wife—even knowing the harm to themselves—desire these things because of past karma.

gloss.en: those involved with a king’s wife

units.iast:
apathyasevinścaurā rājadāraratā api|
jānanta eva svānarthamicchantyārabdhakarmataḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 154
units.deva:
न चात्रैतद्वारयितुमीश्वरेणापि शक्यते।
यत ईश्वर एवाह गीतायामर्जुनं प्रति॥
units.translation: And even the Lord cannot prevent this here, because the Lord himself says to Arjuna in the Gītā:
units.iast:
na cātraitadvārayitumīśvareṇāpi śakyate|
yata īśvara evāha gītāyāmarjunaṃ prati||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 155
units.deva:
सदृशं चेष्टते स्वस्याः प्रकृतेर्ज्ञानवानपि।
प्रकृतिं यान्ति भूतानि निग्रहः किं करिष्यति॥
units.translation: Even a wise person acts in keeping with their own nature. Beings follow their nature; what can restraint accomplish?
units.iast:
sadṛśaṃ ceṣṭate svasyāḥ prakṛterjñānavānapi|
prakṛtiṃ yānti bhūtāni nigrahaḥ kiṃ kariṣyati||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 156
units.deva:
अवश्यं भाविभावानां प्रतीकारो भवेद्यदि।
तदा दुःखैर्न लिप्येरन् नलरामयुधिष्ठिराः॥
units.translation: If what is destined to happen could be averted, Nala, Rāma, and Yudhiṣṭhira would not have been touched by sorrow.
units.iast:
avaśyaṃ bhāvibhāvānāṃ pratīkāro bhavedyadi|
tadā duḥkhairna lipyeran nalarāmayudhiṣṭhirāḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 157
units.deva:
न चेश्वरत्वमीशस्य हीयते तावता यतः।
अवश्यं भाविताप्येष ईश्वरेण एव निर्मिता॥
units.translation: Nor is the Lord’s lordship diminished by this, because this inevitability of what must happen was itself made by the Lord.

gloss.en: the inevitability of what must happen

units.iast:
na ceśvaratvamīśasya hīyate tāvatā yataḥ|
avaśyaṃ bhāvitāpyeṣa īśvareṇa eva nirmitā||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 158
units.deva:
प्रश्नोत्तराभ्यामेवैतद्गम्यतेऽर्जुनकृष्णयोः।
अनिच्छापूर्वकं चास्ति प्रारब्धमिति तच्छृणु॥
units.translation: This is understood from the question and answer between Arjuna and Kṛṣṇa: past karma operates even without one’s willing it. Listen to that.
units.iast:
praśnottarābhyāmevaitadgamyate’rjunakṛṣṇayoḥ|
anicchāpūrvakaṃ cāsti prārabdhamiti tacchṛṇu||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 159
units.deva:
अथ केन प्रयुक्तोऽयं पापं चरति पूरुषः।
अनिच्छन्नपि वार्ष्णेय बलादिव नियोजितः॥
units.translation: Then, impelled by what does a person commit wrongdoing, even unwillingly, O Vārṣṇeya, as if compelled by force?
units.iast:
atha kena prayukto’yaṃ pāpaṃ carati pūruṣaḥ|
anicchannapi vārṣṇeya balādiva niyojitaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 160
units.deva:
काम एष क्रोध एष रजोगुणसमुद्भवः।
महाशनो महापाप्मा विद्ध्येनमिह वैरिणम्॥
units.translation: It is desire; it is anger, born of rajas. It is a great devourer and deeply harmful; know it here as the enemy.
units.iast:
kāma eṣa krodha eṣa rajoguṇasamudbhavaḥ|
mahāśano mahāpāpmā viddhyenamiha vairiṇam||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 161
units.deva:
स्वभावजेन कौन्तेय निबद्धः स्वेन कर्मणा।
कर्तुं नेच्छसि यन्मोहात्करिष्यस्यवशोऽपि तत्॥
units.translation: O Kauṇṭeya, bound by your own nature-born karma, you will do—even against your wish—the very thing you refuse to do through delusion.
units.iast:
svabhāvajena kaunteya nibaddhaḥ svena karmaṇā|
kartuṃ necchasi yanmohātkariṣyasyavaśo’pi tat||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 162
units.deva:
नानिच्छन्तो न चेच्छन्तः परदाक्षिण्यसंयुताः।
सुखदुःखे भजन्त्येतत्परेच्छा पूर्वकर्म हि॥
units.translation: Those who, out of consideration for others, are neither unwilling nor eager experience pleasure and pain. This is indeed past karma operating through another’s wish.
units.iast:
nānicchanto na cecchantaḥ paradākṣiṇyasaṃyutāḥ|
sukhaduḥkhe bhajantyetatparecchā pūrvakarma hi||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 163
units.deva:
कथं तर्हि किमिच्छन्नित्येवमिच्छा निषिध्यते।
नेच्छानिषेधः किन्त्विच्छाबाधो भर्जितबीजवत्॥
units.translation: (Question:) Then how is desire denied by the words “desiring what?” (Reply:) Desire is not denied; it is rendered powerless, like a roasted seed.
units.iast:
kathaṃ tarhi kimicchannityevamicchā niṣidhyate|
necchāniṣedhaḥ kintvicchābādho bharjitabījavat||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 164
units.deva:
भर्जितानि तु बीजानि सन्त्यकार्यकराणि च।
विद्वदिच्छा यथेष्टव्या सत्त्वबोधान्न कार्यकृत्॥
units.translation: Burnt seeds remain, yet cannot produce a result. A knower’s desires may arise, but through knowledge of reality they do not generate karma.
units.iast:
bharjitāni tu bījāni santyakāryakarāṇi ca|
vidvadicchā yatheṣṭavyā sattvabodhānna kāryakṛt||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 165
units.deva:
दग्धबीजमरोहेऽपि भक्षणायोपयुज्यते।
विद्वदिच्छाप्यल्पभोगं कुर्यान्न व्यसनं बहु॥
units.translation: A burnt seed, though it does not sprout, is still useful as food. Likewise, a knower’s desire may produce a little enjoyment, but not much distress.
units.iast:
dagdhabījamarohe’pi bhakṣaṇāyopayujyate|
vidvadicchāpyalpabhogaṃ kuryānna vyasanaṃ bahu||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 166
units.deva:
भोगेन चरितार्थत्वात्प्रारब्धं कर्म हीयते।
भोक्तव्यसत्यताभ्रान्त्याव्यसनं तत्र जायते॥
units.translation: Through being experienced, past karma is exhausted. Distress arises when one mistakenly believes that what must be experienced is real.

gloss.en: because it has run its course
through the mistaken belief that what is to be experienced is real

units.iast:
bhogena caritārthatvātprārabdhaṃ karma hīyate|
bhoktavyasatyatābhrāntyāvyasanaṃ tatra jāyate||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 167
units.deva:
मा विनश्यत्वयं भोगो वर्धतामुत्तरोत्तरम्।
मा विघ्नाः प्रतिबध्नन्तु धन्योऽस्म्यस्मादिति भ्रमः॥
units.translation: “May this enjoyment not end; may it keep increasing; may no obstacles block it; I am blessed because of it”—this is delusion.
units.iast:
mā vinaśyatvayaṃ bhogo vardhatāmuttarottaram|
mā vighnāḥ pratibadhnantu dhanyo’smyasmāditi bhramaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 168
units.deva:
यदभावि न तद्भावि भावि चेन्न तदन्यथा।
इति चिन्ताविषग्नोऽयं बोधो भ्रमनिवर्तकः॥
units.translation: What is not destined to happen will not happen; if something is destined, it will not be otherwise. This understanding destroys the poison of worry and removes delusion.
units.iast:
yadabhāvi na tadbhāvi bhāvi cenna tadanyathā|
iti cintāviṣagno’yaṃ bodho bhramanivartakaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 169
units.deva:
समेऽपि भोगे व्यसनं भ्रान्तो गच्छेन्न बुद्धिमान्।
अशक्यार्थस्य सङ्कल्पाद्भ्रान्तस्य व्यसनं बहु॥
units.translation: Even when enjoyment is the same, the deluded suffer distress; the wise do not. Because the deluded imagine what cannot be attained, their distress is great.
units.iast:
same’pi bhoge vyasanaṃ bhrānto gacchenna buddhimān|
aśakyārthasya saṅkalpādbhrāntasya vyasanaṃ bahu||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 170
units.deva:
मायामयत्वं भोग्यस्य बुद्ध्वास्थामुपसंहरन्।
भुञ्जानोऽपि न सङ्कल्पं कुरुते व्यसनं कुतः॥
units.translation: Knowing that objects of enjoyment are illusory and withdrawing one’s attachment, a person does not form desires even while enjoying them. How, then, could distress arise?
units.iast:
māyāmayatvaṃ bhogyasya buddhvāsthāmupasaṃharan|
bhuñjāno’pi na saṅkalpaṃ kurute vyasanaṃ kutaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 171
units.deva:
स्वप्नेन्द्रजालसदृशमचिन्त्यरचनात्मकम्।
दृष्टनष्टं जगत्पश्यन्कथं तत्रानुरज्जति॥
units.translation: Seeing the world as like a dream and a magic show, beyond explanation and gone once seen, how could one become attached to it?

gloss.en: like a dream and a magic show

units.iast:
svapnendrajālasadṛśamacintyaracanātmakam|
dṛṣṭanaṣṭaṃ jagatpaśyankathaṃ tatrānurajjati||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 172
units.deva:
स्वस्वप्नमापरोक्षेण दृष्ट्वा पश्यन्स्वजागरम्।
चिन्तयेदप्रमत्तः सन्नुभावनुदिनं मुहुः॥
units.translation: When awake, one should recall the dream one directly saw and observe one’s waking state, carefully reflecting on both every day, again and again.
units.iast:
svasvapnamāparokṣeṇa dṛṣṭvā paśyansvajāgaram|
cintayedapramattaḥ sannubhāvanudinaṃ muhuḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 173
units.deva:
चिरं तयोः सर्वसाम्यमनुसन्धाय जागरे।
सत्यत्वबुद्धिं संत्यज्य नानुरज्जति पूर्ववत्॥
units.translation: While awake, after reflecting for a long time on the complete similarity of the two, one gives up the belief that the world is real and is no longer attached to it as before.
units.iast:
ciraṃ tayoḥ sarvasāmyamanusandhāya jāgare|
satyatvabuddhiṃ saṃtyajya nānurajjati pūrvavat||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 174
units.deva:
इन्द्रजालमिदं द्वैतमचिन्त्यरचनात्वतः।
इत्यविस्मरतो हानिः का वा प्रारब्धभोगतः॥
units.translation: For one who does not forget that this dual world is a magic show, whose construction is inconceivable, what harm can come from experiencing past karma?

gloss.en: for one who does not forget

units.iast:
indrajālamidaṃ dvaitamacintyaracanātvataḥ|
ityavismarato hāniḥ kā vā prārabdhabhogataḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 175
units.deva:
निर्बन्धस्तत्त्वविद्याया इन्द्रजालत्वसंस्मृतौ।
प्रारब्धस्याग्रहो भोगे जीवस्य सुखदुःखयोः॥
units.translation: The role of knowledge of reality is to remember the world’s magical nature; past karma’s role is to make the individual experience pleasure and pain.
units.iast:
nirbandhastattvavidyāyā indrajālatvasaṃsmṛtau|
prārabdhasyāgraho bhoge jīvasya sukhaduḥkhayoḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 176
units.deva:
विद्यारब्धे विरुद्ध्येते न भिन्नविषयत्वतः।
जानद्भिरप्यैन्द्रजालो विनोदो दृश्यते खलु॥
units.translation: Knowledge and past karma do not conflict, because their subjects are different. A magic show is still enjoyed even by people who know it is a show.
units.iast:
vidyārabdhe viruddhyete na bhinnaviṣayatvataḥ|
jānadbhirapyaindrajālo vinodo dṛśyate khalu||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 177
units.deva:
जगत्सत्यत्वमापाद्य प्रारब्धं भोजयेद्यदि।
तदा विरोधि विद्याया भोगमात्रान्न सत्यता॥
units.translation: If past karma made the world appear real, it would conflict with knowledge; mere experience does not make the world real.
units.iast:
jagatsatyatvamāpādya prārabdhaṃ bhojayedyadi|
tadā virodhi vidyāyā bhogamātrānna satyatā||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 178
units.deva:
अन्यूनो जायते भोगः कल्पितैः स्वप्नवस्तुभिः।
जाग्रत्वस्तुभिरप्येवमसत्यैर्भोग इष्यताम्॥
units.translation: Enjoyment from imagined dream objects is no less; in the same way, let enjoyment be understood to arise from unreal waking objects too.
units.iast:
anyūno jāyate bhogaḥ kalpitaiḥ svapnavastubhiḥ|
jāgratvastubhirapyevamasatyairbhoga iṣyatām||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 179
units.deva:
यदि विद्यापह्नुवित जगत्प्रारब्ध घातिनी।
तदा स्यान्न तु मायात्वबोधेन तदपह्नवः॥
units.translation: If knowledge of truth wiped out the world, it would destroy past karma too. But knowing that the world is illusory does not make it disappear.
units.iast:
yadi vidyāpahnuvita jagatprārabdha ghātinī|
tadā syānna tu māyātvabodhena tadapahnavaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 180
units.deva:
अनपह्नुत्य लोकास्तदिन्द्रजालमिदं त्विति।
जानन्त्येवानपह्नुत्य भोगं मायात्वधीस्तथा॥
units.translation: People know a magic show is unreal without making the show disappear. In the same way, knowledge of the world’s illusory nature need not remove the experience of it.
units.iast:
anapahnutya lokāstadindrajālamidaṃ tviti|
jānantyevānapahnutya bhogaṃ māyātvadhīstathā||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 181
units.deva:
यत्र त्वस्य जगत् स्वात्मा पश्येत्कस्तत्र केन किम्।
किं जिघ्रेत्किं वदेद्वेति श्रुतौ तु बहु घोषितम्॥
units.translation: (Question:) Scripture has declared at length: When one sees the whole world as one’s own Self, who could see what, by what means? What could one smell or say?
units.iast:
yatra tvasya jagat svātmā paśyetkastatra kena kim|
kiṃ jighretkiṃ vadedveti śrutau tu bahu ghoṣitam||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 182
units.deva:
तेन द्वैतमपह्नुत्य विद्योदेति न चान्यथा।
तथा च विदुषो भोगः कथं स्यादिति चेत् शृणु॥
units.translation: (Objection:) Knowledge arises by negating duality, and in no other way. If so, how could a knower experience anything? (Reply:) Listen.
units.iast:
tena dvaitamapahnutya vidyodeti na cānyathā|
tathā ca viduṣo bhogaḥ kathaṃ syāditi cet śṛṇu||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 183
units.deva:
सुषुप्तिविषया मुक्तिविषया वा श्रुतिस्त्विति।
उक्तं स्वाप्ययसम्पत्योरिति सूत्रे ह्यतिस्फुटम्॥
units.translation: (Reply:) Such scripture concerns deep sleep or liberation; this is clearly stated in the Brahma Sūtra on “absorption and attainment.”

gloss.en: in the Sūtra on absorption and attainment

units.iast:
suṣuptiviṣayā muktiviṣayā vā śrutistviti|
uktaṃ svāpyayasampatyoriti sūtre hyatisphuṭam||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 184
units.deva:
अन्यया याज्ञवल्क्यादेराचार्यत्वं न सम्भवेत्।
द्वैतदृष्टावविद्वत्ता द्वैतादृष्टौ न वाग्वदेत्॥
units.translation: Otherwise, Yājñavalkya and the other sages could not be teachers. If duality were seen, they would be ignorant; if it were not seen, they could not speak.
units.iast:
anyayā yājñavalkyāderācāryatvaṃ na sambhavet|
dvaitadṛṣṭāvavidvattā dvaitādṛṣṭau na vāgvadet||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 185
units.deva:
निर्विकल्पसमाधौ तु द्वैतादर्शनहेतुतः।
सैवापरोक्षविद्येति चेत्सुषुप्तिस्तथा न किम्॥
units.translation: (Question:) In nirvikalpa samādhi, duality is not seen; if that alone is direct knowledge, why would deep sleep not be so as well?
units.iast:
nirvikalpasamādhau tu dvaitādarśanahetutaḥ|
saivāparokṣavidyeti cetsuṣuptistathā na kim||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 186
units.deva:
आत्मतत्त्वं न जानाति सुप्तौ यदि तदा त्वया।
आत्मधीरेव विद्येति वाच्यं न द्वैतविस्मृतिः॥
units.translation: (Reply:) If you say that one does not know the truth of the Self in sleep, then you must say that Self-knowledge alone is knowledge, not merely forgetting duality.
units.iast:
ātmatattvaṃ na jānāti suptau yadi tadā tvayā|
ātmadhīreva vidyeti vācyaṃ na dvaitavismṛtiḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 187
units.deva:
उभयं मिलितं विद्या यदि तर्हि घटादयः।
अर्धविद्याभाजिनः स्युः सकलद्वैतविस्मृतेः॥
units.translation: If knowledge consists of both, then pots and similar things would possess half-knowledge, since they are entirely unaware of duality.

gloss.en: because of complete absence of duality-awareness

units.iast:
ubhayaṃ militaṃ vidyā yadi tarhi ghaṭādayaḥ|
ardhavidyābhājinaḥ syuḥ sakaladvaitavismṛteḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 188
units.deva:
मशकध्वनिमुख्यानां विक्षेपाणां बहुत्वतः।
तत्त्वविद्या तथा न स्याद्घटादीनां यथा दृढा॥
units.translation: Then the pots would have firmer knowledge of reality than you do, since you are distracted by so many things, beginning with the buzz of mosquitoes.

gloss.en: headed by the buzz of mosquitoes
as that of pots and other things

units.iast:
maśakadhvanimukhyānāṃ vikṣepāṇāṃ bahutvataḥ|
tattvavidyā tathā na syādghaṭādīnāṃ yathā dṛḍhā||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 189
units.deva:
आत्मधीरेव विद्येति यदि तर्हि सुखी भव।
दुष्टचित्तं निरुन्ध्याच्चेन्निरुन्धि त्वं यथासुखम्॥
units.translation: If you say that Self-knowledge alone is knowledge, then be content. If you say the troubled mind must be restrained, then restrain it as you please.
units.iast:
ātmadhīreva vidyeti yadi tarhi sukhī bhava|
duṣṭacittaṃ nirundhyāccennirundhi tvaṃ yathāsukham||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 190
units.deva:
तदिष्टमेष्टव्यमायामयत्वस्य समीक्षणात्।
इच्छन्नप्यज्ञवन्नेच्छेत्किमिच्छन्निति हि श्रुतम्॥
units.translation: This is welcome and should be pursued: recognizing that the world is illusory. Though desire may arise, one should not desire as an ignorant person does. Scripture indeed asks, “Desiring what?”
units.iast:
tadiṣṭameṣṭavyamāyāmayatvasya samīkṣaṇāt|
icchannapyajñavannecchetkimicchanniti hi śrutam||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 191
units.deva:
रागो लिङ्गमबोधस्य सन्तु रागादयो बुधे।
इति शास्त्रद्वयं सार्थमेवं सत्यविरोधतः॥
units.translation: “Attachment is a sign of ignorance” and “let attachment and the like be in the wise”—both scriptural statements are meaningful and do not conflict with truth.

gloss.en: because they do not conflict with truth

units.iast:
rāgo liṅgamabodhasya santu rāgādayo budhe|
iti śāstradvayaṃ sārthamevaṃ satyavirodhataḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 192
units.deva:
जगन्मिथ्यात्ववत् स्वात्मासङ्गत्वस्य समीक्षणात्।
कस्य कामायेति वचो भोक्त्रभावविवक्षया॥
units.translation: Seeing the Self’s nonattachment, just as one sees the world’s unreality, the statement “for whose desire?” is meant to express that there is no enjoyer.

gloss.en: just as the world is unreal
intended to express the absence of an enjoyer

units.iast:
jaganmithyātvavat svātmāsaṅgatvasya samīkṣaṇāt|
kasya kāmāyeti vaco bhoktrabhāvavivakṣayā||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 193
units.deva:
पतिजायादिकं सर्वं तत्तद्भोगाय नेच्छति।
किन्त्वात्मभोगार्थमिति श्रुतावुद्घोषितं बहु॥
units.translation: A spouse and all the rest are desired not for their own sake, but for one’s own enjoyment; scripture declares this repeatedly.
units.iast:
patijāyādikaṃ sarvaṃ tattadbhogāya necchati|
kintvātmabhogārthamiti śrutāvudghoṣitaṃ bahu||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 194
units.deva:
किं कूटस्थश्चिदाभासोऽथ वा किमुभयात्मकः।
भोक्ता तत्र न कूटस्थोऽसङ्गत्वाद्भोक्तृतां व्रजेत्॥
units.translation: Who is the enjoyer: Kūṭastha, reflected consciousness, or a combination of both? The unattached Kūṭastha cannot take on the role of enjoyer.

gloss.en: the state of being an enjoyer

units.iast:
kiṃ kūṭasthaścidābhāso’tha vā kimubhayātmakaḥ|
bhoktā tatra na kūṭastho’saṅgatvādbhoktṛtāṃ vrajet||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 195
units.deva:
सुखदुःखाभिमानाख्यो विकारो भोग उच्यते।
कूटस्थस्य विकारी चेत्येतन्न व्याहतं कथम्॥
units.translation: Enjoyment is said to be a change called identification with pleasure and pain. If Kūṭastha were subject to change, how would that not be a contradiction?

gloss.en: called identification with pleasure and pain

units.iast:
sukhaduḥkhābhimānākhyo vikāro bhoga ucyate|
kūṭasthasya vikārī cetyetanna vyāhataṃ katham||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 196
units.deva:
विकारिबुद्ध्यधीनत्वादाभासे विकृतावपि।
निरधिष्ठानविभ्रान्तिः केवला न हि तिष्ठति॥
units.translation: Even though reflected consciousness changes with the changing intellect, a bare illusion cannot stand without a basis.

gloss.en: because it depends on the changing intellect

units.iast:
vikāribuddhyadhīnatvādābhāse vikṛtāvapi|
niradhiṣṭhānavibhrāntiḥ kevalā na hi tiṣṭhati||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 197
units.deva:
उभयात्मक एवातो लोके भोक्ता निगद्यते।
तदृगात्मानमारभ्य कूटस्थः शेषितः श्रुतौ॥
units.translation: Therefore, in ordinary speech, the enjoyer is said to consist of both. In scripture, after beginning with that composite self, only Kūṭastha remains.
units.iast:
ubhayātmaka evāto loke bhoktā nigadyate|
tadṛgātmānamārabhya kūṭasthaḥ śeṣitaḥ śrutau||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 198
units.deva:
आत्मा कतम इत्युक्ते याज्ञवल्क्यो विबोधयन्।
विज्ञानमयमारभ्यासङ्गं तं पर्यशेषयत्॥
units.translation: When asked, “Which is the Self?”, Yājñavalkya, explaining, began with the intellect-sheath and finally established that unattached Self.
units.iast:
ātmā katama ityukte yājñavalkyo vibodhayan|
vijñānamayamārabhyāsaṅgaṃ taṃ paryaśeṣayat||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 199
units.deva:
कोऽयमात्मेत्येवमादौ सर्वत्रात्मविचारतः।
उभयात्मकमारभ्य कूटस्थः शेष्यते श्रुतौ॥
units.translation: In every inquiry into the Self that begins, “What is this Self?”, scripture starts with the composite self and leaves only Kūṭastha.
units.iast:
ko’yamātmetyevamādau sarvatrātmavicārataḥ|
ubhayātmakamārabhya kūṭasthaḥ śeṣyate śrutau||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 200
units.deva:
कूटस्थसत्यतां स्वस्मिन्नध्यस्यात्मा विवेकतः।
तात्विकीं भोक्तृतां मत्वा न कदाचिज्जिहासति॥
units.translation: By discernment, one superimposes Kūṭastha’s reality on oneself; treating one’s enjoyership as real, one never wants to give it up.
units.iast:
kūṭasthasatyatāṃ svasminnadhyasyātmā vivekataḥ|
tātvikīṃ bhoktṛtāṃ matvā na kadācijjihāsati||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 201
units.deva:
भोक्ता स्वस्यैव भोगाय पतिजायादिमिच्छति।
एष लौकिकवृत्तान्तः श्रुत्या सम्यगनूदितः॥
units.translation: The enjoyer desires a spouse and the rest for their own enjoyment. Scripture accurately describes this familiar fact.

gloss.en: a husband, wife, and the rest

units.iast:
bhoktā svasyaiva bhogāya patijāyādimicchati|
eṣa laukikavṛttāntaḥ śrutyā samyaganūditaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 202
units.deva:
भोग्यानां भोक्तृशेषत्वान्मा भोग्येष्वनुरज्यताम्।
भोक्तर्येव प्रधानेऽतोऽनुरागं तं विधित्सति॥
units.translation: Since objects of enjoyment exist for the enjoyer, one should not become attached to them. Since the enjoyer alone is primary, scripture intends to direct that love toward the enjoyer.

gloss.en: because they are for the enjoyer

units.iast:
bhogyānāṃ bhoktṛśeṣatvānmā bhogyeṣvanurajyatām|
bhoktaryeva pradhāne’to’nurāgaṃ taṃ vidhitsati||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 203
units.deva:
या प्रीतिरविवेकानां विषयेष्वनपायिनी।
त्वामनुस्मरतः सा मे हृदयान्मापसर्पतु॥
units.translation: May the unfailing love that undiscerning people have for sense-objects not leave my heart as I remember You.
units.iast:
yā prītiravivekānāṃ viṣayeṣvanapāyinī|
tvāmanusmarataḥ sā me hṛdayānmāpasarpatu||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 204
units.deva:
इति न्यायेन सर्वस्माद्भोग्यजाताद्विरक्तधीः।
उपसंहृत्य तां प्रीतिं भोक्तर्येवं बुभुत्सते॥
units.translation: Following this reasoning, one whose mind is dispassionate toward all objects of enjoyment withdraws that love and seeks to know the enjoyer, the Self.

gloss.en: kinds of objects to be enjoyed

units.iast:
iti nyāyena sarvasmādbhogyajātādviraktadhīḥ|
upasaṃhṛtya tāṃ prītiṃ bhoktaryevaṃ bubhutsate||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 205
units.deva:
स्रक्चन्दनवधूवस्त्रसुवर्णादिषु पामरः।
अप्रमत्तो यथा तद्वन्न प्रमाद्यति भोक्तरि॥
units.translation: Just as an undiscerning person stays intent on garlands, sandalwood paste, young women, clothes, gold, and the like, a seeker should stay alert to the enjoyer and not become heedless.
units.iast:
srakcandanavadhūvastrasuvarṇādiṣu pāmaraḥ|
apramatto yathā tadvanna pramādyati bhoktari||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 206
units.deva:
काव्यनाटकतर्कादिमभ्यस्यति निरन्तरम्।
विजिगीषुर्यथा तद्वन्मुमुक्षुः स्वं विचारयेत्॥
units.translation: Just as someone eager to defeat others continually studies poetry, drama, logic, and the like, a seeker of liberation should inquire into the Self.
units.iast:
kāvyanāṭakatarkādimabhyasyati nirantaram|
vijigīṣuryathā tadvanmumukṣuḥ svaṃ vicārayet||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 207
units.deva:
जपयागोपासनादि कुरुते श्रद्धया यथा।
स्वर्गादिवाञ्छया तद्वच्छ्रद्दध्यात्स्वे मुमुक्षया॥
units.translation: Just as someone seeking heaven performs recitation, sacrifice, worship, and the like with faith, a seeker of liberation should place faith in the Self.

gloss.en: out of the desire for liberation

units.iast:
japayāgopāsanādi kurute śraddhayā yathā|
svargādivāñchayā tadvacchraddadhyātsve mumukṣayā||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 208
units.deva:
चित्तैकाग्र्यं यथा योगी महायासेन साधयेत्।
अणिमादिप्रेप्सयैवं विविच्यात्स्वं मुमुक्षया॥
units.translation: Just as a yogi works very hard to develop one-pointedness of mind in pursuit of powers such as becoming minute, a seeker of liberation should discriminate the Self.

gloss.en: out of the desire for liberation

units.iast:
cittaikāgryaṃ yathā yogī mahāyāsena sādhayet|
aṇimādiprepsayaivaṃ vivicyātsvaṃ mumukṣayā||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 209
units.deva:
कौशलानि विवर्धन्ते तेषामभ्यासपाटवात्।
यथा तद्वद्विवेकोऽस्याप्यभ्यासाद्विशदायते॥
units.translation: Just as their skills grow through practiced proficiency, so the seeker’s discernment becomes clearer through practice.
units.iast:
kauśalāni vivardhante teṣāmabhyāsapāṭavāt|
yathā tadvadviveko’syāpyabhyāsādviśadāyate||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 210
units.deva:
विविञ्चता भोक्तृतत्त्वं जाग्रदादिष्वसङ्गता।
अन्वयव्यतिरेकाभ्यां साक्षिण्यध्यवसीयते॥
units.translation: By examining the nature of the enjoyer, one ascertains through the methods of presence and absence that the witness remains unattached in waking and the other states.

gloss.en: in waking and the other states

units.iast:
viviñcatā bhoktṛtattvaṃ jāgradādiṣvasaṅgatā|
anvayavyatirekābhyāṃ sākṣiṇyadhyavasīyate||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 211
units.deva:
यत्र यद्दृश्यते द्रष्टा जाग्रत्स्वप्नसुषुप्तिषु।
तत्रैव तन्नेतरत्रेत्यनुभूतिर्हि संमता॥
units.translation: In waking, dream, and deep sleep, whatever appears is experienced in that state and not in another; this is accepted as common experience.

gloss.en: in waking, dream, and deep sleep

units.iast:
yatra yaddṛśyate draṣṭā jāgratsvapnasuṣuptiṣu|
tatraiva tannetaratretyanubhūtirhi saṃmatā||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 212
units.deva:
स यत्तत्रेक्षते किंचित्तेनानन्वागतो भवेत्।
दृष्ट्वैव पुण्यं पापं चेत्येवं श्रुतिषु डिण्डिमः॥
units.translation: Whatever one sees in a state is not carried along into another state. Scripture loudly declares this of merit and wrongdoing alike.
units.iast:
sa yattatrekṣate kiṃcittenānanvāgato bhavet|
dṛṣṭvaiva puṇyaṃ pāpaṃ cetyevaṃ śrutiṣu ḍiṇḍimaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 213
units.deva:
जाग्रत्स्वप्नसुषुप्त्यादि प्रपञ्चं यत्प्रकाशते।
तद्ब्रह्माहमिति ज्ञात्वा सर्वबन्धैः प्रमुच्यते॥
units.translation: Knowing, “I am that Brahman which illumines the entire display of waking, dream, deep sleep, and the rest,” one is freed from every bond.
