gloss.en: waking, dream, deep sleep, and the rest

units.iast:
jāgratsvapnasuṣuptyādi prapañcaṃ yatprakāśate|
tadbrahmāhamiti jñātvā sarvabandhaiḥ pramucyate||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 214
units.deva:
एक एव आत्मा मन्तव्यो जाग्रत्स्वप्नसुषुप्तिषु।
स्थानत्रयव्यतीतस्य पुनर्जन्म न विद्यते॥
units.translation: One should understand the Self to be one and the same in waking, dream, and deep sleep. For one who is beyond these three states, rebirth does not exist.

gloss.en: in waking, dream, and deep sleep
for one beyond the three states

units.iast:
eka eva ātmā mantavyo jāgratsvapnasuṣuptiṣu|
sthānatrayavyatītasya punarjanma na vidyate||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 215
units.deva:
त्रिषु धामसु यद्भोग्यं भोक्ता भोगश्च यद्भवेत्।
तेभ्यो विलक्षणः साक्षी चिन्मात्रोऽहं सदाशिवः॥
units.translation: Whatever is the object of enjoyment, the enjoyer, or the enjoyment in the three states, I am distinct from all of them: the witness, pure consciousness alone, Sadāśiva.
units.iast:
triṣu dhāmasu yadbhogyaṃ bhoktā bhogaśca yadbhavet|
tebhyo vilakṣaṇaḥ sākṣī cinmātro’haṃ sadāśivaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 216
units.deva:
एवं विवेचिते तत्त्वे विज्ञामयशब्दितः।
चिदाभासो विकारी यो भोक्तृत्वं तस्य शिष्यते॥
units.translation: Once reality is discriminated in this way, what remains as the enjoyer is the changing reflected consciousness, called the intellect-sheath.
units.iast:
evaṃ vivecite tattve vijñāmayaśabditaḥ|
cidābhāso vikārī yo bhoktṛtvaṃ tasya śiṣyate||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 217
units.deva:
मायिकोऽयं चिदाभासः श्रुतेरनुभवादपि।
इन्द्रजालं जगत्प्रोक्तं तदन्तःपात्ययं यतः॥
units.translation: This reflected consciousness is a product of Māyā, as scripture and experience show. The world is called a magic show because this too is included in it.
units.iast:
māyiko’yaṃ cidābhāsaḥ śruteranubhavādapi|
indrajālaṃ jagatproktaṃ tadantaḥpātyayaṃ yataḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 218
units.deva:
विलोपोऽस्य सुषुप्त्यादौ साक्षिणा ह्यनुभूयते।
एतादृशं स्वस्वभावं विविनक्ति पुनः पुनः॥
units.translation: The witness directly experiences the disappearance of this reflected consciousness in deep sleep and similar states. One should repeatedly discern its nature in this way.

gloss.en: in deep sleep and the like

units.iast:
vilopo’sya suṣuptyādau sākṣiṇā hyanubhūyate|
etādṛśaṃ svasvabhāvaṃ vivinakti punaḥ punaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 219
units.deva:
विविच्य नाशं निश्चित्य पुनर्भोगं न वाञ्छति।
मुमूर्षुः शायितो भूमौ विवाहं कोऽभिवाञ्छति॥
units.translation: Having discerned and confirmed its perishability, one no longer wants enjoyment. Who, lying on the ground and about to die, would long to marry?
units.iast:
vivicya nāśaṃ niścitya punarbhogaṃ na vāñchati|
mumūrṣuḥ śāyito bhūmau vivāhaṃ ko’bhivāñchati||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 220
units.deva:
जिह्रेति व्यवहर्तुं च भोक्ताहमिति पूर्ववत्।
छिन्ननास इव ह्रीतः क्लिश्यन्नारब्धमश्नुते॥
units.translation: Ashamed to speak as before—“I am the enjoyer”—and like someone whose nose has been cut, one suffers while experiencing past karma.

gloss.en: one whose nose has been cut

units.iast:
jihreti vyavahartuṃ ca bhoktāhamiti pūrvavat|
chinnanāsa iva hrītaḥ kliśyannārabdhamaśnute||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 221
units.deva:
यदा स्वस्यापि भोक्तृत्वं मन्तुं जिह्रेत्ययं तदा।
साक्षिण्यारोपयेदेतदिति कैव कथा वृथा॥
units.translation: When one is ashamed even to think, “I am an enjoyer,” why would one superimpose that role on the witness? That would be pointless.

gloss.en: the state of being an enjoyer

units.iast:
yadā svasyāpi bhoktṛtvaṃ mantuṃ jihretyayaṃ tadā|
sākṣiṇyāropayedetaditi kaiva kathā vṛthā||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 222
units.deva:
इत्यभिप्रेत्य भोक्तारमाक्षिपत्यविशङ्कया।
कस्य कामायेति ततः शरीरानुज्वरो न हि॥
units.translation: With this in mind, one confidently rejects the enjoyer. “For whom would there be desire?” Therefore there is no bodily affliction.
units.iast:
ityabhipretya bhoktāramākṣipatyaviśaṅkayā|
kasya kāmāyeti tataḥ śarīrānujvaro na hi||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 223
units.deva:
स्थूलं सूक्ष्मं कारणं च शरीरं त्रिविधं स्मृतम्।
अवश्यं त्रिविधोऽस्त्येव तत्र तत्रोचितो ज्वरः॥
units.translation: The body is known to be threefold: gross, subtle, and causal. In each one there is necessarily a corresponding affliction.
units.iast:
sthūlaṃ sūkṣmaṃ kāraṇaṃ ca śarīraṃ trividhaṃ smṛtam|
avaśyaṃ trividho’styeva tatra tatrocito jvaraḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 224
units.deva:
वातपित्तश्लेष्मजन्या व्याधयः कोटिशस्तनौ।
दुर्गन्धित्वं कुरूपत्वं दाहभङ्गादयस्तथा॥
units.translation: Countless illnesses arise in the body from vāta, pitta, and kapha; foul odor, deformity, burning, fractures, and the like arise as well.

gloss.en: arising from vāta, pitta, and kapha

units.iast:
vātapittaśleṣmajanyā vyādhayaḥ koṭiśastanau|
durgandhitvaṃ kurūpatvaṃ dāhabhaṅgādayastathā||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 225
units.deva:
कामक्रोधादयः शान्तिदान्त्याद्या लिङ्गदेहगाः।
ज्वराद्वयेऽपि बाधन्ते प्राप्त्याप्राप्त्या नरं क्रमात्॥
units.translation: Desire, anger, and the like, as well as calm, restraint, and the like, belong to the subtle body. These two kinds of affliction trouble a person through presence or absence, respectively.

gloss.en: in the two kinds of affliction

units.iast:
kāmakrodhādayaḥ śāntidāntyādyā liṅgadehagāḥ|
jvarādvaye’pi bādhante prāptyāprāptyā naraṃ kramāt||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 226
units.deva:
स्वं परं च न वेत्त्यात्मा विनष्ट इव कारणे।
आगामिदुःखबीजं चेत्येतदिन्द्रेण दर्शितम्॥
units.translation: In the causal state, the individual knows neither self nor other and seems as if destroyed. This causal state is the seed of future sorrow, as Indra showed.
units.iast:
svaṃ paraṃ ca na vettyātmā vinaṣṭa iva kāraṇe|
āgāmiduḥkhabījaṃ cetyetadindreṇa darśitam||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 227
units.deva:
एते ज्वराः शरीरेषु त्रिषु स्वाभाविका मताः।
वियोगे तु ज्वरैस्तानि शरीराण्येव नासते॥
units.translation: These afflictions are considered natural to the three bodies. When separated from the afflictions, the bodies themselves cease to exist.
units.iast:
ete jvarāḥ śarīreṣu triṣu svābhāvikā matāḥ|
viyoge tu jvaraistāni śarīrāṇyeva nāsate||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 228
units.deva:
तन्तोर्वियुज्येन्न पटो वालेभ्यः कम्बलो यथा।
मृदो घटस्तथा देहो ज्वरेभ्योऽपीति दृश्यताम्॥
units.translation: Just as cloth cannot be separated from thread, a blanket from wool, or a pot from clay, so the body cannot be separated from its afflictions—understand it this way.
units.iast:
tantorviyujyenna paṭo vālebhyaḥ kambalo yathā|
mṛdo ghaṭastathā deho jvarebhyo’pīti dṛśyatām||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 229
units.deva:
चिदाभासे स्वतः कोऽपि ज्वरो नास्ति यतश्चितः।
प्रकाशैकस्वभावत्वमेव दृष्टं न चेतरत्॥
units.translation: There is no affliction inherent in reflected consciousness, for it is consciousness. Illumination alone is seen as its nature, and nothing else.

gloss.en: the nature of being illumination alone

units.iast:
cidābhāse svataḥ ko’pi jvaro nāsti yataścitaḥ|
prakāśaikasvabhāvatvameva dṛṣṭaṃ na cetarat||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 230
units.deva:
चिदाभासेऽप्यसम्भाव्या ज्वराः साक्षिणि का कथा।
एवमेवैकतां मेने चिदाभासो ह्यविद्यया॥
units.translation: Afflictions are impossible even in reflected consciousness, so what can be said of the witness? Through ignorance, the reflection takes itself to be identical with the body.
units.iast:
cidābhāse’pyasambhāvyā jvarāḥ sākṣiṇi kā kathā|
evamevaikatāṃ mene cidābhāso hyavidyayā||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 231
units.deva:
साक्षिसत्यत्वमध्यस्य स्वेनोपेते वपुस्त्रये।
तत्सर्वं वास्तवं स्वस्य स्वरूपमिति मन्यते॥
units.translation: By superimposing the witness’s reality on the three bodies identified as one’s own, one thinks that all of them are one’s real nature.
units.iast:
sākṣisatyatvamadhyasya svenopete vapustraye|
tatsarvaṃ vāstavaṃ svasya svarūpamiti manyate||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 232
units.deva:
एतस्मिन्भ्रान्तिकालेऽयं शरीरेषु ज्वरत्स्वथ।
स्वयमेव ज्वरामीति मन्यते हि कुटुम्बिवत्॥
units.translation: While this delusion lasts, when the bodies are afflicted, one thinks, “I myself am suffering,” as a family member does when the family is afflicted.
units.iast:
etasminbhrāntikāle’yaṃ śarīreṣu jvaratsvatha|
svayameva jvarāmīti manyate hi kuṭumbivat||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 233
units.deva:
पुत्रदारेषु तृप्यत्सु तृप्यामीति यथा वृथा।
मन्यते पुरुषस्तद्वदाभासोऽप्यभिमन्यते॥
units.translation: Just as a person foolishly thinks, “I am satisfied,” when their children and wife are satisfied, so reflected consciousness wrongly takes their state to be its own.

gloss.en: identifies itself / takes itself to be

units.iast:
putradāreṣu tṛpyatsu tṛpyāmīti yathā vṛthā|
manyate puruṣastadvadābhāso’pyabhimanyate||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 234
units.deva:
विविच्य भ्रान्तिमुज्झित्वा स्वमप्यगणयन् सदा।
चिन्तयन्साक्षिणं कस्माच्छरीरमनुसंज्वरेत्॥
units.translation: Having discerned the truth, abandoned delusion, and ceased to count oneself as the body, while always contemplating the witness, why would one suffer along with the body?
units.iast:
vivicya bhrāntimujjhitvā svamapyagaṇayan sadā|
cintayansākṣiṇaṃ kasmāccharīramanusaṃjvaret||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 235
units.deva:
अयथावस्तुसर्पादिज्ञानं हेतुः पलायने।
रज्जुज्ञानेऽहिधीध्वस्तौ कृतमप्यनुशोचति॥
units.translation: A false perception of a snake and the like causes one to flee. When knowledge of the rope destroys the snake-notion, one regrets what one did.

gloss.en: perception of a snake and the like

units.iast:
ayathāvastusarpādijñānaṃ hetuḥ palāyane|
rajjujñāne’hidhīdhvastau kṛtamapyanuśocati||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 236
units.deva:
मिथ्याभियोगदोषस्य प्रायश्चित्तत्वसिद्धये।
क्षमापयन्निवात्मानं साक्षिणं शरणं गतः॥
units.translation: To atone for the fault of a false accusation, one takes refuge in the witness as if asking it to forgive oneself.

gloss.en: for the fault of an accusation

units.iast:
mithyābhiyogadoṣasya prāyaścittatvasiddhaye|
kṣamāpayannivātmānaṃ sākṣiṇaṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 237
units.deva:
आवृत्तपापनूत्यर्थं स्नानाद्यावर्तते यथा।
आवर्तयन्निव ध्यानं सदा साक्षिपरायणः॥
units.translation: Just as one repeats bathing and similar acts to atone for recurring sins, so one devoted to the witness repeatedly returns to contemplation.
units.iast:
āvṛttapāpanūtyarthaṃ snānādyāvartate yathā|
āvartayanniva dhyānaṃ sadā sākṣiparāyaṇaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 238
units.deva:
उपस्थकुष्ठिनी वेश्या विलासेषु विलज्जते।
जानतोऽग्रे तथाभासः स्वप्रख्यातौ विलज्जते॥
units.translation: Just as a courtesan with a genital disease is ashamed to display her charms before someone who knows her condition, so reflected consciousness is ashamed to present itself as the doer and enjoyer.
units.iast:
upasthakuṣṭhinī veśyā vilāseṣu vilajjate|
jānato’gre tathābhāsaḥ svaprakhyātau vilajjate||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 239
units.deva:
गृहीतो ब्राह्मणो म्लेच्छैः प्रायश्चित्तं चरन्पुनः।
म्लेच्छैः सङ्कीर्यते नैव तथाभासः शरीरकैः॥
units.translation: A Brahmin taken captive by mlecchas (outsiders in the verse’s social vocabulary) performs expiation and then does not mix with them; likewise, reflected consciousness no longer mixes with the bodies.
units.iast:
gṛhīto brāhmaṇo mlecchaiḥ prāyaścittaṃ caranpunaḥ|
mlecchaiḥ saṅkīryate naiva tathābhāsaḥ śarīrakaiḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 240
units.deva:
यौवराज्ये स्थितो राजपुत्रः साम्राज्यवाञ्छया।
राजानुकारी भवति तथा साक्ष्यनुकार्ययम्॥
units.translation: Just as a prince established as heir apparent acts like the king from a desire for sovereignty, so this reflection imitates the witness.

gloss.en: in the status of heir apparent

units.iast:
yauvarājye sthito rājaputraḥ sāmrājyavāñchayā|
rājānukārī bhavati tathā sākṣyanukāryayam||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 241
units.deva:
यो ब्रह्म वेद ब्रह्मैव भवत्येवेति श्रुतिम्।
श्रुत्वा तदेकचित्तः सन्ब्रह्म वेत्ति न चेतरत्॥
units.translation: Whoever hears the Śruti declaration, “The knower of Brahman becomes Brahman,” fixes the mind on that alone and knows Brahman, nothing else.

gloss.en: with the mind fixed on that alone

units.iast:
yo brahma veda brahmaiva bhavatyeveti śrutim|
śrutvā tadekacittaḥ sanbrahma vetti na cetarat||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 242
units.deva:
देवत्वकामा ह्यग्न्यादौ प्रविशन्ति यथा तथा।
साक्षित्वेनावशेषाय स्वविनाशं स वाञ्छति॥
units.translation: Just as those who desire divine status enter fire and similar rites, so he desires the dissolution of his own reflected identity in order to remain as the witness.
units.iast:
devatvakāmā hyagnyādau praviśanti yathā tathā|
sākṣitvenāvaśeṣāya svavināśaṃ sa vāñchati||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 243
units.deva:
यावत्स्वदेहदाहं स नरत्वं नैव मुञ्चति।
तावदारब्धदेहः स्यान्नाभासत्वविमोचनम्॥
units.translation: A person does not give up being human until his own body has burned away. So long as the body set in motion by past karma remains, reflected consciousness is not released from its reflected status.

gloss.en: the burning of one’s own body
one whose body has been set in motion

units.iast:
yāvatsvadehadāhaṃ sa naratvaṃ naiva muñcati|
tāvadārabdhadehaḥ syānnābhāsatvavimocanam||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 244
units.deva:
रज्जुज्ञानेऽपि कम्पादिः शनैरेवोपशाम्यति।
पुनर्मन्दान्धकारि सा रज्जुः क्षिप्तोरगी भवेत्॥
units.translation: Even after the rope is known, trembling and the like subside only gradually; in dim light, that same rope may again appear to be a snake.

gloss.en: even with knowledge of the rope
a snake imagined to be lying there (traditional reading)

units.iast:
rajjujñāne’pi kampādiḥ śanairevopaśāmyati|
punarmandāndhakāri sā rajjuḥ kṣiptoragī bhavet||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 245
units.deva:
एवमारब्धभोगोऽपि शनैः शाम्यति नो हठात्।
भोगकाले कदाचित्तु मर्त्योऽहमिति भासते॥
units.translation: Likewise, experience already set in motion subsides gradually, not abruptly. During experience, the thought “I am mortal” may sometimes appear.
units.iast:
evamārabdhabhogo’pi śanaiḥ śāmyati no haṭhāt|
bhogakāle kadācittu martyo’hamiti bhāsate||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 246
units.deva:
नैतावतापराधेन तत्त्वज्ञानं विनश्यति।
जीवन्मुक्तिव्रतं नेदं किन्तु वस्तुस्थितिः खलु॥
units.translation: Such a lapse does not destroy knowledge of truth. Liberation while living is not a vow; it is simply the actual state of things.

gloss.en: by this much / because of this
a vow of liberation while living

units.iast:
naitāvatāparādhena tattvajñānaṃ vinaśyati|
jīvanmuktivrataṃ nedaṃ kintu vastusthitiḥ khalu||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 247
units.deva:
दशमोऽपि शिरस्ताडं रुदन्बुद्ध्वा न रोदिति।
शिरोव्रणस्तु मासेन शनैः शाम्यति नो तदा॥
units.translation: Even the tenth man, after realizing the truth, stops weeping though he had been crying and striking his head; the wound on his head, however, heals only gradually over a month.
units.iast:
daśamo’pi śirastāḍaṃ rudanbuddhvā na roditi|
śirovraṇastu māsena śanaiḥ śāmyati no tadā||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 248
units.deva:
दशमामृतिलाभेन जातो हर्षो व्रणव्यथाम्।
तिरोधत्ते मुक्तिलाभस्तथा प्रारब्धदुःखिताम्॥
units.translation: The joy that comes from finding the tenth man alive hides the pain of his wound; in the same way, liberation hides the suffering caused by past karma.

gloss.en: through finding the tenth man alive

units.iast:
daśamāmṛtilābhena jāto harṣo vraṇavyathām|
tirodhatte muktilābhastathā prārabdhaduḥkhitām||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 249
units.deva:
व्रताभावाद्यदाध्यासस्तदा भूयो विविच्यताम्।
रससेवी दिने भुङ्क्ते भूयो भूयो यथा तथा॥
units.translation: Because this is no vow, whenever superimposed identification returns one should examine it again, just as one who takes a mercury preparation eats repeatedly throughout the day.

gloss.en: because this is not a vow
one who takes a mercury preparation

units.iast:
vratābhāvādyadādhyāsastadā bhūyo vivicyatām|
rasasevī dine bhuṅkte bhūyo bhūyo yathā tathā||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 250
units.deva:
शमयत्यौषधेनायं दशमः स्वव्रणं यथा।
भोगेन शमयित्वैतत्प्रारब्धं मुच्यते तथा॥
units.translation: Just as the tenth man heals his wound with medicine, so one is released by quieting this past karma through experiencing its results.
units.iast:
śamayatyauṣadhenāyaṃ daśamaḥ svavraṇaṃ yathā|
bhogena śamayitvaitatprārabdhaṃ mucyate tathā||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 251
units.deva:
किमिच्छन्निति वाक्योक्तः शोकमोक्ष उदीरितः।
आभासस्य ह्यवस्थैषा षष्ठी तृप्तिस्तु सप्तमी॥
units.translation: The phrase “Desiring what?” states release from sorrow. This is the sixth state of the reflection; contentment is the seventh.
units.iast:
kimicchanniti vākyoktaḥ śokamokṣa udīritaḥ|
ābhāsasya hyavasthaiṣā ṣaṣṭhī tṛptistu saptamī||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 252
units.deva:
साङ्कुशा विषयैस्तृप्तिरियं तृप्तिर्निरङ्कुशा।
कृतं कृत्यं प्रापणीयं प्राप्तमित्येव तृप्यति॥
units.translation: Contentment from sense objects is limited; this contentment is unlimited. One is satisfied thinking, “What had to be done is done; what had to be attained is attained.”
units.iast:
sāṅkuśā viṣayaistṛptiriyaṃ tṛptirniraṅkuśā|
kṛtaṃ kṛtyaṃ prāpaṇīyaṃ prāptamityeva tṛpyati||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 253
units.deva:
ऐहिकामुष्मिकव्रातसिद्ध्यै मुक्तेश्च सिद्धये।
बहु कृत्यं पुरास्याभूत्तत्सर्वमधुना कृतम्॥
units.translation: Before this, he had many tasks to complete for worldly and afterlife aims and for the attainment of liberation; now all of them are done.
units.iast:
aihikāmuṣmikavrātasiddhyai mukteśca siddhaye|
bahu kṛtyaṃ purāsyābhūttatsarvamadhunā kṛtam||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 254
units.deva:
तदेतत्कृतकृत्यत्वं प्रतियोगिपुरःसरम्।
अनुसन्दधदेवायमेवं तृप्यति नित्यशः॥
units.translation: By continually keeping this sense of having done what needed to be done in view against the contrasting former state, one remains satisfied.

gloss.en: state of having done what needed to be done
with the contrasting state kept in view

units.iast:
tadetatkṛtakṛtyatvaṃ pratiyogipuraḥsaram|
anusandadhadevāyamevaṃ tṛpyati nityaśaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 255
units.deva:
दुःखिनोऽज्ञाः संसरन्तु कामं पुत्राद्यपेक्षया।
परमानन्दपूर्णोऽहं संसरामि किमिच्छया॥
units.translation: Let the sorrowful, ignorant people wander in saṃsāra, looking to children and the like if they wish. I am full of supreme bliss; why should I wander with desire?
units.iast:
duḥkhino’jñāḥ saṃsarantu kāmaṃ putrādyapekṣayā|
paramānandapūrṇo’haṃ saṃsarāmi kimicchayā||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 256
units.deva:
अनुतिष्ठन्तु कर्माणि परलोकायियासवः।
सर्वलोकात्मकः कस्मादनुतिष्ठामि किं कथम्॥
units.translation: Let those who wish to go to another world perform their rites. Since I am the self of all worlds, why and how should I perform them?

gloss.en: those wishing to go to another world

units.iast:
anutiṣṭhantu karmāṇi paralokāyiyāsavaḥ|
sarvalokātmakaḥ kasmādanutiṣṭhāmi kiṃ katham||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 257
units.deva:
व्याचक्षतान्ते शास्त्राणि वेदानध्यापयन्तु वा।
येऽत्राधिकारिणो मे तु नाधिकारोऽक्रियत्वतः॥
units.translation: Let those qualified for it explain the scriptures or teach the Vedas. I have no qualification for this, because I am actionless.
units.iast:
vyācakṣatānte śāstrāṇi vedānadhyāpayantu vā|
ye’trādhikāriṇo me tu nādhikāro’kriyatvataḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 258
units.deva:
निद्राभिक्षे स्नानशौचे नेच्छामि न करोमि च।
द्रष्टारश्चेत्कल्पयन्ति किं मे स्यादन्यकल्पनात्॥
units.translation: I neither desire nor perform sleep, begging, bathing, or ritual purification. If onlookers imagine these things, what do I gain or lose from someone else’s imagining?
units.iast:
nidrābhikṣe snānaśauce necchāmi na karomi ca|
draṣṭāraścetkalpayanti kiṃ me syādanyakalpanāt||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 259
units.deva:
गुञ्जापुञ्जादि दह्येत नान्यारोपितवह्निना।
नान्यारोपितसंसारधर्मानेवमहं भजे॥
units.translation: A cluster of guñjā berries and the like would not be burned by a fire merely projected onto it by someone else. In the same way, I do not take on worldly conditions that others project onto me.

gloss.en: a cluster of guñjā berries and the like
by a fire projected by someone else

units.iast:
guñjāpuñjādi dahyeta nānyāropitavahninā|
nānyāropitasaṃsāradharmānevamahaṃ bhaje||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 260
units.deva:
शृण्वन्त्वज्ञाततत्त्वास्ते जानन् कस्माच्छृणोम्यहम्।
मन्यन्तां संशयापन्ना न मन्येऽहमसंशयः॥
units.translation: Let those who do not know the truth listen. Knowing it, why should I listen? Let those troubled by doubt reflect; I do not reflect, being free from doubt.

gloss.en: those who do not know the truth

units.iast:
śṛṇvantvajñātatattvāste jānan kasmācchṛṇomyaham|
manyantāṃ saṃśayāpannā na manye’hamasaṃśayaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 261
units.deva:
विपर्यस्तो निदिध्यासेत्किं ध्यानमविपर्यये।
देहात्मत्वविपर्यासं न कदाचिद्भजाम्यहम्॥
units.translation: The confused person should contemplate deeply; what meditation is needed for one who is free of confusion? I never take up the error of identifying the body as the Self.

gloss.en: the error of taking the body as the Self

units.iast:
viparyasto nididhyāsetkiṃ dhyānamaviparyaye|
dehātmatvaviparyāsaṃ na kadācidbhajāmyaham||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 262
units.deva:
अहं मनुष्य इत्यादिव्यवहारो विनाप्यमुम्।
विपर्यासं चिराभ्यस्तवासनातोऽवकल्पते॥
units.translation: Even without this confusion, everyday speech such as “I am a human being” arises from impressions and habits practiced over a long time.
units.iast:
ahaṃ manuṣya ityādivyavahāro vināpyamum|
viparyāsaṃ cirābhyastavāsanāto’vakalpate||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 263
units.deva:
प्रारब्धकर्मणि क्षीणे व्यवहारो निवर्तते।
कर्माक्षये त्वसौ नैव शाम्येद्ध्यानसहस्रतः॥
units.translation: When karma already set in motion is exhausted, everyday dealings cease. But while that karma remains, they will not subside even through a thousand meditations.

gloss.en: when karma already set in motion

units.iast:
prārabdhakarmaṇi kṣīṇe vyavahāro nivartate|
karmākṣaye tvasau naiva śāmyeddhyānasahasrataḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 264
units.deva:
विरलत्वं व्यवहृतेरिष्टं चेद्ध्यानमस्तु ते।
अबाधिकां व्यवहृतिं पश्य ध्यायाम्यहं कुतः॥
units.translation: If you want everyday dealings to become infrequent, then meditate. But see that these dealings do not obstruct knowledge; why should I meditate?
units.iast:
viralatvaṃ vyavahṛteriṣṭaṃ ceddhyānamastu te|
abādhikāṃ vyavahṛtiṃ paśya dhyāyāmyahaṃ kutaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 265
units.deva:
विक्षेपो नास्ति यस्मान्मे न समाधिस्ततो मम।
विक्षेपो वा समाधिर्वा मनसः स्याद्विकारिणः॥
units.translation: Because there is no distraction for me, there is no samādhi for me either. Distraction and samādhi are states of the changing mind.
units.iast:
vikṣepo nāsti yasmānme na samādhistato mama|
vikṣepo vā samādhirvā manasaḥ syādvikāriṇaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 266
units.deva:
नित्यानुभवरूपस्य को मेऽत्रानुभवः पृथक्।
कृतं कृत्यं प्रापणीयं प्राप्तमित्येव निश्चयः॥
units.translation: For one whose nature is ever-present experience, what separate experience could there be here? “What had to be done is done; what had to be attained is attained”—this is the certainty.
units.iast:
nityānubhavarūpasya ko me’trānubhavaḥ pṛthak|
kṛtaṃ kṛtyaṃ prāpaṇīyaṃ prāptamityeva niścayaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 267
units.deva:
व्यवहारो लौकिको वा शास्त्रीयोऽप्यन्यथापि वा।
ममाकर्तुरलेपस्य यथारब्धं प्रवर्तताम्॥
units.translation: Let worldly, scriptural, or any other activity proceed as it has begun; I am the non-doer, untouched by it.
units.iast:
vyavahāro laukiko vā śāstrīyo’pyanyathāpi vā|
mamākarturalepasya yathārabdhaṃ pravartatām||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 268
units.deva:
अथवा कृतकृत्योऽपि लोकानुग्रहकाम्यया।
शास्त्रीयेणैव मार्गेण वर्तेऽहं का मम क्षतिः॥
units.translation: Or, even having done what needed to be done, if I act for the good of the world and follow the scriptural path, what loss is there for me?

gloss.en: having done what needed to be done
from the wish to benefit the world

units.iast:
athavā kṛtakṛtyo’pi lokānugrahakāmyayā|
śāstrīyeṇaiva mārgeṇa varte’haṃ kā mama kṣatiḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 269
units.deva:
देवार्चनस्नानशौचभिक्षादौ वर्ततां वपुः।
तारं जपतु वाक्तद्वत्पठत्वाम्नायमस्तकम्॥
units.translation: Let the body engage in worship of the gods, bathing, purification, begging for alms, and the like. Let speech recite Om and likewise recite the head of the Veda, the Upaniṣads.

gloss.en: begging for alms and the like
the head of the Veda (the Upaniṣads)

units.iast:
devārcanasnānaśaucabhikṣādau vartatāṃ vapuḥ|
tāraṃ japatu vāktadvatpaṭhatvāmnāyamastakam||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 270
units.deva:
विष्णुं ध्यायतु धीर्यद्वा ब्रह्मानन्दे विलीयताम्।
साक्ष्यहं किंचिदप्यत्र न कुर्वे नापि कारये॥
units.translation: Let the intellect meditate on Viṣṇu, or dissolve in the bliss of Brahman. I am the witness; I do nothing here, nor do I cause anything to be done.
units.iast:
viṣṇuṃ dhyāyatu dhīryadvā brahmānande vilīyatām|
sākṣyahaṃ kiṃcidapyatra na kurve nāpi kāraye||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 271
units.deva:
एवं च कलहः कुत्र सम्भवेत्कर्मिण मम।
विभिन्नविषयत्वेन पूर्वापरसमुद्रवत्॥
units.translation: What conflict could there be between a ritualist and me, since our subjects are different, like the eastern and western oceans?

gloss.en: like the eastern and western oceans

units.iast:
evaṃ ca kalahaḥ kutra sambhavetkarmiṇa mama|
vibhinnaviṣayatvena pūrvāparasamudravat||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 272
units.deva:
वपुर्वाग्धीषु निर्बन्धः कर्मिणो न तु साक्षिणि।
ज्ञानिनः साक्ष्यलेपत्वे निर्बन्धो नेतरत्र हि॥
units.translation: The ritualist’s concern is with the body, speech, and intellect, not the witness. The knower’s concern is with the witness’s freedom from taint, not with anything else.

gloss.en: on the witness’s freedom from taint

units.iast:
vapurvāgdhīṣu nirbandhaḥ karmiṇo na tu sākṣiṇi|
jñāninaḥ sākṣyalepatve nirbandho netaratra hi||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 273
units.deva:
एवं चान्योन्यवृत्तान्तानभिज्ञौ बधिराविव।
विवदेतां बुद्धिमन्तो हसन्त्येव विलोक्य तौ॥
units.translation: Not knowing one another’s subject, the two may argue like deaf people; the wise, seeing them, simply laugh.
units.iast:
evaṃ cānyonyavṛttāntānabhijñau badhirāviva|
vivadetāṃ buddhimanto hasantyeva vilokya tau||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 274
units.deva:
यं कर्मी न विजानाति साक्षिणं तस्य तत्त्ववित्।
ब्रह्मत्वं बुध्यतां तत्र कर्मिणः किं विहीयते॥
units.translation: Let the knower of truth understand as Brahman the witness whom the ritualist does not know. What does the ritualist lose by that?
units.iast:
yaṃ karmī na vijānāti sākṣiṇaṃ tasya tattvavit|
brahmatvaṃ budhyatāṃ tatra karmiṇaḥ kiṃ vihīyate||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 275
units.deva:
देहवाग्बुद्धयस्त्यक्ता ज्ञानिनानृतबुद्धितः।
कर्मी प्रवर्तयत्वाभिर्ज्ञानिनो हीयतेऽत्र किम्॥
units.translation: The knower has set aside body, speech, and intellect, understanding them to be unreal. Let the ritualist use them; what does the knower lose by that?

gloss.en: because they are understood as unreal

units.iast:
dehavāgbuddhayastyaktā jñāninānṛtabuddhitaḥ|
karmī pravartayatvābhirjñānino hīyate’tra kim||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 276
units.deva:
प्रवृत्तिर्नोपयुक्ता चेन्निवृत्तिः क्वोपयुज्यते।
बोधे हेतुर्निवृत्तिश्चेद्बुभुत्सायां तथेतरा॥
units.translation: If action is not useful, where is inaction useful? If withdrawal helps bring knowledge, activity can likewise help the seeker who wants to know.
units.iast:
pravṛttirnopayuktā cennivṛttiḥ kvopayujyate|
bodhe heturnivṛttiścedbubhutsāyāṃ tathetarā||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 277
units.deva:
बुद्धश्चेन्न बुभुत्सेत नाप्यसौ बुध्यते पुनः।
अबाधादनुवर्तेत बोधो न त्वन्यसाधनात्॥
units.translation: If the truth is known, there is no further wish to know it, and one does not need to know it again. Knowledge continues because nothing contradicts it, not because of another means.
units.iast:
buddhaścenna bubhutseta nāpyasau budhyate punaḥ|
abādhādanuvarteta bodho na tvanyasādhanāt||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 278
units.deva:
नाविद्या नापि तत्कार्यं बोधं बाधितुमर्हति।
पुरैव तत्त्वबोधेन बाधिते ते उभे यतः॥
units.translation: Neither ignorance nor its effects can negate knowledge, since both have already been negated by knowledge of truth.
units.iast:
nāvidyā nāpi tatkāryaṃ bodhaṃ bādhitumarhati|
puraiva tattvabodhena bādhite te ubhe yataḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 279
units.deva:
बाधितं दृश्यतामक्षैस्तेन बाधो न शङ्क्यते।
जीवन्नाखुर्न मार्जारं हन्ति हन्यात्कथं मृतः॥
units.translation: Even if what has been negated is seen by the senses, there is no reason to think that it can negate knowledge. A living mouse cannot kill a cat; how could a dead one?
units.iast:
bādhitaṃ dṛśyatāmakṣaistena bādho na śaṅkyate|
jīvannākhurna mārjāraṃ hanti hanyātkathaṃ mṛtaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 280
units.deva:
अपि पाशुपतास्त्रेण विद्धश्चेन्न ममार यः।
निष्फलेषु वितुन्नाङ्गो नङ्क्ष्यतीत्यत्र का प्रमा॥
units.translation: If one did not die even when pierced by the Pāśupata weapon, what proof is there that he will perish with his limbs pierced by ineffective arrows?
units.iast:
api pāśupatāstreṇa viddhaścenna mamāra yaḥ|
niṣphaleṣu vitunnāṅgo naṅkṣyatītyatra kā pramā||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 281
units.deva:
आदावविद्यया चित्रैः स्वकार्यैर्जृम्भमाणया।
युद्ध्वा बोधोऽजयत् सोऽद्य सुदृढो बाध्यतां कथम्॥
units.translation: At first, knowledge fought and defeated ignorance as it swelled through its many effects. Now that knowledge is firmly established—how could it be obstructed?
units.iast:
ādāvavidyayā citraiḥ svakāryairjṛmbhamāṇayā|
yuddhvā bodho’jayat so’dya sudṛḍho bādhyatāṃ katham||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 282
units.deva:
तिष्ठन्त्वज्ञानतत्कार्यशवा बोधेन मारिताः।
न भीतिर्बोधसम्राजः कीर्तिः प्रत्युत तस्य तैः॥
units.translation: Let ignorance and its effects—the corpses struck down by knowledge—remain. The emperor of knowledge has nothing to fear from them; on the contrary, they only increase his renown.
units.iast:
tiṣṭhantvajñānatatkāryaśavā bodhena māritāḥ|
na bhītirbodhasamrājaḥ kīrtiḥ pratyuta tasya taiḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 283
units.deva:
य एवमतिशूरेण बोधेन न वियुज्यते।
निवृत्त्या वा प्रवृत्त्या वा देहादिगतयास्य किम्॥
units.translation: Whoever remains joined to such heroic knowledge—what can bodily activity or withdrawal do to him?

gloss.en: belonging to the body and the like

units.iast:
ya evamatiśūreṇa bodhena na viyujyate|
nivṛttyā vā pravṛttyā vā dehādigatayāsya kim||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 284
units.deva:
प्रवृत्तावाग्रहो न्याय्यो बोधहीनस्य सर्वथा।
स्वर्गाय वापवर्गाय योजितव्यं यतो नृभिः॥
units.translation: It is entirely proper for one without knowledge to insist on activity, since people should be engaged in action for heaven or liberation.
units.iast:
pravṛttāvāgraho nyāyyo bodhahīnasya sarvathā|
svargāya vāpavargāya yojitavyaṃ yato nṛbhiḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 285
units.deva:
विद्वांश्चेत्तादृशां मध्ये तिष्ठेत्तदनुरोधतः।
कायेन मनसा वाचा करोत्येवाखिलाः क्रियाः॥
units.translation: If a knower stands among people of that kind, he performs all actions with body, mind, and speech, in keeping with them.
units.iast:
vidvāṃścettādṛśāṃ madhye tiṣṭhettadanurodhataḥ|
kāyena manasā vācā karotyevākhilāḥ kriyāḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 286
units.deva:
एष मध्ये बुभुत्सानां यदा तिष्ठेत्तदा पुनः।
बोधायैषां क्रियाः सर्वा दूषयंस्त्यजतु स्वयम्॥
units.translation: When he stands among seekers of knowledge, then, to bring them to understanding, let him point out the faults in all actions and give them up himself.
units.iast:
eṣa madhye bubhutsānāṃ yadā tiṣṭhettadā punaḥ|
bodhāyaiṣāṃ kriyāḥ sarvā dūṣayaṃstyajatu svayam||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 287
units.deva:
अविद्वदनुसारेण वृत्तिर्बुद्धस्य युज्यते।
स्तनन्धयानुसारेण वर्तते तत्पिता यतः॥
units.translation: A knower’s conduct should accord with the conduct of the unknowing, just as a father behaves in step with his infant.
units.iast:
avidvadanusāreṇa vṛttirbuddhasya yujyate|
stanandhayānusāreṇa vartate tatpitā yataḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 288
units.deva:
अधिक्षिप्तस्ताडितो वा बालेन स्वपिता तदा।
न क्लिश्यति न कुप्येच्च बालं प्रत्युत लालयेत्॥
units.translation: When a child rebukes or strikes his own father, the father is neither distressed nor angry; instead, he comforts the child.
units.iast:
adhikṣiptastāḍito vā bālena svapitā tadā|
na kliśyati na kupyecca bālaṃ pratyuta lālayet||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 289
units.deva:
निन्दितः स्तूयमानो वा विद्वानज्ञैर्न निन्दति।
न स्तौति किन्तु तेषां स्याद्यथा बोधस्तथा चरेत्॥
units.translation: Whether blamed or praised by ignorant people, the knower does not blame or praise them in return; rather, he acts in whatever way will bring them understanding.
units.iast:
ninditaḥ stūyamāno vā vidvānajñairna nindati|
na stauti kintu teṣāṃ syādyathā bodhastathā caret||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 290
units.deva:
येनायं नटनेनात्र बुध्यते कार्यमेव तत्।
अज्ञप्रबोधान्नैवान्यत्कार्यमस्त्यत्र तद्विदः॥
units.translation: Whatever manner of conduct enables this person to understand here—that alone is the task. For the knower, there is no other task here than awakening the ignorant.
units.iast:
yenāyaṃ naṭanenātra budhyate kāryameva tat|
ajñaprabodhānnaivānyatkāryamastyatra tadvidaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 291
units.deva:
कृतकृत्यतया तृप्तः प्राप्तप्राप्यतया पुनः।
तृप्यनेवं स्वमनसा मन्यतेऽसौ निरन्तरम्॥
units.translation: Content with having done what had to be done, and having attained what had to be attained, he continually thinks to himself:

gloss.en: from having done what had to be done
from having attained what had to be attained

units.iast:
kṛtakṛtyatayā tṛptaḥ prāptaprāpyatayā punaḥ|
tṛpyanevaṃ svamanasā manyate’sau nirantaram||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 292
units.deva:
धन्योऽहं धन्योऽहं नित्यं स्वात्मानमञ्जसा वेद्मि।
धन्योऽहं धन्योऽहं ब्रह्मानन्दो विभाति मे स्पष्टम्॥
units.translation: Blessed am I, blessed am I: I always know my own Self directly. Blessed am I, blessed am I: the bliss of Brahman shines clearly for me.
units.iast:
dhanyo’haṃ dhanyo’haṃ nityaṃ svātmānamañjasā vedmi|
dhanyo’haṃ dhanyo’haṃ brahmānando vibhāti me spaṣṭam||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 293
units.deva:
धन्योऽहं धन्योऽहं दुःखं सांसारिकं न वीक्षेऽद्य।
धन्योऽहं धन्योऽहं स्वस्याज्ञानं पलायितं क्वापि॥
units.translation: Blessed am I, blessed am I: I no longer see worldly sorrow. Blessed am I, blessed am I: my ignorance has fled—I know not where.
units.iast:
dhanyo’haṃ dhanyo’haṃ duḥkhaṃ sāṃsārikaṃ na vīkṣe’dya|
dhanyo’haṃ dhanyo’haṃ svasyājñānaṃ palāyitaṃ kvāpi||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 294
units.deva:
धन्योऽहं धन्योऽहं कर्तव्यं मे न विद्यते किञ्चित्।
धन्योऽहं धन्योऽहं प्राप्तव्यं सर्वमद्य सम्पन्नम्॥
units.translation: Blessed am I, blessed am I: I have nothing left that needs to be done. Blessed am I, blessed am I: everything that had to be attained is now accomplished.
units.iast:
dhanyo’haṃ dhanyo’haṃ kartavyaṃ me na vidyate kiñcit|
dhanyo’haṃ dhanyo’haṃ prāptavyaṃ sarvamadya sampannam||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 295
units.deva:
धन्योऽहं धन्योऽहं तृप्तिर्मे कोपमा भवेल्लोके।
धन्योऽहं धन्योऽहं धन्यो धन्यो धन्यः पुनः पुनः॥
units.translation: Blessed am I, blessed am I: what could compare in the world with my contentment? Blessed am I, blessed am I—blessed, blessed, again and again.
units.iast:
dhanyo’haṃ dhanyo’haṃ tṛptirme kopamā bhavelloke|
dhanyo’haṃ dhanyo’haṃ dhanyo dhanyo dhanyaḥ punaḥ punaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 296
units.deva:
अहो पुण्यमहो पुण्यं फलितं फलितं दृढम्।
अस्य पुण्यस्य सम्पत्तेरहो वयमहो वयम्॥
units.translation: Wonderful, wonderful—my merit has borne firm fruit, again and again! Wonderful are we, wonderful are we, through the fruition of this merit!
units.iast:
aho puṇyamaho puṇyaṃ phalitaṃ phalitaṃ dṛḍham|
asya puṇyasya sampatteraho vayamaho vayam||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 297
units.deva:
अहो शास्त्रमहो शास्त्रमहो गुरुरहो गुरुः।
अहो ज्ञानमहो ज्ञानमहो सुखमहो सुखम्॥
units.translation: Wonderful are the scriptures, wonderful are the scriptures! Wonderful is the teacher, wonderful is the teacher! Wonderful is knowledge, wonderful is knowledge! Wonderful is bliss, wonderful is bliss!
units.iast:
aho śāstramaho śāstramaho gururaho guruḥ|
aho jñānamaho jñānamaho sukhamaho sukham||

units.label: Chapter 7 · Verse 298
units.deva:
तृप्तिदीपमिमं नित्यं येऽनुसन्दधते बुधाः।
ब्रह्मानन्दे निमज्जन्तस्ते तृप्यन्ति निरन्तरम्॥
units.translation: The wise who continually contemplate this Lamp of Contentment, immersed in the bliss of Brahman, remain content without interruption.
units.iast:
tṛptidīpamimaṃ nityaṃ ye’nusandadhate budhāḥ|
brahmānande nimajjantaste tṛpyanti nirantaram||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 1
units.deva:
खादित्यदीपिते कुड्ये दर्पणादित्यदीप्तिवत्।
कूटस्थभासितो देहो धीस्थजीवेन भास्यते॥
units.translation: Just as a wall lit by the sun in the sky is also lit by sunlight reflected in a mirror, the body lit by Kūṭastha is further lit by the jīva reflected in the intellect.

gloss.en: lit by the sun in the sky
like sunlight reflected in a mirror
by the jīva located in the intellect

units.iast:
khādityadīpite kuḍye darpaṇādityadīptivat|
kūṭasthabhāsito deho dhīsthajīvena bhāsyate||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 2
units.deva:
अनेकदर्पणादित्यदीप्तीनां बहुसन्धिषु।
इतरा व्यज्यते तासामभावेऽपि प्रकाशते॥
units.translation: In the many gaps between sunlight reflected by many mirrors, the other light—the sun itself—appears; it shines even when those reflections are absent.

gloss.en: of sunlight reflected in many mirrors

units.iast:
anekadarpaṇādityadīptīnāṃ bahusandhiṣu|
itarā vyajyate tāsāmabhāve’pi prakāśate||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 3
units.deva:
चिदाभासविशिष्टानां तथानेकधियामसौ।
सन्धिं धियामभावं च भासयन्प्रविविच्यताम्॥
units.translation: Likewise, that witness which makes manifest both the gaps among many intellects associated with reflected consciousness and the absence of those intellects should be carefully distinguished.
units.iast:
cidābhāsaviśiṣṭānāṃ tathānekadhiyāmasau|
sandhiṃ dhiyāmabhāvaṃ ca bhāsayanpravivicyatām||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 4
units.deva:
घटैकाकारधीस्था चिद्घटमेवावभासयेत्।
घटस्य ज्ञातता ब्रह्मचैतन्येनावभास्यते॥
units.translation: Consciousness present in a pot-shaped thought reveals the pot itself; the pot’s being-known is revealed by Brahman-consciousness.
units.iast:
ghaṭaikākāradhīsthā cidghaṭamevāvabhāsayet|
ghaṭasya jñātatā brahmacaitanyenāvabhāsyate||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 5
units.deva:
अज्ञातत्वेन ज्ञातोऽयं घटो बुद्ध्युदयात्पुरा।
ब्रह्मणैवोपरिष्टात्तु ज्ञातत्वेनेत्यसौ भिदा॥
units.translation: Before the intellect arises, this pot is known as unknown; afterward, it is known as known through Brahman alone. This is the difference.

gloss.en: before the rise of the intellect

units.iast:
ajñātatvena jñāto’yaṃ ghaṭo buddhyudayātpurā|
brahmaṇaivopariṣṭāttu jñātatvenetyasau bhidā||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 6
units.deva:
चिदाभासान्तधीवृत्तिर्ज्ञानं लोहान्तकुन्तवत्।
जाड्यमज्ञानमेताभ्यां व्याप्तः कुम्भो द्विधोच्यते॥
units.translation: An intellect-thought tipped with reflected consciousness is cognition, like a spear tipped with iron. Inertness is non-cognition; by these two, a pot is described as known or unknown.

gloss.en: like a spear with an iron tip

units.iast:
cidābhāsāntadhīvṛttirjñānaṃ lohāntakuntavat|
jāḍyamajñānametābhyāṃ vyāptaḥ kumbho dvidhocyate||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 7
units.deva:
अज्ञातो ब्रह्मणा भास्यो ज्ञातः कुम्भस्तथा न किम्।
ज्ञातत्वजननेनैव चिदाभासपरिक्षयः॥
units.translation: An unknown pot is made manifest by Brahman; why not a known pot as well? The reflected consciousness ceases with the very production of knownness.
units.iast:
ajñāto brahmaṇā bhāsyo jñātaḥ kumbhastathā na kim|
jñātatvajananenaiva cidābhāsaparikṣayaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 8
units.deva:
आभासहीनया बुद्ध्या ज्ञातत्वं नैव जन्यते।
तादृग्बुद्धेर्विशेषः को मृदादेः स्याद्विकारिणः॥
units.translation: Knownness cannot be produced by an intellect without reflected consciousness. How would such an intellect differ from inert clay and the like?
units.iast:
ābhāsahīnayā buddhyā jñātatvaṃ naiva janyate|
tādṛgbuddherviśeṣaḥ ko mṛdādeḥ syādvikāriṇaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 9
units.deva:
ज्ञात इत्युच्यते कुम्भो मृदा लिप्तो न कुत्रचित्।
धीमात्रव्याप्तकुम्भस्य ज्ञातत्वं नेष्यते तथा॥
units.translation: A pot smeared with clay is never called “known.” Likewise, knownness is not attributed to a pot pervaded by intellect alone.

gloss.en: of a pot pervaded by intellect alone

units.iast:
jñāta ityucyate kumbho mṛdā lipto na kutracit|
dhīmātravyāptakumbhasya jñātatvaṃ neṣyate tathā||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 10
units.deva:
ज्ञातत्वं नाम कुम्भेऽतश्चिदाभासफलोदयः।
न फलं ब्रह्मचैतन्यं मनात्प्रागपि सत्वतः॥
units.translation: A pot’s being-known is the effect produced by reflected consciousness. Brahman-consciousness is not an effect, because it exists even before any act of cognition.

gloss.en: the arising of the effect of reflected consciousness

units.iast:
jñātatvaṃ nāma kumbhe’taścidābhāsaphalodayaḥ|
na phalaṃ brahmacaitanyaṃ manātprāgapi satvataḥ||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 11
units.deva:
परागर्थप्रमेयेषु या फलत्वेन संमता
संवित्सैवेह मेयोऽर्थो वेदान्तोक्ति प्रमाणतः॥
units.translation: Among external objects of knowledge, consciousness is regarded as the result of cognition; according to Vedānta, that very consciousness is the object to be known here.
units.iast:
parāgarthaprameyeṣu yā phalatvena saṃmatā
saṃvitsaiveha meyo’rtho vedāntokti pramāṇataḥ||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 12
units.deva:
इति वार्तिककारेण चित्सदृश्यं विवक्षितम्
ब्रह्मचित्फलयोर्भेदः साहस्र्यां विश्रुतो यतः॥
units.translation: The author of the Vārttika means a likeness of pure consciousness, because the Upadeśa-sāhasrī clearly teaches a difference between Brahman-consciousness and result-consciousness.

gloss.en: by the author of the Vārttika

units.iast:
iti vārtikakāreṇa citsadṛśyaṃ vivakṣitam
brahmacitphalayorbhedaḥ sāhasryāṃ viśruto yataḥ||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 13
units.deva:
आभास उदितस्तस्माज्ज्ञातत्वं जनयेद्घटे।
तत्पुनर्ब्रह्मणा भास्यमज्ञातत्ववदेव हि॥
units.translation: The reflection arises and therefore produces the pot’s knownness. That knownness, like its unknownness, is then made manifest by Brahman.
units.iast:
ābhāsa uditastasmājjñātatvaṃ janayedghaṭe|
tatpunarbrahmaṇā bhāsyamajñātatvavadeva hi||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 14
units.deva:
धीवृत्त्याभासकुम्भानां समूहो भास्यते चिता।
कुम्भमात्रफलत्वात्स एक आभासतः स्फुरेत्॥
units.translation: Pure consciousness reveals the whole group—the mental modification, the reflection, and the pot. But because the cognitive result is only the pot, the pot itself appears through reflected consciousness.

gloss.en: because the result is only the pot

units.iast:
dhīvṛttyābhāsakumbhānāṃ samūho bhāsyate citā|
kumbhamātraphalatvātsa eka ābhāsataḥ sphuret||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 15
units.deva:
चैतन्यं द्विगुणं कुम्भे ज्ञातत्वेन स्फुरेत्ततः।
अन्येऽनुव्यवसायाख्यमाहुरेतद्यथोदितम्॥
units.translation: Therefore, in a pot, consciousness shines twofold as its being-known. Others call this subsequent awareness (anuvyavasāya).
units.iast:
caitanyaṃ dviguṇaṃ kumbhe jñātatvena sphurettataḥ|
anye’nuvyavasāyākhyamāhuretadyathoditam||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 16
units.deva:
घटोऽयमित्यसावुक्तिराभासस्य प्रसादतः।
विज्ञातो घट इत्युक्तिर्ब्रह्मानुग्रहतो भवेत्॥
units.translation: The statement “This is a pot” comes from the favor of reflected consciousness; the statement “The pot is known” comes from the favor of Brahman.
units.iast:
ghaṭo’yamityasāvuktirābhāsasya prasādataḥ|
vijñāto ghaṭa ityuktirbrahmānugrahato bhavet||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 17
units.deva:
आभासब्रह्मणी देहाद्बहिर्यद्वद्विवेचिते।
तद्वदाभासकूटस्थौ विविच्येतां वपुष्यपि॥
units.translation: Just as reflected consciousness and Brahman have been distinguished outside the body, so reflection and Kūṭastha should also be distinguished within the body.
units.iast:
ābhāsabrahmaṇī dehādbahiryadvadvivecite|
tadvadābhāsakūṭasthau vivicyetāṃ vapuṣyapi||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 18
units.deva:
अहंवृत्तौ चिदाभासः कामक्रोधादिकासु च।
संव्याप्य वर्तते तप्ते लोहे वह्निर्यथा तथा॥
units.translation: Just as fire pervades heated iron, reflected consciousness pervades the “I”-thought and desire, anger, and the like.

gloss.en: in desire, anger, and the like

units.iast:
ahaṃvṛttau cidābhāsaḥ kāmakrodhādikāsu ca|
saṃvyāpya vartate tapte lohe vahniryathā tathā||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 19
units.deva:
स्वमात्रं भासयेत्तप्तं लोहं नान्यत्कदाचन।
एवमाभाससहिता वृत्तयः स्वस्वभासिकाः॥
units.translation: Heated iron reveals only itself, never anything else. In the same way, thoughts accompanied by reflected consciousness each reveal their own objects.
units.iast:
svamātraṃ bhāsayettaptaṃ lohaṃ nānyatkadācana|
evamābhāsasahitā vṛttayaḥ svasvabhāsikāḥ||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 20
units.deva:
क्रमाद्विच्छिद्य विच्छिद्य जायन्ते वृत्तयोऽखिलाः।
सर्वा अपि विलीयन्ते सुप्तिमूर्च्छासमाधिषु॥
units.translation: All mental modifications arise intermittently, one after another; they all dissolve during sleep, fainting, and samādhi.
units.iast:
kramādvicchidya vicchidya jāyante vṛttayo’khilāḥ|
sarvā api vilīyante suptimūrcchāsamādhiṣu||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 21
units.deva:
सन्धयोऽखिलवृत्तीनामभावाश्चावभासिताः।
निर्विकारेण येनासौ कूटस्थ इति गीयते॥
units.translation: The intervals among all mental modifications, and their absences, are made manifest by that changeless awareness; it is called Kūṭastha.
units.iast:
sandhayo’khilavṛttīnāmabhāvāścāvabhāsitāḥ|
nirvikāreṇa yenāsau kūṭastha iti gīyate||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 22
units.deva:
घटे द्विगुणचैतन्यं यथा बाह्ये तथान्तरे।
वृत्तिष्वपि ततस्तत्र वैशद्यं सन्धितोऽधिकम्॥
units.translation: Just as consciousness is twofold in the cognition of an external pot, so it is in internal thoughts as well; therefore the thoughts are clearer than the intervals between them.
units.iast:
ghaṭe dviguṇacaitanyaṃ yathā bāhye tathāntare|
vṛttiṣvapi tatastatra vaiśadyaṃ sandhito’dhikam||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 23
units.deva:
ज्ञातताज्ञातते न स्तो घटवद्वृत्तिषु क्वचित्।
स्वस्य स्वेनागृहीतत्वात्ताभिश्चाज्ञाननाशनात्॥
units.translation: Unlike a pot, mental modifications are never said to be either known or unknown: the intellect cannot grasp itself, and through its modifications it removes ignorance.

gloss.en: because of the destruction of ignorance

units.iast:
jñātatājñātate na sto ghaṭavadvṛttiṣu kvacit|
svasya svenāgṛhītatvāttābhiścājñānanāśanāt||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 24
units.deva:
द्विगुणीकृतचैतन्ये जन्मनाशानुभूतितः।
अकूटस्थं तदन्यत्तु कूटस्थमविकारितः॥
units.translation: Because consciousness made twofold is experienced as arising and ceasing, it is not Kūṭastha; the other is Kūṭastha because it is changeless.

gloss.en: because arising and ceasing are experienced

units.iast:
dviguṇīkṛtacaitanye janmanāśānubhūtitaḥ|
akūṭasthaṃ tadanyattu kūṭasthamavikāritaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 25
units.deva:
अन्तःकरणतद्वृत्तिसाक्षीत्यादावनेकधा।
कूटस्थः एव सर्वत्र पूर्वाचार्यैर्विनिश्चितः॥
units.translation: Earlier teachers have established everywhere that Kūṭastha itself is the witness, in statements such as “the witness of the inner instrument and its thoughts.”
units.iast:
antaḥkaraṇatadvṛttisākṣītyādāvanekadhā|
kūṭasthaḥ eva sarvatra pūrvācāryairviniścitaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 26
units.deva:
आत्माभासाश्रयश्चैवं मुखाभासाश्रया यथा।
गम्यन्ते शास्त्रयुक्तिभ्यामित्याभासश्च वर्णितः॥
units.translation: The Self, its reflection, and its basis are understood, as are a face, its reflection, and the mirror; scripture and reasoning establish this. Thus reflected consciousness has also been explained.

gloss.en: the Self, its reflection, and its basis
a face, its reflection, and its basis

units.iast:
ātmābhāsāśrayaścaivaṃ mukhābhāsāśrayā yathā|
gamyante śāstrayuktibhyāmityābhāsaśca varṇitaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 27
units.deva:
बुद्ध्यवच्छिन्नकूटस्थो लोकान्तरगमागमौ।
कर्तुं शक्तो घटाकाश इवाभासेन किं वद॥
units.translation: (Objection) Kūṭastha limited by the intellect can go to other worlds and return, like space within a pot. What need is there for reflected consciousness? Tell me.
units.iast:
buddhyavacchinnakūṭastho lokāntaragamāgamau|
kartuṃ śakto ghaṭākāśa ivābhāsena kiṃ vada||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 28
units.deva:
शृण्वसङ्गः परिच्छेदमात्राज्जीवो भवेन्न हि।
अन्यथा घटकुड्याद्यैरवच्छिन्नस्य जीवता॥
units.translation: (Reply) Listen: the unattached [Kūṭastha] does not become an individual self merely by being limited. Otherwise, even space limited by a pot, wall, and the like would become an individual self.

gloss.en: by a pot, wall, and the like

units.iast:
śṛṇvasaṅgaḥ paricchedamātrājjīvo bhavenna hi|
anyathā ghaṭakuḍyādyairavacchinnasya jīvatā||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 29
units.deva:
न कुड्यसादृशी बुद्धिः स्वच्छत्वादिति चेत्तथा।
अस्तु नाम परिच्छेदे किं स्वाच्छ्येन भवेत्तव॥
units.translation: (Objection) If you say that the intellect is unlike a wall because it is transparent, so be it; but what does transparency change about its being limited?
units.iast:
na kuḍyasādṛśī buddhiḥ svacchatvāditi cettathā|
astu nāma paricchede kiṃ svācchyena bhavettava||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 30
units.deva:
प्रस्थेन दारुजन्येन कांस्यजन्येन वा न हि।
विक्रेतुस्तण्डुलादिनां परिमाणं विशिष्यते॥
units.translation: Whether the measure is made of wood or bronze, the quantity of rice and similar grains measured for the seller does not differ.
units.iast:
prasthena dārujanyena kāṃsyajanyena vā na hi|
vikretustaṇḍulādināṃ parimāṇaṃ viśiṣyate||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 31
units.deva:
परिमाणविशेषेऽपि प्रतिबिम्बो विशिष्यते।
कांस्ये यदि तदा बुद्धावप्याभासो भवेद्बलात्॥
units.translation: Even if a bronze measure produces a reflection despite a difference in measurement, then a reflection must necessarily arise in the intellect too.

gloss.en: even with a difference in measurement

units.iast:
parimāṇaviśeṣe’pi pratibimbo viśiṣyate|
kāṃsye yadi tadā buddhāvapyābhāso bhavedbalāt||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 32
units.deva:
ईषद्भासनमाभासः प्रतिबिम्बस्तथाविधः।
बिम्बलक्षणहीनः सन्बिम्बवद्भासते स हि॥
units.translation: Ābhāsa means a faint appearance; a reflection is of the same kind. Though lacking the features of the original, it appears like the original.

gloss.en: lacking the features of the original

units.iast:
īṣadbhāsanamābhāsaḥ pratibimbastathāvidhaḥ|
bimbalakṣaṇahīnaḥ sanbimbavadbhāsate sa hi||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 33
units.deva:
ससङ्गत्वविकाराभ्यां बिम्बलक्षणहीनता।
स्फूर्तिरूपत्वमेतस्य बिम्बवद्भासनं विदुः॥
units.translation: Because it is associated and changeable, reflected consciousness lacks the features of the original. The wise say that it resembles the original only in its manifesting nature.

gloss.en: the lack of the original’s features

units.iast:
sasaṅgatvavikārābhyāṃ bimbalakṣaṇahīnatā|
sphūrtirūpatvametasya bimbavadbhāsanaṃ viduḥ||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 34
units.deva:
न हि धीभावभावित्वादाभासोऽस्ति धियः पृथक्।
इति चेदल्पमेवोक्तं धीरप्येवं स्वदेहतः॥
units.translation: (Objection) If reflected consciousness is not separate from the intellect because it exists only when the intellect exists, little has been said: the intellect too could be treated as not separate from its body.

gloss.en: because it exists only when the intellect exists

units.iast:
na hi dhībhāvabhāvitvādābhāso’sti dhiyaḥ pṛthak|
iti cedalpamevoktaṃ dhīrapyevaṃ svadehataḥ||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 35
units.deva:
देहे मृतेऽपि बुद्धिश्चेच्छास्त्रादस्ति तथा सति।
बुद्धेरन्यश्चिदाभासः प्रवेशश्रुतिषु श्रुतः॥
units.translation: (Objection) Scripture says that the intellect exists even after the body dies. (Reply) In that case, reflected consciousness is distinct from the intellect, as the scriptural passages on entry declare.

gloss.en: in the scriptural passages on entry

units.iast:
dehe mṛte’pi buddhiścecchāstrādasti tathā sati|
buddheranyaścidābhāsaḥ praveśaśrutiṣu śrutaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 36
units.deva:
धीयुक्तस्य प्रवेशश्चेन्नैतरेये धियः पृथक्।
आत्मा प्रवेशं सङ्कल्प्य प्रविष्ट इति गीयते॥
units.translation: (Objection) The entrant is accompanied by the intellect. (Reply) The Aitareya says otherwise: the Self resolved to enter and entered, distinct from the intellect.

gloss.en: of one joined with the intellect

units.iast:
dhīyuktasya praveśaścennaitareye dhiyaḥ pṛthak|
ātmā praveśaṃ saṅkalpya praviṣṭa iti gīyate||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 37
units.deva:
कथं न्विदं साक्षदेहं मदृते स्यादितीरणात्।
विदार्य मूर्ध्नः सीमानं प्रविष्टः संसरत्ययम्॥
units.translation: At the thought, “How can this body with its sense organs exist without me?” the Self split the crown’s seam, entered, and began to transmigrate.

gloss.en: body together with its sense organs

units.iast:
kathaṃ nvidaṃ sākṣadehaṃ madṛte syāditīraṇāt|
vidārya mūrdhnaḥ sīmānaṃ praviṣṭaḥ saṃsaratyayam||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 38
units.deva:
कथं प्रविष्टोऽसङ्गश्चेत्सृष्टिर्वास्य कथं वद।
मायिकत्वं तयोस्तुल्यं विनाशश्च समस्तयोः॥
units.translation: (Objection) If the unattached Self has entered, how can it remain unattached? Tell me, then, how it creates. Entry and creation are equally māyic, and both cease with māyā.
units.iast:
kathaṃ praviṣṭo’saṅgaścetsṛṣṭirvāsya kathaṃ vada|
māyikatvaṃ tayostulyaṃ vināśaśca samastayoḥ||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 39
units.deva:
समुत्थायैव भूतेभ्यस्तान्येवानुविनश्यति।
विस्पष्टमिति मैत्रेय्य याज्ञवल्क्य उवाच हि॥
units.translation: “Having arisen from these elements, it dissolves back into those very elements”—this was stated plainly by Yājñavalkya to Maitreyi.
units.iast:
samutthāyaiva bhūtebhyastānyevānuvinaśyati|
vispaṣṭamiti maitreyya yājñavalkya uvāca hi||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 40
units.deva:
अविनाश्ययमात्मेति कूटस्थः प्रविवेचितः।
मात्रासंसर्ग इत्येवमसङ्गत्वस्य कीर्तनात्॥
units.translation: The statement “This Self is imperishable” distinguishes Kūṭastha. The Śruti’s statement about freedom from contact with sense-objects proclaims its non-attachment.
units.iast:
avināśyayamātmeti kūṭasthaḥ pravivecitaḥ|
mātrāsaṃsarga ityevamasaṅgatvasya kīrtanāt||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 41
units.deva:
जीवापेतं वाव किल शरीरं म्रियते न सः।
इत्यत्र न विमोक्षोऽर्थः किन्तु लोकान्तरे गतिः॥
units.translation: Here, “The body left by the jīva indeed dies, but the jīva does not die” means not liberation, but passage to another world.
units.iast:
jīvāpetaṃ vāva kila śarīraṃ mriyate na saḥ|
ityatra na vimokṣo’rthaḥ kintu lokāntare gatiḥ||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 42
units.deva:
नाहं ब्रह्मेति बुध्येत स विनाशीति चेन्न तत्।
सामानाधिकरण्यस्य बाधायामपि सम्भवात्॥
units.translation: If you object, “If the jīva is perishable, how could it understand ‘I am Brahman’?”—that objection fails: a sentence can identify one reality by cancelling a false notion.

gloss.en: in cancellation of a false notion

units.iast:
nāhaṃ brahmeti budhyeta sa vināśīti cenna tat|
sāmānādhikaraṇyasya bādhāyāmapi sambhavāt||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 43
units.deva:
योऽयं स्थाणुः पुमानेष पुंधिया स्थाणुधीरिव।
ब्रह्मास्मीति धिया शेषा ह्यहं बुद्धिर्निवर्तते॥
units.translation: Just as the thought “this post is a man” removes the thought “this is a post,” the thought “I am Brahman” removes the remaining “I”-notion.

gloss.en: by the thought “it is a man”

units.iast:
yo’yaṃ sthāṇuḥ pumāneṣa puṃdhiyā sthāṇudhīriva|
brahmāsmīti dhiyā śeṣā hyahaṃ buddhirnivartate||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 44
units.deva:
नैष्कर्म्यसिद्धावप्येवमाचार्यैः स्पष्टमीरितम्।
सामानाधिकरण्यस्य बाधार्थत्वं ततोऽस्तु तत्॥
units.translation: The teachers state this clearly in the Naiṣkarmya-siddhi too; so let same-referent wording be understood as serving the cancellation of a false notion.
units.iast:
naiṣkarmyasiddhāvapyevamācāryaiḥ spaṣṭamīritam|
sāmānādhikaraṇyasya bādhārthatvaṃ tato’stu tat||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 45
units.deva:
सर्वं ब्रह्मेति जगता सामानाधिकरण्यवत्।
अहं ब्रह्मेति जीवेन सामानाधिकृतिर्भवेत्॥
units.translation: Just as “All this is Brahman” treats the world and Brahman as one referent, “I am Brahman” may likewise treat the jīva and Brahman as one referent.
units.iast:
sarvaṃ brahmeti jagatā sāmānādhikaraṇyavat|
ahaṃ brahmeti jīvena sāmānādhikṛtirbhavet||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 46
units.deva:
सामानाधिकरण्यस्य बाधार्थत्वं निराकृतम्।
प्रयत्नतो विवरणे कूटस्थत्वविवक्षया॥
units.translation: The Vivaraṇa deliberately rejects the cancellation-based reading of same-referent wording, intending Kūṭastha as the meaning.

gloss.en: with Kūṭastha as the intended meaning

units.iast:
sāmānādhikaraṇyasya bādhārthatvaṃ nirākṛtam|
prayatnato vivaraṇe kūṭasthatvavivakṣayā||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 47
units.deva:
शोधितस्त्वं पदार्थो यः कूटस्थो ब्रह्मरूपताम्।
तस्य वक्तुं विवरणे तथोक्तमितरत्र च॥
units.translation: The clarified meaning of “you” is Kūṭastha, whose nature is Brahman; the Vivaraṇa and other works state this.
units.iast:
śodhitastvaṃ padārtho yaḥ kūṭastho brahmarūpatām|
tasya vaktuṃ vivaraṇe tathoktamitaratra ca||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 48
units.deva:
देहेन्द्रियादियुक्तस्य जीवाभासभ्रमस्य या।
अधिष्ठानचितिः सैषा कूटस्थात्र विवक्षिता॥
units.translation: Here, Kūṭastha means the underlying consciousness that supports the mistaken appearance of the reflected jīva, associated with body, senses, and the rest.

gloss.en: of what is associated with body, senses, and the rest
of the mistaken appearance of the reflected jīva

units.iast:
dehendriyādiyuktasya jīvābhāsabhramasya yā|
adhiṣṭhānacitiḥ saiṣā kūṭasthātra vivakṣitā||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 49
units.deva:
जगद्भ्रमस्य सर्वस्य यदधिष्ठानमीरितम्।
त्रय्यन्तेषु तदत्र स्याद्ब्रह्मशब्दविवक्षितम्॥
units.translation: The Upanishads call “Brahman” that on which the appearance of the whole world rests.
units.iast:
jagadbhramasya sarvasya yadadhiṣṭhānamīritam|
trayyanteṣu tadatra syādbrahmaśabdavivakṣitam||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 50
units.deva:
एतस्मिन्नेव चैतन्ये जगदारोप्यते यदा।
तदा तदेकदेशस्य जीवाभासस्य का कथा॥
units.translation: When the world is superimposed on this very consciousness, what more need be said of the jīva-reflection, which is only a part of that world?
units.iast:
etasminneva caitanye jagadāropyate yadā|
tadā tadekadeśasya jīvābhāsasya kā kathā||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 51
units.deva:
जगत्तदेकदेशाख्यसमारोप्यस्य भेदतः।
तत्त्वंपदार्थौ भिन्नौ स्तो वस्तुतस्त्वेकता चितः॥
units.translation: The meanings of “that” and “you” seem different because the superimposed world and its part, the jīva, differ; in reality, consciousness is one.

gloss.en: of the superimposed appearances called “the world” and “a part of it”

units.iast:
jagattadekadeśākhyasamāropyasya bhedataḥ|
tattvaṃpadārthau bhinnau sto vastutastvekatā citaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 52
units.deva:
कर्तृत्वादीन्बुद्धिधर्मान्स्फूर्त्याख्यां चात्मरूपताम्।
दधद्विभाति पुरत आभासोऽतो भ्रमो भवेत्॥
units.translation: The reflection appears before us, bearing both the intellect’s qualities, such as agency, and the Self’s quality of luminosity; therefore it can be mistaken for the Self.
units.iast:
kartṛtvādīnbuddhidharmānsphūrtyākhyāṃ cātmarūpatām|
dadhadvibhāti purata ābhāso’to bhramo bhavet||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 53
units.deva:
का बुद्धिः कोऽयमाभासः को वात्रात्मा जगत्कथम्।
इत्यनिर्णयतो मोहः सोऽयं संसार इष्यते॥
units.translation: “What is the intellect? What is this reflection of consciousness? What is the Self here, and how is the world here?” This uncertainty is confusion; it is called saṃsāra.

gloss.en: from uncertainty; lack of clear understanding

units.iast:
kā buddhiḥ ko’yamābhāsaḥ ko vātrātmā jagatkatham|
ityanirṇayato mohaḥ so’yaṃ saṃsāra iṣyate||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 54
units.deva:
बुद्ध्यादीनां स्वरूपं यो विविनक्ति स तत्त्ववित्।
स एव मुक्त इत्येवं वेदान्तेषु विनिश्चयः॥
units.translation: Whoever clearly discerns the true nature of the intellect and the rest is a knower of reality; that person alone is liberated. This is the firm conclusion of the Vedānta texts.

gloss.en: of the intellect and the rest

units.iast:
buddhyādīnāṃ svarūpaṃ yo vivinakti sa tattvavit|
sa eva mukta ityevaṃ vedānteṣu viniścayaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 55
units.deva:
एवं च सति बन्धः स्यात्कस्येत्यादिकुतर्कजाः।
विडम्बनादृढं खण्ड्याः खण्डनोक्तिप्रकारतः॥
units.translation: When this is so, absurd objections born of bad reasoning—such as “Whose is bondage?”—should be firmly refuted by the method stated in Khaṇḍana.

gloss.en: by the method stated in Khaṇḍana

units.iast:
evaṃ ca sati bandhaḥ syātkasyetyādikutarkajāḥ|
viḍambanādṛḍhaṃ khaṇḍyāḥ khaṇḍanoktiprakārataḥ||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 56
units.deva:
वृत्तेः साक्षितया वृत्तेः प्रागभावस्य च स्थितः।
बुभुत्सायां तथाज्ञोऽस्मीत्याभासाज्ञानवस्तुनः॥
units.translation: Kūṭastha remains the witness of each mental thought and of its prior absence; it also witnesses the desire to know and the ignorance that appears as “I am ignorant.”

gloss.en: when there is a desire to know

units.iast:
vṛtteḥ sākṣitayā vṛtteḥ prāgabhāvasya ca sthitaḥ|
bubhutsāyāṃ tathājño’smītyābhāsājñānavastunaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verses 57–58
units.deva:
असत्यालम्बनत्वेन सत्यः सर्वजडस्य तु।
साधकत्वेन चिद्रूपः सदा प्रेमास्पदत्वतः॥
आनन्दरूपः सर्वार्थसाधकत्वेन हेतुना।
सर्व सम्बन्धवत्त्वेन सम्पूर्णः शिवसंज्ञितः॥
units.translation: As the support of the unreal, it is real; because it enables all inert things to appear, it is consciousness; because it is always loved, it is bliss. As the means to every aim and the ground of all relations, it is complete and is called Śiva.

gloss.en: as the support of what is unreal
is of the nature of consciousness
because it is the object of love
is of the nature of bliss
as the means to every aim
because it is related to all

units.iast:
asatyālambanatvena satyaḥ sarvajaḍasya tu|
sādhakatvena cidrūpaḥ sadā premāspadatvataḥ||
ānandarūpaḥ sarvārthasādhakatvena hetunā|
sarva sambandhavattvena sampūrṇaḥ śivasaṃjñitaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 59
units.deva:
इति शैवपुराणेषु कूटस्थः प्रविवेचितः।
जीवेशत्वादिरहितः केवलः स्वप्रभः शिवः॥
units.translation: Thus the Śaiva Purāṇas carefully distinguish Kūṭastha as free from jīva-hood, lordship, and the rest: it is alone, self-luminous, and Śiva.

gloss.en: free from jīva-hood, lordship, and the rest

units.iast:
iti śaivapurāṇeṣu kūṭasthaḥ pravivecitaḥ|
jīveśatvādirahitaḥ kevalaḥ svaprabhaḥ śivaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 60
units.deva:
मायाभासेन जीवेशौ करोतीति श्रुतत्वतः।
मायिकावेव जीवेशौ स्वच्छौ तौ काचकुम्भवत्॥
units.translation: Because Śruti says Māyā creates the jīva and Īśvara through a reflection of consciousness, both are indeed made by Māyā; like glass pots, they are transparent.

gloss.en: through a reflection of consciousness in Māyā
both are indeed made by Māyā

units.iast:
māyābhāsena jīveśau karotīti śrutatvataḥ|
māyikāveva jīveśau svacchau tau kācakumbhavat||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 61
units.deva:
अन्नजन्यं मनोदेहात्स्वच्छं यद्वत्तथैव तौ।
मायिकावपि सर्वस्मादन्यस्मात्स्वच्छतां गतौ॥
units.translation: Just as the mind, though born from food, is clearer than the body, so the jīva and Īśvara, though made by Māyā, are clearer than all other things.
units.iast:
annajanyaṃ manodehātsvacchaṃ yadvattathaiva tau|
māyikāvapi sarvasmādanyasmātsvacchatāṃ gatau||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 62
units.deva:
चिद्रूपत्वं च सम्भाव्यं चित्त्वेनैव प्रकाशनात्।
सर्वकल्पनशक्ताया मायाया दुष्करं न हि॥
units.translation: Since they reveal things through consciousness alone, it is reasonable to regard them as conscious; Māyā, which can project everything, finds nothing difficult.

gloss.en: being of the nature of consciousness
of her who can project everything

units.iast:
cidrūpatvaṃ ca sambhāvyaṃ cittvenaiva prakāśanāt|
sarvakalpanaśaktāyā māyāyā duṣkaraṃ na hi||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 63
units.deva:
अस्मन्निद्रापि जीवेशौ चेतनौ स्वप्नगौ सृजेत्।
महामाया सृजत्येतावित्याश्चर्यं किमत्र ते॥
units.translation: Even our sleep can create a conscious jīva and Īśvara as dream figures. If Great Māyā creates these two, what is surprising about that?
units.iast:
asmannidrāpi jīveśau cetanau svapnagau sṛjet|
mahāmāyā sṛjatyetāvityāścaryaṃ kimatra te||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 64
units.deva:
सर्वज्ञत्वादिकं चेशे कल्पयित्वा प्रदर्शयेत्।
धर्मिणं कल्पयेद्यास्याः को भारो धर्मकल्पने॥
units.translation: Māyā projects and displays omniscience and the other qualities in Īśvara. If she can project the bearer of qualities, what difficulty is there in projecting the qualities?
units.iast:
sarvajñatvādikaṃ ceśe kalpayitvā pradarśayet|
dharmiṇaṃ kalpayedyāsyāḥ ko bhāro dharmakalpane||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 65
units.deva:
कूटस्थेऽप्यतिशङ्का स्यादिति चेन्मातिशङ्क्यताम्।
कूटस्थमायिकत्वे तु प्रमाणं न हि वर्तते॥
units.translation: If you say that doubt may arise even about Kūṭastha, do not entertain it: there is no evidence that Kūṭastha is made by Māyā.

gloss.en: as to whether Kūṭastha is made by Māyā

units.iast:
kūṭasthe’pyatiśaṅkā syāditi cenmātiśaṅkyatām|
kūṭasthamāyikatve tu pramāṇaṃ na hi vartate||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 66
units.deva:
वस्तुत्वं घोषयन्त्यस्य वेदान्ताः सकला अपि।
सपत्नरूपं वस्त्वन्यन्न सहन्तेऽत्र किंचन॥
units.translation: All the Vedānta texts proclaim the reality of Kūṭastha and admit no other rival reality here.
units.iast:
vastutvaṃ ghoṣayantyasya vedāntāḥ sakalā api|
sapatnarūpaṃ vastvanyanna sahante’tra kiṃcana||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 67
units.deva:
श्रुत्यर्थं विशदीकुर्मो न तर्कान्वच्मि किंचन।
तेन तार्किकशंकानामत्र कोऽवसरो वद॥
units.translation: We make the meaning of Śruti clear; we set out no arguments. Tell me, what place is there here for the logicians’ doubts?
units.iast:
śrutyarthaṃ viśadīkurmo na tarkānvacmi kiṃcana|
tena tārkikaśaṃkānāmatra ko’vasaro vada||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 68
units.deva:
तस्मात्कुतर्कं सन्त्यज्य मुमुक्षुः श्रुतिमाश्रयेत्।
श्रुतौ तु मायाजीवेशौ करोतीति प्रदर्शितम्॥
units.translation: Therefore, a seeker of liberation should give up false reasoning and rely on Śruti. Scripture teaches that Māyā creates the jīva and Īśvara.
units.iast:
tasmātkutarkaṃ santyajya mumukṣuḥ śrutimāśrayet|
śrutau tu māyājīveśau karotīti pradarśitam||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 69
units.deva:
ईक्षणादिप्रवेशान्ता सृष्टिरीशकृता भवेत्।
जाग्रदादिविमोक्षन्तः संसारो जीवकर्तृकः॥
units.translation: Īśvara’s creation runs from the first resolve to create to the final entry; the jīva’s saṃsāra, made by the jīva, runs from waking experience to liberation.

gloss.en: beginning with the resolve to create

units.iast:
īkṣaṇādipraveśāntā sṛṣṭirīśakṛtā bhavet|
jāgradādivimokṣantaḥ saṃsāro jīvakartṛkaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 70
units.deva:
असङ्ग एव कूटस्थः सर्वदा नास्य कश्चन।
भवत्यतिशयस्तेन मनस्येवं विचार्यताम्॥
units.translation: Kūṭastha is always unattached, and no change ever arises in it. Reflect on it in this way.
units.iast:
asaṅga eva kūṭasthaḥ sarvadā nāsya kaścana|
bhavatyatiśayastena manasyevaṃ vicāryatām||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 71
units.deva:
न निरोधो न चोत्पत्तिर्न बद्धो न च साधकः।
न मुमुक्षुर्न वै मुक्त इत्येषा परमार्थता॥
units.translation: There is no cessation, no arising; no one bound, no practitioner, no seeker of liberation, and no liberated one. This is the ultimate truth.
units.iast:
na nirodho na cotpattirna baddho na ca sādhakaḥ|
na mumukṣurna vai mukta ityeṣā paramārthatā||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 72
units.deva:
अवाङ्मनसगम्यं तं श्रुतिर्बोधयितुं सदा।
जीवमीशं जगद्वापि समाश्रित्यावबोधयेत्॥
units.translation: Though beyond the reach of speech and mind, Śruti teaches that reality by referring to the jīva, Īśvara, or the world.

gloss.en: beyond the reach of speech and mind
taking as its support; referring to

units.iast:
avāṅmanasagamyaṃ taṃ śrutirbodhayituṃ sadā|
jīvamīśaṃ jagadvāpi samāśrityāvabodhayet||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 73
units.deva:
यया यया भवेत्पुंसां व्युत्पत्तिः प्रत्यगात्मनि।
सा सैव प्रक्रियेह स्यात्साध्वीत्याचार्यभाषितम्॥
units.translation: Whatever method helps people understand the inner Self is the very method that should be accepted here as sound, the teacher says.

gloss.en: is what the teacher has said

units.iast:
yayā yayā bhavetpuṃsāṃ vyutpattiḥ pratyagātmani|
sā saiva prakriyeha syātsādhvītyācāryabhāṣitam||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 74
units.deva:
श्रुतितात्पर्यमखिलमबुध्वा भ्राम्यते जडः।
विवेकी त्वखिलं बुध्वा तिष्ठत्यानन्दवारिधौ॥
units.translation: Not understanding the full purport of Śruti, the dull-minded person wanders; the discerning person, understanding it all, remains in the ocean of bliss.
units.iast:
śrutitātparyamakhilamabudhvā bhrāmyate jaḍaḥ|
vivekī tvakhilaṃ budhvā tiṣṭhatyānandavāridhau||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 75
units.deva:
मायामेघो जगन्नीरं वर्षत्वेष यथा तथा।
चिदाकाशस्य नो हानिर्न वा लाभ इति स्थितिः॥
units.translation: Let the cloud of Māyā pour the waters of the world as it may; the space of consciousness suffers neither loss nor gain. This is the settled truth.
units.iast:
māyāmegho jagannīraṃ varṣatveṣa yathā tathā|
cidākāśasya no hānirna vā lābha iti sthitiḥ||

units.label: Chapter 8 · Verse 76
units.deva:
इमं कूटस्थदीपं योऽनुसन्धत्ते निरन्तरम्।
स्वयं कूटस्थरूपेण दीप्यतेऽसौ निरन्तरम्॥
units.translation: Whoever constantly contemplates this Lamp of Kūṭastha shines constantly as Kūṭastha itself.
units.iast:
imaṃ kūṭasthadīpaṃ yo’nusandhatte nirantaram|
svayaṃ kūṭastharūpeṇa dīpyate’sau nirantaram||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 1
units.deva:
संवादिभ्रमवद्ब्रह्मतत्त्वोपास्त्यापि मुच्यते।
उत्तरे तापनियेऽतः श्रुतोपास्तिरनेकधा॥
units.translation: As an error can sometimes lead to the right result by coincidence, contemplation of Brahman’s reality can also bring liberation. For this reason, the Uttara Tāpanīya teaches many forms of worship.

gloss.en: like an error that happens to lead to the right result

units.iast:
saṃvādibhramavadbrahmatattvopāstyāpi mucyate|
uttare tāpaniye’taḥ śrutopāstiranekadhā||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 2
units.deva:
मणिप्रदीपप्रभयोर्मणिबुद्ध्याभिधावतोः।
मिथ्याज्ञानाविशेषेऽपि विशेषोऽर्थक्रियां प्रति॥
units.translation: Two people run toward the lights of a gem and a lamp, each thinking the light is a gem. Though their mistaken beliefs are alike, the practical result differs.

gloss.en: of the light of a gem and a lamp
of the two who run toward them

units.iast:
maṇipradīpaprabhayormaṇibuddhyābhidhāvatoḥ|
mithyājñānāviśeṣe’pi viśeṣo’rthakriyāṃ prati||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 3
units.deva:
दीपोपवरकस्यान्तर्वर्तते तत्प्रभा बहिः।
दृश्यते द्वार्यथान्यत्र तद्वद्दृष्टा मणेः प्रभा॥
units.translation: A lamp inside a room casts light that is seen outside at the doorway; similarly, a gem’s light can be seen from somewhere else.
units.iast:
dīpopavarakasyāntarvartate tatprabhā bahiḥ|
dṛśyate dvāryathānyatra tadvaddṛṣṭā maṇeḥ prabhā||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 4
units.deva:
दूरे प्रभाद्वयं दृष्ट्वा मणिबुद्ध्याभिधावतोः।
प्रभायां मणिबुद्धिस्तु मिथ्याज्ञानं द्वयोरपि॥
units.translation: Seeing two lights in the distance, two people run toward them thinking they are gems. Though both take the lights for gems, their mistaken ideas are alike.

gloss.en: of the two who run toward them

units.iast:
dūre prabhādvayaṃ dṛṣṭvā maṇibuddhyābhidhāvatoḥ|
prabhāyāṃ maṇibuddhistu mithyājñānaṃ dvayorapi||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 5
units.deva:
न लभ्यते मणिर्दीपप्रभां प्रत्यभिधावता।
प्रभायां धावतावश्यं लभ्यतैव मणिर्मणेः॥
units.translation: The person who runs after lamplight does not obtain a gem; the one who runs toward the gem’s light certainly finds the gem.
units.iast:
na labhyate maṇirdīpaprabhāṃ pratyabhidhāvatā|
prabhāyāṃ dhāvatāvaśyaṃ labhyataiva maṇirmaṇeḥ||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 6
units.deva:
दीपप्रभामणिभ्रान्तिर्विसंवादिभ्रमः स्मृतः।
मणिप्रभामणिभ्रान्तिः संवादिभ्रम उच्यते॥
units.translation: Mistaking lamplight for a gem is called a misleading error; mistaking a gem’s radiance for the gem is called an error that leads to the right result.

gloss.en: mistaking a gem’s radiance for the gem
an error that leads to the right result

units.iast:
dīpaprabhāmaṇibhrāntirvisaṃvādibhramaḥ smṛtaḥ|
maṇiprabhāmaṇibhrāntiḥ saṃvādibhrama ucyate||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 7
units.deva:
बाष्पं धूमतया बुध्वा तत्राङ्गारानुमानतः।
वह्निर्यदृच्छया लब्धः स संवादिभ्रमो मतः॥
units.translation: Someone mistakes vapor for smoke, infers embers and fire there, and by chance finds fire. This is considered an error that leads to the right result.

gloss.en: an error that leads to the right result

units.iast:
bāṣpaṃ dhūmatayā budhvā tatrāṅgārānumānataḥ|
vahniryadṛcchayā labdhaḥ sa saṃvādibhramo mataḥ||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 8
units.deva:
गोदावर्युदकं गङ्गोदकं मत्वा विशुद्धये।
सम्प्रोक्ष्य शुद्धिमाप्नोति स संवादिभ्रमो मतः॥
units.translation: Thinking Godāvarī water is Ganges water, a person sprinkles it for purification and attains purity. This is considered an error that leads to the right result.

gloss.en: an error that leads to the right result

units.iast:
godāvaryudakaṃ gaṅgodakaṃ matvā viśuddhaye|
samprokṣya śuddhimāpnoti sa saṃvādibhramo mataḥ||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 9
units.deva:
ज्वरेणाप्तः सन्निपातं भ्रान्त्या नारायणं स्मरन्।
मृतः स्वर्गमवाप्नोति स संवादिभ्रमो मतः॥
units.translation: Afflicted by fever and delirious, a person remembers Nārāyaṇa; after dying, he reaches heaven. This is considered an error that leads to the right result.

gloss.en: an error that leads to the right result

units.iast:
jvareṇāptaḥ sannipātaṃ bhrāntyā nārāyaṇaṃ smaran|
mṛtaḥ svargamavāpnoti sa saṃvādibhramo mataḥ||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 10
units.deva:
प्रत्यक्षस्यानुमानस्य तथा शास्त्रस्य गोचरे।
उक्तन्यायेन संवादिभ्रमाः सन्तीह कोटिशः॥
units.translation: Countless errors that lead to the right result occur in direct perception, inference, and scripture, by the reasoning just stated.

gloss.en: errors that happen to lead to the right result

units.iast:
pratyakṣasyānumānasya tathā śāstrasya gocare|
uktanyāyena saṃvādibhramāḥ santīha koṭiśaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 11
units.deva:
अन्यथा मृत्तिकादारुशिलाः स्युर्देवताः कथम्।
अग्नित्वादिधियोपास्याः कथं वा योषिदादयः॥
units.translation: Otherwise, how could clay, wood, and stone be worshipped as deities, or a woman and the like be worshipped with the thought “she is fire”?

gloss.en: with the thought “fire” and the like

units.iast:
anyathā mṛttikādāruśilāḥ syurdevatāḥ katham|
agnitvādidhiyopāsyāḥ kathaṃ vā yoṣidādayaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 12
units.deva:
अयथावस्तुविज्ञानात्फलं लभ्यत ईप्सितम्।
काकतालीयतः सोऽयं संवादिभ्रम उच्यते॥
units.translation: Sometimes a desired result comes from a mistaken understanding of what is real. Like a crow landing as a palm fruit falls, this coincidence is called an error that leads to the right result.

gloss.en: from mistaken understanding of what is real
an error that happens to lead to the right result

units.iast:
ayathāvastuvijñānātphalaṃ labhyata īpsitam|
kākatālīyataḥ so’yaṃ saṃvādibhrama ucyate||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 13
units.deva:
स्वयं भ्रमोऽपि संवादी यथा सम्यक्फलप्रदः।
ब्रह्मतत्त्वोपासनापि तथा मुक्तिफलप्रदा॥
units.translation: An error can itself happen to lead to a correct result; likewise, contemplation of Brahman’s reality yields liberation.

gloss.en: can agree with the truth; lead to the right result

units.iast:
svayaṃ bhramo’pi saṃvādī yathā samyakphalapradaḥ|
brahmatattvopāsanāpi tathā muktiphalapradā||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 14
units.deva:
वेदान्तेभ्यो ब्रह्मतत्त्वमखण्डैकरसात्मकम्।
परोक्षमवगम्यैतदहमस्मीत्युपासते॥
units.translation: Having learned indirectly from the Vedānta texts that Brahman is one, undivided reality, one contemplates: “I am this [reality].”
units.iast:
vedāntebhyo brahmatattvamakhaṇḍaikarasātmakam|
parokṣamavagamyaitadahamasmītyupāsate||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 15
units.deva:
प्रत्यग्व्यक्तिमनुल्लिख्य शास्त्राद्विष्ण्वादिमूर्तिवत्।
अस्ति ब्रह्मेति सामान्यज्ञानमात्रं परोक्षधीः॥
units.translation: Without relating it to the individual inner Self, the general scriptural knowledge “Brahman exists,” like scriptural knowledge of Viṣṇu’s forms, is only indirect understanding.

gloss.en: without bringing into view; without relating
as with the forms of Viṣṇu and others

units.iast:
pratyagvyaktimanullikhya śāstrādviṣṇvādimūrtivat|
asti brahmeti sāmānyajñānamātraṃ parokṣadhīḥ||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 16
units.deva:
चतुर्भुजाद्यवगतावपि मूर्तिमनुल्लिखन्।
अक्षैः परोक्षज्ञान्येव न तदा विष्णुमीक्षते॥
units.translation: Even if one knows that Viṣṇu has four arms and the like, without bringing his form into view one has only indirect knowledge and does not then see Viṣṇu with the eyes.
units.iast:
caturbhujādyavagatāvapi mūrtimanullikhan|
akṣaiḥ parokṣajñānyeva na tadā viṣṇumīkṣate||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 17
units.deva:
परोक्षत्वापराधेन भवेन्नातत्त्ववेदनम्।
प्रमाणेनैव शास्त्रेण सत्यमूर्तेर्विभासनात्॥
units.translation: Because this knowledge is indirect, it is not therefore false; authoritative scripture reveals the true form.

gloss.en: because of the defect of being indirect
false knowledge; knowing what is unreal

units.iast:
parokṣatvāparādhena bhavennātattvavedanam|
pramāṇenaiva śāstreṇa satyamūrtervibhāsanāt||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 18
units.deva:
सच्चिदानन्दरूपस्य शास्त्राद्भानेऽप्यनुल्लिखन्।
प्रत्यंचं साक्षिणं तत्तु ब्रह्म साक्षान्न वीक्षते॥
units.translation: Even when scripture reveals Brahman as existence, consciousness, and bliss, one does not see Brahman directly without recognizing it as the inner witness.

gloss.en: of Brahman as existence, consciousness, and bliss
not bringing into view; not recognizing

units.iast:
saccidānandarūpasya śāstrādbhāne’pyanullikhan|
pratyaṃcaṃ sākṣiṇaṃ tattu brahma sākṣānna vīkṣate||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 19
units.deva:
शास्त्रोक्तेनैव मार्गेण सच्चिदानन्दनिर्णयात्।
परोक्षमपि तज्ज्ञानं तत्त्वज्ञानं न तु भ्रमः॥
units.translation: Because the truth of existence, consciousness, and bliss is established by the very method stated in scripture, that knowledge, though indirect, is knowledge of reality and not an error.

gloss.en: because the truth of existence, consciousness, and bliss is established

units.iast:
śāstroktenaiva mārgeṇa saccidānandanirṇayāt|
parokṣamapi tajjñānaṃ tattvajñānaṃ na tu bhramaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 20
units.deva:
ब्रह्म यद्यपि शास्त्रेषु प्रत्यक्त्वेनैव वर्णितम्।
महावाक्यैस्तथाप्येतद्दुर्बोधमविचारिणः॥
units.translation: Although scripture describes Brahman as the inner Self, this is still difficult to understand without inquiry, even through the great statements.

gloss.en: for one who does not inquire

units.iast:
brahma yadyapi śāstreṣu pratyaktvenaiva varṇitam|
mahāvākyaistathāpyetaddurbodhamavicāriṇaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 21
units.deva:
देहाद्यात्मत्वविभ्रान्तौ जागृत्यां न हठात्पुमान्।
ब्रह्मात्मत्वेन विज्ञातुं क्षमते मन्दधीत्वतः॥
units.translation: While the confusion “the body and the rest are the Self” remains active, a dull-minded person cannot suddenly know Brahman as the Self.

gloss.en: in the confusion that the body and the rest are the Self

units.iast:
dehādyātmatvavibhrāntau jāgṛtyāṃ na haṭhātpumān|
brahmātmatvena vijñātuṃ kṣamate mandadhītvataḥ||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 22
units.deva:
ब्रह्ममात्रं सुविज्ञेयं श्रद्धालोः शास्त्रदर्शिनः।
अपरोक्षद्वैतबुद्धिः परोक्षाद्वैतबुद्ध्यनुत्॥
units.translation: For one who trusts scripture, Brahman alone is easy to understand: directly seeing duality does not cancel an indirect understanding of nonduality.

gloss.en: does not cancel indirect understanding of nonduality

units.iast:
brahmamātraṃ suvijñeyaṃ śraddhāloḥ śāstradarśinaḥ|
aparokṣadvaitabuddhiḥ parokṣādvaitabuddhyanut||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 23
units.deva:
अपरोक्षशिलाबुद्धिर्न परोक्षेशतां नुदेत्।
प्रतिमादिषु विष्णुत्वे को वा विप्रतिपद्यते॥
units.translation: Directly seeing a stone image does not cancel indirect understanding of the Lord; who disputes that Viṣṇu is present in sacred images?

gloss.en: direct awareness that the image is stone
indirect knowledge of the Lord’s presence

units.iast:
aparokṣaśilābuddhirna parokṣeśatāṃ nudet|
pratimādiṣu viṣṇutve ko vā vipratipadyate||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 24
units.deva:
