अश्रद्धालोरविश्वासो नोदाहरणमर्हति।
श्रद्धालोरेव सर्वत्र वैदिकेष्वधिकारतः॥
units.translation: The disbelief of a faithless person is not a relevant counterexample, since only the faithful are eligible for Vedic practices.
units.iast:
aśraddhāloraviśvāso nodāharaṇamarhati|
śraddhāloreva sarvatra vaidikeṣvadhikārataḥ||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 25
units.deva:
सकृदाप्तोपदेशेन परोक्षज्ञानमुद्भवेत्।
विष्णुमूर्त्युपदेशो हि न मीमांसामपेक्षते॥
units.translation: A single instruction from a trusted teacher can give indirect knowledge; teaching the form of Viṣṇu requires no further inquiry.

gloss.en: by instruction from a trusted teacher

units.iast:
sakṛdāptopadeśena parokṣajñānamudbhavet|
viṣṇumūrtyupadeśo hi na mīmāṃsāmapekṣate||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 26
units.deva:
कर्मोपास्ती विचार्येतेऽनुष्ठेयाविनिर्णयात्।
बहुशाखाविप्रकीर्णं निर्णेतुं कः प्रभुर्नरः॥
units.translation: Rituals and contemplations are examined because their proper performance must be determined. What person could reconcile directions scattered across many branches of the Vedas?

gloss.en: because what should be performed is uncertain

units.iast:
karmopāstī vicāryete’nuṣṭheyāvinirṇayāt|
bahuśākhāviprakīrṇaṃ nirṇetuṃ kaḥ prabhurnaraḥ||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 27
units.deva:
निर्णितोऽर्थः कल्पसूत्रैर्ग्रथितस्तावतास्तिकः।
विचारमन्तरेणापि शक्तोऽनुष्ठातुमञ्जसा॥
units.translation: The Kalpa-sūtras organize what has been settled; with that guidance, a person of faith can perform it easily, without further inquiry.

gloss.en: a person of faith in the Veda

units.iast:
nirṇito’rthaḥ kalpasūtrairgrathitastāvatāstikaḥ|
vicāramantareṇāpi śakto’nuṣṭhātumañjasā||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 28
units.deva:
उपास्तीनामनुष्ठानमार्षग्रन्थेषु वर्णितम्।
विचाराक्षममर्त्याश्च तत्श्रुत्वोपासते गुरोः॥
units.translation: The sages describe the practice of worship in their works; people unable to investigate learn it from a teacher and then practice it.
units.iast:
upāstīnāmanuṣṭhānamārṣagrantheṣu varṇitam|
vicārākṣamamartyāśca tatśrutvopāsate guroḥ||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 29
units.deva:
वेदवाक्यानि निर्णेतुमिच्छन्मीमांसतां जनः।
आप्तोपदेशमन्त्रेण ह्यनुष्ठानं तु सम्भवेत्॥
units.translation: A person who wants to determine the meaning of Vedic statements should investigate; practical observance, however, is possible by following a trusted teacher’s instruction.

gloss.en: by the guiding words of a trusted teacher

units.iast:
vedavākyāni nirṇetumicchanmīmāṃsatāṃ janaḥ|
āptopadeśamantreṇa hyanuṣṭhānaṃ tu sambhavet||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 30
units.deva:
ब्रह्मसाक्षात्कृतिस्त्वेवं विचारेण विना नृणाम्।
आप्तोपदेशमात्रेण न सम्भवति कुत्रचित्॥
units.translation: Direct realization of Brahman, however, is never possible for people through a trusted teacher’s instruction alone, without inquiry.

gloss.en: by a trusted teacher’s instruction alone

units.iast:
brahmasākṣātkṛtistvevaṃ vicāreṇa vinā nṛṇām|
āptopadeśamātreṇa na sambhavati kutracit||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 31
units.deva:
परोक्षज्ञानमश्रद्धा प्रतिबध्नाति नेतरत्।
अविचारोऽपरोक्षस्य ज्ञानस्य प्रतिबन्धकः॥
units.translation: Lack of faith alone blocks indirect knowledge; lack of inquiry is the obstacle to direct knowledge.
units.iast:
parokṣajñānamaśraddhā pratibadhnāti netarat|
avicāro’parokṣasya jñānasya pratibandhakaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 32
units.deva:
विचाराप्यपरोक्षेण ब्रह्मात्मानं न वेत्ति चेत्।
आपरोक्ष्यावसानत्वाद्भूयोभूयो विचारयेत्॥
units.translation: If inquiry still does not reveal Brahman as the Self directly, one should inquire again and again, because inquiry culminates in direct knowledge.
units.iast:
vicārāpyaparokṣeṇa brahmātmānaṃ na vetti cet|
āparokṣyāvasānatvādbhūyobhūyo vicārayet||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 33
units.deva:
विचारयन्नामरणं नैवात्मानं लभेत चेत्।
जन्मान्तरे लभेतैव प्रतिबन्धक्षये सति॥
units.translation: If someone inquires until death and still does not attain the Self, they will surely attain it in another birth when the obstacle has been removed.

gloss.en: when the obstacle has been removed

units.iast:
vicārayannāmaraṇaṃ naivātmānaṃ labheta cet|
janmāntare labhetaiva pratibandhakṣaye sati||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 34
units.deva:
इह वामुत्र वा विद्येत्येवं सूत्रकृतोदितम्।
शृण्वन्तोऽप्यत्र बहवो यन्न विद्युरिति श्रुतिः॥
units.translation: The author of the Sūtras says that knowledge may arise in this life or another. Śruti says that many people hear the teaching here and still do not know the truth.

gloss.en: by the author of the Sūtras

units.iast:
iha vāmutra vā vidyetyevaṃ sūtrakṛtoditam|
śṛṇvanto’pyatra bahavo yanna vidyuriti śrutiḥ||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 35
units.deva:
गर्भ एव शयानः सन्वामदेवोऽवबुद्धवान्।
पूर्वाभ्यस्तविचारेण यद्वदध्ययनादिषु॥
units.translation: Vāmadeva understood while still lying in the womb through inquiry practiced before, just as [it happens] with study and the like.
units.iast:
garbha eva śayānaḥ sanvāmadevo’vabuddhavān|
pūrvābhyastavicāreṇa yadvadadhyayanādiṣu||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 36
units.deva:
बहुवारमधीतेऽपि तदा नायाति चेत्पुनः।
दिनान्तरेऽनधीत्यैव पूर्वाधीतं स्मरेत्पुमान्॥
units.translation: Even after studying something many times, if it does not come to mind then, a person may remember on another day what was studied earlier without studying again.
units.iast:
bahuvāramadhīte’pi tadā nāyāti cetpunaḥ|
dināntare’nadhītyaiva pūrvādhītaṃ smaretpumān||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 37
units.deva:
कालेन परिपच्यन्ते कृषिदर्भादयो यथा।
तद्वदात्मविचारोऽपि शनैः कालेन पच्यते॥
units.translation: Just as crops, darbha grass, and the like ripen over time, self-inquiry too matures gradually with time.

gloss.en: crops, darbha grass, and the like

units.iast:
kālena paripacyante kṛṣidarbhādayo yathā|
tadvadātmavicāro’pi śanaiḥ kālena pacyate||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 38
units.deva:
पुनःपुनर्विचारोऽपि त्रिविधप्रतिबन्धतः।
न वेत्ति तत्त्वमित्येतद्वार्तिके सम्यगीरितम्॥
units.translation: Even with repeated inquiry, a person may not know the truth because of three kinds of obstacle; this is stated clearly in the Vārtika.

gloss.en: because of three kinds of obstacle

units.iast:
punaḥpunarvicāro’pi trividhapratibandhataḥ|
na vetti tattvamityetadvārtike samyagīritam||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 39
units.deva:
कुतस्तज्ज्ञानमिति चेत्तद्धि बन्धपरिक्षयात्।
असावपि च भूतो वा भावी वा वर्तते तथा॥
units.translation: If you ask, “How does that knowledge arise?” it is from the complete removal of the obstruction. That obstruction may itself lie in the past or in the future.

gloss.en: from the complete exhaustion of bondage; removal of the obstruction

units.iast:
kutastajjñānamiti cettaddhi bandhaparikṣayāt|
asāvapi ca bhūto vā bhāvī vā vartate tathā||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 40
units.deva:
अधीतवेदवेदार्थोऽप्यत एव न मुच्यते।
हिरण्यनिधिदृष्टान्तादिदमेव हि दर्शितम्॥
units.translation: Thus, even a person who has studied the Veda and its meaning is not thereby freed. This very point is shown by the example of a hidden gold treasure.

gloss.en: one who has studied the Veda and the meaning of the Veda
by the example of a hidden gold treasure

units.iast:
adhītavedavedārtho’pyata eva na mucyate|
hiraṇyanidhidṛṣṭāntādidameva hi darśitam||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 41
units.deva:
अतीतेनापि महिषीस्नेहेन प्रतिबन्धतः।
भिक्षुस्तत्त्वं न वेदेति गाथा लोके प्रगीयते॥
units.translation: A verse is widely sung among people: “Because of past attachment to a mahiṣī, a monk does not know the truth.” Here mahiṣī can mean either a queen or a female buffalo.

gloss.en: through attachment to a mahiṣī (queen or female buffalo)

units.iast:
atītenāpi mahiṣīsnehena pratibandhataḥ|
bhikṣustattvaṃ na vedeti gāthā loke pragīyate||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 42
units.deva:
अनुसृत्य गुरुः स्नेहं महिष्यां तत्त्वमुक्तवान्।
ततो यथावद्वेदैष प्रतिबन्धस्य संक्षयात्॥
units.translation: Taking account of the monk’s attachment to the female buffalo, the teacher taught him the truth; when the obstacle was removed, the monk knew it correctly.
units.iast:
anusṛtya guruḥ snehaṃ mahiṣyāṃ tattvamuktavān|
tato yathāvadvedaiṣa pratibandhasya saṃkṣayāt||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 43
units.deva:
प्रतिबन्धो वर्तमानो विषयासक्तिलक्षणः।
प्रज्ञामान्द्यं कुतर्कश्च विपर्ययदुराग्रहः॥
units.translation: The present obstacle is characterized by attachment to sense objects, dullness of understanding, faulty reasoning, and stubborn insistence on a mistaken view.

gloss.en: stubborn insistence on a mistaken view

units.iast:
pratibandho vartamāno viṣayāsaktilakṣaṇaḥ|
prajñāmāndyaṃ kutarkaśca viparyayadurāgrahaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 44
units.deva:
शमाद्यैः श्रवणाद्यैश्च तत्र तत्रोचितैः क्षयम्।
नीतेऽस्मिन्प्रतिबन्धेऽतः स्वस्य ब्रह्मत्वमश्नुते॥
units.translation: When this obstacle is brought to an end through inner calm and the other disciplines, and through listening and the other practices suited to each case, one realizes one’s own nature as Brahman.

gloss.en: by inner calm and the rest

units.iast:
śamādyaiḥ śravaṇādyaiśca tatra tatrocitaiḥ kṣayam|
nīte’sminpratibandhe’taḥ svasya brahmatvamaśnute||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 45
units.deva:
आगामिप्रतिबन्धश्च वामदेवे समीरितः।
एकेन जन्मना क्षीणो भरतस्य त्रिजन्मभिः॥
units.translation: The future obstacle is also illustrated by Vāmadeva: it was exhausted in one birth for him, and over three births in Bharata’s case.
units.iast:
āgāmipratibandhaśca vāmadeve samīritaḥ|
ekena janmanā kṣīṇo bharatasya trijanmabhiḥ||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 46
units.deva:
योगभ्रष्टस्य गीतायामतीते बहुजन्मनि।
प्रतिबन्धक्षयः प्रोक्तो न विचारोऽप्यनर्थकः॥
units.translation: The Gītā says that the obstacle of one who has fallen from yoga is removed over many past births; inquiry too is never fruitless.

gloss.en: of one who has fallen from yoga

units.iast:
yogabhraṣṭasya gītāyāmatīte bahujanmani|
pratibandhakṣayaḥ prokto na vicāro’pyanarthakaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 47
units.deva:
प्राप्य पुण्यकृतां लोकानात्मतत्त्वविचारतः।
शुचीनां श्रीमतां गेहे योगभ्रष्टोऽभिजायते॥
units.translation: Having reached the worlds of the meritorious through inquiry into the truth of the Self, one who has fallen from yoga is born in the family of the pure and prosperous.

gloss.en: of those who have done meritorious deeds
through inquiry into the truth of the Self
one who has fallen from yoga

units.iast:
prāpya puṇyakṛtāṃ lokānātmatattvavicārataḥ|
śucīnāṃ śrīmatāṃ gehe yogabhraṣṭo’bhijāyate||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 48
units.deva:
अथवा योगिनामेव कुले भवति धीमताम्।
निस्पृहः ब्रह्मतत्त्वस्य विचारात्तद्धि दुर्लभम्॥
units.translation: Or he is born only in the family of wise yogis, dispassionate through inquiry into the truth of Brahman; that birth is indeed hard to obtain.
units.iast:
athavā yogināmeva kule bhavati dhīmatām|
nispṛhaḥ brahmatattvasya vicārāttaddhi durlabham||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 49
units.deva:
तत्र तं बुद्धिसंयोगं लभते पौर्वदेहिकम्।
यतते च ततो भूयस्तस्मादेतद्धि दुर्लभम्॥
units.translation: There he regains the understanding from his previous life and then strives again with greater effort; for that birth is indeed hard to obtain.

gloss.en: from a former body; from a previous life

units.iast:
tatra taṃ buddhisaṃyogaṃ labhate paurvadehikam|
yatate ca tato bhūyastasmādetaddhi durlabham||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 50
units.deva:
पूर्वाभ्यासेन तेनैव ह्रियते ह्यवशोऽपि सः।
अनेकजन्मसंसिद्धस्ततो याति परां गतिम्॥
units.translation: Carried by that very previous practice, even against his will, he is perfected over many births and then reaches the highest goal.
units.iast:
pūrvābhyāsena tenaiva hriyate hyavaśo’pi saḥ|
anekajanmasaṃsiddhastato yāti parāṃ gatim||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 51
units.deva:
ब्रह्मलोकाभिवाञ्छायां सम्यक्सत्यां निरुध्यताम्।
विचारयेद्य आत्मानं न तु साक्षात्करोत्ययम्॥
units.translation: When the desire for Brahmaloka is firmly present, it should be restrained. Whoever inquires into the Self does not, however, realize it directly.

gloss.en: when desire for Brahmaloka is present

units.iast:
brahmalokābhivāñchāyāṃ samyaksatyāṃ nirudhyatām|
vicārayedya ātmānaṃ na tu sākṣātkarotyayam||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 52
units.deva:
वेदान्तविज्ञानसुनिश्चितार्थाः इति शास्त्रतः।
ब्रह्मलोके सकल्पान्ते ब्रह्मणा सह मुच्यते॥
units.translation: Scripture says that those who have firmly ascertained the meaning through Vedānta knowledge are liberated with Brahmā in Brahmaloka at the end of a kalpa.

gloss.en: those whose understanding is firmly settled through Vedānta knowledge
at the end of a cosmic cycle (kalpa)

units.iast:
vedāntavijñānasuniścitārthāḥ iti śāstrataḥ|
brahmaloke sakalpānte brahmaṇā saha mucyate||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 53
units.deva:
केषांचित्स विचारोऽपि कर्मणा प्रतिबद्ध्यते।
श्रवणायापि बहुभिर्यो न लभ्य इति श्रुतेः॥
units.translation: For some, even inquiry is obstructed by karma. As Śruti says, the Self is not attained by many even as an object of hearing.
units.iast:
keṣāṃcitsa vicāro’pi karmaṇā pratibaddhyate|
śravaṇāyāpi bahubhiryo na labhya iti śruteḥ||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 54
units.deva:
अत्यन्तबुद्धिमान्द्याद्वा सामग्र्या वाप्यसम्भवात्।
यो विचारं न लभते ब्रह्मोपासीत सोऽनिशम्॥
units.translation: Whoever cannot undertake inquiry because of extreme dullness of understanding or lack of the necessary means should meditate on Brahman continually.

gloss.en: because of extreme dullness of understanding

units.iast:
atyantabuddhimāndyādvā sāmagryā vāpyasambhavāt|
yo vicāraṃ na labhate brahmopāsīta so’niśam||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 55
units.deva:
निर्गुणब्रह्मतत्त्वस्य न ह्युपास्तेरसम्भवः।
सगुणब्रह्मणीवात्र प्रत्ययावृत्तिसम्भवात्॥
units.translation: Meditation on the reality of attributeless Brahman is indeed possible, because repeated contemplation is possible here just as it is for Brahman with attributes.

gloss.en: of the reality of attributeless Brahman

units.iast:
nirguṇabrahmatattvasya na hyupāsterasambhavaḥ|
saguṇabrahmaṇīvātra pratyayāvṛttisambhavāt||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 56
units.deva:
अवाङ्मनसगम्यं तन्नोपास्यमिति चेत्तदा।
अवाङ्मनसगम्यस्य वेदनं च न सम्भवेत्॥
units.translation: If you say, “That is beyond speech and mind, so it cannot be meditated upon,” then knowledge of what is beyond speech and mind would also be impossible.

gloss.en: beyond the reach of speech and mind
of what is beyond speech and mind

units.iast:
avāṅmanasagamyaṃ tannopāsyamiti cettadā|
avāṅmanasagamyasya vedanaṃ ca na sambhavet||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 57
units.deva:
वागाद्यगोचराकारमित्येवं यदि वेत्त्यसौ।
वागाद्यगोचराकारमित्युपासित नो कुतः॥
units.translation: If this person knows Brahman as beyond the reach of speech and the like, why not meditate on it as beyond the reach of speech and the like?

gloss.en: having a nature beyond speech and the like
having a nature beyond speech and the like

units.iast:
vāgādyagocarākāramityevaṃ yadi vettyasau|
vāgādyagocarākāramityupāsita no kutaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 58
units.deva:
सगुणत्वमुपास्यत्वाद्यदि वेद्यत्वतोऽपि तत्।
वेद्यं चेल्लक्षणावृत्त्या लक्षितं समुपास्यताम्॥
units.translation: If you say that being an object of meditation makes Brahman qualified, that is also because it is knowable. If it is knowable through indirect indication, let Brahman so indicated be meditated upon.

gloss.en: because it is fit to be meditated upon

units.iast:
saguṇatvamupāsyatvādyadi vedyatvato’pi tat|
vedyaṃ cellakṣaṇāvṛttyā lakṣitaṃ samupāsyatām||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 59
units.deva:
ब्रह्म विद्धि तदेव त्वं नत्विदं यदुपासते।
इति श्रुतेरुपास्यत्वं निषिद्धं ब्रह्मणो यदि॥
units.translation: The objection is that Śruti’s words, “Know that alone as Brahman—you, not this which people worship,” forbid meditation on Brahman.

gloss.en: the status of being fit for meditation

units.iast:
brahma viddhi tadeva tvaṃ natvidaṃ yadupāsate|
iti śruterupāsyatvaṃ niṣiddhaṃ brahmaṇo yadi||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 60
units.deva:
विदितादन्यदेवेति श्रुतेर्वेद्यत्वमस्य न।
यथा श्रुत्यैव वेद्यं तत्तथा श्रुत्याप्युपास्यताम्॥
units.translation: The reply: Śruti says, “It is indeed other than what is known,” so Brahman is not knowable as an object. Yet just as Śruti makes it knowable, let it also be meditated upon through Śruti.
units.iast:
viditādanyadeveti śrutervedyatvamasya na|
yathā śrutyaiva vedyaṃ tattathā śrutyāpyupāsyatām||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 61
units.deva:
अवास्तवी वेद्यता चेदुपास्यत्वं तथा न किम्।
वृत्तिव्याप्तिर्वेद्यता चेदुपास्यत्वेऽपि तत्समम्॥
units.translation: If knowability is unreal, why should being an object of meditation not be the same? If knowing means that a thought reaches its object, the same applies to meditation too.

gloss.en: knowability; being an object of knowledge
the reach of a mental modification

units.iast:
avāstavī vedyatā cedupāsyatvaṃ tathā na kim|
vṛttivyāptirvedyatā cedupāsyatve’pi tatsamam||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 62
units.deva:
का ते भक्तिरुपास्तौ चेत्कस्ते द्वेषस्तदीरय।
मानाभावो न वाच्योऽस्यां बहुश्रुतिषु दर्शनात्॥
units.translation: “Why are you devoted to meditation?”—then state your objection: “Why are you against it?” Lack of scriptural support should not be claimed, since meditation is found in many Śruti texts.
units.iast:
kā te bhaktirupāstau cetkaste dveṣastadīraya|
mānābhāvo na vācyo’syāṃ bahuśrutiṣu darśanāt||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 63
units.deva:
उत्तरस्मिंस्तापनीये शैब्यप्रश्नेऽथ काठके।
माण्डूक्यादौ च सर्वत्र निर्गुणोपास्तिरीरिता॥
units.translation: Meditation on attributeless Brahman is taught in the Uttara Tāpanīya, in Śaibya’s question [in the Praśna Upaniṣad], in the Kāṭha, in the Māṇḍūkya, and in other texts.

gloss.en: in the Māṇḍūkya and the like

units.iast:
uttarasmiṃstāpanīye śaibyapraśne’tha kāṭhake|
māṇḍūkyādau ca sarvatra nirguṇopāstirīritā||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 64
units.deva:
अनुष्ठानप्रकारोऽस्याः पञ्चीकरण ईरितः।
ज्ञानसाधनमेतच्चेन्नेति केनात्र वर्णितम्॥
units.translation: The method of practicing this [meditation] is stated in the Pañcīkaraṇa. If this is a means to knowledge, who here has denied it?
units.iast:
anuṣṭhānaprakāro’syāḥ pañcīkaraṇa īritaḥ|
jñānasādhanametaccenneti kenātra varṇitam||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 65
units.deva:
नानुतिष्ठति कोऽप्येतदिति चेन्नानुतिष्ठतु।
पुरुषस्यापराधेन किमुपास्तिः प्रदुष्यति॥
units.translation: If you say, “No one practices this,” let them not practice it. How is meditation itself spoiled by a person’s failing?
units.iast:
nānutiṣṭhati ko’pyetaditi cennānutiṣṭhatu|
puruṣasyāparādhena kimupāstiḥ praduṣyati||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 66
units.deva:
इतोऽप्यतिशयं मत्वा मन्त्रान्वश्यादिकारिणः।
मूढा जपन्तु तेभ्योऽतिमूढाः कृषिमुपासताम्॥
units.translation: Thinking these mantras superior even to this [meditation], let the deluded chant mantras that bring subjugation and the like; those still more deluded may take up farming as their object.

gloss.en: that produce subjugation and the like
let them devote themselves to; attend to

units.iast:
ito’pyatiśayaṃ matvā mantrānvaśyādikāriṇaḥ|
mūḍhā japantu tebhyo’timūḍhāḥ kṛṣimupāsatām||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 67
units.deva:
तिष्ठन्तु मूढाः प्रकृता निर्गुणोपास्तिरीर्यते।
विद्यैक्यात्सर्वशाखास्थान्गुणानत्रोपसंहरेत्॥
units.translation: Let ordinary fools remain as they are; here meditation on attributeless Brahman is taught. Since this meditation is one, one should gather here the qualities found in all branches [of the Veda].
units.iast:
tiṣṭhantu mūḍhāḥ prakṛtā nirguṇopāstirīryate|
vidyaikyātsarvaśākhāsthānguṇānatropasaṃharet||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 68
units.deva:
आनन्दादेर्विधेयस्य गुणसङ्घस्य संहृतिः।
आनन्दादय इत्यस्मिन्सूत्रे व्यासेन वर्णिता॥
units.translation: The combining of the prescribed group of qualities beginning with bliss is described by Vyāsa in the sūtra called “Ānandādayaḥ.”
units.iast:
ānandādervidheyasya guṇasaṅghasya saṃhṛtiḥ|
ānandādaya ityasminsūtre vyāsena varṇitā||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 69
units.deva:
अस्थूलादेर्निषेध्यस्य गुणसङ्घस्य संहृतिः।
तथा व्यासेन सूत्रेऽस्मिनुक्ताक्षरधियान्त्विति॥
units.translation: Likewise, Vyāsa states in the sūtra beginning “Akṣaradhiyāṃ tu” that the negated qualities, beginning with “not gross,” are to be gathered together.
units.iast:
asthūlāderniṣedhyasya guṇasaṅghasya saṃhṛtiḥ|
tathā vyāsena sūtre’sminuktākṣaradhiyāntviti||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 70
units.deva:
निर्गुणब्रह्मतत्त्वस्य विद्यायां गुणसंहृतिः।
न युज्येतेत्युपालम्भो व्यासं प्रत्येव मां तु न॥
units.translation: If you object that gathering qualities into a meditation on the reality of attributeless Brahman is improper, your objection is aimed at Vyāsa too, not at me alone.

gloss.en: of the reality of attributeless Brahman

units.iast:
nirguṇabrahmatattvasya vidyāyāṃ guṇasaṃhṛtiḥ|
na yujyetetyupālambho vyāsaṃ pratyeva māṃ tu na||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 71
units.deva:
हिरण्यस्मश्रुसूर्यादिमूर्तीनामनुदाहृतेः।
अविरुद्धं निर्गुणत्वमिति चेत्तुष्यतां त्वया॥
units.translation: If you say, “Since no forms such as the golden-bearded Sun are mentioned, attributelessness is not contradicted,” then be satisfied with that.
units.iast:
hiraṇyasmaśrusūryādimūrtīnāmanudāhṛteḥ|
aviruddhaṃ nirguṇatvamiti cettuṣyatāṃ tvayā||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 72
units.deva:
गुणानां लक्षकत्वेन न तत्त्वेऽन्तःप्रवेशनम्।
इति चेदस्त्वेवमेव ब्रह्मतत्त्वमुपास्यताम्॥
units.translation: If you say, “Qualities serve as indicators but do not enter into Brahman’s true nature,” let it be so; meditate on the reality of Brahman precisely that way.
units.iast:
guṇānāṃ lakṣakatvena na tattve’ntaḥpraveśanam|
iti cedastvevameva brahmatattvamupāsyatām||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 73
units.deva:
आनन्दादिभिरस्थूलादिभिःस्वात्मात्र लक्षितः।
अखण्डैकरसः सोऽहमस्मीत्येवमुपासते॥
units.translation: Here one’s own Self is indicated by qualities beginning with bliss and by negations beginning with “not gross.” It is indivisible and of one essence; one meditates, “I am that.”
units.iast:
ānandādibhirasthūlādibhiḥsvātmātra lakṣitaḥ|
akhaṇḍaikarasaḥ so’hamasmītyevamupāsate||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 74
units.deva:
बोधोपास्त्योर्विशेषः क इति चेदुच्यते शृणु।
वस्तुतन्त्रो भवेद्बोधः कर्तृतन्त्रमुपासनम्॥
units.translation: If you ask what the difference is between knowledge and meditation, listen: knowledge depends on the object; meditation depends on the person who meditates.

gloss.en: dependent on the person who acts

units.iast:
bodhopāstyorviśeṣaḥ ka iti ceducyate śṛṇu|
vastutantro bhavedbodhaḥ kartṛtantramupāsanam||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 75
units.deva:
विचाराज्जायते बोधोऽनिच्छा यं न निवर्तयेत्।
स्वोत्पत्तिमात्रात्संसारे दहत्यखिलसत्यताम्॥
units.translation: Knowledge arises from inquiry, and unwillingness cannot make it disappear. By arising alone, it burns away the whole world’s claim to reality.
units.iast:
vicārājjāyate bodho’nicchā yaṃ na nivartayet|
svotpattimātrātsaṃsāre dahatyakhilasatyatām||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 76
units.deva:
तावता कृतकृत्यः सन्नित्यतृप्तिमुपागतः।
जीवन्मुक्तिमनुप्राप्य प्रारब्धक्षयमीक्षते॥
units.translation: Having done what had to be done and reached lasting contentment, one attains liberation while living and awaits the exhaustion of prārabdha karma, the karma already bearing fruit.

gloss.en: having done what had to be done

units.iast:
tāvatā kṛtakṛtyaḥ sannityatṛptimupāgataḥ|
jīvanmuktimanuprāpya prārabdhakṣayamīkṣate||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 77
units.deva:
आप्तोपदेशं विश्वस्य श्रद्धालुरविचारयन्।
चिन्तयेत्प्रत्ययैरन्यैरनन्तरितवृत्तिभिः॥
units.translation: Trusting a reliable teacher’s instruction, a faithful person who does not inquire should contemplate with a stream of thought unbroken by other ideas.

gloss.en: the instruction of a reliable teacher
with a mental flow unbroken by [other thoughts]

units.iast:
āptopadeśaṃ viśvasya śraddhāluravicārayan|
cintayetpratyayairanyairanantaritavṛttibhiḥ||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 78
units.deva:
यावच्चिन्त्यस्वरूपत्वाभिमानः स्वस्य जायते।
तावद्विचिन्त्य पश्चाच्च तथैवामृति धारयेत्॥
units.translation: He should meditate until the conviction arises in himself, “I am of the very nature of what I contemplate.” After that, he should maintain that same contemplation until death.

gloss.en: the conviction of being the nature of what is contemplated

units.iast:
yāvaccintyasvarūpatvābhimānaḥ svasya jāyate|
tāvadvicintya paścācca tathaivāmṛti dhārayet||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 79
units.deva:
ब्रह्मचारी भिक्षमाणो युतः संवर्गविद्यया।
संवर्गरूपतां चित्ते धारयित्वा ह्यभिक्षत॥
units.translation: A brahmacārin begging for alms, endowed with the Saṃvarga teaching, held in mind that he was of the nature of Saṃvarga and indeed begged.
units.iast:
brahmacārī bhikṣamāṇo yutaḥ saṃvargavidyayā|
saṃvargarūpatāṃ citte dhārayitvā hyabhikṣata||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 80
units.deva:
पुरुषस्वेच्छया कर्तुमकर्तुं कर्तुमन्यथा।
शक्योपास्तिरतो नित्यं कुर्यात्प्रत्ययसन्ततिम्॥
units.translation: Because meditation may be done, not done, or done differently according to a person’s own will, one should always sustain a continuous stream of contemplation.

gloss.en: according to a person’s own will

units.iast:
puruṣasvecchayā kartumakartuṃ kartumanyathā|
śakyopāstirato nityaṃ kuryātpratyayasantatim||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 81
units.deva:
वेदाध्यायी ह्यप्रमत्तोऽधीते स्वप्नेऽपि वासितः।
जपिता तु जपत्येव तथा ध्यातापि वासयेत्॥
units.translation: A diligent student of the Veda studies even in dreams, conditioned by habit; the chanter indeed chants, and the meditator likewise should cultivate that habit.

gloss.en: student of the Veda; one who studies the Veda

units.iast:
vedādhyāyī hyapramatto’dhīte svapne’pi vāsitaḥ|
japitā tu japatyeva tathā dhyātāpi vāsayet||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 82
units.deva:
विरोधिप्रत्ययं त्यक्त्वा नैरन्तर्येण भावयन्।
लभते वासनावेशात्स्वप्नादावपि भावनाम्॥
units.translation: Giving up contrary thoughts and contemplating without interruption, one gains the contemplative thought even in dreams and the like through the force of the latent impression.

gloss.en: through the force of the latent impression

units.iast:
virodhipratyayaṃ tyaktvā nairantaryeṇa bhāvayan|
labhate vāsanāveśātsvapnādāvapi bhāvanām||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 83
units.deva:
भुञ्जानोऽपि निज आरब्धमास्थातिशयतोऽनिशम्।
ध्यातुं शक्तो न सन्देहो विषयव्यसनी यथा॥
units.translation: There is no doubt that, even while experiencing what has already begun for him [his prārabdha karma], a person can meditate without pause through intense commitment—just as someone absorbed in sense objects keeps dwelling on them.

gloss.en: what has begun; here, karma already bearing fruit
through intense earnestness; through great commitment

units.iast:
bhuñjāno’pi nija ārabdhamāsthātiśayato’niśam|
dhyātuṃ śakto na sandeho viṣayavyasanī yathā||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 84
units.deva:
परव्यसनिनी नारी व्यग्रापि गृहकर्मणि।
तदेवास्वादयत्यन्तः परसङ्गरसायनम्॥
units.translation: A woman absorbed in a lover, even while occupied with household work, inwardly savors that very nectar of intimacy with another.

gloss.en: a woman absorbed in another; devoted to a lover
the nectar of intimacy with another

units.iast:
paravyasaninī nārī vyagrāpi gṛhakarmaṇi|
tadevāsvādayatyantaḥ parasaṅgarasāyanam||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 85
units.deva:
परसङ्गं स्वादयन्त्या अपि नो गृहकर्म तत्।
कुण्ठी भवेदपि त्वेतदापातेनैव वर्तते॥
units.translation: Even while savoring a lover’s company, her household work does not disappear altogether; it carries on only on the surface.
units.iast:
parasaṅgaṃ svādayantyā api no gṛhakarma tat|
kuṇṭhī bhavedapi tvetadāpātenaiva vartate||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 86
units.deva:
गृहकृत्यव्यसनिनी यथा सम्यक्करोति तत्।
परव्यसनिनी तद्वन्न करोत्येव सर्वथा॥
units.translation: A woman absorbed in household tasks does them properly; a woman absorbed in a lover does not do them that way in every respect.

gloss.en: a woman absorbed in household tasks
a woman absorbed in another; devoted to a lover

units.iast:
gṛhakṛtyavyasaninī yathā samyakkaroti tat|
paravyasaninī tadvanna karotyeva sarvathā||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 87
units.deva:
एवं ध्यानैकनिष्ठोऽपि लेशाल्लौकिकमाचरेत्।
तत्त्ववित्त्वविरोधित्वाल्लौकिकं सम्यगाचरेत्॥
units.translation: Thus, even one wholly devoted to meditation performs worldly activity only a little; but a knower of reality performs worldly activity properly because it does not conflict [with that knowledge].

gloss.en: only a little; to a small degree

units.iast:
evaṃ dhyānaikaniṣṭho’pi leśāllaukikamācaret|
tattvavittvavirodhitvāllaukikaṃ samyagācaret||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 88
units.deva:
मायामयः प्रपञ्चोऽयमात्मा चैतन्यरूपधृक्।
इति बोधे विरोधः को लौकिकव्यवहारिणः॥
units.translation: This world is fashioned by Māyā, and the Self is of the nature of consciousness. What conflict is there, for one engaged in worldly dealings, in this understanding?

gloss.en: for one engaged in worldly dealings

units.iast:
māyāmayaḥ prapañco’yamātmā caitanyarūpadhṛk|
iti bodhe virodhaḥ ko laukikavyavahāriṇaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 89
units.deva:
अपेक्षते व्यवहृतिर्न प्रपञ्चस्य वस्तुताम्।
नाप्यात्मजाड्यं किंत्वेषा साधनान्येव काङ्क्षति॥
units.translation: Worldly activity does not require the manifest world to be ultimately real, nor does it require the Self to be inert; it requires only the means [for action].
units.iast:
apekṣate vyavahṛtirna prapañcasya vastutām|
nāpyātmajāḍyaṃ kiṃtveṣā sādhanānyeva kāṅkṣati||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 90
units.deva:
मनोवाक्कायतद्बाह्यपदार्थाः साधनानि तान्।
तत्त्वविन्नोपमृद्नाति व्यवहारोऽस्य नो कुतः॥
units.translation: The mind, speech, body, and external objects are those means. The knower of reality does not destroy them; how, then, would worldly activity be absent for him?

gloss.en: how could there not be?; how could it be absent?

units.iast:
manovākkāyatadbāhyapadārthāḥ sādhanāni tān|
tattvavinnopamṛdnāti vyavahāro’sya no kutaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 91
units.deva:
उपमृद्नाति चित्तं चेद्ध्यातासौ न तु तत्त्ववित्।
न बुद्धिं मर्दयन् दृष्टो घटतत्त्वस्य वेदिता॥
units.translation: If one subdues the mind, that person is a meditator, not a knower of reality. A knower of what a pot is has not been seen grinding down the intellect.

gloss.en: of the nature of a pot

units.iast:
upamṛdnāti cittaṃ ceddhyātāsau na tu tattvavit|
na buddhiṃ mardayan dṛṣṭo ghaṭatattvasya veditā||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 92
units.deva:
सकृत्प्रत्ययमात्रेण घटश्चेद्भासते तदा।
स्वप्रकाशोऽयमात्मा किं घटवच्च न भासते॥
units.translation: If a pot appears through a single cognition alone, why does this self-luminous Self not appear like a pot?
units.iast:
sakṛtpratyayamātreṇa ghaṭaścedbhāsate tadā|
svaprakāśo’yamātmā kiṃ ghaṭavacca na bhāsate||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 93
units.deva:
स्वप्रकाशतया किं ते तद्बुद्धिस्तत्त्ववेदनम्।
बुद्धिश्च क्षणनाश्येति चोद्यं तुल्यं घटादिषु॥
units.translation: Does the Self’s self-luminosity make your cognition of it knowledge of reality? The objection that cognition perishes in a moment applies just as much to pots and the like.
units.iast:
svaprakāśatayā kiṃ te tadbuddhistattvavedanam|
buddhiśca kṣaṇanāśyeti codyaṃ tulyaṃ ghaṭādiṣu||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 94
units.deva:
घटादौ निश्चिते बुद्धिर्नश्यत्येव यदा घटः।
इष्टो नेतुं तदा शक्य इति चेत्सममात्मनि॥
units.translation: If you say that once a pot and the like are ascertained, the cognition indeed disappears, yet the pot can be brought to mind when wanted, the same applies to the Self.

gloss.en: with respect to a pot and the like

units.iast:
ghaṭādau niścite buddhirnaśyatyeva yadā ghaṭaḥ|
iṣṭo netuṃ tadā śakya iti cetsamamātmani||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 95
units.deva:
निश्चित्य सकृदात्मानं यदापेक्षा तदैव तत्।
वक्तुं मन्तुं तथा ध्यातुं शक्नोत्येव हि तत्त्ववित्॥
units.translation: Having ascertained the Self once, the knower of reality can indeed, whenever needed, speak of it, reflect on it, and meditate on it.
units.iast:
niścitya sakṛdātmānaṃ yadāpekṣā tadaiva tat|
vaktuṃ mantuṃ tathā dhyātuṃ śaknotyeva hi tattvavit||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 96
units.deva:
उपासक इव ध्यायन् लौकिकं विस्मरेद्यदि।
विस्मरत्येव सा ध्यानाद्विस्मृतिर्न तु वेदनात्॥
units.translation: If, while meditating like a worshipper, he forgets worldly matters, let him forget. That forgetting comes from meditation, not from knowledge.
units.iast:
upāsaka iva dhyāyan laukikaṃ vismaredyadi|
vismaratyeva sā dhyānādvismṛtirna tu vedanāt||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 97
units.deva:
ध्यानं त्वैच्छिकमेतस्य वेदनान्मुक्तिसिद्धितः।
ज्ञानादेव तु कैवल्यमिति शास्त्रेषु डिण्डिमः॥
units.translation: Meditation is voluntary for him, since liberation is secured through knowledge; the scriptures proclaim loudly that freedom comes from knowledge alone.
units.iast:
dhyānaṃ tvaicchikametasya vedanānmuktisiddhitaḥ|
jñānādeva tu kaivalyamiti śāstreṣu ḍiṇḍimaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 98
units.deva:
तत्त्वविद्यदि न ध्यायेत्प्रवर्तेत तदा बहिः।
प्रवर्ततां सुखेनायं को बाधोऽस्य प्रवर्तने॥
units.translation: If the knower of reality does not meditate, he may then turn outward. Let him do so happily; what obstacle is there to his activity?
units.iast:
tattvavidyadi na dhyāyetpravarteta tadā bahiḥ|
pravartatāṃ sukhenāyaṃ ko bādho’sya pravartane||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 99
units.deva:
अतिप्रसङ्ग इति चेत्प्रसङ्गं तावदीरय।
प्रसङ्गो विधिशास्त्रं चेन्न तत्तत्त्वविदं प्रति॥
units.translation: If you object, “That leads to an excessive consequence,” first state the objection. If you mean that scriptural injunctions apply, they do not apply to a knower of reality.

gloss.en: the objection; the point at issue

units.iast:
atiprasaṅga iti cetprasaṅgaṃ tāvadīraya|
prasaṅgo vidhiśāstraṃ cenna tattattvavidaṃ prati||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 100
units.deva:
वर्णाश्रमवयोवस्थाभिमानो यस्य विद्यते।
तस्यैव हि निषेधाश्च विधयः सकला अपि॥
units.translation: All the scriptural prohibitions and injunctions belong only to one who identifies with caste, life-stage, age, and condition.
units.iast:
varṇāśramavayovasthābhimāno yasya vidyate|
tasyaiva hi niṣedhāśca vidhayaḥ sakalā api||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 101
units.deva:
वर्णाश्रमादयो देहे मायया परिकल्पिताः।
नात्मनो बोधरूपस्येत्येवं तस्य विनिश्चयः॥
units.translation: He is certain that caste, life-stage, and the like are imagined by Māyā in the body, and do not belong to the Self, whose nature is consciousness.
units.iast:
varṇāśramādayo dehe māyayā parikalpitāḥ|
nātmano bodharūpasyetyevaṃ tasya viniścayaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 102
units.deva:
समाधिमथ कर्माणि मा करोतु करोतु वा।
हृदयेनास्तसर्वास्थो मुक्त एवोत्तमाशयः॥
units.translation: Whether he does or does not practice samādhi or action, the one whose heart has let go of every expectation is indeed liberated, of noble disposition.
units.iast:
samādhimatha karmāṇi mā karotu karotu vā|
hṛdayenāstasarvāstho mukta evottamāśayaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 103
units.deva:
नैष्कर्म्येण न तस्यार्थस्तस्यार्थोऽस्ति न कर्मभिः।
न समाधानजप्याभ्यां यस्य निर्वासनं मनः॥
units.translation: One whose mind is free of latent desires has nothing to gain from actionlessness, actions, samādhi, or recitation.
units.iast:
naiṣkarmyeṇa na tasyārthastasyārtho’sti na karmabhiḥ|
na samādhānajapyābhyāṃ yasya nirvāsanaṃ manaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 104
units.deva:
आत्मासङ्गस्ततोऽन्यत्स्यादिन्द्रजालं हि मायिकम्।
इत्यचञ्चलनिर्णिते कुतो मनसि वासना॥
units.translation: The Self is unattached; everything other than it is a magical display made by Māyā. When this is firmly settled in the mind, where could a latent desire arise?
units.iast:
ātmāsaṅgastato’nyatsyādindrajālaṃ hi māyikam|
ityacañcalanirṇite kuto manasi vāsanā||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 105
units.deva:
एवं नास्ति प्रसङ्गोऽपि कुतोऽस्यातिप्रसञ्जनम्।
प्रसङ्गो यस्य तस्यैव शङ्क्येतातिप्रसञ्जनम्॥
units.translation: Thus, there is no rule applying to him; how could he violate one? Only for someone to whom a rule applies could a violation be suspected.
units.iast:
evaṃ nāsti prasaṅgo’pi kuto’syātiprasañjanam|
prasaṅgo yasya tasyaiva śaṅkyetātiprasañjanam||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 106
units.deva:
विध्यभावान्न बालस्य दृश्यतेऽतिप्रसञ्जनम्।
स्यात्कुतोऽतिप्रसङ्गोऽस्य विध्यभावे समे सति॥
units.translation: A child is not seen to violate a rule because no injunction applies to him. With the same absence of injunction for the knower, how could there be a violation?
units.iast:
vidhyabhāvānna bālasya dṛśyate’tiprasañjanam|
syātkuto’tiprasaṅgo’sya vidhyabhāve same sati||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 107
units.deva:
न किंचिद्वेत्ति बालश्चेत्सर्वं वेत्त्येव तत्त्ववित्।
अल्पज्ञस्यैव विधयः सर्वे स्युर्नान्ययोर्द्वयोः॥
units.translation: If you say, “A child knows nothing,” the knower of reality indeed knows all. All injunctions are for the one who knows little, not for either of the other two.
units.iast:
na kiṃcidvetti bālaścetsarvaṃ vettyeva tattvavit|
alpajñasyaiva vidhayaḥ sarve syurnānyayordvayoḥ||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 108
units.deva:
शापानुग्रहसामर्थ्यं यस्यासौ तत्त्वविद्यदि।
न तत् शापादिसामर्थ्यं फलं स्यात्तपसो यतः॥
units.translation: If you say, “One who can curse or bless is a knower of reality,” that power to curse and the like is not [knowledge]; it is a result of austerity.

gloss.en: power to curse and the like

units.iast:
śāpānugrahasāmarthyaṃ yasyāsau tattvavidyadi|
na tat śāpādisāmarthyaṃ phalaṃ syāttapaso yataḥ||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 109
units.deva:
व्यासादेरपि सामर्थ्यं दृश्यते तपसो बलात्।
शापादिकारणादन्यत्तपोज्ञानस्य कारणम्॥
units.translation: Vyāsa and others are also seen to have such powers through the force of austerity. Austerity that produces knowledge is different from austerity that produces powers such as cursing.

gloss.en: from the cause of cursing and the like

units.iast:
vyāsāderapi sāmarthyaṃ dṛśyate tapaso balāt|
śāpādikāraṇādanyattapojñānasya kāraṇam||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 110
units.deva:
द्वयं यस्यास्ति तस्यैव सामर्थ्यज्ञानयोर्जनिः।
एकैकं तु तपः कुर्वन्नेकैकं लभते फलम्॥
units.translation: Both power and knowledge arise only for one who has both [kinds of austerity]; practicing each kind yields its own result.
units.iast:
dvayaṃ yasyāsti tasyaiva sāmarthyajñānayorjaniḥ|
ekaikaṃ tu tapaḥ kurvannekaikaṃ labhate phalam||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 111
units.deva:
सामर्थ्यहीनो निन्द्यश्चेद्यतिभिर्विधिवर्जितः।
निन्द्यन्ते यतयोऽप्यन्यैरनिशं भोगलंपटैः॥
units.translation: If ascetics criticize a monk who lacks powers and observances, those ascetics are in turn constantly criticized by people attached to pleasure.
units.iast:
sāmarthyahīno nindyaścedyatibhirvidhivarjitaḥ|
nindyante yatayo’pyanyairaniśaṃ bhogalaṃpaṭaiḥ||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 112
units.deva:
भिक्षावस्त्रादि रक्षेयुर्यद्येते भोगतुष्टये।
अहो यतित्वमेतेषां वैराग्यभरमन्थरम्॥
units.translation: If these people protect alms, clothes, and the like for their own enjoyment—ah, their ascetic life is slowed by the heavy load of renunciation!

gloss.en: the state of being an ascetic
made sluggish by the weight of renunciation

units.iast:
bhikṣāvastrādi rakṣeyuryadyete bhogatuṣṭaye|
aho yatitvameteṣāṃ vairāgyabharamantharam||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 113
units.deva:
वर्णाश्रमपरान्मूर्खा निन्दन्त्वित्युच्यते यदि।
देहात्ममतयो बुद्धं निन्दन्त्वाश्रममानिनः॥
units.translation: If one says, “Let fools criticize those devoted to varṇa and āśrama duties,” then let those who identify the Self with the body and pride themselves on their āśrama criticize the awakened one too.

gloss.en: those devoted to varṇa and āśrama duties
those whose view is that the body is the Self
those who pride themselves on their āśrama

units.iast:
varṇāśramaparānmūrkhā nindantvityucyate yadi|
dehātmamatayo buddhaṃ nindantvāśramamāninaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 114
units.deva:
तदित्थं तत्त्वविज्ञाने साधनानुपमर्दनात्।
ज्ञानिनाचरितुं शक्यं सम्यग्राज्यादि लौकिकम्॥
units.translation: Thus, because knowledge of reality does not destroy the means of action, a knower can properly carry out worldly activities, even ruling a kingdom and the like.

gloss.en: because the means are not destroyed
ruling a kingdom and the like

units.iast:
taditthaṃ tattvavijñāne sādhanānupamardanāt|
jñāninācarituṃ śakyaṃ samyagrājyādi laukikam||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 115
units.deva:
मिथ्यात्वबुद्ध्या तत्रेच्छा नास्ति चेत्तर्हि मास्तु तत्।
ध्यायन्वाथ व्यवहरन्यथारब्धं वसत्वयम्॥
units.translation: If, because he sees things as unreal, he has no desire for worldly activity, let that be so. Let him live meditating or acting, according to what has already begun [his prārabdha karma].

gloss.en: with the understanding that it is unreal
let it not be; let it be absent

units.iast:
mithyātvabuddhyā tatrecchā nāsti cettarhi māstu tat|
dhyāyanvātha vyavaharanyathārabdhaṃ vasatvayam||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 116
units.deva:
उपासकस्तु सततं ध्यायन्नेव वसेदिति।
ध्यानेनैव कृतं तस्य ब्रह्मत्वं विष्णुतादिवत्॥
units.translation: The meditator, however, should remain constantly meditating. His identity with Brahman is produced by meditation, just as [a worshipper’s identity with] Viṣṇu and the like is [produced].

gloss.en: like identity with Viṣṇu and the like

units.iast:
upāsakastu satataṃ dhyāyanneva vasediti|
dhyānenaiva kṛtaṃ tasya brahmatvaṃ viṣṇutādivat||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 117
units.deva:
ध्यानोपादानकं यत्तद्ध्यानाभावे विलीयते।
वास्तवी ब्रह्मता नैव ज्ञानाभावे विलीयते॥
units.translation: Whatever is produced by meditation dissolves when meditation is absent; real Brahmanhood does not dissolve when knowledge is absent.
units.iast:
dhyānopādānakaṃ yattaddhyānābhāve vilīyate|
vāstavī brahmatā naiva jñānābhāve vilīyate||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 118
units.deva:
ततोऽभिज्ञापकं ज्ञानं न नित्यं जनयत्यदः।
ज्ञापकाभावमात्रेण न हि सत्यं विलीयते॥
units.translation: Therefore knowledge, as a revealer, does not produce that eternal reality; what is real does not disappear merely because its revealer is absent.

gloss.en: merely because the revealer is absent

units.iast:
tato’bhijñāpakaṃ jñānaṃ na nityaṃ janayatyadaḥ|
jñāpakābhāvamātreṇa na hi satyaṃ vilīyate||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 119
units.deva:
अस्त्येव उपासकस्यापि वास्तवी ब्रह्मतेति चेत्।
पामराणां तिरश्चां च वास्तवी ब्रह्मता न किम्॥
units.translation: If you say, “Brahmanhood is real in the meditator too,” is Brahmanhood not real in the ignorant and in animals as well?
units.iast:
astyeva upāsakasyāpi vāstavī brahmateti cet|
pāmarāṇāṃ tiraścāṃ ca vāstavī brahmatā na kim||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 120
units.deva:
अज्ञानादपुमर्थत्वमुभयत्रापि तत्समम्।
उपवासाद्यथा भिक्षा वरं ध्यानं तथान्यथः॥
units.translation: Ignorance makes the lack of life’s true aim the same in both cases. Just as alms are better than fasting, meditation is better than the alternative.

gloss.en: absence of a human goal; lack of life’s true aim

units.iast:
ajñānādapumarthatvamubhayatrāpi tatsamam|
upavāsādyathā bhikṣā varaṃ dhyānaṃ tathānyathaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 121
units.deva:
पामराणां व्यवहृतेर्वरं कर्माद्यनुष्ठितिः।
ततोऽपि सगुणोपास्तिर्निर्गुणोपासनं ततः॥
units.translation: For ordinary people, carrying out ritual duties and the like is better than ordinary worldly pursuits; worship of Brahman with attributes is better still, and worship of attributeless Brahman is better than that.

gloss.en: than worldly activity; than ordinary dealings

units.iast:
pāmarāṇāṃ vyavahṛtervaraṃ karmādyanuṣṭhitiḥ|
tato’pi saguṇopāstirnirguṇopāsanaṃ tataḥ||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 122
units.deva:
यावद्विज्ञानसामीप्यं तावच्छ्रैष्ठ्यं विवर्धते।
ब्रह्मज्ञानाय ते साक्षान्निर्गुणोपासनं शनैः॥
units.translation: For you, the closer it is to direct knowledge, the greater its superiority; meditation on the attributeless [Brahman] thus gradually leads directly to knowledge of Brahman.
units.iast:
yāvadvijñānasāmīpyaṃ tāvacchraiṣṭhyaṃ vivardhate|
brahmajñānāya te sākṣānnirguṇopāsanaṃ śanaiḥ||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 123
units.deva:
यथा संवादिविभ्रान्तिः फलकाले प्रमायते।
विद्यायते तथोपास्तिर्मुक्तिकालेऽतिपाकतः॥
units.translation: Just as a leading misconception is confirmed as valid when its result comes, so meditation, when fully ripened, comes to function as knowledge at the time of liberation.

gloss.en: a leading misconception; an error that proves useful
is confirmed as valid; becomes valid knowledge

units.iast:
yathā saṃvādivibhrāntiḥ phalakāle pramāyate|
vidyāyate tathopāstirmuktikāle’tipākataḥ||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 124
units.deva:
संवादिभ्रमतः पुंसः प्रवृत्तस्यान्यमानतः।
प्रमेति चेत्तथोपास्तिर्मान्तरे कारणायताम्॥
units.translation: If you say that valid knowledge arises for someone who has acted on a leading misconception through another means [of knowledge], then let meditation likewise become a cause of another means [of direct knowledge].

gloss.en: who has acted; who has proceeded

units.iast:
saṃvādibhramataḥ puṃsaḥ pravṛttasyānyamānataḥ|
prameti cettathopāstirmāntare kāraṇāyatām||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 125
units.deva:
मूर्तिध्यानस्य मन्त्रादेरपि कारणता यदि।
अस्तु नाम तथाप्यत्र प्रत्यासत्तिर्विशिष्यते॥
units.translation: If meditation on a form, a mantra, and the like can also be a cause, let that be so; even then, this [meditation] is distinguished by its special closeness [to direct knowledge].

gloss.en: of a mantra and the like

units.iast:
mūrtidhyānasya mantrāderapi kāraṇatā yadi|
astu nāma tathāpyatra pratyāsattirviśiṣyate||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 126
units.deva:
निर्गुणोपासनं पक्वं समाधिः स्याच्छनैस्ततः।
यः समाधिर्निरोधाख्यः सोऽनायासेन लभ्यते॥
units.translation: When meditation on the attributeless [Brahman] matures, samādhi gradually arises; that samādhi, called nirodha, is attained without effort.
units.iast:
nirguṇopāsanaṃ pakvaṃ samādhiḥ syācchanaistataḥ|
yaḥ samādhirnirodhākhyaḥ so’nāyāsena labhyate||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 127
units.deva:
निरोधलाभे पुंसोऽन्तरसङ्गं वस्तु शिष्यते।
पुनः पुनर्वासितेऽस्मिन्वाक्याज्जायेत तत्त्वधीः॥
units.translation: When a person attains cessation, the unattached reality remains within. When this is repeatedly impressed through a [scriptural] sentence, knowledge of reality arises.
units.iast:
nirodhalābhe puṃso’ntarasaṅgaṃ vastu śiṣyate|
punaḥ punarvāsite’sminvākyājjāyeta tattvadhīḥ||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 128
units.deva:
निर्विकारासङ्गनित्यस्वप्रकाशैकपूर्णताः।
बुद्धौ झटिति शास्त्रोक्ता आरोहन्त्यविवादतः॥
units.translation: The qualities stated in scripture—changelessness, nonattachment, eternality, self-luminosity, oneness, and fullness—arise in the intellect at once, beyond dispute.
units.iast:
nirvikārāsaṅganityasvaprakāśaikapūrṇatāḥ|
buddhau jhaṭiti śāstroktā ārohantyavivādataḥ||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 129
units.deva:
योगाभ्यासस्त्वेतदर्थोऽमृतबिन्द्वादिषु श्रुतः।
एवं च दृष्टद्वारापि हेतुत्वादन्यतो वरम्॥
units.translation: Yoga practice for this purpose is taught in the Amṛtabindu and other [Upaniṣads]. Because it is a cause through a directly evident result as well, it is better than the other [means].

gloss.en: in the Amṛtabindu and the like
through a directly seen means; through an evident result

units.iast:
yogābhyāsastvetadartho’mṛtabindvādiṣu śrutaḥ|
evaṃ ca dṛṣṭadvārāpi hetutvādanyato varam||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 130
units.deva:
उपेक्ष्य तत्तीर्थयात्रां जपादीनेव कुर्वताम्।
पिण्डं समुत्सृज्य करं लेढीति न्याय आपतेत्॥
units.translation: For those who neglect that [meditation] and only undertake pilgrimage, recitation, and the like, the maxim “throw away a mouthful of food and lick the hand” applies.

gloss.en: a mouthful; a lump of food

units.iast:
upekṣya tattīrthayātrāṃ japādīneva kurvatām|
piṇḍaṃ samutsṛjya karaṃ leḍhīti nyāya āpatet||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 131
units.deva:
उपासकानामप्येवं विचारत्यागतो यदि।
बाधं तस्माद्विचारस्यासम्भवे योग ईरितः॥
units.translation: If meditators too face this obstacle because they give up inquiry, then yoga is prescribed when inquiry is not possible.
units.iast:
upāsakānāmapyevaṃ vicāratyāgato yadi|
bādhaṃ tasmādvicārasyāsambhave yoga īritaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 132
units.deva:
बहुव्याकुलचित्तानां विचारात्तत्त्वधीर्न हि।
योगो मुख्यस्ततस्तेषां धीदर्पस्तेन नश्यति॥
units.translation: Those whose minds are greatly disturbed do not gain knowledge of reality through inquiry. Yoga is therefore their primary means, and it removes the dullness of their intellect.

gloss.en: of those whose minds are greatly disturbed
the intellect’s dullness; its impaired force

units.iast:
bahuvyākulacittānāṃ vicārāttattvadhīrna hi|
yogo mukhyastatasteṣāṃ dhīdarpastena naśyati||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 133
units.deva:
अव्याकुलधियां मोहमात्रेणाच्छादितात्मनाम्।
साङ्ख्यनामा विचाराः स्यान्मुख्यो झटिति सिद्धितः॥
units.translation: For those whose intellects are undisturbed and whose inner nature is covered only by delusion, inquiry called Sāṅkhya is primary because it succeeds quickly.

gloss.en: of those whose intellects are undisturbed
of those whose inner nature is covered
because of success; because it succeeds

units.iast:
avyākuladhiyāṃ mohamātreṇācchāditātmanām|
sāṅkhyanāmā vicārāḥ syānmukhyo jhaṭiti siddhitaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 134
units.deva:
यत्साङ्ख्यैः प्राप्यते स्थानं तद्योगैरपि गम्यते।
एकं साङ्ख्यं च योगं च यः पश्यति स पश्यति॥
units.translation: The state reached by Sāṅkhya thinkers is reached by yogis too. Whoever sees Sāṅkhya and Yoga as one truly sees.
units.iast:
yatsāṅkhyaiḥ prāpyate sthānaṃ tadyogairapi gamyate|
ekaṃ sāṅkhyaṃ ca yogaṃ ca yaḥ paśyati sa paśyati||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 135
units.deva:
तत्कारणं साङ्ख्ययोगाधिगम्यमिति हि श्रुतिः।
यस्तु श्रुतेर्विरुद्धः स आभासः साङ्ख्ययोगयोः॥
units.translation: Scripture says that the source is to be attained through Sāṅkhya and Yoga. Whatever in either system contradicts scripture is a mere semblance.

gloss.en: to be attained through Sāṅkhya and Yoga
in Sāṅkhya and Yoga; of the two systems

units.iast:
tatkāraṇaṃ sāṅkhyayogādhigamyamiti hi śrutiḥ|
yastu śruterviruddhaḥ sa ābhāsaḥ sāṅkhyayogayoḥ||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 136
units.deva:
उपासनं नातिपक्वमिह यस्य परत्र सः।
मरणे ब्रह्मलोके वा तत्त्वं विज्ञाय मुच्यते॥
units.translation: If someone’s meditation has not ripened sufficiently here, later—at death or in Brahmā’s world—he knows reality and is released.
units.iast:
upāsanaṃ nātipakvamiha yasya paratra saḥ|
maraṇe brahmaloke vā tattvaṃ vijñāya mucyate||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 137
units.deva:
यं यं चापि स्मरन्भावं त्यजत्यन्ते कलेवरम्।
तं तमेवैति यच्चित्तस्तेन यातीति शास्त्रतः॥
units.translation: Whatever state a person remembers when leaving the body at the end, that very state he reaches; one goes according to the thought held in mind, says scripture.

gloss.en: that very one; that same state

units.iast:
yaṃ yaṃ cāpi smaranbhāvaṃ tyajatyante kalevaram|
taṃ tamevaiti yaccittastena yātīti śāstrataḥ||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 138
units.deva:
अन्त्यप्रत्ययतो नूनं भाविजन्म तथा सति।
निर्गुणप्रत्ययोऽपि स्यात्सगुणोपासने यथा॥
units.translation: A future birth is certainly determined by the final thought. In the same way as in worship with attributes, a thought of the attributeless [Brahman] can also arise.

gloss.en: in worship of Brahman with attributes

units.iast:
antyapratyayato nūnaṃ bhāvijanma tathā sati|
nirguṇapratyayo’pi syātsaguṇopāsane yathā||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 139
units.deva:
नित्यं निर्गुणरूपं तन्नाममात्रेण गीयताम्।
अर्थतोमोक्ष एवैष संवादि भ्रमवन्मतः॥
units.translation: Let that [Brahman] be praised by the names “eternal” and “attributeless” alone; in meaning, it is liberation itself, regarded like a leading misconception that yields its result.

gloss.en: let it be sung; let it be praised

units.iast:
nityaṃ nirguṇarūpaṃ tannāmamātreṇa gīyatām|
arthatomokṣa evaiṣa saṃvādi bhramavanmataḥ||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 140
units.deva:
तत्सामर्थ्याज्जायते धीर्मूलाविद्यानिवर्तिका।
अविमुक्तोपासनेन तारकब्रह्म बुद्धिवत्॥
units.translation: Through the power of that meditation, understanding that removes root ignorance arises, just as knowledge of Tāraka Brahman arises through worship of Avimukta.
units.iast:
tatsāmarthyājjāyate dhīrmūlāvidyānivartikā|
avimuktopāsanena tārakabrahma buddhivat||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 141
units.deva:
सकामो निष्काम इति ह्यशरीरो निरिन्द्रियः।
अभयं हीति मुक्तत्वं तापनीये फलं श्रुतम्॥
units.translation: The Tāpanīya states liberation as the result, described with the words “with desire, without desire, bodiless, without senses, and fearless.”
units.iast:
sakāmo niṣkāma iti hyaśarīro nirindriyaḥ|
abhayaṃ hīti muktatvaṃ tāpanīye phalaṃ śrutam||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 142
units.deva:
उपासनस्य सामर्थ्याद्विद्योत्पत्तिर्भवेत्ततः।
नान्यः पन्था इति ह्येतच्छास्त्रं नैव विरुध्यते॥
units.translation: Through the power of meditation, knowledge arises; therefore the scriptural statement “there is no other path” is not contradicted.
units.iast:
upāsanasya sāmarthyādvidyotpattirbhavettataḥ|
nānyaḥ panthā iti hyetacchāstraṃ naiva virudhyate||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 143
units.deva:
निष्कामोपासनान्मुक्तिस्तापनीये समीरिता।
ब्रह्मलोकः सकामस्य शैब्यप्रश्ने समीरितः॥
units.translation: The Tāpanīya states liberation as the result of desireless meditation; the Śaibya question [in the Praśna Upaniṣad] states Brahmā’s world as the result for one who meditates with desire.

gloss.en: for one who meditates with desire
in the Śaibya question [in the Praśna Upaniṣad]

units.iast:
niṣkāmopāsanānmuktistāpanīye samīritā|
brahmalokaḥ sakāmasya śaibyapraśne samīritaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 144
units.deva:
य उपास्ते त्रिमात्रेण ब्रह्मलोके स नीयते।
स एतस्माज्जीवघनात्परं पुरुषमीक्षते॥
units.translation: Whoever meditates with the three measures [of Oṃ] is led to Brahmā’s world; there he sees the Supreme Person beyond this mass of living beings.
units.iast:
ya upāste trimātreṇa brahmaloke sa nīyate|
sa etasmājjīvaghanātparaṃ puruṣamīkṣate||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 145
units.deva:
अप्रतीकाधिकरणे तत्क्रतुर्न्याय ईरितः।
ब्रह्मलोकफलं तस्मात्सकामस्येति वर्णितम्॥
units.translation: In the Apratīka section, the principle that one becomes what one resolves upon is stated; therefore Brahmā’s world is described as the result for a person who meditates with desire.

gloss.en: in the Apratīka section [of the Brahma Sūtras]
for one who meditates with desire

units.iast:
apratīkādhikaraṇe tatkraturnyāya īritaḥ|
brahmalokaphalaṃ tasmātsakāmasyeti varṇitam||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 146
units.deva:
निर्गुणोपास्तिसामर्थ्यात्तत्र तत्त्वमवेक्षणत्।
पुनरावर्तते नायं कल्पान्ते तु विमुच्यते॥
units.translation: Through the power of meditation on the attributeless [Brahman], he realizes reality there and does not return; at the end of the kalpa, he is liberated.

gloss.en: through the power of meditation on the attributeless
at the end of a kalpa

units.iast:
nirguṇopāstisāmarthyāttatra tattvamavekṣaṇat|
punarāvartate nāyaṃ kalpānte tu vimucyate||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 147
units.deva:
प्रणवोपास्तयः प्रायो निर्गुणा एव वेदगाः।
क्वचित्सगुणता प्रोक्ता प्रणवोपासनस्य हि॥
units.translation: Vedic meditations on Oṃ are generally on attributeless Brahman, though in some places meditation on Oṃ is said to be with attributes.
units.iast:
praṇavopāstayaḥ prāyo nirguṇā eva vedagāḥ|
kvacitsaguṇatā proktā praṇavopāsanasya hi||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 148
units.deva:
परापरब्रह्मरूप ओङ्कार उपवर्णितः।
पिप्पलादेन मुनिना सत्यकामाय पृच्छते॥
units.translation: The sage Pippalāda described Oṃ to Satyakāma, who had asked, as having the form of both the higher and lower Brahman.

gloss.en: having the form of higher and lower Brahman
to the one asking; to the questioner

units.iast:
parāparabrahmarūpa oṅkāra upavarṇitaḥ|
pippalādena muninā satyakāmāya pṛcchate||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 149
units.deva:
एतदालम्बनं ज्ञात्वा यो यदिच्छति तस्य तत्।
इति प्रोक्तं यमेनापि पृच्छते नचिकेतसे॥
units.translation: Yama too told the questioning Naciketas: “Knowing this support [Oṃ], one obtains whatever one desires.”
units.iast:
etadālambanaṃ jñātvā yo yadicchati tasya tat|
iti proktaṃ yamenāpi pṛcchate naciketase||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 150
units.deva:
इह वा मरणे वास्य ब्रह्मलोकेऽथवा भवेत्।
ब्रह्मसाक्षात्कृतिः सम्यगुपासीनस्य निर्गुणम्॥
units.translation: For one who meditates properly on the attributeless [Brahman], direct realization of Brahman may occur here, at death, or in Brahmā’s world.
units.iast:
iha vā maraṇe vāsya brahmaloke’thavā bhavet|
brahmasākṣātkṛtiḥ samyagupāsīnasya nirguṇam||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 151
units.deva:
अर्थोऽयमात्मगीतायामपि स्पष्टमुदीरितः।
विचाराक्षम आत्मानमुपासीतेति सन्ततम्॥
units.translation: This point, too, is clearly stated in the Ātmā Gītā: “One unable to inquire should constantly meditate on the Self.”
units.iast:
artho’yamātmagītāyāmapi spaṣṭamudīritaḥ|
vicārākṣama ātmānamupāsīteti santatam||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 152
units.deva:
साक्षात्कर्तुमशक्तोऽपि चिन्तयेन्मामशङ्कितः।
कालेनानुभवारूढो भवेयं फलतो ध्रुवम्॥
units.translation: Even if a person cannot realize Me directly, he should contemplate Me without doubt; in time, I will surely become established in direct experience as the result.

gloss.en: I will be; I will become

units.iast:
sākṣātkartumaśakto’pi cintayenmāmaśaṅkitaḥ|
kālenānubhavārūḍho bhaveyaṃ phalato dhruvam||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 153
units.deva:
यथागाधनिधेर्लब्धौ नोपायः खननं विना।
मल्लाभेऽपि तथा स्वात्मचिन्तां मुक्त्वा न चापरः॥
units.translation: Just as there is no means to obtain a deep treasure except by digging, so too, for attaining Me, there is no other means apart from contemplation of one’s own Self.
units.iast:
yathāgādhanidherlabdhau nopāyaḥ khananaṃ vinā|
mallābhe’pi tathā svātmacintāṃ muktvā na cāparaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 154
units.deva:
देहोपलमपाकृत्य बुद्धिकुद्दलकात्पुनः।
खात्वा मनोभुवं भूयो गृह्णीयान्मां निधिं पुमान्॥
units.translation: A person should clear away the stone of bodily identification, then dig again into the ground of the mind with the intellect as the pickaxe, and grasp Me, the treasure.
units.iast:
dehopalamapākṛtya buddhikuddalakātpunaḥ|
khātvā manobhuvaṃ bhūyo gṛhṇīyānmāṃ nidhiṃ pumān||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 155
units.deva:
अनुभूतेरभावेऽपि ब्रह्मास्मीत्येव चिन्त्यताम्।
अप्यसत् प्राप्यते ध्यानान्नित्याप्तं ब्रह्म किं पुनः॥
units.translation: Even without direct realization, one should think, “I am Brahman.” By meditation even what is unreal is attained; how much more so Brahman, which is ever attained?
units.iast:
anubhūterabhāve’pi brahmāsmītyeva cintyatām|
apyasat prāpyate dhyānānnityāptaṃ brahma kiṃ punaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 156
units.deva:
अनात्मबुद्धिशैथिल्यं फलं ध्यानाद्दिने दिने।
पश्यन्नपि न चेद्ध्यायेत्कोऽपरोऽस्मात् पशुवद्॥
units.translation: Though seeing that the result of meditation day after day is the loosening of the notion that the non-Self is the Self, if a person still does not meditate, what else is he but like an animal?

gloss.en: the notion that the non-Self is the Self

units.iast:
anātmabuddhiśaithilyaṃ phalaṃ dhyānāddine dine|
paśyannapi na ceddhyāyetko’paro’smāt paśuvad||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 157
units.deva:
देहाभिमानं विध्वस्य ध्यानादात्मानमद्वयम्।
पश्यन्मर्त्यो मृतो भूत्वा ह्यत्र ब्रह्म समश्नुते॥
units.translation: Having destroyed identification with the body and, through meditation, seeing the nondual Self, a mortal—having become “dead” to bodily identity—indeed attains Brahman here.
units.iast:
dehābhimānaṃ vidhvasya dhyānādātmānamadvayam|
paśyanmartyo mṛto bhūtvā hyatra brahma samaśnute||

units.label: Chapter 9 · Verse 158
units.deva:
ध्यानदीपमिमं सम्यक्परामृषति यो नरः।
मुक्तसंशय एवायं ध्यायति ब्रह्म सन्ततम्॥
units.translation: Whoever carefully examines this Lamp of Meditation is indeed free from doubt and meditates continually on Brahman.
units.iast:
dhyānadīpamimaṃ samyakparāmṛṣati yo naraḥ|
muktasaṃśaya evāyaṃ dhyāyati brahma santatam||

units.label: Chapter 10 · Verse 1
units.deva:
परमात्माद्वयानन्दपूर्णः पूर्वं स्वमायया।
स्वयमेव जगद्भूत्वा प्राविशज्जीवरूपतः॥
units.translation: The Supreme Self, full of nondual bliss, first became the world through its own Māyā and entered it in the form of the jīva.

gloss.en: in the form of the jīva

units.iast:
paramātmādvayānandapūrṇaḥ pūrvaṃ svamāyayā|
svayameva jagadbhūtvā prāviśajjīvarūpataḥ||

units.label: Chapter 10 · Verse 2
units.deva:
देवाद्युत्तमदेहेषु प्रविष्टो देवताभवत्।
मर्त्याद्यधमदेहेषु स्थितो भजति देवताम्॥
units.translation: Entering superior bodies, beginning with those of the gods, it became a deity; dwelling in inferior bodies, beginning with those of humans, it worships a deity.
units.iast:
devādyuttamadeheṣu praviṣṭo devatābhavat|
martyādyadhamadeheṣu sthito bhajati devatām||

units.label: Chapter 10 · Verse 3
units.deva:
अनेकजन्मभजनात्स्वविचारं चिकीर्षति।
विचारेण विनष्टायां मायायां शिष्यते स्वयम्॥
units.translation: Through worship in many births, one wishes to undertake inquiry into oneself; when inquiry destroys Māyā, the Self alone remains.
units.iast:
anekajanmabhajanātsvavicāraṃ cikīrṣati|
vicāreṇa vinaṣṭāyāṃ māyāyāṃ śiṣyate svayam||

units.label: Chapter 10 · Verse 4
units.deva:
अद्वयानन्दरूपस्य सद्वयत्वं च दुःखिता।
बन्धः प्रोक्तः स्वरूपेण स्थितिर्मुक्तिरितीर्यते॥
units.translation: For the one whose nature is nondual bliss, the state of duality and misery is called bondage; abiding in one’s own nature is called liberation.

gloss.en: of one whose nature is nondual bliss

units.iast:
advayānandarūpasya sadvayatvaṃ ca duḥkhitā|
bandhaḥ proktaḥ svarūpeṇa sthitirmuktiritīryate||

units.label: Chapter 10 · Verse 5
units.deva:
अविचारकृतो बन्धो विचारेण निवर्तते।
तस्माज्जीवपरात्मानौ सर्वदैव विचारयेत्॥
units.translation: Bondage caused by lack of inquiry is removed by inquiry. Therefore one should always inquire into the individual Self and the Supreme Self.

gloss.en: the individual Self and the Supreme Self

units.iast:
avicārakṛto bandho vicāreṇa nivartate|
tasmājjīvaparātmānau sarvadaiva vicārayet||

units.label: Chapter 10 · Verse 6
units.deva:
अहमित्यभिमन्ता यः कर्तासौ तस्य साधनम्।
मनस्तस्य क्रिये अन्तर्बहिर्वृत्ति क्रमोत्थिते॥
units.translation: Whoever conceives “I am” is the agent; the mind is that person’s instrument, and its two operations—an inward and an outward mental mode—arise in sequence.
units.iast:
ahamityabhimantā yaḥ kartāsau tasya sādhanam|
manastasya kriye antarbahirvṛtti kramotthite||

units.label: Chapter 10 · Verse 7
units.deva:
अन्तर्मुखाहमित्येषा वृत्तिः कर्तारमुल्लिखेत्।
बहिर्मुखेदमित्येषा बाह्यं वस्त्विदमुल्लिखेत्॥
units.translation: An inward-facing mental mode, in the form “I,” marks the agent; an outward-facing mode, in the form “this,” marks this external object.
units.iast:
antarmukhāhamityeṣā vṛttiḥ kartāramullikhet|
bahirmukhedamityeṣā bāhyaṃ vastvidamullikhet||

units.label: Chapter 10 · Verse 8
units.deva:
इदमो ये विशेषाः स्युर्गन्धरूपरसादयः।
असाङ्कर्येण तान्भिद्याद्घ्राणादीन्द्रियपञ्चकम्॥
units.translation: Whatever particulars belong to “this”—smell, form, taste, and the like—the five sense organs, beginning with the nose, should distinguish without confusion.

gloss.en: smell, form, taste, and the like
the group of five sense organs

units.iast:
idamo ye viśeṣāḥ syurgandharūparasādayaḥ|
asāṅkaryeṇa tānbhidyādghrāṇādīndriyapañcakam||

units.label: Chapter 10 · Verse 9
units.deva:
कर्तारं च क्रियां तद्वद्व्यावृत्तविषयानपि।
स्फोरयेदेकयत्नेन योऽसौ साक्ष्यत्र चिद्वपुः॥
units.translation: That which, in one act, reveals the agent, the action, and the distinct objects is here the witness, whose nature is consciousness.
units.iast:
kartāraṃ ca kriyāṃ tadvadvyāvṛttaviṣayānapi|
sphorayedekayatnena yo’sau sākṣyatra cidvapuḥ||

units.label: Chapter 10 · Verse 10
units.deva:
ईक्षे शृणोमि जिघ्रामि स्वादयामि स्पृशाम्यहम्।
इति भासयते सर्वं नृत्यशालास्थदीपवत्॥
units.translation: Like a lamp in a dance hall, the witness illuminates everything as “I see,” “I hear,” “I smell,” “I taste,” and “I touch.”

gloss.en: like a lamp standing in a dance hall

units.iast:
īkṣe śṛṇomi jighrāmi svādayāmi spṛśāmyaham|
iti bhāsayate sarvaṃ nṛtyaśālāsthadīpavat||

units.label: Chapter 10 · Verse 11
units.deva:
नृत्यशालास्थितो दीपः प्रभुं सभ्यांश्च नर्तकीम्।
दीपयेदविशेषेण तदभावेऽपि दीप्यते॥
units.translation: A lamp standing in a dance hall illuminates the patron, the audience, and the dancer without distinction; it shines even when they are absent.
units.iast:
nṛtyaśālāsthito dīpaḥ prabhuṃ sabhyāṃśca nartakīm|
dīpayedaviśeṣeṇa tadabhāve’pi dīpyate||

units.label: Chapter 10 · Verse 12
units.deva:
अहङ्कारं धियं साक्षी विषयानपि भासयेत्।
अहङ्काराद्यभावेऽपि स्वयं भात्येव पूर्ववत्॥
units.translation: The witness illumines the ego, the intellect, and the sense objects; even when the ego and the rest are absent, it shines by itself as before.
units.iast:
ahaṅkāraṃ dhiyaṃ sākṣī viṣayānapi bhāsayet|
ahaṅkārādyabhāve’pi svayaṃ bhātyeva pūrvavat||

units.label: Chapter 10 · Verse 13
units.deva:
निरन्तरं भासमाने कूटस्थे ज्ञप्तिरूपतः।
तद्भासा भास्यमानेयं बुद्धिर्नृत्यत्यनेकधा॥
units.translation: While the changeless witness shines continuously as awareness, this intellect, illumined by its light, dances in many ways.
units.iast:
nirantaraṃ bhāsamāne kūṭasthe jñaptirūpataḥ|
tadbhāsā bhāsyamāneyaṃ buddhirnṛtyatyanekadhā||

units.label: Chapter 10 · Verse 14
units.deva:
अहङ्कारः प्रभुः सभ्या विषया नर्तकी मतिः।
तालादिधारिण्यक्षाणि दीपः साक्ष्यवभासकः॥
units.translation: The ego is the patron, the objects are the audience, and the intellect is the dancer; the sense organs hold the rhythm, while the witness that illumines them is the lamp.

gloss.en: holding the rhythm and the like

units.iast:
ahaṅkāraḥ prabhuḥ sabhyā viṣayā nartakī matiḥ|
tālādidhāriṇyakṣāṇi dīpaḥ sākṣyavabhāsakaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 10 · Verse 15
units.deva:
स्वस्थानसंस्थितो दीपः सर्वतो भासयेद्यथा।
स्थिरस्थायी तथा साक्षी बहिरन्तः प्रकाशयेत्॥
units.translation: Just as a lamp, remaining in its own place, illuminates everything around it, so the stationary witness illumines what is inside and outside.
units.iast:
svasthānasaṃsthito dīpaḥ sarvato bhāsayedyathā|
sthirasthāyī tathā sākṣī bahirantaḥ prakāśayet||

units.label: Chapter 10 · Verse 16
units.deva:
बहिरन्तर्विभागोऽयं देहापेक्षो न साक्षिणि।
विषया बाह्यदेशस्था देहस्यान्तरहङ्कृतिः॥
units.translation: This division into outside and inside depends on the body, not on the witness: objects are located outside, and the ego is inside the body.
units.iast:
bahirantarvibhāgo’yaṃ dehāpekṣo na sākṣiṇi|
viṣayā bāhyadeśasthā dehasyāntarahaṅkṛtiḥ||

units.label: Chapter 10 · Verse 17
units.deva:
अन्तस्था धीः सहैवाक्षैर्बहिर्याति पुनः पुनः।
भास्यबुद्धिस्थचाञ्चल्यं साक्षिण्यारोप्यते वृथा॥
units.translation: The mind located within goes outward again and again together with the sense organs; the restlessness in the illumined mind is falsely attributed to the witness.

gloss.en: the restlessness located in the illumined mind

units.iast:
antasthā dhīḥ sahaivākṣairbahiryāti punaḥ punaḥ|
bhāsyabuddhisthacāñcalyaṃ sākṣiṇyāropyate vṛthā||

units.label: Chapter 10 · Verse 18
units.deva:
गृहान्तरगतः स्वल्पो गवाक्षादातपोऽचलः।
तत्र हस्ते नर्त्यमाने नृत्यतीवातपो यथा॥
units.translation: A small patch of sunlight entering a room through a window is motionless; when a hand is moved there, the light seems to dance.

gloss.en: is moved; is made to dance

units.iast:
gṛhāntaragataḥ svalpo gavākṣādātapo’calaḥ|
tatra haste nartyamāne nṛtyatīvātapo yathā||

units.label: Chapter 10 · Verse 19
units.deva:
निजस्थानस्थितः साक्षी बहिरन्तर्गमागमौ।
अकुर्वन्बुद्धिचाञ्चल्यात्करोतीव तथा तथा॥
units.translation: The witness remains in its own place and makes no outward or inward movement; because of the mind’s restlessness, it seems to move to and fro.

gloss.en: in those ways; to and fro

units.iast:
nijasthānasthitaḥ sākṣī bahirantargamāgamau|
akurvanbuddhicāñcalyātkarotīva tathā tathā||

units.label: Chapter 10 · Verse 20
units.deva:
न बाह्यो नान्तरः साक्षी बुद्धेर्देशौ हि तावुभौ।
बुद्ध्याद्यशेषसंशान्तौ यत्र भात्यस्ति तत्र सः॥
units.translation: The witness is neither external nor internal, for both are locations of the intellect. When the intellect and the rest have become completely still, the witness is there, shining.
units.iast:
na bāhyo nāntaraḥ sākṣī buddherdeśau hi tāvubhau|
buddhyādyaśeṣasaṃśāntau yatra bhātyasti tatra saḥ||

units.label: Chapter 10 · Verse 21
units.deva:
देशः कोऽपि न भासेत यदि तर्ह्यस्त्वदेशभाक्।
सर्वदेशप्रक्लृप्त्यैव सर्वगत्वं न तु स्वतः॥
units.translation: If no place appears, let the witness be without a location. Its being everywhere comes only from the conception of all locations, not from its own nature.

gloss.en: through the conception of all locations

units.iast:
deśaḥ ko’pi na bhāseta yadi tarhyastvadeśabhāk|
sarvadeśapraklṛptyaiva sarvagatvaṃ na tu svataḥ||

units.label: Chapter 10 · Verse 22
units.deva:
अन्तर्बहिर्वा सर्वं वा यं देशं परिकल्पयेत्।
बुद्धिस्तद्देशगः साक्षी तथा वस्तुषु योजयेत्॥
units.translation: Whatever place the intellect imagines—inside, outside, or anywhere—the witness is present there; the same should be understood of objects.
units.iast:
antarbahirvā sarvaṃ vā yaṃ deśaṃ parikalpayet|
buddhistaddeśagaḥ sākṣī tathā vastuṣu yojayet||

units.label: Chapter 10 · Verse 23
units.deva:
यद्यद्रूपमादौ कल्प्येत बुद्ध्या तत्तत्प्रकाशयन्।
तस्य तस्य भवेत्साक्षी स्वतः वाग्बुद्ध्यगोचरः॥
units.translation: Whatever form the intellect may imagine, the witness illumines each one; by its own nature, it is beyond the reach of speech and intellect.
units.iast:
yadyadrūpamādau kalpyeta buddhyā tattatprakāśayan|
tasya tasya bhavetsākṣī svataḥ vāgbuddhyagocaraḥ||

units.label: Chapter 10 · Verse 24
units.deva:
कथं तादृङ्मया ग्राह्यमिति चेन्मैव गृह्यताम्।
सर्वग्रहोपसंशान्तौ स्वयमेवावशिष्यते॥
units.translation: If someone asks, “How can such a thing be grasped by me?”, let it not be grasped. When all grasping has ceased, it remains by itself.
units.iast:
kathaṃ tādṛṅmayā grāhyamiti cenmaiva gṛhyatām|
sarvagrahopasaṃśāntau svayamevāvaśiṣyate||

units.label: Chapter 10 · Verse 25
units.deva:
न तत्र मानापेक्षास्ति स्वप्रकाशस्वरूपतः।
तादृग्व्युत्पत्त्यपेक्षा चेच्छ्रुतिं पठ गुरोर्मुखात्॥
units.translation: No means of knowledge is needed for it, since its nature is self-luminous. If you need instruction of that kind, study the Śruti from a teacher’s mouth.

gloss.en: need for a means of knowledge

units.iast:
na tatra mānāpekṣāsti svaprakāśasvarūpataḥ|
tādṛgvyutpattyapekṣā cecchrutiṃ paṭha gurormukhāt||

units.label: Chapter 10 · Verse 26
units.deva:
यदि सर्वग्रहत्यागोऽशक्यस्तर्हि धियं व्रज।
शरणं तदधीनोऽन्तर्बहिर्वैषोऽनुभूयताम्॥
units.translation: If giving up all grasping is impossible, take refuge in the intellect; with it as your support, experience this [witness] within and without.

gloss.en: dependent on it; with it as support

units.iast:
yadi sarvagrahatyāgo’śakyastarhi dhiyaṃ vraja|
śaraṇaṃ tadadhīno’ntarbahirvaiṣo’nubhūyatām||

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 1
units.deva:
ब्रह्मानन्दं प्रवक्ष्यामि ज्ञाते तस्मिन्नशेषतः।
ऐहिकामुष्मिकानर्थव्रातं हित्वा सुखायते॥
units.translation: I will explain the bliss of Brahman. When it is fully known, one becomes happy, having left behind the mass of this-worldly and otherworldly troubles.
units.iast:
brahmānandaṃ pravakṣyāmi jñāte tasminnaśeṣataḥ|
aihikāmuṣmikānarthavrātaṃ hitvā sukhāyate||

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 2
units.deva:
ब्रह्मवित्परमाप्नोति शोकं तरति चात्मवित्।
रसो ब्रह्मरसं लब्ध्वानन्दी भवति नान्यथा॥
units.translation: The knower of Brahman attains the Highest; the knower of the Self crosses sorrow. Brahman is the essence; having attained that essence, one becomes blissful, and not otherwise.
units.iast:
brahmavitparamāpnoti śokaṃ tarati cātmavit|
raso brahmarasaṃ labdhvānandī bhavati nānyathā||

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 3
units.deva:
प्रतिष्ठां विन्दते स्वस्मिन्यदा स्यादथ सोऽभयः।
कुरुतेऽस्मिन्नन्तरं चेदथ तस्य भयं भवेत्॥
units.translation: When one finds a firm footing in oneself, one becomes fearless. If one makes a distinction in this [Self], fear arises for that person.
units.iast:
pratiṣṭhāṃ vindate svasminyadā syādatha so’bhayaḥ|
kurute’sminnantaraṃ cedatha tasya bhayaṃ bhavet||

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 4
units.deva:
वायुः सूर्यो वह्निरिन्द्रो मृत्युर्जन्मान्तरेऽन्तरम्।
कृत्वा धर्मं विजानन्तोऽप्यस्माद्भीत्या चरन्ति हि॥
units.translation: Vāyu, the Sun, Fire, Indra, and Death, having performed dharma with a sense of difference in previous births, even while knowing, act from fear of this [Brahman].
units.iast:
vāyuḥ sūryo vahnirindro mṛtyurjanmāntare’ntaram|
kṛtvā dharmaṃ vijānanto’pyasmādbhītyā caranti hi||

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 5
units.deva:
आनन्दं ब्रह्मणो विद्वान्न बिभेति कुतश्चन।
एतमेव तपेन्नैषा चिन्ता कर्माग्निसम्भृता॥
units.translation: The knower of the bliss of Brahman fears nothing at all; the worry kindled by the fire of karma does not scorch this person.

gloss.en: kindled by the fire of karma

units.iast:
ānandaṃ brahmaṇo vidvānna bibheti kutaścana|
etameva tapennaiṣā cintā karmāgnisambhṛtā||

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 6
units.deva:
एवं विद्वान्कर्मणि द्वे हित्वात्मानं स्मरेत्सदा।
कृते च कर्मणि स्वात्मरूपेणैवैष पश्यति॥
units.translation: Thus the knower, having left behind the two kinds of action, should always remember the Self; even when action is done, this person sees it only as the form of the Self.

gloss.en: as the form of one’s own Self

units.iast:
evaṃ vidvānkarmaṇi dve hitvātmānaṃ smaretsadā|
kṛte ca karmaṇi svātmarūpeṇaivaiṣa paśyati||

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 7
units.deva:
भिद्यते हृदयग्रन्थिश्च्छिद्यन्ते सर्वसंशयाः।
क्षीयन्ते चास्य कर्माणि तस्मिन्दृष्टे परावरे॥
units.translation: When the higher and lower [Brahman] is seen, the knot of the heart is broken, all doubts are cut, and this person’s karmas are exhausted.
units.iast:
bhidyate hṛdayagranthiścchidyante sarvasaṃśayāḥ|
kṣīyante cāsya karmāṇi tasmindṛṣṭe parāvare||

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 8
units.deva:
तमेव विद्वानत्येति मृत्युं पन्था न चेतरः।
ज्ञात्वा देवं पाशहानिः क्षीणैः क्लेशैर्न जन्मभाक्॥
units.translation: Knowing Him alone, one passes beyond death; there is no other path. Having known the shining one, one is freed from bonds, one’s afflictions are exhausted, and one is not subject to rebirth.
units.iast:
tameva vidvānatyeti mṛtyuṃ panthā na cetaraḥ|
jñātvā devaṃ pāśahāniḥ kṣīṇaiḥ kleśairna janmabhāk||

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 9
units.deva:
देवं मत्वा हर्षशोकौ जहात्यत्रैव धैर्यवान्।
नैनं कृताकृते पुण्यपापे तापयतः क्वचित्॥
units.translation: Having known the shining one, the steadfast person gives up joy and sorrow here itself; the merit and demerit of actions done or omitted never scorch this person.
units.iast:
devaṃ matvā harṣaśokau jahātyatraiva dhairyavān|
nainaṃ kṛtākṛte puṇyapāpe tāpayataḥ kvacit||

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 10
units.deva:
इत्यादिश्रुतयो बह्व्यः पुराणैः स्मृतिभिः सह।
ब्रह्मज्ञानेऽनर्थहानिमानन्दं चाप्यघोषयन्॥
units.translation: Thus many Śruti passages, together with the Purāṇas and Smṛtis, proclaim that knowledge of Brahman removes troubles and brings bliss.
units.iast:
ityādiśrutayo bahvyaḥ purāṇaiḥ smṛtibhiḥ saha|
brahmajñāne’narthahānimānandaṃ cāpyaghoṣayan||

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 11
units.deva:
आनन्दस्त्रिविधो ब्रह्मानन्दो विद्यासुखं तथा।
विषयानन्द इत्यादौ ब्रह्मानन्दो विविच्यते॥
units.translation: Bliss is threefold: the bliss of Brahman, the joy of knowledge, and the bliss of objects. Of these, the bliss of Brahman is examined first.
units.iast:
ānandastrividho brahmānando vidyāsukhaṃ tathā|
viṣayānanda ityādau brahmānando vivicyate||

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 12
units.deva:
भृगुः पुत्रः पितुः श्रुत्वा वरुणाद्ब्रह्मलक्षणम्।
अन्नप्राणमनोबुद्धिस्त्यक्त्वानन्दं विजज्ञीवान्॥
units.translation: Bhṛgu, having heard the definition of Brahman from his father Varuṇa, set aside food, life-breath, mind, and intellect, and came to know bliss.
units.iast:
bhṛguḥ putraḥ pituḥ śrutvā varuṇādbrahmalakṣaṇam|
annaprāṇamanobuddhistyaktvānandaṃ vijajñīvān||

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 13
units.deva:
आनन्दादेव भूतानि जायन्ते तेन जीवनम्।
तेषां लयश्च तत्रातो ब्रह्मानन्दो न संशयः॥
units.translation: Beings are born from bliss alone, live by it, and dissolve back into it; therefore it is the bliss of Brahman, without doubt.
units.iast:
ānandādeva bhūtāni jāyante tena jīvanam|
teṣāṃ layaśca tatrāto brahmānando na saṃśayaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 14
units.deva:
भूतोत्पत्तेः पुरा भूमा त्रिपुटीद्वैतवर्जनात्।
ज्ञातृज्ञानज्ञेयरूपा त्रिपुटी प्रलये हि न॥
units.translation: Before beings arise, there is the Infinite, free from the duality of the threefold division. At dissolution too, the triad of knower, knowing, and known does not exist.

gloss.en: because the duality of the triad is absent

units.iast:
bhūtotpatteḥ purā bhūmā tripuṭīdvaitavarjanāt|
jñātṛjñānajñeyarūpā tripuṭī pralaye hi na||

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 15
units.deva:
विज्ञानमय उत्पन्नो ज्ञाता ज्ञानं मनोमयः।
ज्ञेयाः शब्दादयो नैतत्त्रयमुत्पत्तितः पुरा॥
units.translation: When they arise, the intellect-sheath is the knower, the mind-sheath is the knowing, and sound and the like are the objects known; this triad did not exist before creation.
units.iast:
vijñānamaya utpanno jñātā jñānaṃ manomayaḥ|
jñeyāḥ śabdādayo naitattrayamutpattitaḥ purā||

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 16
units.deva:
त्रयाभावे तु निर्द्वैतः पूर्ण एवानुभूयते।
समाधिसुप्तिमूर्च्छासु पूर्णः सृष्टेः पुरा तथा॥
units.translation: When the triad is absent, the complete nondual Self is indeed experienced. It is complete in samādhi, sleep, and swoon, and likewise before creation.
units.iast:
trayābhāve tu nirdvaitaḥ pūrṇa evānubhūyate|
samādhisuptimūrcchāsu pūrṇaḥ sṛṣṭeḥ purā tathā||

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 17
units.deva:
यो भूमा तत्सुखं नाल्पे सुखं त्रेधा विभेदिनि।
सनत्कुमारः प्राहैवं नारदायातिशोकिने॥
units.translation: What is infinite is happiness; there is no happiness in the finite, divided into three. Sanatkumāra spoke thus to the deeply grieving Nārada.
units.iast:
yo bhūmā tatsukhaṃ nālpe sukhaṃ tredhā vibhedini|
sanatkumāraḥ prāhaivaṃ nāradāyātiśokine||

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 18
units.deva:
सपुराणान्पञ्च वेदान् शास्त्राणि विविधानि च।
ज्ञात्वाप्यनात्मवित्त्वेन नारदोऽतिशुशोच ह॥
units.translation: Though Nārada had learned the five Vedas along with the Purāṇas and many kinds of treatises, he grieved greatly because he did not know the Self.

gloss.en: because he did not know the Self

units.iast:
sapurāṇānpañca vedān śāstrāṇi vividhāni ca|
jñātvāpyanātmavittvena nārado’tiśuśoca ha||

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 19
units.deva:
वेदाभ्यासात्पुरा तापत्रयमात्रेण शोकिता।
पश्चात्त्वभ्यासविस्मारभङ्गगर्वैश्च शोकिता॥
units.translation: Before Vedic study, his sorrow came only from the threefold suffering; afterward, the strain of study, forgetfulness, lapses, and pride also brought sorrow.
units.iast:
vedābhyāsātpurā tāpatrayamātreṇa śokitā|
paścāttvabhyāsavismārabhaṅgagarvaiśca śokitā||

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 20
units.deva:
सोऽहं विद्वान्प्रशोचामि शोकपारं नयस्व माम्।
इत्युक्तः सुखमेवास्य पारमित्यभ्यधादृषिः॥
units.translation: “Though learned, I grieve; lead me to the far shore of sorrow,” he said. The sage replied, “Happiness alone is the far shore of this [sorrow].”
units.iast:
so’haṃ vidvānpraśocāmi śokapāraṃ nayasva mām|
ityuktaḥ sukhamevāsya pāramityabhyadhādṛṣiḥ||

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 21
units.deva:
सुखं वैषयिकं शोकसहस्रेणावृतत्वतः।
दुःखमेवेति मत्वाह नाल्पेऽस्ति सुखमित्यसौ॥
units.translation: Because pleasure from objects is covered by a thousand sorrows, this person considers it nothing but suffering and says, “There is no happiness in the finite.”
units.iast:
sukhaṃ vaiṣayikaṃ śokasahasreṇāvṛtatvataḥ|
duḥkhameveti matvāha nālpe’sti sukhamityasau||

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 22
units.deva:
ननु द्वैते सुखं माभूदद्वैतेऽप्यस्ति नो सुखम्।
अस्ति चेदुपलभ्येत तथा च त्रिपुटी भवेत्॥
units.translation: “Let there be no happiness in duality; there is no happiness in nonduality either. If happiness exists, it would be experienced, and then a triad would arise.”
units.iast:
nanu dvaite sukhaṃ mābhūdadvaite’pyasti no sukham|
asti cedupalabhyeta tathā ca tripuṭī bhavet||

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 23
