units.deva:
मास्त्वद्वैते सुखं किन्तु सुखमद्वैतमेव हि।
किं मानमिति चेन्नास्ति मानाकाङ्क्षा स्वयं प्रभे॥
units.translation: “Let there be no happiness in nonduality; nonduality itself is happiness indeed. If you ask, ‘What is the evidence?’, no evidence is needed for what is self-luminous.”
units.iast:
māstvadvaite sukhaṃ kintu sukhamadvaitameva hi|
kiṃ mānamiti cennāsti mānākāṅkṣā svayaṃ prabhe||

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 24
units.deva:
स्वप्रभत्वे भवद्वाक्यं मानं यस्माद्भवानिदम्।
अद्वैतमभ्युपेत्यास्मिन्सुखं नास्तीति भाषते॥
units.translation: Your own statement is evidence that nonduality is self-luminous: you accept that this nonduality exists, then say that happiness is not in it.
units.iast:
svaprabhatve bhavadvākyaṃ mānaṃ yasmādbhavānidam|
advaitamabhyupetyāsminsukhaṃ nāstīti bhāṣate||

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 25
units.deva:
नाभ्युपैम्यहमद्वैतं त्वद्वचोऽनूद्य दूषणम्।
वच्मीति चेत्तदा ब्रूहि किमासीद्द्वैततः पुरा॥
units.translation: “I do not accept nonduality; I am only repeating your words in order to refute them,” if you say this, then tell us what existed before duality.
units.iast:
nābhyupaimyahamadvaitaṃ tvadvaco’nūdya dūṣaṇam|
vacmīti cettadā brūhi kimāsīddvaitataḥ purā||

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 26
units.deva:
किमद्वैतमुत द्वैतमन्यो वा कोटिरन्तिमः।
अप्रसिद्धो न द्वितीयोऽनुत्पत्तेः शिष्यतेऽग्रिमः॥
units.translation: Was it nonduality, duality, or a third alternative? The last is unestablished; duality is ruled out because it had not arisen; therefore the first remains.
units.iast:
kimadvaitamuta dvaitamanyo vā koṭirantimaḥ|
aprasiddho na dvitīyo’nutpatteḥ śiṣyate’grimaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 27
units.deva:
अद्वैतसिद्धिर्युक्त्यैव नानुभूत्येति चेद्वद।
निर्दृष्टान्ता सदृष्टान्ता वा कोट्यन्तरमत्र नो॥
units.translation: If you say nonduality is established by reasoning alone, not by experience, tell me: does your position have an example or not? There is no third alternative.
units.iast:
advaitasiddhiryuktyaiva nānubhūtyeti cedvada|
nirdṛṣṭāntā sadṛṣṭāntā vā koṭyantaramatra no||

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 28
units.deva:
नानुभूतिर्न दृष्टान्त इति युक्तिस्तु शोभते।
सदृष्टान्तत्वपक्षे तु दृष्टान्तं वद मे मतम्॥
units.translation: “There is no experience, and no example”—what fine reasoning! But if you take the position that there is an example, tell me one that I would accept.

gloss.en: if taking the position that it has an example

units.iast:
nānubhūtirna dṛṣṭānta iti yuktistu śobhate|
sadṛṣṭāntatvapakṣe tu dṛṣṭāntaṃ vada me matam||

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 29
units.deva:
अद्वैतः प्रलयो द्वैतानुपलम्भेन सुप्तिवत्।
इति चेत्सुप्तिरद्वैतेत्यत्र दृष्टान्तमीरय॥
units.translation: “Dissolution is nondual because duality is not perceived, as in deep sleep,” if you say this, give an example for the claim that deep sleep is nondual.
units.iast:
advaitaḥ pralayo dvaitānupalambhena suptivat|
iti cetsuptiradvaitetyatra dṛṣṭāntamīraya||

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 30
units.deva:
दृष्टान्तः परसुप्तिश्चेदहो ते कौशलं महत्।
यः स्वसुप्तिं न वेत्त्यस्य परसुप्तौ तु का कथा॥
units.translation: “If another person’s sleep is your example, how clever! If one does not know one’s own sleep, what can one say about another’s?”
units.iast:
dṛṣṭāntaḥ parasuptiścedaho te kauśalaṃ mahat|
yaḥ svasuptiṃ na vettyasya parasuptau tu kā kathā||

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 31
units.deva:
निश्चेष्टत्वात्परः सुप्तो यथाहमिति चेत्तदा।
उदाहर्तुः सुषुप्तेस्ते स्वप्रभत्वं बलाद्भवेत्॥
units.translation: If you say, “Another person is asleep because he is inactive, just as I am [in sleep],” then your own deep sleep must serve as the example for self-luminosity.

gloss.en: of the one giving the example

units.iast:
niśceṣṭatvātparaḥ supto yathāhamiti cettadā|
udāhartuḥ suṣupteste svaprabhatvaṃ balādbhavet||

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 32
units.deva:
नेन्द्रियाणि न दृष्टान्तस्तथाप्यङ्गीकरोषि ताम्।
इदमेव स्वप्रभत्वं यद्भानं साधनैर्विना॥
units.translation: There are no sense organs and no [other] example, yet you accept that [state]. This very awareness shining without instruments is self-luminosity.
units.iast:
nendriyāṇi na dṛṣṭāntastathāpyaṅgīkaroṣi tām|
idameva svaprabhatvaṃ yadbhānaṃ sādhanairvinā||

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 33
units.deva:
स्तामद्वैतस्वप्रभत्वे वद सुप्तौ सुखं कथम्।
शृणु दुःखं तदा नास्ति ततस्ते शिष्यते सुखम्॥
units.translation: “Granted that nonduality is self-luminous, tell me: how is there happiness in sleep?” Listen: sorrow is absent then; therefore happiness alone remains for you.
units.iast:
stāmadvaitasvaprabhatve vada suptau sukhaṃ katham|
śṛṇu duḥkhaṃ tadā nāsti tataste śiṣyate sukham||

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 34
units.deva:
अन्धः सन्नप्यनन्धः स्याद्विद्धोऽविद्धोऽथ रोग्यपि।
अरोगीति श्रुतिः प्राह तच्च सर्वे जना विदुः॥
units.translation: Scripture says, “Though blind, one is not blind; though wounded, one is unwounded; though ill, one is not ill.” Everyone knows this.
units.iast:
andhaḥ sannapyanandhaḥ syādviddho’viddho’tha rogyapi|
arogīti śrutiḥ prāha tacca sarve janā viduḥ||

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 35
units.deva:
न दुःखाभावमात्रेण सुखं लोष्टशिलादिषु।
द्वयाभावस्य दृष्टत्वादिति चेद्विषमं वचः॥
units.translation: If you argue, “Mere absence of sorrow does not mean happiness, since neither is experienced in clods, stones, and the like,” that is a faulty argument.
units.iast:
na duḥkhābhāvamātreṇa sukhaṃ loṣṭaśilādiṣu|
dvayābhāvasya dṛṣṭatvāditi cedviṣamaṃ vacaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 36
units.deva:
मुखदैन्यप्रकाशाभ्यां परदुःखसुखोहनम्।
दैन्याद्यभावतो लोष्टे दुःखाद्यूहो न सम्भवेत्॥
units.translation: One infers another person’s sorrow or joy from the face’s dejected or bright appearance; because such signs are absent in a clod of earth, one cannot infer sorrow and the like there.

gloss.en: from brightness; by the two signs

units.iast:
mukhadainyaprakāśābhyāṃ paraduḥkhasukhohanam|
dainyādyabhāvato loṣṭe duḥkhādyūho na sambhavet||

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 37
units.deva:
स्वकीयसुखदुःखे तु नोहनीये ततस्तयोः।
भावो वेद्योऽनुभूत्यैव तदभावोऽपि नान्यतः॥
units.translation: One’s own happiness and sorrow are not inferred; their presence is known by direct experience alone, and their absence too is known only by experience.
units.iast:
svakīyasukhaduḥkhe tu nohanīye tatastayoḥ|
bhāvo vedyo’nubhūtyaiva tadabhāvo’pi nānyataḥ||

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 38
units.deva:
तथा सति सुषुप्तौ च दुःखाभावोऽनुभूतितः।
विरोधिदुःखराहित्यात्सुखं निर्विघ्नमिष्यताम्॥
units.translation: In the same way, the absence of sorrow in deep sleep is known by experience; because opposing sorrow is absent, happiness should be accepted as unobstructed.
units.iast:
tathā sati suṣuptau ca duḥkhābhāvo’nubhūtitaḥ|
virodhiduḥkharāhityātsukhaṃ nirvighnamiṣyatām||

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 39
units.deva:
महत्तरप्रयासेन मृदुशय्यादिसाधनम्।
कुतः सम्पाद्यते सुप्तौ सुखं चेत्तत्र नो भवेत्॥
units.translation: If there is no happiness in sleep, why are means such as a soft bed obtained with such great effort?

gloss.en: a soft bed and the like

units.iast:
mahattaraprayāsena mṛduśayyādisādhanam|
kutaḥ sampādyate suptau sukhaṃ cettatra no bhavet||

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 40
units.deva:
दुःखनाशार्थमेवैतदिति चेद्रोगिणस्तथा।
भवत्वरोगिणस्ते तत्सुखायैवेति निश्चिनु॥
units.translation: If you say this is only to remove pain, let that be so for the sick; but understand that for the healthy it is indeed for happiness.
units.iast:
duḥkhanāśārthamevaitaditi cedrogiṇastathā|
bhavatvarogiṇaste tatsukhāyaiveti niścinu||

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 41
units.deva:
तर्हि साधनजन्यत्वात्सुखं वैषयिकं भवेत्।
भवत्येवात्र निद्रायाः पूर्वं शय्यासनादिजम्॥
units.translation: (Objection) Then, because happiness is produced by means, it would be object-related. (Reply) The happiness before sleep, born from a bed, a seat, and the like, is indeed so.

gloss.en: born from a bed, a seat, and the like

units.iast:
tarhi sādhanajanyatvātsukhaṃ vaiṣayikaṃ bhavet|
bhavatyevātra nidrāyāḥ pūrvaṃ śayyāsanādijam||

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 42
units.deva:
निद्रायां तु सुखं यत्तज्जन्यते केन हेतुना।
सुखाभिमुखधीरादौ पश्चान्मज्जेत्परे सुखे॥
units.translation: But what cause produces the happiness that is in sleep? At first the mind is directed toward happiness; afterwards it sinks into supreme happiness.
units.iast:
nidrāyāṃ tu sukhaṃ yattajjanyate kena hetunā|
sukhābhimukhadhīrādau paścānmajjetpare sukhe||

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 43
units.deva:
जाग्रद्व्यापृतिभिः श्रान्तो विश्रम्याथ विरोधिनि।
अपनीते स्वस्थचितोऽनुभवेद्विषये सुखम्॥
units.translation: Wearied by the activities of waking, after resting and when the opposing discomfort has been removed, one with a settled mind experiences happiness in an object.

gloss.en: when the opposing obstacle is removed

units.iast:
jāgradvyāpṛtibhiḥ śrānto viśramyātha virodhini|
apanīte svasthacito’nubhavedviṣaye sukham||

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 44
units.deva:
आत्माभिमुखधीवृत्तौ स्वानन्दः प्रतिबिम्बति।
अनुभूयैनमत्रापि त्रिपुट्या श्रान्तिमाप्नुयात्॥
units.translation: When the mind’s thought is directed toward the Self, one’s own bliss is reflected. Even experiencing it here, one may grow weary through the triad of knower, knowing, and known.

gloss.en: in a mental thought turned toward the Self

units.iast:
ātmābhimukhadhīvṛttau svānandaḥ pratibimbati|
anubhūyainamatrāpi tripuṭyā śrāntimāpnuyāt||

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 45
units.deva:
तत्श्रमस्यापनुत्यर्थं जीवो धावेत्परात्मनि।
तेनैक्यं प्राप्य तत्रत्यो ब्रह्मानन्दः स्वयं भवेत्॥
units.translation: To remove that weariness, the jīva would hasten to the supreme Self. Having attained oneness with it, the jīva itself would become the Brahman-bliss present there.
units.iast:
tatśramasyāpanutyarthaṃ jīvo dhāvetparātmani|
tenaikyaṃ prāpya tatratyo brahmānandaḥ svayaṃ bhavet||

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 46
units.deva:
दृष्टान्ताः शकुनिः श्येनः कुमारश्च महानृपः।
महाब्राह्मण इत्येते सुप्त्यानन्दे श्रुतीरिताः॥
units.translation: The examples cited by the Śruti for the bliss of sleep are a bird, a falcon, a child, a great king, and a great Brahmin.

gloss.en: in regard to the bliss of sleep

units.iast:
dṛṣṭāntāḥ śakuniḥ śyenaḥ kumāraśca mahānṛpaḥ|
mahābrāhmaṇa ityete suptyānande śrutīritāḥ||

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 47
units.deva:
शकुनिः सूत्रबद्धः सन्दिक्षु व्यापृत्य विश्रमम्।
अलब्ध्वा बन्धनस्थानं हस्तस्तम्भाद्युपाश्रयेत्॥
units.translation: A bird tied with a cord, having flown about in all directions without finding rest, would resort to its tethering place, such as a hand or a post.

gloss.en: the place where it is tied
would resort to; would take shelter at

units.iast:
śakuniḥ sūtrabaddhaḥ sandikṣu vyāpṛtya viśramam|
alabdhvā bandhanasthānaṃ hastastambhādyupāśrayet||

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 48
units.deva:
जीवोपाधिर्मनस्तद्वद्धर्माधर्मफलाप्तये।
स्वप्ने जाग्रति च भ्रान्त्वा क्षीणे कर्मणि लीयते॥
units.translation: The mind, the jīva’s limiting adjunct, likewise wanders in dream and waking to obtain the fruits of merit and demerit. When karma is exhausted, it dissolves.

gloss.en: to obtain the fruits of merit and demerit

units.iast:
jīvopādhirmanastadvaddharmādharmaphalāptaye|
svapne jāgrati ca bhrāntvā kṣīṇe karmaṇi līyate||

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 49
units.deva:
श्येनो वेगेन नीडैकलम्पटः शयितुं व्रजेत्।
जीवः सुप्त्यै तथा धावेद्ब्रह्मानन्दैकलम्पटः॥
units.translation: The falcon, intent only on its nest, would swiftly go to lie down. Likewise the jīva, intent solely on Brahman-bliss, hastens to sleep.

gloss.en: eagerly attached only to its nest

units.iast:
śyeno vegena nīḍaikalampaṭaḥ śayituṃ vrajet|
jīvaḥ suptyai tathā dhāvedbrahmānandaikalampaṭaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 50
units.deva:
अतिबालस्तनं पीत्वा मृदुशय्यागतो हसन्।
रागद्वेषाद्यनुत्पत्तेरानन्दैकस्वभावभाक्॥
units.translation: A very young child, having suckled at the breast, reaches a soft bed smiling; because attachment, aversion, and the like have not arisen, it partakes solely of bliss as its nature.

gloss.en: having gone to a soft bed
partaking solely of bliss as its nature

units.iast:
atibālastanaṃ pītvā mṛduśayyāgato hasan|
rāgadveṣādyanutpatterānandaikasvabhāvabhāk||

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 51
units.deva:
महाराजः सार्वभौमः सुतृप्तः सर्वभोगतः।
मानुषानन्दसीमानं प्राप्यानन्दैकमूर्तिभाक्॥
units.translation: A great emperor, fully satisfied by all enjoyments, having reached the limit of human happiness, becomes the very embodiment of bliss.

gloss.en: becoming the very embodiment of bliss

units.iast:
mahārājaḥ sārvabhaumaḥ sutṛptaḥ sarvabhogataḥ|
mānuṣānandasīmānaṃ prāpyānandaikamūrtibhāk||

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 52
units.deva:
महाविप्रो ब्रह्मवेदी कृतकृत्यत्वलक्षणाम्।
विद्यानन्दस्य परमां काष्ठां प्राप्यावतिष्ठते॥
units.translation: A great Brahmin, a knower of Brahman, having reached the highest limit of knowledge-bliss, marked by having done all that needs to be done, remains established there.

gloss.en: marked by having done all that needs to be done

units.iast:
mahāvipro brahmavedī kṛtakṛtyatvalakṣaṇām|
vidyānandasya paramāṃ kāṣṭhāṃ prāpyāvatiṣṭhate||

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 53
units.deva:
मुग्धबुद्धातिबुद्धानां लोके सिद्धा सुखात्मता।
उदाहृतानामन्ये तु दुःखिनो न सुखात्मकाः॥
units.translation: In the world, the innocent, the discerning, and the deeply wise are recognized as happy by nature; the others among those cited are sorrowful, not happy by nature.
units.iast:
mugdhabuddhātibuddhānāṃ loke siddhā sukhātmatā|
udāhṛtānāmanye tu duḥkhino na sukhātmakāḥ||

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 54
units.deva:
कुमारादिवदेवायं ब्रह्मानन्दैकतत्परः।
स्त्रीपरिष्वक्तवद्वेद न बाह्यं नापि चान्तरम्॥
units.translation: Like the child and the other examples, this one is solely intent on Brahman-bliss. Like a person embraced by a woman, he knows neither the outer nor the inner.

gloss.en: like the child and the others
like one embraced by a woman

units.iast:
kumārādivadevāyaṃ brahmānandaikatatparaḥ|
strīpariṣvaktavadveda na bāhyaṃ nāpi cāntaram||

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 55
units.deva:
बाह्यं रथ्यादिकं वृत्तं गृहकृत्यं यथान्तरम्।
तथा जागरणं बाह्यं नाडीस्थः स्वप्न आन्तरः॥
units.translation: Just as events in the street and the like are external, while activity in the house is internal, so waking is external, while dream, situated in the nāḍīs (subtle channels), is internal.
units.iast:
bāhyaṃ rathyādikaṃ vṛttaṃ gṛhakṛtyaṃ yathāntaram|
tathā jāgaraṇaṃ bāhyaṃ nāḍīsthaḥ svapna āntaraḥ||

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 56
units.deva:
पितापि सुप्तावपितेत्यादौ जीवत्ववारणात्।
सुप्तौ ब्रह्मैव नो जीव संसारित्वासमीक्षणात्॥
units.translation: Because statements such as “Even a father is not a father in sleep” exclude individual selfhood, in sleep Brahman alone is present, not the jīva, since no state of transmigration is observed.

gloss.en: in statements beginning with this and the like
because transmigratory existence is not observed

units.iast:
pitāpi suptāvapitetyādau jīvatvavāraṇāt|
suptau brahmaiva no jīva saṃsāritvāsamīkṣaṇāt||

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 57
units.deva:
पितृत्वाद्यभिमानो यः सुखदुःखाकरः स हि।
तस्मिन्नपगते तीर्णः सर्वान् शोकान्भवत्ययम्॥
units.translation: Identification as a father and the like is indeed a source of happiness and sorrow. When it falls away, this person has crossed beyond every sorrow.

gloss.en: identification as a father and the like
a source of happiness and sorrow

units.iast:
pitṛtvādyabhimāno yaḥ sukhaduḥkhākaraḥ sa hi|
tasminnapagate tīrṇaḥ sarvān śokānbhavatyayam||

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 58
units.deva:
सुषुप्तिकाले सकले विलीने तमसावृतः।
सुखरूपमुपैतीति ब्रूते ह्याथर्वणी श्रुतिः॥
units.translation: When everything has dissolved during deep sleep, one covered by darkness reaches the form of happiness: so says the Atharvan Śruti.
units.iast:
suṣuptikāle sakale vilīne tamasāvṛtaḥ|
sukharūpamupaitīti brūte hyātharvaṇī śrutiḥ||

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 59
units.deva:
सुखमस्वाप्समत्राहं नैव किंचिदवेदिषम्।
इति द्वे तु सुखाज्ञाने परामृशति चोत्तितः॥
units.translation: On waking, one recalls two things—happiness and ignorance—and says, “I slept happily; I knew nothing at all.”
units.iast:
sukhamasvāpsamatrāhaṃ naiva kiṃcidavediṣam|
iti dve tu sukhājñāne parāmṛśati cottitaḥ||

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 60
units.deva:
परामर्शोऽनुभूतेऽस्तीत्यासीदनुभवस्तदा।
चिदात्मत्वत्स्वतो भाति सुखमज्ञानधीस्ततः॥
units.translation: Recollection implies that there was experience then. Because happiness is of the nature of consciousness, it shines by itself; for that reason, cognition of ignorance is also possible.

gloss.en: of experience; of what was experienced
because of being of the nature of consciousness

units.iast:
parāmarśo’nubhūte’stītyāsīdanubhavastadā|
cidātmatvatsvato bhāti sukhamajñānadhīstataḥ||

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 61
units.deva:
ब्रह्मविज्ञानमानन्दमिति वाजसनेयिनः।
पठन्त्यतः स्वप्रकाशं सुखं ब्रह्मैव नेतरत्॥
units.translation: The Vāja-saneyins say: ‘Brahman is of the nature of consciousness and bliss’. Therefore the self-luminous bliss is Brahman itself and nothing else.

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 62
units.deva:
यदज्ञानं तत्र लीनौ तौ विज्ञानमनोमयौ।
तयोर्हि विलयावस्था निद्राज्ञानं च सैव हि॥
units.translation: The mind and the intellect sheaths are latent in the state called ignorance. Deep sleep is the condition in which these sheaths are latent and it is therefore a state of ignorance.

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 63
units.deva:
विलीनघृतवत्पश्चात्स्याद्विज्ञानमयो घनः।
विलीनावस्थ आनन्दमयशब्देन कथ्यते॥
units.translation: Just as melted butter again becomes solid, the two sheaths in the states following deep sleep again become manifest. The state in which the mind and intellect are latent is called the bliss-sheath.

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 64
units.deva:
सुप्तिपूर्वक्षणे बुद्धिवृत्तिर्या सुखबिम्बिता।
सैव तद्बिम्बसहिता लीनानन्दमयस्ततः॥
units.translation: The modifications (Vṛtti) of the intellect in which, just before sleep, bliss is reflected becomes latent in the state of deep sleep along with the reflected bliss and is known as the bliss-sheath.

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 65
units.deva:
अन्तर्मुखोऽयमानन्दमयो ब्रह्मसुखं तदा।
भुङ्क्ते चिद्बिम्बयुक्ताभिरज्ञानोत्पन्नवृत्तिभिः॥
units.translation: This Vṛtti thus turned within, which is termed the bliss-sheath, enjoys the bliss reflected on it in association with the modifications of ignorance, catching the reflection of consciousness.

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 66
units.deva:
अज्ञानवृत्तयः सूक्ष्मा विस्पष्टा बुद्धिवृत्तयः।
इति वेदान्तसिद्धान्तपारगाः प्रवदन्ति हि॥
units.translation: The adepts in Vedānta say that the modifications of ignorance are subtle (sūkṣmā), whereas those of the intellect are gross (vispaṣṭā, manifest).

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 67
units.deva:
माण्डुक्यतापनीयादिश्रुतिष्वेतदतिस्फुटम्।
आनन्दमयभोक्तृत्वं ब्रह्मानन्दे च भोग्यता॥
units.translation: This is fully explained in the Māṇḍukya and Tāpanīya Upaniṣads. It is the sheath of bliss which is the enjoyer and it is the bliss of Brahman which is enjoyed.

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 68
units.deva:
एकीभूतः सुषुप्तस्थः प्रज्ञानघनतां गतः।
आनन्दमय आनन्दभुक्चेतोमयवृत्तिभिः॥
units.translation: This profusion of bliss (Ānandamayaḥ), having become concentrated into one mass of consciousness in the deep sleep, enjoys the (reflected) bliss of Brahman with the help of modifications (Vṛttis) reflecting a superabundance of consciousness.

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 69
units.deva:
विज्ञानमयमुख्यैर्यो रूपैर्युक्तः पुराधुना।
स लयेनैकतां प्राप्तो बहुतण्डुलपिष्टवत्॥
units.translation: The self (Cid-ābhāsa) in the waking and dream states, is connected or associated with various sheaths such as Vijñānamaya and appears as many (i.e., plays various roles). In the deep sleep state, however, they get merged and become latent like a dough of many (powdered) wheat-grains.

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 70
units.deva:
प्रज्ञानानि पुरा बुद्धिवृत्तयोऽथ घनोऽभवत्।
घनत्वं हिमबिन्दूनामुदग्देशे यथा तथा॥
units.translation: The modifications of the intellect, which are instruments of cognition, unite and become one in the state of sleep, just as drops of cold water in the Himalayan regions solidify into a mass of ice.

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 71
units.deva:
तद्घनत्वं साक्षिभावं दुःखाभावं प्रचक्षते।
लौकिकास्तार्किका यावद्दुःखवृत्तिविलोपनात्॥
units.translation: This witness state of compact consciousness, ordinary people and the logicians say, is characterised by the absence of suffering, because in that state the mental modifications of pain and misery subside.

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 72
units.deva:
अज्ञानबिम्बिता चित्स्यान्मुखमानन्दभोजने।
भुक्तं ब्रह्मसुखं त्यक्त्वा बहिर्यात्यथ कर्मणा॥
units.translation: In the enjoyment of the bliss of Brahman in deep sleep, the consciousness reflected in ignorance is the means. Prompted by its Karma, good or bad, the Jīva gives up the enjoyment of bliss and goes out to the waking state.

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 73
units.deva:
कर्म जन्मान्तरेऽभूद्यत्तद्योगाद्बुद्ध्यते पुनः।
इति कैवल्यशाखायां कर्मजो बोध ईरितः॥
units.translation: The Kaivalya Upaniṣad says that a Jīva passes from the sleeping to the waking state owing to the effects of the actions of former births. Reawakening thus is a result of actions.

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 74
units.deva:
कंचित्कालं प्रबुद्धस्य ब्रह्मानन्दस्य वासना।
अनुगच्छेद्यतस्तूष्णीमास्ते निर्विषयः सुखी॥
units.translation: For a short time after the waking up the impression of the bliss of Brahman enjoyed during sleep continues. For he remains for some time calm and happy, without taking any interest in the enjoyment of external objects.

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 75
units.deva:
कर्मभिः प्रेरितः पश्चान्नाना दुःखानि भावयन्।
शनैर्विस्मरति ब्रह्मानन्दमेषोऽखिलो जनः॥
units.translation: Then, impelled by his past actions ready to bear fruits, he begins to think of duties and their implementation entailing sufferings of many kinds and gradually forgets the bliss of Brahman experienced (a few minutes before).

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 76
units.deva:
प्रागूर्ध्वमपि निद्रायाः पक्षपातो दिने दिने।
ब्रह्मानन्दे नृणां तेन प्राज्ञोऽस्मिन्विवदेत कः॥
units.translation: Experiencing the bliss of Brahman before and after sleep day after day man develops a predilection for it. How can a man, therefore, doubt it (i.e., the existence of the bliss of Brahman)?

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 77
units.deva:
ननु तूष्णीं स्थितौ ब्रह्मानन्दश्चेद्भाति लौकिकाः।
अलसाश्चरितार्थाः स्युः शास्त्रेण गुरुणात्र किम्॥
units.translation: (Objection): Well, if a mere state of quietude were enjoyment of the bliss of Brahman then the lazy and the worldly would achieve the end of their life. What then is the use of the teacher and the scriptures?

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 78
units.deva:
बाढं ब्रह्मेति विद्युश्चेत्कृतार्थास्तावतैव ते।
गुरुशास्त्रे विनात्यन्तं गम्भीरं ब्रह्म वेत्ति कः॥
units.translation: (Reply): Your contention would be correct, if he realised that the bliss that he experienced was the bliss of Brahman. But who can know Brahman that is so immensely profound without the help of the teacher and the scripture?

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 79
units.deva:
जानाम्यहं त्वदुक्त्याद्य कुतो मे न कृतार्थता।
शृण्वत्र त्वादृशं वृत्तं प्राज्ञं मन्यस्य कस्यचित्॥
units.translation: (Objection): I know what Brahman is from what you yourself have said. Why then am I without the bliss of realisation? (Reply): Listen to the story of a man who like yourself imagined that he was wise.

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 80
units.deva:
चतुर्वेदविदे देयमिति शृण्वन्नवोचत।
वेदाश्चत्वार इत्येवं वेद्मि मे दीयतां धनम्॥
units.translation: This man, hearing that a large reward was offered to anyone who knew the four Vedas, said, ‘I know from you that there are four Vedas. So give me the reward’.

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 81
units.deva:
साङ्ख्यमेवैष जानाति न तु वेदानशेषतः।
यदि तर्हि तमप्येवं नाशेषं ब्रह्म वेत्सि हि॥
units.translation: (Objection): He knew the number, not the text, of the Vedas fully. (Reply): You too have not known Brahman fully.

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 82
units.deva:
अखण्डैकरसानन्दे मायातत्कार्यवर्जिते।
अशेषत्वसशेषत्ववार्तावसर एव कः॥
units.translation: (Objection): Brahman is by nature indivisible and is bliss absolute, untouched by Māyā and its effects. How can you speak of the knowledge of Brahman as complete or incomplete?

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 83
units.deva:
शब्दानेव पठस्याहो तेषामर्थं च पश्यसि।
शब्दपाठेऽर्थबोधस्ते सम्पाद्यत्वेन शिष्यते॥
units.translation: (Reply): Do you simply say the word ‘Brahman’ or do you see its meaning? If you know only the word, it remains for you to acquire knowledge of its meaning.

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 84
units.deva:
अर्थे व्याकरणाद्बुद्धे साक्षात्कारोऽवशिष्यते।
स्यात्कृतार्थत्वधीर्यावत्तावद्गुरुमुपास्व भोः॥
units.translation: Even if with the help of grammar and so forth you learn its meaning, still realisation remains. Serve your teacher until you have realised Brahman and known that there is nothing further to be known.

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 85
units.deva:
आस्तामेतद्यत्र यत्र सुखं स्याद्विषयैर्विना।
तत्र सर्वत्र विद्ध्येतां ब्रह्मानन्दस्य वासनाम्॥
units.translation: Leave the vain argument alone and know that whenever happiness is felt in the absence of objects, that happiness is an impression of the bliss of Brahman.

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 86
units.deva:
विषयेष्वपि लब्धेषु तदिच्छोपरमे सति।
अन्तर्मुखमनोवृत्तावानन्दः प्रतिबिम्बति॥
units.translation: Even when on the acquisition of the desired external objects the desire becomes quiescent and the Vṛtti is directed inward, it reflects the bliss of Brahman. (This is what is known as ‘reflected’ bliss or Viṣayānanda or bliss derived from the enjoyment of external things.)

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 87
units.deva:
ब्रह्मानन्दो वासना च प्रतिबिम्ब इति त्रयम्।
अन्तरेण जगत्यस्मिन्नानन्दो नास्ति कश्चन॥
units.translation: There are thus only three kinds of bliss experienced in the world: (1) Brahmānanda, the bliss of Brahman; (2) Vāsanānanda, the bliss arising in the quiescent mind out of the impressions of Brahmānanda and (3) Viṣayānanda, the bliss resulting from the fulfilment of the desire to be in contact with external objects.

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 88
units.deva:
तथा च विषयानन्दो वासनानन्द इत्यमू।
आनन्दौ जनयन्नास्ते ब्रह्मानन्दः स्वयंप्रभः॥
units.translation: Of these, the self-revealing bliss of Brahman gives rise to the other two kinds of bliss, the Vāsanānanda and the Viṣayānanda.

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 89
units.deva:
श्रुतियुक्त्यनुभूतिभ्यः स्वप्रकाशचिदात्मके।
ब्रह्मानन्दे सुप्तिकाले सिद्धे सत्यन्यदा शृणु॥
units.translation: The fact that the bliss of Brahman is self-revealing in deep sleep is established by the authority of the scriptures, by reasoning and by one’s experience. Now hear about its experience at other times.

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 90
units.deva:
य आनन्दमयः सुप्तौ स विज्ञानमयात्मताम्।
गत्वा स्वप्नं प्रबोधं वा प्राप्नोति स्थानभेदतः॥
units.translation: The Jīva which is called Ānandamaya, enjoying bliss of Brahman during sleep gets identified with the intellect-sheath during the dreaming and waking states, as he changes his seat from one state to another.

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 91
units.deva:
नेत्रे जागरणं कण्ठे स्वप्नः सुप्तिर्हृदम्बुजे।
आपादमस्तकं देहं व्याप्य जागर्ति चेतनः॥
units.translation: The Śruti says that in the waking state the Jīva abides in the eye i.e., the gross body; in the dreaming state in the throat and in deep sleep in the lotus of the heart. In the waking state the Jīva pervades the whole gross body from head to foot.

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 92
units.deva:
देहतादात्म्यमापन्नस्तप्तायः पिण्डवत्ततः।
अहं मनुष्य इत्येवं निश्चित्यैवावतिष्ठते॥
units.translation: In the waking state the Jīva gets identified with the body, as fire with a red-hot ball of iron. As a result of this he comes to feel with certainty: ‘I am a man’.

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 93
units.deva:
उदासीनः सुखी दुःखीत्यवस्थात्रयमेत्यसौ।
सुखदुःखे कर्मकार्ये त्वौदासीन्यं स्वभावतः॥
units.translation: The Jīva experiences the three states of detachment, joy and suffering. Joy and suffering are the results of actions; detachment comes naturally.

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 94
units.deva:
बाह्यभोगान्मनोराज्यात्सुखदुःखे द्विधा मते।
सुखदुःखान्तरालेषु भवेत्तूष्णीमवस्थितिः॥
units.translation: Pain and pleasure are of two sorts as the experience is limited within the mind or is external to it also. The state of detachment appears in the intervals between pain and pleasure.

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 95
units.deva:
न कापि चिन्ता मेऽस्त्यद्य सुखमास इति ब्रुवन्।
औदासीन्ये निजानन्दभानं वक्त्यखिलः जनः॥
units.translation: ‘Now I have no worries, I am happy’, thus do people describe the natural bliss of the Self in the state of detachment.

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 96
units.deva:
अहमस्मीत्यहङ्कारसामान्येनावृतत्वतः।
निजानन्दो न मुख्योऽयं किन्त्वसौ तस्य वासना॥
units.translation: But in this state the natural bliss of the Self is not primary for it is obscured by the idea of egoity and the bliss so experienced is not the bliss of Brahman but only an impression of it.

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 97
units.deva:
नीरपूरितभाण्डस्य बाह्ये शैत्यं न तज्जलम्।
किन्तु नीरगुणस्तेन नीरसत्तानुमीयते॥
units.translation: The outside of a pot full of water feels cold. Actually there is no water outside but coldness only. It is from this property of water that the presence of water inside is inferred.

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 98
units.deva:
यावद्यावदहङ्कारो विस्मृतोऽभ्यासयोगतः।
तावत्तावत्सूक्ष्मदृष्टेर्निजानन्दोऽनुमीयते॥
units.translation: Similarly, as one forgets one’s egoity by continued practice, one can comprehend through intuitive perception one’s natural state of bliss.

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 99
units.deva:
सर्वात्मना विस्मृतः सन्सूक्ष्मतां परमां व्रजेत्।
अलीनत्वान्न निद्रैषा ततो देहोऽपि नो पतेत्॥
units.translation: By continued practice of all kinds the ego becomes exceedingly refined. This state is not sleep because the ego is not completely absorbed; moreover the body does not, as in sleep, fall to the ground.

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 100
units.deva:
न द्वैतं भासते नापि निद्रा तत्रास्ति यत्सुखम्।
स ब्रह्मानन्द इत्याह भगवानर्जुनं प्रति॥
units.translation: The bliss in which there is no experience of duality and which is not sleep either, is the bliss of Brahman. So said Lord Kṛṣṇa to Arjuna.

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 101
units.deva:
शनैः शनैरुपरमेद्बुद्ध्या धृतिगृहीतया।
आत्मसंस्थं मनः कृत्वा न किंचिदपि चिन्तयेत्॥
units.translation: ‘By the steady application of reason and discrimination an aspirant should gradually control his mind. He should keep the mind fixed on the Self and restrain it from thinking of anything else’.

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 102
units.deva:
यतो यतो निश्चरति मनश्चञ्चलमस्थिरम्।
ततस्ततो नियम्यैतदात्मन्येव वशं नयेत्॥
units.translation: ‘Whenever the mind which is restless and fickle, wanders away, the aspirant should restrain it and concentrate it on the Self’.

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 103
units.deva:
प्रशान्तमनसं ह्येनं योगिनं सुखमुत्तमम्।
उपैति शान्तरजसं ब्रह्मभूतमकल्मषम्॥
units.translation: ‘The Yogī whose mind is perfectly tranquil, whose passions are subdued, who is sinless and has become Brahman, attains the supreme bliss’.

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 104
units.deva:
यत्रोपरमते चित्तं निरुद्धं योगसेवया।
यत्र चैवात्मनात्मानं पश्यन्नात्मनि तुष्यति॥
units.translation: ‘When by practice of Yoga, his mind is withdrawn and concentrated, the Yogī sees the Self by the Self and finds supreme satisfaction in the Self’.

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 105
units.deva:
सुखमात्यन्तिकं यत्तद्बुद्धिग्राह्यमतीन्द्रियम्।
वेत्ति यत्र न चैवायं स्थितश्चलति तत्त्वतः॥
units.translation: ‘When he obtains that supreme bliss which is beyond the senses, but which can be grasped by the intellect, he becomes firmly rooted in it and is never moved from it’.

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 106
units.deva:
यं लब्ध्वा चापरं लाभं मन्यते नाधिकं ततः।
यस्मिन् स्थितो न दुःखेन गुरुणापि विचाल्यते॥
units.translation: ‘Attaining it he considers no other gain as superior. Once established in it he is not disturbed even by great sorrow’.

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 107
units.deva:
तं विद्याद्दुःखसंयोगवियोगं योगसंज्ञितम्।
स निश्चयेन योक्तव्यो योगोऽनिर्विण्णचेतसा॥
units.translation: ‘This science of separation from the painful association is called Yoga. This Yoga must be practised with faith and a steady and undespairing mind’.

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 108
units.deva:
युञ्जन्नेवं सदात्मानं योगि विगतकल्मषः।
सुखेन ब्रह्मसंस्पर्शमत्यन्तं सुखमश्नुते॥
units.translation: ‘A Yogī who is free from imperfections and is ever united with his Self, experiences easily the supreme bliss of identity with Brahman’.

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 109
units.deva:
उत्सेक उदधेर्यद्वत्कुशाग्रेणैकबिन्दुना।
मनसो निग्रहस्तद्वद्भवेदपरिखेदतः॥
units.translation: ‘The control of the mind can be achieved by untiring practice over a long period, even as the ocean can be dried up by baling its waters out drop by drop with a blade of grass.’

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 110
units.deva:
बृहद्रथस्य राजर्षेः शाकायन्यो मुनिः सुखम्।
प्राह मैत्राख्यशाखायां समाध्युक्तिपुरःसरम्॥
units.translation: In the Maitrāyaṇī Upaniṣad of the Yajur Veda, sage Sākāyanya spoke of the great bliss experienced in Samādhi to the royal sage Bṛhad-ratha while discoursing on Samādhi.

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 111
units.deva:
यथा निरिन्धनो वह्निः स्वयोनावुपशाम्यति।
तथा वृत्तिक्षयाच्चित्तं स्वयोनावुपशाम्यति॥
units.translation: ‘As fire without fuel dies down and becomes latent in its cause, so the mind, when its modifications have been silenced, merges in its cause’.

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 112
units.deva:
स्वयोनावुपशान्तस्य मनसः सत्यकामिनः।
इन्द्रियार्थविमूढस्यानृताः कर्मवशानुगाः॥
units.translation: ‘To the mind fixed on Reality, merged in its cause and impervious to the sensations arising from the sense-objects, the joys and sorrows (together with their occasions and materials) experienced as a result of the fructifying Karma seem unreal’.

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 113
units.deva:
चित्तमेव हि संसारस्तत्प्रयत्नेन शोधयेत्।
यच्चित्तस्तन्मयो मर्त्यो गुह्यमेतत्सनातनम्॥
units.translation: ‘The mind is indeed the world. It should be purified with great effort. It is an ancient truth that the mind assumes the forms of the objects to which it is applied.’

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 114
units.deva:
चित्तस्य हि प्रसादेन हन्ति कर्म शुभाशुभम्।
प्रसन्नात्मात्मनि स्थित्वा सुखमक्षयमश्नुते॥
units.translation: ‘Through the purification of his mind a man destroys the impressions of his good and evil Karma and the purified mind abiding in Ātman enjoys undiminishing bliss’.

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 115
units.deva:
समासक्तं यथा चित्तं जन्तोर्विषयगोचरे।
यद्येवं ब्रह्मणि स्यात्तत्को न मुच्येत बन्धनात्॥
units.translation: ‘If a man were to focus his mind on Brahman, as he commonly does on the objects of senses, what bondage would he not be free from?’

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 116
units.deva:
मनो हि द्विविधं प्रोक्तं शुद्धं चाशुद्धमेव च।
अशुद्धं कामसम्पर्काच्छुद्धं कामविवर्जितम्॥
units.translation: ‘Mind has been described as of two types, pure (śuddha) and impure (aśuddha). The impure is that which is tainted by desires, the pure is that which is free from desires’.

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 117
units.deva:
मन एव मनुष्याणां कारणं बन्धमोक्षयोः।
बन्धाय विषयासक्तं मुक्त्यै निर्विषयं स्मृतम्॥
units.translation: ‘The mind alone is the cause of bondage and release. Attachment to objects leads to bondage and freedom from attachment to them leads to release’.

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 118
units.deva:
न शक्यते वर्णयितुं गिरा तदा
स्वयं तदन्तःकरणेन गृह्यते॥
units.translation: ‘The bliss arising from absorption in the contemplation of the Self, when all sins and taints are washed off through the practice of Samādhi, cannot be described in words. One must feel it in one’s own heart’.

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 119
units.deva:
यद्यप्यसौ चिरं कालं समाधिर्दुर्लभो नृणाम्।
तथापि क्षणिको ब्रह्मानन्दं निश्चाययत्यसौ॥
units.translation: Though it is rare for men to keep their minds long in the state of absorption, still even a glimpse of it confers conviction about the bliss of Brahman.

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 120
units.deva:
श्रद्धालुर्व्यसनी योऽत्र निश्चिनोत्येव सर्वथा।
निश्चिते तु सकृत्तस्मिन्विश्वसित्यन्यदाप्ययम्॥
units.translation: A man who has full faith in the truth of this bliss and is ceaselessly industrious about getting it, is sure to have it even for a short while; but this is enough to convince him of its reality at other times also.

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 121
units.deva:
तादृक्पुमानुदासीनकालेऽप्यानन्दवासनाम्।
उपेक्ष्य मुख्यमानन्दं भावयत्येव तत्परः॥
units.translation: Such a man ignores the bliss experienced in the state of mental quiescence and is ever devoted to the supreme bliss and meditates on it.

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 122
units.deva:
परव्यसनिनी नारी व्यग्रापि गृहकर्मणि।
तदेवास्वादयत्यन्तः परसङ्गरसायनम्॥
units.translation: A woman devoted to a paramour, though engaged in household duties, with all the time be dwelling in mind on the pleasures with him.

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 123
units.deva:
एवं तत्त्वे परे शुद्धे धीरो विश्रान्तिमागतः।
तदेवास्वादयत्यन्तर्बहिर्व्यवहारन्नपि॥
units.translation: Similarly the wise one who has found peace in the supreme Reality will be ever enjoying within the bliss of Brahman even when engaged in worldly matters.

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 124
units.deva:
धीरत्वमक्षप्राबल्येऽप्यानन्दास्वादवाञ्छया।
तिरस्कृत्याखिलाक्षाणि तच्चिन्तायां प्रवर्तनम्॥
units.translation: Wisdom consists in subjugating the desires for sense-pleasure, even when the passions are strong and in engaging the mind in meditation on Brahman with the desire to enjoy the bliss.

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 125
units.deva:
भारवाही शिरोभारं मुक्त्वास्ते विश्रमं गतः।
संसारव्यापृतित्यागे तादृग्बुद्धिस्तु विश्रमः॥
units.translation: A man carrying a burden on his head feels relief when he removes the load; similarly a man freed from worldly entanglements feels he is in rest.

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 126
units.deva:
विश्रान्तिं परमां प्राप्तस्त्वौदासीन्ये यथा तथा।
सुखदुःखदशायां च तदानन्दैकतत्परः॥
units.translation: Thus relieved of burden and enjoying rest, he fixes his mind on the contemplation of the bliss of Brahman, whether in the state of detachment or experiencing pain or pleasure according to fructifying Karma.

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 127
units.deva:
अग्निप्रवेशहेतौ धीः शृङ्गारे यादृशी तथा।
धीरस्योदेति विषयेऽनुसन्धानविरोधिनी॥
units.translation: As a Satī about to enter the fire considers the delay in putting on clothes and ornaments to be irritating, so also one devoted to the achievement of the bliss of Brahman, feels about worldly objects that obstruct the practice of meditation on bliss.

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 128
units.deva:
अविरोधिसुखे बुद्धिः स्वानन्दे च गमागमौ।
कुर्वन्त्यास्ते क्रमादेषा काकाक्षिवदितस्ततः॥
units.translation: The sage, looking now at the bliss of Brahman and now at such worldly objects as are not opposed to it, is like a crow that turns its eye from one side to another.

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 129
units.deva:
एकैव दृष्टिः काकस्य वामदक्षिणनेत्रयोः।
यात्यायात्येवमानन्दद्वये तत्त्वविदो मतिः॥
units.translation: The crow has only a single vision which alternates between the right and left eye. Similarly the vision of the knower of Truth alternates between the two types of bliss (of Brahman and the world).

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 130
units.deva:
भुञ्जानो विषयानन्दं ब्रह्मानन्दं च तत्त्ववित्।
द्विभाषाभिज्ञवद्विद्यादुभौ लौकिकवैदिकौ॥
units.translation: Enjoying both the bliss of Brahman taught in the scriptures and the worldly bliss unopposed to it, the knower of truth knows them both in the same way as one who knows two languages.

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 131
units.deva:
दुःखप्राप्तौ न चोद्वेगो यथा पूर्वं यतो द्विदृक्।
गङ्गामग्नार्धकायस्य पुंसः शीतोष्णधीर्यथा॥
units.translation: When the knower experiences sufferings, he is not disturbed by them as he would have been before. Just as a man half-immersed in the cool water of the Ganges feels both the heat of the sun and the coolness of the water, so he feels the misery of the world and the bliss of Brahman at the same time.

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 132
units.deva:
इत्थं जागरणे तत्त्वविदो ब्रह्मसुखं सदा।
भाति तद्वासनाजन्ये स्वप्ने तद्भासते तथा॥
units.translation: The knower of truth, experiencing the bliss of Brahman in the waking state experiences it also in the dreaming state, because it is the impressions received in the waking state that give rise to dreams.

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 133
units.deva:
अविद्यावासनाप्यस्तीत्यतस्तद्वासनोत्थिते।
स्वप्ने पूर्ववदेवैष सुखं दुःखं च वीक्षते॥
units.translation: The impressions of ignorance still continue in the dreaming state. So in a dream a wise man will experience sometimes joy and sometimes suffering, without being affected by either.

units.label: Chapter 11 · Verse 134
units.deva:
ब्रह्मानन्दाभिधे ग्रन्थे ब्रह्मानन्दप्रकाशकम्।
योगिप्रत्यक्षमध्याये प्रथमेऽस्मिन्नुदीरितम्॥
units.translation: In this Chapter, the first of the five dealing with the bliss of Brahman, is described direct realisation of the Yogī revealing the bliss of Brahman.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 1
units.deva:
नन्वेवं वासनानन्दाद्ब्रह्मानन्दादपीतरम्।
वेत्तु योगी निजानन्दं मूढस्यात्रास्ति का गतिः॥
units.translation: (Question): A Yogī can enjoy the natural bliss of the Self which is different from the bliss of mental quiescence and the bliss of deep sleep; but what will happen to the ignorant man?

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 2
units.deva:
धर्माधर्मवशादेष जायतां म्रियतामपि।
पुनः पुनर्देहलक्षैः किं नो दाक्षिण्यतो वद॥
units.translation: (Reply): The ignorant are born in innumerable bodies and they die again and again – all owing to their righteous or unrighteous deeds. What is the use of our sympathy for them?

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 3
units.deva:
अस्ति वोऽनुजिघृक्षुवाद्दाक्षिण्येन प्रयोजनम्।
तर्हि ब्रूहि स मूढः किं जिज्ञासुर्वा पराङ्मुखः॥
units.translation: (Doubt): Because of the desire of the teacher to help his ignorant pupils he can do something for them. (Reply): Then you must tell whether they are willing to learn the spiritual truth or are averse to it.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 4
units.deva:
उपास्तिं कर्म वा ब्रूयाद्विमुखाय यथोचितम्।
मन्दप्रज्ञं तु जिज्ञासुमात्मानन्देन बोधयेत्॥
units.translation: If they are still devoted to external objects, some suitable kind of worship or ritual can be prescribed for them. If, on the other hand, they, though spiritually dull, desire to learn the truth, they can be instructed in the knowledge of the bliss of the Self.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 5
units.deva:
बोधयामास मैत्रेयीं याज्ञवल्क्यो निजप्रियाम्।
न वा अरे पत्युरर्थे पतिः प्रिय इतीरयन्॥
units.translation: Yājñavalkya instructed this by pointing out to his beloved wife, Maitreyī, that ‘a wife does not love her husband for his sake’.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 6
units.deva:
पतिर्जाया पुत्रवित्ते पशुब्राह्मणबाहुजाः।
लोका देवा वेदभूते सर्वं चात्मार्थतः प्रियम्॥
units.translation: The husband, wife or son, riches or animals, Brahmanahood or Kshatriyahood, the different worlds, the gods, the Vedas, the elements and all other objects are dear to one for the sake of one’s own Self.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 7
units.deva:
पत्याविच्छा यदा पत्न्यास्तदा प्रीतिं करोति सा।
क्षुदनुष्ठानरोगाद्यैस्तदा नेच्छति तत्पतिः॥
units.translation: A wife shows affection to her husband when she desires his company; the husband too reciprocates but not when he is engaged in worship or afflicted with illness, hunger and so forth.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 8
units.deva:
पतिश्चात्मन एवार्थे न जायार्थे कदाचन।
अन्योऽन्यप्रेरणेऽप्येवं स्वेच्छयैव प्रवर्तनम्॥
units.translation: Her love is not for her husband’s sake but for her own. Similarly the husband’s love also is for his own satisfaction and not for hers. Thus even in the mutual love between husband and wife the incentive is one’s own desire for happiness.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 9
units.deva:
श्मश्रुकण्टकवेधेन बालो रुदति तत्पिता।
चुम्बत्येव न सा प्रीतिर्बालार्थे स्वार्थ एव सा॥
units.translation: A child, when kissed by its father, may cry, being pricked by the latter’s bristly beard, still its father goes on kissing the child – it is not for its sake but for his own.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 10
units.deva:
निरिच्छमपि रत्नादि वित्तं यत्नेन पालयन्।
प्रीतिं करोति सा स्वार्थे वित्तार्थत्वं न शङ्कितम्॥
units.translation: Wealth and gems have no likes or dislikes of their own, but their owner looks after them with love and care. It is for his own sake, none doubts it to be for theirs.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 11
units.deva:
अनिच्छति बलीवर्दे विवाहयिषते बलात्।
प्रीतिः सा वणिगर्थैव बलीवर्दार्थता कुतः॥
units.translation: A merchant forces his bullock, though unwilling, to carry a load. He loves the bullock for his own sake, how can it be for the bullock’s?

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 12
units.deva:
ब्राह्मण्यं मेऽस्ति पूज्योऽहमिति तुष्यति पूजया।
अचेतनाया जातेर्नो सन्तुष्टिः पुंस एव सा॥
units.translation: A Brāhmaṇa knowing that he deserves respect, is satisfied when he receives it. This satisfaction is not felt for his caste, an insentient abstraction, but for the man himself.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 13
units.deva:
क्षत्रियोऽहं तेन राज्यं करोमीत्यत्र राजता।
न जातेर्वैश्यजात्यादौ योजनायेदमीरितम्॥
units.translation: A king feels exalted that he is a Kṣatriya and hence is a ruler, but the feeling is not for the caste. The same applies to men of Vaiśya and other castes also.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 14
units.deva:
स्वर्गलोकब्रह्मलोकौ स्तां ममेत्यभिवाञ्छनम्।
लोकयोर्नोपकाराय स्वभोगायैव केवलम्॥
units.translation: The desire, ‘May I attain the region of heaven or of Brahmā’, is not for the well-being of those regions but only for one’s own enjoyment.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 15
units.deva:
ईशविष्ण्वादयो देवाः पूज्यन्ते पापनष्टये।
न तन्निष्पापदेवार्थं स्वार्थं तत्तूपयुज्यते॥
units.translation: People worship Śiva, Viṣṇu and other deities to destroy sins. It is not for the sake of the deities who are already free from sins, but for their own sake.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 16
units.deva:
ऋगादयो ह्यधीयन्ते दुर्ब्राह्मण्यानवाप्तये।
न तत् प्रसक्तं वेदेषु मनुष्येषु प्रसज्यते॥
units.translation: The Brāhmaṇas study the Ṛg and other Vedas to avoid falling from their (respectable) Brahminhood; this applies to men only and not to the Vedas.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 17
units.deva:
भूम्यादिपञ्चभूतानि स्थानतृट्पाकशोषणैः।
हेतुभिश्चावकाशेन वाञ्छन्त्येषां न हेतवे॥
units.translation: People want the five elements, viz., earth, water, fire, air and Ākāśa, because of their usefulness to them in giving shelter, quenching their thirst, cooking, drying and space for movement and not for the sake of the elements themselves.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 18
units.deva:
स्वामिभृत्यादिकं सर्वं स्वोपकाराया वाञ्छति।
तत्तत्कृतोपकारस्तु तस्य तस्य न विद्यते॥
units.translation: People desire to have servants or masters for their own benefit and not for the benefit of (servants or masters) themselves.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 19
units.deva:
सर्वव्यवहृतिष्वेवमनुसन्धातुमीदृशम्।
उदाहरणबाहुल्यं तेन स्वां वासयेन्मतिम्॥
units.translation: There are plenty of such examples to enable one to study and come to the same conclusion on all occasions. By these one should convince one’s mind that for every man the Self is the only real object of love.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 20
units.deva:
रागो वध्वादि विषये श्रद्धा यागादि कर्मणि।
भक्तिः स्याद्गुरुदेवादाविच्छा त्वप्राप्तवस्तुनि॥
units.translation: (Doubt): What type of love is it that the scriptures say is felt towards the Self? Is it the passionate attachment which is felt towards wife and other objects, the faith which is experienced in sacrifices and other rituals, the devotion which a man cherishes towards God and his teacher or is it the desire one feels for something one does not possess?

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 21
units.deva:
तर्ह्यस्तु सात्विकी वृत्तिः सुखमात्रानुवर्तिनी।
प्राप्ते नष्टेऽपि सद्भावादिच्छतो व्यतिरिच्यते॥
units.translation: (Reply): The real love of the Self is that which, in the absence of these emotions, manifests itself owing to the preponderance of Sāttvikā quality in the intellect. This love of the Self is different from desire, for it exists even when desire is present or destroyed.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 22
units.deva: सुखसाधनतोपाधेरन्नपानादयः प्रियाः॥
units.translation: (Doubt): Be it so, but food, drink etc., are liked because of their quality of giving happiness (and not for their own sake).

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 23
units.deva:
आत्मानुकुल्यादन्नादिसमश्चेदमुनात्र कः।
अनुकुलयितव्यः स्यान्नैकस्मिन्कर्मकर्तृता॥
units.translation: If you say that the Self is also a means to happiness like food and drink, then we ask: who is it that enjoys happiness? One and the same thing cannot be both the subject and the object of enjoyment.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 24
units.deva:
सुखे वैषयिके प्रीतिमात्रमात्मा त्वतिप्रियः।
सुखे व्यभिचरत्येषा नात्मनि व्यभिचारिणी॥
units.translation: Love for the means to happiness is partial love, but the love for the Self is infinite. The love for the means passes from one object to another, but the love for the Self is steadfast.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 25
units.deva:
एकं त्यक्त्वान्यदादत्ते सुखं वैषयिकं सदा।
नात्मा त्याज्यो न चादेयस्तस्मिन्व्यभिचरेत्कथम्॥
units.translation: Love for an object of happiness always passes from one to another; (they are objects that can be accepted or rejected); but the Self cannot be treated like that; so how can love of Self change?

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 26
units.deva:
हानादानविहीनोऽस्मिन्नुपेक्षा चेत्तृणादिवत्।
उपेक्षितुः स्वरूपत्वान्नोपेक्ष्यत्वं निजात्मनः॥
units.translation: (Doubt): Even though it cannot be accepted or rejected the Self may be regarded as an object of indifference, like a piece of straw. (Reply): No, because it is the very Self of the person who is to regard it with indifference.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 27a
units.deva:
रोगक्रोधाभिभूतानां मुमूर्षा वीक्ष्यते क्वचित्।
ततो द्वेषाद्भवेत्त्याज्य आत्मेति यदि तन्न हि॥
units.translation: (Doubt): People begin to hate the Self when they are overpowered by disease or anger and wish to die. (Reply): This is not so.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 28a
units.deva:
त्यक्तुं योग्यस्य देहस्य नात्मता त्यक्तुरेव सा।
न त्यक्तर्यस्ति स द्वेषस्त्याज्ये द्वेषे तु का क्षतिः॥
units.translation: When they desire to do away with the body it is an object for rejection, not their Self. The Self is the subject that desires the end of the body and it feels no hatred for itself. What harm is there if they hate the body, an object?

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 27b
units.deva:
आत्मार्थत्वेन सर्वस्य प्रीतेश्चात्मा ह्यतिप्रियः।
यथा पितुः पुत्रमित्रात्पुत्रः प्रियतरस्तथा॥
units.translation: All objects are desired for the sake of the Self and hence of all the objects that are loved the Self is dearest. A man’s son is dearer to him than his son’s friends.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 28b
units.deva:
मा न भूवमहं किन्तु भूयासं सर्वदेत्यसौ।
आशीः सर्वस्य दृस्तेति प्रत्यक्षा प्रीतिरात्मनि॥
units.translation: ‘May I never perish, may I ever exist’ is the desire seen in all. So love for the Self is quite evident.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 29
units.deva:
इत्यादिभिस्त्रिभिः प्रीतौ सिद्धायामेवमात्मनि।
पुत्रभार्यादिशेषत्वमात्मनः कैश्चिदिर्रितम्॥
units.translation: Though the Self as the object of the highest love is taught by the scriptures and proved both by reasoning and experience, there are some who hold that the Self is merely secondary to son, wife etc., as an object of love.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 30
units.deva:
एतद्विवक्षया पुत्रे मुख्यात्मत्वं श्रुतीरितम्।
आत्मा वै पुत्रनामेति तच्चोपनिषदि स्फुटम्॥
units.translation: To support this they quote the Śruti: ‘The son indeed is the Self’, which shows the superiority of the son. This has been clearly spoken of in the Upaniṣad.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 31
units.deva:
सोऽस्यायमात्मा पुण्येभ्यः कर्मेभ्यः प्रतिधीयते।
अथास्येतर आत्मायं कृतकृत्यः प्रमीयते॥
units.translation: ‘The (father’s) Self, born in the form of the son, becomes his substitute for the performance of meritorious deeds. The Self of the father, having fulfilled its purpose (by begetting a son) and having reached old age, departs’.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 32
units.deva:
सत्यप्यात्मनि लोकोऽस्ति नापुत्रस्यात एव हि।
अनुशिष्टं पुत्रमेव लोक्यमाहुर्मनीषिणः॥
units.translation: A verse in the Bṛhad-āraṇyaka Upaniṣad says that in spite of the existence of the Self a man who has no son does not go to heaven. So the thinkers said that a son who is well trained in the Vedas helps his father to attain heaven.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 33
units.deva:
मनुष्यलोको जय्यः स्यात्पुत्रेणैवेतरेण नो।
मुमूर्षुर्मन्त्रयेत्पुत्रं त्वं ब्रह्मेत्यादिमन्त्रकैः॥
units.translation: The joys of this world can be attained through the son and not by other things. The dying father therefore should instruct his son the Vedic truth, ‘You are Brahman’.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 34
units.deva:
इत्यादिश्रुतयः प्राहुः पुत्रभार्यादिशेषताम्।
लौकिका अपि पुत्रस्य प्राधान्यमनुमन्यते॥
units.translation: These Vedic verses are quoted to prove the importance of son, wife and so forth (and one’s own Self as secondary). Ordinary people too admit the greater importance of a son.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 35
units.deva:
स्वस्मिन्मृतेऽपि पुत्रादिर्जीवेद्वित्तादिना यथा।
तथैव यत्नं कुरुते मुख्याः पुत्रादयस्ततः॥
units.translation: A father labours hard to acquire wealth for the maintenance of his sons and others after his death. Hence the son is superior to the Self.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 36
units.deva:
बाधमेतावता नात्मा शेषो भवति कस्य चित्।
गौणमिथ्यामुख्यभेदैरात्मायं भवति त्रिधा॥
units.translation: All right, but these texts do not prove the Self to be less important. It is to be remembered that the word ‘Self’ is used in three senses, figurative (gauṇa), illusory (mithyā) and fundamental (mukhya).

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 37
units.deva:
देवदत्तस्तु सिंहोऽयमित्यैक्यं गौणमेतयोः।
भेदस्य भासमानत्वात्पुत्रादेरात्मता तथा॥
units.translation: In the expression ‘Deva-datta is a lion’, the identification is figurative, for the difference between the two is evident. Similar is the case of the son and others as the Self.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 38
units.deva:
भेदोऽस्ति पञ्चकोषेषु साक्षिणो न तु भात्यसौ।
मिथ्यात्मतातः कोषाणां स्थाणोर्चौरात्मता यथा॥
units.translation: Difference exists between the five sheaths and the Witness, though it is not evident and so the sheaths are illusory, like the thief seen in the stump of a tree.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 39
units.deva:
न भाति भेदो नाप्यस्ति साक्षिणोऽप्रतियोगिनः।
सर्वान्तरत्वात् तस्यैव मुख्यमात्मत्वमिष्यते॥
units.translation: The witness-consciousness is without a second and therefore in it there neither appears nor is any difference. As it is the innermost essence it is accepted that the word ‘Self’ in its fundamental sense refers to the Witness itself.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 40
units.deva:
सत्येवं व्यवहारेषु येषु यस्यात्मतोचिता।
तेषु तस्यैव शेषित्वं सर्वस्यान्यस्य शेषता॥
units.translation: As the word ‘Self’ has these three meanings in daily use the suitable one becomes primary, the other two becoming merely secondary.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 41
units.deva:
मुमूर्षोर्गृहरक्षादौ गौणात्मैवोपयुज्यते।
न मुख्यात्मा न मिथ्यात्मा पुत्रः शेषी भवत्यतः॥
units.translation: In the case of a dying man, giving charge of the family property and tradition to his son, the figurative meaning of ‘Self’ fits in, not the primary or the illusory meaning.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 42
units.deva:
अध्येता वह्निरित्यत्र सन्नप्यग्निर्न गृह्यते।
अयोग्यत्वेन योग्यत्वाद्बटुरेवात्र गृह्यते॥
units.translation: In the sentence ‘the reciter is the fire’ the term ‘reciter’ cannot actually refer to fire, for the latter is incapable of reciting, but must mean a Brahma-cāri who is able to do so.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 43
units.deva:
कृशोऽहं पुष्टिमाप्स्यामीत्यादौ देहात्मतोचिता।
न पुत्रं विनियुङ्क्तेऽत्र पुष्टिहेत्वन्नभक्षणे॥
units.translation: In such expressions as ‘I am thin and I must get fatter’, the body should be taken as the Self. For the sake of one’s own growing fat nobody engages his son in eating.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 44
units.deva:
तपसा स्वर्गमेष्यामीत्यादौ कर्त्रात्मतोचिता।
अनपेक्ष्य वपुर्भोगं चरेत्कृच्छ्रादिकं ततः॥
units.translation: In such expressions as ‘I shall attain heaven by austerities’ the doer (the intellect-sheath) should be regarded as the Self. So ignoring the physical enjoyment people practise severe austerities.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 45
units.deva:
मोक्ष्येऽहमित्यत्र युक्तं चिदात्मत्वं तदा पुमान्।
तद्वेत्ति गुरुशास्त्राभ्यां न तु किंचिच्चिकीर्षति॥
units.translation: When a man says, ‘I shall be free’, he then acquires knowledge (of the Self) from the teacher and the scripture and desires nothing else. Here the word ‘I’ should be regarded as the witness Self.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 46
units.deva:
विप्रक्षत्रादयो यद्वद्बृहस्पतिसवादिषु।
व्यवस्थितास्तथा गौणमिथ्यामुख्या यथोचितम्॥
units.translation: Just as Brāhmaṇas, Kṣatriyas and Vaiśyas are entitled to perform the sacrifices called Bṛhaspati-sava, Rāja-sūya and Vaiśya-stoma according to their fitness, so the figurative, illusory and fundamental selves are meant in different contexts.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 47
units.deva:
तत्र तत्रोचिते प्रीतिरात्मन्येवातिशायिनी।
अनात्मनि तु तच्छेषे प्रीतिरन्यत्र नोभयम्॥
units.translation: Infinite love is always left for the Self which is primary in any particular context; and for whatever is related to it there is just moderate love and for all other things there is no love whatsoever.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 48
units.deva:
उपेक्ष्यं द्वेष्यमित्यन्यत् द्वेधा मार्गतृणादिकम्।
उपेक्ष्यं व्याघ्रसर्पादि द्वेष्यमेवं चतुर्विधम्॥
units.translation: Other things are of two kinds, to be ignored or hated. Straws lying on the road are disregarded, whereas tigers and snakes are hated. So things are of four kinds: loved, dearly loved, disregarded or hated.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 49
units.deva:
आत्मा शेष उपेक्ष्यं च द्वेष्यं चेति चतुर्ष्वपि।
न व्यक्तिनियमः किन्तु तत्तत्कार्यात्तथा तथा॥
units.translation: The Self, things related to the Self and objects to be disregarded or hated – of these four categories of things there is no sacro-sanctity attached to any one of them that it would always be primary or secondary etc. But it (their being primary or secondary etc.,) depends on the effect they produce under particular circumstances.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 50
units.deva:
स्याद्व्याघ्रः संमुखो द्वेष्यो ह्युपेक्ष्यस्तु पराङ्मुखः।
लालनादनुकूलश्चेद्विनोदायेति शेषताम्॥
units.translation: When a tiger confronts man, it is hated; when it is away, it is disregarded; and when it has been tamed and made friendly, it causes joy; thus it is related to him and is loved.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 51
units.deva:
व्यक्तीनां नियमो मा भूल्लक्षणात्तुव्यवस्थितिः।
आनुकूल्यं प्रातिकूल्यं द्वयाभावश्च लक्षणम्॥
units.translation: Even though no thing is primary or secondary by itself, there are some characteristics to distinguish them under certain circumstances. These characteristics are: their being favourable, unfavourable, or neither of these.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 52
units.deva:
आत्मा प्रेयान्प्रियः शेषो द्वेष्योपेक्ष्ये तदन्ययोः।
इति व्यवस्थितो लोको याज्ञवल्क्यमतं च तत्॥
units.translation: The popular conclusion is that the Self is the dearest, the objects related to it are dear and the rest are either disregarded or hated. This is also the verdict of Yājñavalkya.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 53
units.deva:
अन्यत्रापि श्रुतिः प्राह पुत्राद्वित्तात्तथान्यतः।
सर्वस्मादान्तरं तत्त्वं तदेतत्प्रेय ईक्षताम्॥
units.translation: Elsewhere too the Śruti declares: ‘Know this Self as the dearest which is more intrinsic than son, wealth and so forth’.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 54
units.deva:
श्रौत्या विचारदृष्ट्यायं साक्ष्येवात्मा न चेतरः।
कोषान्पञ्च विविच्यान्तर्वस्तुदृष्टिर्विचारणा॥
units.translation: Through the eye of discrimination following the Śruti it becomes clear that the witness-consciousness is the real Self. Discrimination means separating the five sheaths and seeing the inner substance.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 55
units.deva:
जागरस्वप्नसुप्तीनामागमापायभासनम्।
यतो भवत्यसावात्मा स्वप्रकाशचिदात्मकः॥
units.translation: That is the self-luminous consciousness, the Self, which is the witness of the presence and absence of the states of waking, dreaming and deep sleep.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 56
units.deva:
शेषाः प्राणादिवित्तान्ता आसन्नास्तारतम्यतः।
प्रीतिस्तथा तारतम्यात्तेषु सर्वेषु वीक्ष्यते॥
units.translation: The various objects of enjoyment, from life down to wealth, are objects of varying degrees of love according to their proximity to the Self.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 57
units.deva:
वित्तात्पुत्रः प्रियः पुत्रात्पिण्डः पिण्डात्तथेन्द्रियम्।
इन्द्रियाच्च प्रियः प्राणः प्राणादात्मा परः प्रियः॥
units.translation: A son is dearer than wealth, the body dearer than the son, the sense-organs dearer than the body, life and mind dearer than the sense organs and the Self is supremely dearer than life and mind.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 58
units.deva:
एवं स्थिते विवादोऽत्र प्रतिबुद्धविमूढयोः।
श्रुत्योदाहारि तत्रात्मा प्रेयानित्येव निर्णयः॥
units.translation: In the Śruti there is a dialogue between a wise and a dull-witted man which illustrates the point that the Self is the dearest of all objects.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 59
units.deva:
साक्ष्येव दृश्यादन्यस्मात्प्रेयानित्याह तत्त्ववित्।
प्रेयान्पुत्रादिरेवेमं भोक्तुं साक्षीति मूढधीः॥
units.translation: The wise man holds that the witness-consciousness, is dearer than all objects. The dull-witted man maintains that son and other objects are dearer and that the witness-consciousness enjoys the happiness caused by these objects.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 60
units.deva:
आत्मनोऽन्यं प्रियं ब्रूते शिष्यश्च प्रतिवाद्यपि।
तस्योत्तरं वाचो बोधशापौ कुर्यात्तयोः क्रमात्॥
units.translation: The ignorant disciple and the confirmed opponent both assert that something other than the Self (Ātman) is the object of greatest love. The reply given will prove to be an instruction to the disciple and a curse to the confirmed opponent.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 61
units.deva:
प्रियं त्वां रोत्स्यतीत्येवमुत्तरं वक्ति तत्त्ववित्।
स्वोक्तप्रियस्य दुष्टत्वं शिष्यो वेत्ति विवेकतः॥
units.translation: The wise man quotes the scripture in his reply: ‘Your dearest thing will make you weep’. The pupil analyses this reply and finds out his error in considering something other than the Self as the dearest.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 62
units.deva:
अलभ्यमानस्तनयः पितरौ क्लेशयेच्चिरम्।
लब्धोऽपि गर्भपातेन प्रसवेन च बाधते॥
units.translation: When a married couple desire to have a son and do not have one, they are disappointed and miserable. After conception, a miscarriage or the pain of labour causes sorrow.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 63
units.deva:
जातस्य ग्रहरोगादि कुमारस्य च मूकता।
उपनीतेऽप्यविद्यत्वमनुद्वाहश्च पण्डिते॥
units.translation: When a son is born he may suffer from diseases or from the position of the planets at his birth, or he may be stupid or obstinate, or after the investiture of sacred thread, he may study nothing or if he is learned, he may remain unmarried.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 64
units.deva:
पुनश्च परदारादि दारिद्र्यं च कुटुम्बिनः।
पित्रोः दुःखस्य नास्त्यन्तो धनी चेन्म्रियते तदा॥
units.translation: Again he may start pursuing the wives of others, or he may have an unwieldy family and remain in poverty, or he may grow wealthy and yet die in his youth. Infinite are the sorrows of parents.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 65
units.deva:
एवं विविच्य पुत्रादौ प्रीतिं त्यक्त्वा निजात्मनि।
निश्चित्य परमां प्रीतिं वीक्षते तमहर्निशम्॥
units.translation: Having considered all this, the disciple must abstain from forming an attachment to other things. He should focus his love on the Self and contemplate It day and night.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 66
units.deva:
आग्रहाद्ब्रह्मविद्द्वेषादपि पक्षममुञ्चतः।
वादिनो नरकः प्रोक्तो दोषश्च बहुयोनिषु॥
units.translation: The confirmed opponent, who does not give up his contention due to obstinacy and hostility to the knower of truth, sinks into the depths of darkness and suffers the pains of innumerable births.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 67
units.deva:
ब्रह्मविद्ब्रह्मरूपत्वादीश्वरस्तेन वर्णितम्।
यद्यत्तत्तत्तथैव स्यात्तच्छिष्यप्रतिवादिनोः॥
units.translation: The knower of Brahman is of the nature of Brahman and is described as Īśvara, the all-powerful. Whatever he says will come to pass for the pupil and the opponent.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 68
units.deva:
यस्तु साक्षिणमात्मानं सेवते प्रियमुत्तमम्।
तस्य प्रेयानसावात्मा न नश्यति कदाचन॥
units.translation: He who contemplates the witness Self as the dearest of all objects will find that this dearest Self never suffers destruction.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 69
units.deva:
परप्रेमास्पदत्वेन परमानन्दरूपता।
सुखवृद्धिः प्रीतिवृद्धौ सार्वभौमादिषु श्रुता॥
units.translation: The Supreme Self, being the object of dearest love, is the source of infinite joy. The Śruti has it that from the sovereignty of this world to position of Hiraṇya-garbha, everywhere, wherever there is greater love there is greater bliss.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 70
units.deva:
चैतन्यवत्सुखं चास्य स्वभावश्चेच्चिदात्मनः।
धीवृत्तिष्वनुवर्तेत सर्वास्वपि चितिर्यथा॥
units.translation: (Doubt): If the nature of the Self is bliss as well as consciousness, bliss should be found in all the modifications of the mind, as is consciousness.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 71
units.deva:
मैवमुष्णप्रकाशात्मा दीपस्तस्य प्रभा गृहे।
व्याप्नोति नोष्णता तद्वच्चितेरेवानुवर्तनम्॥
units.translation: (Reply): Not so. A lamp burning in a room emits both light and heat, but it is only the light that fills the room and not heat; similarly, it is only consciousness which accomplishes the Vṛttis (and not bliss).

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 72
units.deva:
गन्धरूपरसस्पर्शेष्वपि सत्सु यथा पृथक्।
एकाक्षेणैक एवार्थो गृह्यते नेतरस्तथा॥
units.translation: An object may be characterised by odour, colour, taste and touch, yet each of these properties is cognised by one particular sense-organ and not the others. It is the same with the bliss of the Self.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 73
units.deva:
चिदानन्दौ नैव भिन्नौ गन्धाद्यास्तु विलक्षणाः।
इति चेत् तदभेदोऽपि साक्षिण्यन्यत्र वा वद॥
units.translation: (Doubt): Odours, taste and so forth differ from one another, but in the Self consciousness and bliss are identical. (Reply): Tell whether this identity is in the witness Self or elsewhere?

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 74
units.deva:
आद्ये गन्धादयोऽप्येवमभिन्नाः पुष्पवर्तिनः।
अक्षभेदेन तद्भेदे वृत्तिभेदात्तयोर्भिदा॥
units.translation: The odour, colour and other properties of a flower are not separate from one another in the flower. If it be said that the separation of these properties is brought about by the sense-organs, we rejoin that the seeming difference between consciousness and bliss is produced by (the predominance of Rajas or Sattva in) the Vṛttis.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 75
units.deva:
सत्ववृत्तौ चित्सुखैक्यं तद्वृत्तेर्निर्मलत्वतः।
रजोवृत्तेस्तु मालिन्यात्सुखांशोऽत्र तिरस्कृतः॥
units.translation: When there is a predominance of Sattva in the Vṛttis, we realise, because of their purity, that bliss and consciousness are one and the same, but when Rajas predominates, because of its impurity, the bliss is obscured.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 76
units.deva:
तिन्तिणीफलमत्यम्लं लवणेन युतं यदा।
तदाम्लस्य तिरस्कारादीषदग्नं यथा तथा॥
units.translation: As the intensely sour taste of tamarind when mixed with salt is lessened and taste less sour, so with bliss (when it is obscured by Rajas).

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 77
units.deva:
ननु प्रियतमत्वेन परमानन्दतात्मनि।
विवेक्तुं शक्यतामेवं विना योगेन किं भवेत्॥
units.translation: (Doubt): By discrimination one can feel that the Self is the dearest, but without the practice of Yoga what good is it (for liberation)?

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 78
units.deva:
यद्योगेन तदेवैति वदामो ज्ञानसिद्धये।
योगः प्रोक्तो विवेकेन ज्ञानं किं नोपजायते॥
units.translation: (Reply): The goal which is reached by Yoga can also be reached by discrimination. Yoga is a means to knowledge; doesn’t knowledge arise from discrimination?

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 79
units.deva:
यत् साङ्ख्यैः प्राप्यते स्थानं तद्योगैरपि गम्यते।
इति स्मृतं फलैकत्वं योगिनां च विवेकिनाम्॥
units.translation: ‘The state achieved by the Sāṅkhyas is also achieved by the Yogīs’. Thus it has been said in the Gītā about the identity of the fruit of both Yoga and discrimination (viveka).

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 80
units.deva:
असाध्यः कस्यचिद्योगः कस्यचिज्ज्ञाननिश्चयः।
इत्थं विचार्यमार्गौ द्वौ जगाद परमेश्वरः॥
units.translation: Knowing that for some Yoga is difficult and for some others knowledge, the great Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa speaks of these two paths.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 81
units.deva:
योगे कोऽतिशयस्तेऽत्र ज्ञानमुक्तं समं द्वयोः।
रागद्वेषाद्यभावश्च तुल्यो योगिविवेकिनोः॥
units.translation: What speciality is there in Yoga when knowledge has been declared as common to both? Both the Yogī and the Vivekī (he who practises discrimination) are alike freed from attachment and aversion.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 82
units.deva:
न प्रीतिर्विषयेष्वस्ति प्रेयानात्मेति जानतः।
कुतो रागः कुतो द्वेषः प्रातिकूल्यमपश्यतः॥
units.translation: One who knows the Self as the dearest has no love for any object of enjoyment. So how can he have attachment? And how can he who sees no object inimical to himself have any aversion?

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 83
units.deva:
देहादेः प्रतिकूलेषु द्वेषस्तुल्योद्वयोरपि।
द्वेषं कुर्वन्न योगी चेदविवेक्यपि तादृशः॥
units.translation: Both the Yogī and the Vivekī dislike objects unfavourable to the body, mind etc. If it be said that he who has aversion for such objects is not a Yogī, then we rejoin that equally so is he not a Vivekī.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 84
units.deva:
द्वैतस्य प्रतिभानं तु व्यवहारे द्वयोः समम्।
समाधौ नेति चेत्तद्वन्नाद्वैतत्वविवेकिनः॥
units.translation: It may be said that though in the world of relative experience both accept the conception of duality, the Yogī has the advantage that there is no duality for him while in the state of Samādhi. Our reply is that he who practises discrimination about the non-duality does not experience duality at that time.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 85
units.deva:
विवक्ष्यते तदस्माभिरद्वैतानन्दनामके।
अध्याये हि तृतीये तत्सर्वमप्यतिमङ्गलम्॥
units.translation: In the next chapter, called the ‘Bliss of Non-duality’ we will enlarge on the theme of the absence of duality. Therefore things told till now are free from defects.

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 86
units.deva:
सदा पश्यन्निजानन्दमपश्यन्नखिलं जगत्।
अर्थाद्योगीति चेत्तर्हि सन्तुष्टो वर्धतां भवान्॥
units.translation: (Doubt): He is a true Yogī who in his contemplation is ever-conscious of the bliss of the Self and is unconscious of the external world. (Reply): May the blessings of contentment ever abide with you. (For the point is gained, this is the position of the Vivekin also).

units.label: Chapter 12 · Verse 87
units.deva:
ब्रह्मानन्दभिधे ग्रन्थे मन्दानुग्रहसिद्धये।
द्वितीयेऽध्याय एतस्मिन्नात्मानन्दो विवेचितः॥
units.translation: In this second chapter of the section in which the bliss of Brahman is discussed (Chapter 11) we have dealt with the bliss of the Self (Ātmānanda) for the good of persons of spiritually dull intellect.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 1
units.deva:
योगानन्दः पुरोक्तो यः स आत्मानन्द इष्यताम्।
कथं ब्रह्मत्वमेतस्य सद्वयस्येति चेच्छृणु॥
units.translation: The bliss of Yoga which was described earlier may be said to be the bliss of the Self. (Doubt): How can the bliss of the embodied Self which is in duality be identical with the bliss of Brahman (who is non-dual)? (Reply): Please listen.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 2
units.deva:
आकाशादि स्वदेहान्तं तैत्तिरीयश्रुतीरितम्।
जगन्नास्त्यन्यदानन्दादद्वैतब्रह्मता ततः॥
units.translation: As described in the Taittirīya Upaniṣad, the whole world, from Ākāśa to the physical body, is not different from bliss. Therefore the bliss of the Self is of the nature of the non-dual Brahman.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 3
units.deva:
आनन्दाद्ध्येव तज्जातं तिष्ठत्यानन्द एव तत्।
आनन्द एव लीनं चेत्युक्तानन्दात्कथं पृथक्॥
units.translation: The world is born of bliss, it abides in bliss and is merged in bliss. How then can it be anything other than this bliss?

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 4
units.deva:
कुलालाद्घट उत्पन्नो भिन्नश्चेति न शङ्क्यताम्।
मृद्वदेषः उपादानं न निमित्तं कुलालवत्॥
units.translation: The pot made by a potter is different from him, but let this not create any doubt, for like the clay, bliss is the material cause of the universe, not like the potter the efficient cause.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 5
units.deva:
स्थितिर्लयश्च कुम्भस्य कुलाले स्तो न हि क्वचित्।
दृष्टौ तौ मृदि तद्वत्स्यादुपादानं तयोः श्रुतेः॥
units.translation: The existence and destruction of the pot are never seen to rest in the potter, but its material cause, the clay. Similarly, according to the Śruti passages their (the existence and destruction of the universe) material cause is bliss.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 6
units.deva:
उपादानं त्रिधा भिन्नं विवर्ति परिणामि च।
आरम्भकं च तत्रान्त्यौ न निरंशेऽवकाशिनौ॥
units.translation: The material cause is of three kinds: (1) the Vivarta, which gives rise to a phenomenal appearance, not materially related to the cause; (2) the Pariṇāma which gives rise to an effect which is a modification or change of state of the cause; and (3) the Ārambha, which consists of effect being different from the causes. The last two (which presuppose parts) have no scope with reference to partless Brahman.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 7
units.deva:
आरम्भवादिनोऽन्यस्मादन्यस्योत्पत्तिमूचिरे।
तन्तोः पटस्य निष्पत्तेर्भिन्नौ तन्तुपटौ खलु॥
units.translation: The Ārambha-vādins accept the production of one kind of material from another, as cloth from threads and they consider threads and cloth to be quite different.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 8
units.deva:
अवस्थान्तरतापत्तिरेकस्य परिणामिता।
स्यात् क्षीरं दधि मृत्कुम्भः सुवर्णं कुण्डलं यथा॥
units.translation: Pariṇāma is the change of one state of the same substance into another, as milk into curd, clay into a pot and gold into an ear-ring.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 9
units.deva:
अवस्थान्तरभानं तु विवर्तो रज्जुसर्पवत्।
निरंशेऽप्यस्त्यसौ व्योम्नि तलमालिन्यकल्पनात्॥
units.translation: But Vivarta is mere appearance of change of a thing or its state, not a real change: like a rope appearing as a snake. It is seen even in a partless substance, e.g., the Ākāśa (which has no shape or colour) appearing as the blue dome.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 10
units.deva:
ततो निरंश आनन्दे विवर्तो जगदिष्यताम्।
मायाशक्तिः कल्पिका स्यादैन्द्र जालिकशक्तिवत्॥
units.translation: So the illusive appearance of the world in the partless bliss can be explained. Like the power of a magician, the power of Māyā may be said to bring the objective world into being.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 11
units.deva:
शक्तिः शक्तात्पृथङ्नास्ति तद्वद्दृष्टेर्न चाभिदा।
प्रतिबन्धस्य दृष्टत्वाच्छक्त्यभावे तु कस्य सः॥
units.translation: Power does not exist apart from the possessor of power, for it is always seen as inseparable from him. Nor can it be said to be identical with him, for its obstruction is met with. If identical, in the absence of power, of what is the obstruction?

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 12
units.deva:
शक्तेः कार्यानुमेयत्वादकार्ये प्रतिबन्धनम्।
ज्वलतोऽग्नेरदाहे स्यान्मन्त्रादि प्रतिबन्धता॥
units.translation: Power is inferred from its effect. When its effects are not seen we conclude that there is some obstruction to it. For instance, if the flames of a fire do not burn, we infer the presence of some obstruction, such as incantation etc.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 13
units.deva:
देवात्मशक्तिं स्वगुणैर्निगूढां मुनयोऽविदन्।
परास्य शक्तिर्विविधा क्रियाज्ञानबलात्मिका॥
units.translation: The sages perceived that the power of Brahman called Māyā is concealed by its own qualities. Many are the aspects of this divine power, which is manifest as action, knowledge and will.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 14
units.deva:
इति वेदवचः प्राह वसिष्ठश्च तथाब्रवीत्।
सर्वशक्तिपरं ब्रह्म नित्यमापूर्णमद्वयम्॥
units.translation: ‘The supreme Brahman is eternal, perfect, non-dual and omnipotent’, so says the Veda and Vasiṣṭha supports this.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 15
units.deva:
यथोल्लसति शक्त्यासौ प्रकाशमधिगच्छति।
चिच्छक्तिर्ब्रह्मणो राम! शरीरेषूपलभ्यते॥
units.translation: ‘With whatever power He means to sport, that power becomes manifest. O Rāma, the power of Brahman which manifests itself as consciousness is felt in the bodies of all beings’.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 16
units.deva:
स्पन्दशक्तिश्च वातेषु दार्ढ्यशक्तिस्तथोपले।
द्रवशक्तिस्तथाम्भःसु दाहशक्तिस्तथानले॥
units.translation: ‘This power abides as movement in the air, as hardness in stone, as liquidity in water, as the power to burn in fire’.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 17
units.deva:
शून्यशक्तिस्तथाकाशे नाशशक्तिर्विनाशिनि।
यथाण्डान्तर्महासर्पो जगदस्ति तथात्मनि॥
units.translation: ‘Similarly it abides as emptiness in Ākāśa and as perishability in the objects which are subject to destruction. As a huge serpent is latent in the egg, so the world is latent in the Self’.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 18
units.deva:
फलपत्रलतापुष्पशाखाविटपमूलवान्।
वृक्षबीजे यथा वृक्षस्तथेदं ब्रह्मणि स्थितम्॥
units.translation: ‘Just as a tree with its fruits, leaves, tendrils, flowers, branches, twigs and roots is latent in the seed, so does this world abide in Brahman’.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 19
units.deva:
क्वचित्कश्चित्कदाचिच्च तस्मादुद्यन्ति शक्तयः।
देशकालविचित्रत्वात्क्ष्मातलादिव शालयः॥
units.translation: ‘Due to variations in space and time, somewhere, some times, some powers emanate from Brahman, just as varieties of paddy from the earth.’

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 20
units.deva:
स आत्मा सर्वगो राम! नित्योदितमहावपुः।
यन्मनाङ्मननीं शक्तिं धत्ते तन्मन उच्यते॥
units.translation: ‘O Rāma, when the all-pervasive, eternal and infinite Self assumes the power of cognition, we call it the mind.’

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 21
units.deva:
इत्यादिका स्थितिरियं हि गता प्रतिष्ठाम्
आख्यायिका सुभगबालजनोदितेव॥
units.translation: ‘O Prince, first arises the mind, then the notion of bondage and release and then the universe consisting of many worlds. Thus all this manifestation has been fixed or settled (in human minds), like the tales told to amuse children’.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 22
units.deva:
बालस्य हि विनोदाय धात्री शक्ति शुभां कथाम्।
क्वचित्सन्ति महाबाहो! राजपुत्रास्त्रयः शुभाः॥
units.translation: ‘To amuse a child, O mighty one, the nurse relates some beautiful story: Once upon a time there were three handsome princes’.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 23
units.deva:
द्वौ न जातौ तथैकस्तु गर्भ एव हि न स्थितः।
वसन्ति ते धर्मयुता अत्यन्तासति पत्तने॥
units.translation: ‘Two of them were never born and the third was never even conceived in his mother’s womb. They lived righteously in a city which never existed.’

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 24
units.deva:
स्वकीयाच्छून्यनगरान्निर्गत्य विमलाशयाः।
गच्छन्तो गगने वृक्षान्ददृशुः फलशालिनः॥
