units.translation: ‘These holy princes came out of their city of non-existence and while roaming saw trees, laden with fruits, growing in the sky’.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 25
units.deva:
भविष्यन्नगरे तत्र राजपुत्रास्त्रयोऽपि ते।
सुखमद्य स्थिता पुत्र! मृगयाव्यवहारिणः॥
units.translation: ‘Then the three princes, my child, went to a city which was yet to be built and lived there happily, passing their time in games and hunting’.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 26
units.deva:
धात्र्यैवं कथिता राम! बालकाख्यायिका शुभा।
निश्चयं स ययौ बालो निर्विचारणया धिया॥
units.translation: ‘O Rāma, the nurse thus narrated the beautiful children’s tale. The child too through want of discrimination believed it to be true’.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 27
units.deva:
इयं संसार रचना विचारोज्झितचेतसाम्।
बालकाख्यायिकेवेत्थमवस्थितिमुपागता॥
units.translation: ‘Thus to those who have no discrimination the world appears to be real like the tale repeated to the child’.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 28
units.deva:
इत्यादिभिरुपाख्यानैर्मायाशक्तेस्तु विस्तरम्।
वसिष्ठः कथयामास सैव शक्तिर्निरूप्यते॥
units.translation: By such entertaining tales Vasiṣṭha described the power of Māyā. This power is now being described more fully.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 29
units.deva:
कार्यादाश्रयतः सैषा भवेच्छक्तिर्विलक्षणा।
स्फोटाङ्गारौ दृश्यमानौ शक्तिस्तत्रानुमीयते॥
units.translation: This power is different both from its effect and also from its substratum. The blister (which is the effect) and the charcoal (the substratum) are cognised objects; but the power to burn is inferred from the effect (viz., the blister).

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 30
units.deva:
पृथुबुध्नोदराकारो घटः कार्योऽत्र मृत्तिका।
शब्दादिभिः पञ्चगुणैर्युक्ता शक्तिस्त्वतद्विधा॥
units.translation: The pot with its properties of thickness, roundness and so forth, is the product of power acting on the clay with its five properties of sound, touch, form, taste and smell, but the power is different here (from both the pot and the clay).

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 31
units.deva:
न पृथ्वादिर्न शब्दादिः शक्तावस्तु यथा तथा।
अत एव ह्यचिन्त्यैषा न निर्वचनमर्हति॥
units.translation: In the power (that creates the pot) there is neither form nor quality; as it is it remains (even when it has produced the effect, it undergoes no change). It is therefore said to be beyond thought and description.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 32
units.deva:
कार्योत्पत्तेः पुरा शक्तिर्निगूढा मृद्यवस्थिता।
कुलालादिसहायेन विकाराकारतां व्रजेत्॥
units.translation: Before the creation of the pot, the power (of giving rise to a pot) is implicit in the clay. With the help of the potter and other means the clay is transformed into a pot.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 33
units.deva:
पृथ्व्यादि विकारान्तं स्पर्शादिगुणमृत्तिकाम्।
एकीकृत्य घटं प्राहुर्विचारविकला जनाः॥
units.translation: People of immature minds confound the properties of the effect with those of the cause, the clay and speak of it as the pot.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 34
units.deva:
कुलालव्यापृतेः पूर्वो यावानंश स नो घटः।
पश्चात्तु पृथुबुध्नादिमत्त्वे युक्ता हि कुम्भता॥
units.translation: The clay, before the potter worked on it, cannot be called a pot. But it is proper to call it a pot when it acquires the properties such as thickness, hollowness and so forth.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 35
units.deva:
स घटो न मृदो भिन्नो वियोगे सत्यनीक्षणात्।
नाप्यभिन्नः पुरा पिण्डदशायामनवेक्षणात्॥
units.translation: The pot is not different from the clay, as it has no existence apart from the clay; it is neither identical with the clay, as in the unmoulded clay it is not perceived.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 36
units.deva:
अतोऽनिर्वचनीयोऽयं शक्तिवत्तेन शक्तिजः।
अव्यक्तव्ये शक्तिरुक्ता व्यक्तत्ये घटनामभृत्॥
units.translation: Therefore the pot (a product of power) can only be called indescribable, like the power which produces it. Hence the product of power when imperceptible is simply called power and when perceptible it is called a pot.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 37
units.deva:
ऐन्द्रजालिकनिष्ठापि माया न व्यज्यते पुरा।
पश्चाद्गन्धर्वसेनादिरूपेण व्यक्तिमाप्नुयात्॥
units.translation: A magician’s power is not apparent earlier; it is only when he brings it into operation that it appears as an army of Gandharvas and the like.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 38
units.deva:
एवं मायामयत्वेन विकारस्यानृतात्मताम्।
विकाराधारमृद्वस्तुसत्यत्वं चाब्रवीच्छ्रुतिः॥
units.translation: Thus being illusive, in the scriptures, the products of power are called unreal whereas reality is predicated only of the entity in which the power inheres, e.g., of the clay in which the pot inheres.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 39
units.deva:
वाङ्निष्पाद्यं नाममात्रं विकारो नास्य सत्यता।
स्पर्शादि गुणयुक्ता तु सत्या केवलमृत्तिका॥
units.translation: A pot taken as a product of power is only a name composed of words; it is not a real entity. Only the clay that possesses sound, touch, form, taste and smell, is a real entity.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 40
units.deva:
व्यक्ताव्यक्ते तदाधार इति त्रिष्वाद्ययोर्द्वयोः।
पर्यायः कालभेदेन तृतीयस्त्वनुगच्छति॥
units.translation: Of the three entities, the manifest (i.e., product of power), the unmanifest (i.e., the power itself), and the substratum in which they both inhere, the first two exist by turns (thus cancelling one another); but the third persists in both (and at all times).

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 41
units.deva:
निस्तत्त्वं भासमानं च व्यक्तमुत्पत्तिनाशभाक्।
तदुत्पत्तौ तस्य नाम वाचा निष्पाद्यते नृभिः॥
units.translation: A product of power though visible has no real substance, as it is subject to creation and destruction. When it appears, it is given a name by men.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 42
units.deva:
व्यक्ते नष्टेऽपि नामैतन्नृवक्त्रेष्वनुवर्तते।
तेन नाम्ना निरूप्यत्वाद्व्यक्तं तद्रूपमुच्यते॥
units.translation: When the product perishes, its name continues to be used by men. Since it is indicated only by name, it is said to be of nominal existence.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 43
units.deva:
निस्तत्त्वत्वाद्विनाशित्वाद्वाचारम्भणनामतः।
व्यक्तस्य न तु तद्रूपं सत्यं किञ्चिन्मृदादिवत्॥
units.translation: This form of the product (of power, like the pot) is not real like clay, because it is unsubstantial, destructible and a mere name based upon words.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 44
units.deva:
व्यक्तकाले ततः पूर्वमूर्ध्वमप्येकरूपभाक्।
सतत्त्वमविनाशं च सत्यं मृद्वस्तु कथ्यते॥
units.translation: The substance clay is said to be the real entity because by nature it is unchanged, substantial and indestructible at all times, before the production of the pot, after its destruction and even while it is manifest.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 45
units.deva:
व्यक्तं घटो विकारश्चेत्येतैर्नामभिरीरितः।
अर्थश्चेदनृतः कस्मान्न मृद्बोधे निवर्तते॥
units.translation: (Doubt): If the thing indicated by the three terms i.e., the manifest, the pot and the modified form is unreal, why is it not destroyed when the knowledge of its substratum (clay) dawns?

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 46
units.deva:
निवृत्त एव यस्मात्ते तत्सत्यत्वमतिर्गता।
ईदृङ्निवृत्तिरेवात्र बोधजा न त्वभासनम्॥
units.translation: (Reply): With the knowledge of the substratum the pot is destroyed, for your idea of the reality of the pot is removed. This is what is meant by the destruction of the pot through knowledge; it does not mean that the pot would cease to appear.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 47
units.deva:
पुमानधोमुखः नीरे भातोऽप्यस्ति न वस्तुतः।
तटस्थमर्त्यवत्तस्मिन्नैवास्था कस्यचित्क्वचित्॥
units.translation: Though a man appears head downwards when reflected in water, he is not so. No one would ever mistake it for the real person standing on the bank.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 48
units.deva:
ईदृग्बोधे पुमर्थत्वं मतमद्वैतवादिनाम्।
मृद्रूपस्यापरित्यागाद्विवर्तत्वं घटे स्थितम्॥
units.translation: According to the doctrine of the non-dualists, such knowledge (i.e., the knowledge of the unreality of the superimposed thing, the world), gives liberation, the supreme goal of life. As the substratum clay is not rejected, the appearance of a pot in it is accepted.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 49
units.deva:
परिणामे पूर्वरूपं त्यजेत्तत्क्षीररूपवत्।
मृत्सुवर्णे निवर्तेते घटकुण्डलयोर्न हि॥
units.translation: In an actual modification of the substratum, when milk is turned into curd (for example), the former form, milk, disappears. But in the modification of clay into a pot or gold into an ear-ring, the substratum does not change.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 50
units.deva:
घटे नष्टे न मृद्भावः कपालानामवेक्षणात्।
मैवं चूर्णेऽस्ति मृद्रूपं स्वर्णरूपं त्वतिस्फुटम्॥
units.translation: (Doubt): When a pot is broken into pieces, they do not resemble the original clay, for broken pieces only are seen. (Reply): It is not so, for when reduced to powder they do. The persistence of gold in the ear-ring is very clear.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 51
units.deva:
क्षीरादौ परिणामोऽस्तु पुनस्तद्भाववर्जनात्।
एतावता मृदादीनां दृष्टान्तत्वं न हीयते॥
units.translation: When milk is turned into curd, actual change of substance takes place. Milk ceases to exist as such and cannot be recovered from the curd. By this, the case of a clay-pot or a gold-ring (as examples of Vivarta) does not suffer.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 52
units.deva:
आरम्भवादिनः कार्ये मृदो द्वैगुण्यमापतेत्।
रूपस्पर्शादयः प्रोक्ताः कार्य कारणयोः पृथक्॥
units.translation: According to the Ārambha-vādins, clay should have two sets of properties, viz., those of the cause and those of the effect, for they hold, the properties of the effects are different from those of the cause, which is, however, not the case.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 53
units.deva:
मृत्सुवर्णमयश्चेति दृष्टान्तत्रयमारुणिः।
प्राहातो वासयेत्कार्यानृतत्वं सर्ववस्तुषु॥
units.translation: The sage Āruṇi (Uddālaka) mentions the three examples of clay, gold and iron (only to show that all effects are only phenomenal). Therefore one should fix in mind the unreality of all effects.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 54
units.deva:
कारणज्ञानतः कार्यविज्ञानं चापि सोऽवदत्।
सत्यज्ञानेऽनृतज्ञां कथमत्रोपपद्यते॥
units.translation: Āruṇi holds that a knowledge of the cause implies a knowledge of all its effects. But how would a knowledge of the unreal effects arise from a knowledge of their real cause?

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 55
units.deva:
समृत्कस्य विकारस्य कार्यता लोकदृष्टितः।
वास्तवोऽत्र मृदंशोऽस्य बोधः कारणबोधतः॥
units.translation: According to the common view, an effect, such as a pot, is a modification of its material cause, clay; the clay portion of the pot is the real substance. Therefore when the cause of the pot is known, the real portion of substance of the pot is also known.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 56
units.deva:
अनृतांशो न बोद्धव्यस्तद्बोधानुपयोगतः।
तत्त्वज्ञानं पुमर्थं स्यान्नानृत अंशावबोधनम्॥
units.translation: The unreal portion of the effect need not be known, because its knowledge serves no useful purpose. A knowledge of the real substance is necessary for men, whereas a knowledge of the unreal portion is useless.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 57
units.deva:
तर्हि कारणविज्ञानात्कर्यज्ञामितीरिते।
मृद्बोधान्मृत्तिका बुद्धेत्युक्तं स्यात्कोऽत्र विस्मयः॥
units.translation: (Doubt): The statement that through the knowledge of the cause you arrive at a knowledge of the effect amounts to saying that by a knowledge of clay you acquire a knowledge of clay. What is there wonderful about it?

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 58
units.deva:
सत्यं कार्येषु वस्त्वंशः कारणात्मेति जानतः।
विस्मयो मास्त्विहाज्ञस्य विस्मयः केन वार्यते॥
units.translation: (Reply): The real substance in the effect (pot) is identical with its cause. This may not be surprising to the wise but who can prevent the ignorant being surprised at this?

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 59
units.deva:
आरम्भी परिणामी च लौकिकश्चैककारणे।
ज्ञाते सर्वमतं श्रुत्वा प्राप्नुवन्त्येव विस्मयम्॥
units.translation: The followers of Ārambha-vāda and Pariṇāma-vāda and ordinary men may find it puzzling to hear that a knowledge of the cause should give a knowledge of all its effects.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 60
units.deva:
अद्वैतेऽभिमुखीकर्तुमेवात्रैकस्य बोधतः।
सर्वबोधः श्रुतौ नैव नानात्वस्य विवक्षया॥
units.translation: To direct the attention of the pupil to the non-dual truth, the Chāndogya Upaniṣad teaches that by a knowledge of the one cause all its effects are known. It does not speak of the multiplicity of effects.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 61
units.deva:
एकमृत्पिण्डविज्ञानात्सर्वमृण्मयधीर्यथा।
तथैकब्रह्मबोधेन जगद्बुद्धिर्विभाव्यताम्॥
units.translation: Just by knowing a lump of clay one knows all objects made of clay, so by knowing the one Brahman one knows (the real element of) the whole phenomenal world.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 62
units.deva:
सच्चित्सुखात्मकं ब्रह्म नामरूपात्मकं जगत्।
तापनीये श्रुतं ब्रह्म सच्चिदानन्दलक्षणम्॥
units.translation: The nature of Brahman is existence, consciousness and bliss, whereas the nature of the world is name and form. In the Nṛsiṃha-Uttara-Tāpanīya Upaniṣad existence, consciousness and bliss are said to be the ‘indications’ of Brahman.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 63
units.deva:
सद्रूपमारुणिः प्राह प्रज्ञानं ब्रह्म बह्वृचाः।
सनत्कुमार आनन्दमेवमन्यत्र गम्यताम्॥
units.translation: Āruṇi described Brahman as of the nature of existence, the Bahv-ṛcas of the Ṛg-Veda as consciousness and Sanat-kumāra as bliss. The same is declared in other Upaniṣads.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 64
units.deva:
विचिन्त्य सर्वरूपाणि कृत्वा नामानि तिष्ठति।
अहं व्याकरवाणीमे नामरूपे इति श्रुतिः॥
units.translation: After creating names and forms Brahman remains established in His nature, i.e., remains as immutable as ever, says the Puruṣa Sūkta. Another Śruti says that Brahman as the Self reveals names and forms.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 65
units.deva:
अव्याकृतं पुरा सृष्टेरूर्ध्वं व्याक्रीयते द्विधा।
अचिन्त्यशक्तिर्मायैषा ब्रह्मण्यव्याकृताभिधा॥
units.translation: Another Śruti says that before creation the universe was unmanifest and that afterwards it became manifest as name and form. Here Māyā, the inexplicable power of Brahman, is referred to as ‘unmanifest’.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 66
units.deva:
अविक्रियब्रह्मनिष्ठा विकारं यात्यनेकधा।
मायां तु प्रकृतिं विद्यान्मायिनं तु महेश्वरम्॥
units.translation: This Māyā, which rests unmanifest in the immutable Brahman, subsequently undergoes numerous modifications. ‘Know Māyā as Prakṛti (the material cause of the universe), and the supreme Lord as the Ruler (substratum) of Māyā’.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 67
units.deva:
आद्यो विकार आकाशः सोऽस्ति भात्यपि च प्रियः।
अवकाशस्तस्य रूपं तन्मिथ्या न तु तत्त्रयम्॥
units.translation: The first modification of Māyā is Ākāśa; it exists, is manifest and is dear to all. The special form of Ākāśa is space which is unreal, but its other three properties (derived from its cause, Brahman), are not unreal.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 68
units.deva:
न व्यक्तेः पूर्वमस्त्येव न पश्चाच्च विनाशतः।
आदावन्ते च यन्नास्ति वर्तमानेऽपि तत्तथा॥
units.translation: The spatial property does not exist before manifestation and ceases also to exist after destruction. That which is non-existent before creation and after dissolution is so even in the present (i.e., during creation).

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 69
units.deva:
अव्यक्तादीनि भूतानि व्यक्तमध्यानि भारत।
अव्यक्तनिधनानीवेत्याह कृष्णोऽर्जुनं प्रति॥
units.translation: Śrī Kṛṣṇa said to Arjuna: ‘O descendant of Bhārata, beings are unmanifest in the beginning, manifest in the present and unmanifest again at the end’.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 70
units.deva:
मृद्वत्ते सच्चिदानन्दा अनुगच्छन्ति सर्वद।
निराकाशे सदादीनामनुभूतिर्निजात्मनि॥
units.translation: Just as clay exists (in its modifications such as the pot) in all the three divisions of time, so existence, consciousness and bliss ever pervade the Ākāśa, when the idea of space is negated from Ākāśa, what remains is one’s own Self-existence, consciousness and bliss (infinity).

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 71
units.deva:
अवकाशे विस्मृतेऽथ तत्र किं भाति ते वद।
शून्यमेवेति चेदस्तु नाम तादृग्विभाति हि॥
units.translation: When the idea of space is negated from Ākāśa, what remains of it? If you say, ‘Nothing remains’, we accept it and say that that which is represented by the word ‘nothing’ is revealed.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 72
units.deva:
तादृक्त्वादेव तत्सत्त्वमौदासीन्येन तत्सुखम्।
आनुकूल्यप्रातिकूल्यहीनं यत्तन्निजं सुखम्॥
units.translation: Because it is such that we must attribute existence to the remaining entity. Being productive of no misery, it is bliss, for the absence of both the favourable and the unfavourable is the bliss of the Self.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 73
units.deva:
आनुकूल्ये हर्षधीः स्यात्प्रातिकूल्ये तु दुःखधीः।
द्वयाभावे निजानन्दो निजं दुःखं तु न क्वचित्॥
units.translation: One gets pleasure from a favourable object and grief from an unfavourable one; but in the natural state, free from both, there is the natural bliss of the Self. There is never any experience of misery in that state.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 74
units.deva:
निजानन्दे स्थिते हर्षशोकयोर्व्यत्ययः क्षणात्।
मनसः क्षणिकत्वेन तयोर्मानसतेष्यताम्॥
units.translation: The natural bliss of the Self is uniform and steady, but the mind due to its fickle nature, passes in a moment from joy to sorrow. So both are to be looked upon as the creations of the mind.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 75
units.deva:
आकाशेऽप्येवमानन्दः सत्ताभाने तु संमते।
वाय्वादिदेहपर्यन्तवस्तुष्वेवं विभाव्यताम्॥
units.translation: Thus in Ākāśa also we accept bliss, i.e., it is fundamentally existence, consciousness and bliss and similarly we can establish that the fundamental nature of all objects from air to the physical body is essentially the same.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verses 76–77
units.deva:
गतिस्पर्शौ वायुरूपं वह्नेर्दाहप्रकाशने।
जलस्य द्रवता भूमेः काठिन्यं चेति निर्णयः॥
असाधारण आकाशे ओषध्यन्नवपुःष्वपि।
एवं विभाव्य मनसा तत्तद्रूपं यथोचितम्॥
units.translation: The special properties of air have been determined as motion and touch; of fire, heat and light; of water, liquidity; and of earth, solidity. Similarly the special properties of plants, foods, bodies and other objects can be thought of by the mind.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 78
units.deva:
अनेकधा विभिन्नेषु नामरूपेषु चैकधा।
तिष्ठन्ति सच्चिदानन्दाविसंवादः न कस्यचित्॥
units.translation: In the manifold objects, different in names and forms, the common element is existence, consciousness and bliss. Nobody can dispute this.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 79
units.deva:
निस्तत्त्वे नामरूपे द्वे जन्मनाशयुते च ते।
बुद्ध्या ब्रह्मणि वीक्षस्व समुद्रे बुद्बुदादिवत्॥
units.translation: Both name and form are without any real existence because they are subject to creation and destruction. So know them as superimposed by the intellect on Brahman, just as waves and foam are on the ocean.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 80
units.deva:
सच्चिदानन्दरूपेऽस्मिन् पूर्णे ब्रह्मणि वीक्षिते।
स्वयमेवावजानाति नामरूपे शनैः शनैः॥
units.translation: With the direct knowledge of Brahman, the eternal existence, consciousness and bliss, names and forms slowly come to be disregarded.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 81
units.deva:
यावद्यावदवज्ञा स्यात्तावत्तावत्तदीक्षणम्।
यावद्यावद्वीक्ष्यते तत्तावत्तावदुभे त्यजेत्॥
units.translation: The more is duality negated, the clearer does the realisation of Brahman become and as realisation becomes perfect, names and forms come to be disregarded of themselves.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 82
units.deva:
तदभ्यासेन विद्यायां सुस्थितायामयं पुमान्।
जीवन्नेव भवेन्मुक्तो वपुरस्तु यथा तथा॥
units.translation: When through the continuous practice of meditation a man is established in the knowledge of Brahman, he becomes liberated even while living. Then the fate of his body does not matter.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 83
units.deva:
तच्चिन्तनं तत्कथनमन्योन्यं तत्प्रबोधनम्।
एतदेकपरत्वं च तदभ्यासं विदुर्बुधाः॥
units.translation: Thinking of Him, speaking of Him and making one another understand Him – this is what the wise call ‘practice of Brahman-realisation’.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 84
units.deva:
वासनानेककालिना दीर्घकालं निरन्तरम्।
सादरं चाभ्यस्यमाने सर्वथैव निवर्तते॥
units.translation: The longstanding impressions of the world on the mind are loosened if this training of knowledge is constantly practised with earnestness for a long time.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 85
units.deva:
मृच्छक्तिवद्ब्रह्मशक्तिरनेकाननृतान्सृजेत्।
यद्वा जीवगता निद्रा स्वप्नश्चात्र निदर्शनम्॥
units.translation: As the power inherent in the clay brings the pot into existence, so the power of Māyā inherent in Brahman creates many unreal things. This is illustrated by sleep and dream conditions of living beings.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 86
units.deva:
निद्राशक्तिर्यथा जीवे दुर्घटस्वप्नकारिणी।
ब्रह्मण्येषा तथा माया सृष्टिस्थित्यन्तकारिणी॥
units.translation: Just as in the sleeping state a power inherent in the Jīva gives rise to impossible dreams, so the power of Māyā inherent in Brahman, projects, maintains and destroys the universe.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 87
units.deva:
स्वप्ने वियद्गतिं पश्येत्स्वमूर्धच्छेदनं यथा।
मुहूर्ते वत्सरौघं च मृतं पुत्रादिकं पुनः॥
units.translation: In dream a man may see himself flying in the sky or being beheaded. In a moment he may live through the experience of many years. Or he may dream of seeing a dead son and so forth.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 88
units.deva:
इदं युक्तमिदं नेति व्यवस्था तत्र दुर्लभा।
यथा यथेक्ष्यते यद्यत्तत्तद्युक्तं तथा तथा॥
units.translation: ‘This is proper (possible) and this is not’ such discrimination is not possible then. Whatever one perceives in dreams seems to be in the right place.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 89
units.deva:
ईदृशो महिमा दृष्टो निद्राशक्तेर्यदा तदा।
मायाशक्तेरचिन्त्योऽयं महिमेति किमद्भुतम्॥
units.translation: When such is the glory of the power of sleep and dream, what is there to wonder at the unimaginable glory of the power of Māyā?

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 90
units.deva:
शयाने पुरुषे निद्रा स्वप्नं बहुविधं सृजेत्।
ब्रह्मण्येवं निर्विकारे विकारान्कल्पयत्यसौ॥
units.translation: In a sleeping man various dreams are created; similarly the power of Māyā creates diverse appearances in the immutable Brahman.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 91
units.deva:
खानिलाग्निजलोर्व्यण्डलोकप्राणिशिलादिकाः।
विकाराः प्राणिधीष्वन्तश्चिच्छाया प्रतिबिम्बति॥
units.translation: Ākāśa, air, fire, water, earth, the universe, the different Lokas (worlds) and animate and inanimate objects are appearances produced by Māyā. Pure consciousness appears as a reflection in the intellects of living beings.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 92
units.deva:
चेतनाचेतनेष्वेषु सच्चिदानन्दलक्षणम्।
समानं ब्रह्म भिद्येते नामरूपे पृथक्पृथक्॥
units.translation: Brahman characterised as existence, consciousness and bliss is the common basis of both the animate and inanimate objects; they differ only in their names and forms.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 93
units.deva:
ब्रह्मण्येते नामरूपे पटे चित्रमिव स्थिते।
उपेक्ष्य नामरूपे द्वे सच्चिदानन्दधीर्भवेत्॥
units.translation: Just as many objects are seen in a picture, so the various names and forms exist in Brahman. By negating both names and forms, one can understand that what remains is existence, consciousness and bliss.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 94
units.deva:
जलस्थेऽधोमुखे स्वस्य देहे दृष्टेऽप्युपेक्ष्य तम्।
तीरस्थ एव देहे स्वे तात्पर्यं स्याद्यथा तथा॥
units.translation: Even though a man standing on the bank of a river sees his body reflected upside down in the water, he nevertheless identifies himself with his own body in the shore; similarly an aspirant after realisation of Brahman should know himself as Brahman.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 95
units.deva:
सहस्रशो मनोराज्ये वर्तमाने सदैव तत्।
सर्वैरूपेक्ष्यते तद्वदुपेक्षा नामरूपयोः॥
units.translation: Just as in day-dreaming, people see thousands of mental pictures, but in the practical world they disregard them all, so should names and forms be disregarded.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 96
units.deva:
क्षणे क्षणे मनोराज्यं भवत्येवान्यथान्यथा।
गतं गतं पुनर्नास्ति व्यवहारो बहिस्तथा॥
units.translation: Different mental creations are formed every moment, while those which pass are lost for ever. The objects of the practical world should be looked upon similarly.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 97
units.deva:
न बाल्यं यौवने लभ्यं यौवनं स्थविरे तथा।
मृतः पिता पुनर्नास्ति नायात्येव गतं दिनम्॥
units.translation: Childhood is lost in youth and youth is lost in old age. The father once dead does not return. The day which is past never comes back.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 98
units.deva:
मनोराज्याद्विशेषः कः क्षणध्वंसिनि लौकिके।
अतोऽस्मिन्भासमानेऽपि तत्सत्यत्वधियं त्यजेत्॥
units.translation: How do the objects of the practical world, which are destroyed every moment, differ from the forms created by the mind in imagination? Though they appear, the idea of their reality should be given up.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 99
units.deva:
उपेक्षिते लौकिके धीर्निर्विघ्ना ब्रह्मचिन्तने।
नटवत्कृत्रिमास्थायां निर्वहत्येव लौकिकम्॥
units.translation: When the objects of the world are disregarded, the mind freed from obstacles rests in the contemplation of Brahman. Then like an actor, a wise man is engaged in worldly concerns with assumed faith (and so is not affected by them).

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 100
units.deva:
प्रवहत्यपि नीरेऽधः स्थिरा प्रौढ शिला यथा।
नामरूपान्यथात्वेऽपि कूटस्थं ब्रह्म नान्यथा॥
units.translation: As the big rock lying in the bed of a river remains unmoved, though the water flows over it, so also while names and forms constantly change, the unchanging Brahman does not become otherwise.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 101
units.deva:
निष्छिद्रे दर्पणे भाति वस्तुगर्भं बृहद्वियत्।
सच्चित्घने तथा नानाजगद्गर्भमिदं वियत्॥
units.translation: As the sky with all its contents is reflected in a flawless mirror, so the Ākāśa with all the universe within it is reflected on the one partless Brahman, who is nothing but absolute consciousness and existence.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 102
units.deva:
अदृष्ट्वा दर्पणं नैव तदन्तस्थे क्षणं यथा।
अमत्वा सच्चिदानन्दं नामरूपमतिः कुतः॥
units.translation: Without seeing the mirror it is impossible to see the objects reflected in it. Similarly wherefrom can there be any knowledge of names and forms without a knowledge of their substratum, which is existence, consciousness and bliss?

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 103
units.deva:
प्रथमं सच्चिदानन्दे भासमानेऽथ तावता।
बुद्धिं नियम्य नैवोर्ध्वं धारयेन्नामरूपयोः॥
units.translation: Having learnt of Brahman as existence, consciousness and bliss, one should fix the mind firmly on Him and should restrain it from dwelling on names and forms.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 104
units.deva:
एवं च निर्जगद्ब्रह्म सच्चिदानन्दलक्षणम्।
अद्वैतानन्द एतस्मिन्विश्राम्यन्तु जनाश्चिरम्॥
units.translation: Thus Brahman is realised as existence, consciousness and bliss and devoid of the phenomenal universe. May all people find rest in this secondless bliss of Brahman.

units.label: Chapter 13 · Verse 105
units.deva:
ब्रह्मानन्दाभिधे ग्रन्थे तृतीयेऽध्याय ईरितः।
अद्वैतानन्द एव स्याज्जगन्मिथ्यात्वचिन्तया॥
units.translation: In this third chapter of the section called ‘the Bliss of Brahman’, is described the bliss of Non-duality which is to be obtained by meditating on the unreality of the world.

units.label: Chapter 14 · Verse 1
units.deva:
योगेनात्मविवेकेन द्वैतमिथ्यात्वचिन्तया।
ब्रह्मानन्दं पश्यतोऽथ विद्यानन्दो निरूप्यते॥
units.translation: Now is being described the bliss of knowledge experienced by him who has realised the bliss of Brahman through Yoga, discrimination of the Self and thinking of the unreality of duality.

units.label: Chapter 14 · Verse 2
units.deva:
विषयानन्दवद्विद्यानन्दोधीवृत्तिरूप्कः।
दुःखाभावादिरूपेण प्रोक्त एष चतुर्विधः॥
units.translation: Like the bliss arising from the contact of the mind with external objects, the bliss arising from the knowledge of Brahman is a modification of the intellect. It is said to have four aspects, in the forms of absence of sorrow etc.

units.label: Chapter 14 · Verse 3
units.deva:
दुःखाभावश्च कामाप्तिः कृतकृत्योऽहमित्यसौ।
प्राप्तप्राप्योऽहमित्येवं चातुर्विध्यमुदाहृतम्॥
units.translation: The four aspects of the bliss of knowledge are: absence of sorrow, the fulfilment of all desires, the feeling ‘I have done all that was to be done’, and also the feeling ‘I have achieved all that was to be achieved’.

units.label: Chapter 14 · Verse 4
units.deva:
ऐहिकं च आमुष्मिकं चेत्येवं दुःखं द्विधेरितम्।
निवृत्तिमैहिकस्याह बृहदारण्यकं वचः॥
units.translation: Sorrow is twofold, that of this world and that of the next. The cessation of the sorrow of this world has been described in the words of the Bṛhad-āraṇyaka Upaniṣad.

units.label: Chapter 14 · Verse 5
units.deva:
आत्मानं चेद्विजानीयादयमस्मीति पूरुषः।
किमिच्छन्कस्य कामाय शरीरमनुसंज्वरेत्॥
units.translation: ‘When a man (Puruṣa) has realised the identity of his own Self with That (Paramātman), desiring what and to please whom should he allow his body and mind to be afflicted?’

units.label: Chapter 14 · Verse 6
units.deva:
जीवात्मा परमात्मा चेत्यात्मा द्विविध ईरितः।
चित्तादात्म्यात्त्रिभिर्देहैर्जीवः सन्भोक्तृतां व्रजेत्॥
units.translation: The Self is spoken of as of two types: the individual Self and the supreme Self. The consciousness, through identification with the three bodies, thinks itself as the Jīva and becomes an enjoyer.

units.label: Chapter 14 · Verse 7
units.deva:
परमात्मा सच्चिदानन्दस्तादात्म्यं नामरूपयोः।
गत्वा भोग्यत्वमापन्नस्तद्विवेके तु नोभयम्॥
units.translation: The supreme Self, who is by nature existence, consciousness and bliss, identifying itself with names and forms becomes the objects of enjoyment. When by discrimination it is disidentified from the three bodies and names and forms, there is neither the enjoyer nor anything to be enjoyed.

units.label: Chapter 14 · Verse 8
units.deva:
भोग्यमिच्छन्भोक्तुरर्थे शरीरमनुसंज्वरेत्।
ज्वरास्त्रिषु शरीरेषु स्थिता न त्वात्मनो ज्वराः॥
units.translation: Desiring the objects of enjoyment for the sake of the enjoyer, the Jīva suffers, being identified with the body. The sufferings are in the three bodies, but there are no sufferings for the Self.

units.label: Chapter 14 · Verse 9
units.deva:
व्याधयो धातुवैषम्ये स्थूलदेहे स्थिता ज्वराः।
कामक्रोधादयः सूक्ष्मे द्वयोर्बीजं तु कारणे॥
units.translation: The diseases due to the disequilibrium of the bodily humours are the suffering of the gross body; desire, anger etc., are the suffering of the subtle body; and the source of the sufferings of both the gross and subtle bodies is the suffering of the causal body.

units.label: Chapter 14 · Verse 10
units.deva:
अद्वैतानन्दमार्गेण परात्मनि विवेचिते।
अपश्यन्वास्तवं भोग्यं किं नामेच्छेत्परात्मवित्॥
units.translation: The knower of the supreme Self, while discriminating about it as mentioned in the Chapter on the ‘Bliss of Non-duality’, sees no reality in any object of enjoyment. What then should he desire?

units.label: Chapter 14 · Verse 11
units.deva:
आत्मानन्दोक्तरीत्यास्मिन्जीवात्मन्यवधारिते।
भोक्ता नैवास्ति कोऽप्यत्र शरीरानुज्वरः कुतः॥
units.translation: When the individual Self is determined (to be identical with the immutable) through the methods mentioned in Chapter 12 on the ‘Bliss of the Self’, there remains no enjoyer in this body. So how can there be sufferings which are the result of identification with the body?

units.label: Chapter 14 · Verse 12
units.deva:
पुण्यपापद्वये चिन्ता दुःखमामुष्मिकं भवेत्।
प्रथमाध्याय एवोक्तं चिन्ता नैनं तपेदिति॥
units.translation: Anxiety regarding virtue and vice are the sufferings of the future life. It has already been told in Chapter 11 that such anxiety cannot affect the illumined man.

units.label: Chapter 14 · Verse 13
units.deva:
यथा पुष्करपर्णेऽस्मिन्नपामश्लेषणं तथा।
वेदनादूर्ध्वमागामिकर्मणोऽश्लेषणं बुधे॥
units.translation: As water does not stick to the leaves of a lotus so after realisation future actions cannot stick to the knower.

units.label: Chapter 14 · Verse 14
units.deva:
इषीकातृणतूलस्य वह्निदाहः क्षणाद्यथा।
तथा सञ्चितकर्मास्य दग्धं भवति वेदनात्॥
units.translation: Just as the cotton-like flowers of the Iṣīkā reed are burnt by fire in a moment, so the accumulated past actions of the knower are burnt up because of realisation.

units.label: Chapter 14 · Verse 15
units.deva:
यथैधांसि समिद्धोऽग्निर्भस्मसात्कुरुतेऽर्जुन।
ज्ञानाग्निः सर्वकर्माणि भस्मसात्कुरुते तथा॥
units.translation: Śrī Kṛṣṇa says: ‘Just as a blazing fire reduces the fuel to ashes, so, O Arjuna, the fire of knowledge burns up all actions’.

units.label: Chapter 14 · Verse 16
units.deva:
यस्य नाहंकृतो भावो बुद्धिर्यस्य न लिप्यते।
हत्वापि स इमां लोकान्न हन्ति न निबध्यते॥
units.translation: ‘He who has no notion of I-ness and whose mind is not tainted by desire for results of action is not really a killer even if he kills people; he is not bound by his actions’.

units.label: Chapter 14 · Verse 17
units.deva:
मातापित्रोर्वधः स्तेयं भ्रूणहत्यान्यदीदृशम्।
न मुक्तिं नाशयेत्पापं मुखकान्तिर्न नश्यति॥
units.translation: In the Kauśītaki Upaniṣad it is said that killing of parents, stealing, causing abortion and such other sins do not affect his illumination, nor is the colour (serenity) of his countenance marred.

units.label: Chapter 14 · Verse 18
units.deva:
दुःखाभाववदेवास्य सर्वकामाप्तिरीरिता।
सर्वान्कामानसावाप्य ह्यमृतो भवदित्यतः॥
units.translation: It has been said in the Aitareya Upaniṣad that like the cessation of all sorrows, the knower achieves all the desired objects also: ‘He becomes immortal, achieving all the desired objects’.

units.label: Chapter 14 · Verse 19
units.deva:
जक्षन्क्रीडन्रतिं प्राप्तः स्त्रीभिर्यानैस्तथेतरैः।
शरीरं न स्मरेत्प्राणं कर्मणा जीवयेदमुम्॥
units.translation: In the Chāndogya Upaniṣad it is said that the knower of Truth may be seen laughing, playing, rejoicing with women, vehicles and other things but he does not remember the body. The vital breath, impelled by his fructifying actions keeps him alive.

units.label: Chapter 14 · Verse 20
units.deva:
सर्वान्कामान्सहाप्नोति नान्यवज्जन्मकर्मभिः।
वर्तन्ते श्रोत्रिये भोगा युगपत्क्रमवर्जिताः॥
units.translation: ‘The knower of Brahman attains fulfilment of all his desires’. For him unlike others, there are no enjoyments through rebirths and actions. His bliss is unqualified and immediate and devoid of sequence or degree.

units.label: Chapter 14 · Verses 21–22
units.deva:
युवा रूपी च विद्यावान्नीरोगो दृढचित्तवान्।
सैन्योपेतः सर्वपृथ्वीं वित्तपूर्णां प्रपालयन्॥
सर्वैर्मानुष्यकैर्भोगैः सम्पन्नस्तृप्तभूमिपः।
यमानन्दमवाप्नोति ब्रह्मविच्च तमश्नुते॥
units.translation: Whatever bliss is attained by a satisfied king who is young, handsome, learned, healthy, strong of mind, who has suitable army and rules over the whole world full of wealth and as such is endowed with the totality of all human enjoyments, even that bliss the knower of Brahman achieves.

units.label: Chapter 14 · Verse 23
units.deva:
मर्त्येभोगे द्वयोर्नास्ति कामस्तृप्तिरतः समा।
भोगान्निष्कामतैकस्य परस्यापि विवेकतः॥
units.translation: For both the king and the knower there is no attraction for worldly enjoyment and so their happiness and contentment are comparable. One has desirelessness because of enjoyment, the other because of discrimination.

units.label: Chapter 14 · Verse 24
units.deva:
श्रोत्रियत्वाद्वेदशास्त्रैर्भोग्यदोषानवेक्षते।
राजा बृहद्रथो दोषांस्तान्गाथाभिरुदाहरत्॥
units.translation: The knower of Brahman knows through his knowledge of the Vedic scriptures the defects of the objects of enjoyment. King Bṛhad-ratha gave examples of those defects in some songs.

units.label: Chapter 14 · Verse 25
units.deva:
देहदोषाश्चित्तदोषा भोग्यदोषा अनेकशः।
शुना वान्ते पायसे नो कामस्तद्वद्विवेकिनः॥
units.translation: Thus Bṛhad-ratha described the defects pertaining to the body, the mind and the objects of enjoyment. As no one has liking for porridge vomited by a dog, likewise the man of discrimination also has no liking for the body etc.

units.label: Chapter 14 · Verse 26
units.deva:
निष्कामत्वे समेऽप्यत्र राज्ञः साधन सञ्चये।
दुःखमासीद्भाविनाशादितिभीरनुवर्तते॥
units.translation: Though there is similarity between the king and the knower of Truth in desirelessness, there was misery for the king in accumulating the objects of enjoyment and the fear of losing them in future follows him.

units.label: Chapter 14 · Verse 27
units.deva:
नोभयं श्रोत्रियस्यातस्तदानन्दोऽधिकोऽन्यतः।
गन्धर्वानन्द आशास्ति राज्ञो नास्ति विवेकिनः॥
units.translation: Both these miseries are absent for the knower; so his bliss is more than that of the king. Besides, the king may have desire for the bliss of the Gandharvas, but the knower has none.

units.label: Chapter 14 · Verse 28
units.deva:
अस्मिन्कल्पे मनुष्यः सन्पुण्यपापविशेषतः।
गन्धर्वत्वं समापन्नो मर्त्यो गन्धर्व उच्यते॥
units.translation: One who has become a Gandharva, because of the particular result of his meritorious actions as a man in the present cycle, is called a ‘human Gandharva’.

units.label: Chapter 14 · Verse 29
units.deva:
पूर्वकल्पे कृतात्पुण्यात्कल्पादावेव चेद्भवेत्।
गन्धर्वत्वं तादृषोऽत्र देवगन्धर्व उच्यते॥
units.translation: If one becomes a Gandharva in the very beginning of the cycle, because of his meritorious actions in the earlier cycle, he is called a ‘celestial Gandharva’.

units.label: Chapter 14 · Verse 30
units.deva:
अग्निष्वात्तादयो लोके पितरश्चिरवासिनः।
कल्पादावेव देवत्वं गता आजानदेवताः॥
units.translation: The Agni-svattas and others who dwell for a long time in their region are called the Pitṛs. Those who have achieved the state of deities in the beginning of their cycle are called Ājāna-devatās.

units.label: Chapter 14 · Verse 31
units.deva:
अस्मिन्कल्पेऽश्वमेधादि कर्म कृत्वा महत्पदम्।
अवाप्याजानदेवैर्याः पूज्यास्ताः कर्मदेवताः॥
units.translation: Those who obtain the glorious position and are fit for worship by the Ājāna-devatās by performing the Aśva-medha sacrifice and other good actions, are the Karma-devatās.

units.label: Chapter 14 · Verse 32
units.deva:
यमाग्निमुख्याः देवाः स्युर्जाताविन्द्रबृहस्पती।
प्रजापतिर्विराट् प्रोक्तो ब्रह्मा सूत्रात्मनामकः॥
units.translation: Yama and Agni are foremost among the gods. Indra and Bṛhas-pati are well known (and superior to them). Prajā-pati is mentioned as Virāṭ and Brahmā is called the Sūtrātman or Hiraṇya-garbha.

units.label: Chapter 14 · Verse 33
units.deva:
सार्वभौमादिसूत्रान्ता उत्तरोत्तरकामिनः।
अवाङ्मनसगम्योऽयमात्मानन्दस्ततः परः॥
units.translation: From the king to Brahmā each desires the joy of the one higher than himself; but the bliss of the Self which is beyond the grasp of the mind and the senses, is superior to that of all others.

units.label: Chapter 14 · Verse 34
units.deva:
तैस्तैः काम्येषु सर्वेषु सुखेषु श्रोत्रियो यतः।
निस्पृहस्तेन सर्वेषामानन्दाः सन्ति तस्य ते॥
units.translation: As the knower of the Vedas has no desire for all those coveted pleasures, the bliss of all creatures are his.

units.label: Chapter 14 · Verse 35
units.deva:
सर्वकामाप्तिरेषोक्ता यद्वा साक्षि चिदात्मता।
स्वदेहवत्सर्वदेहेष्वपि भोगानवेक्षते॥
units.translation: This is described as ‘achieving all the desired objects’. Or it may be explained as the witness-consciousness of the knower experiencing the enjoyments of all the bodies, like those through his own body.

units.label: Chapter 14 · Verse 36
units.deva:
अज्ञस्याप्येतदस्त्येव न तु तृप्तिरबोधतः।
यो वेद सोऽश्नुते सर्वान्कामानितियब्रवीच्छ्रुतिः॥
units.translation: (Doubt): Being the witness-consciousness, even the ignorant man has this (universal enjoyment). (Reply): No, being devoid of the knowledge of himself as the witness he does not experience satisfaction. The Śruti says that he who knows the truth achieves all the desired objects.

units.label: Chapter 14 · Verse 37
units.deva:
यद्वा सर्वात्मता स्वस्य साम्ना गायति सर्वदा।
अहमन्नं तथान्नादश्चेति सामस्वधीयते॥
units.translation: Or he enjoys everything because he becomes all, as that famous passage which expresses his all-pervading selfhood sings: ‘I am the food as well as the eater of the food’.

units.label: Chapter 14 · Verse 38
units.deva:
दुःखाभावश्च कामाप्तिरुभे ह्येवं निरूपिते।
कृतकृत्यत्वमन्यच्च प्राप्तप्राप्यत्वमीक्ष्यताम्॥
units.translation: Thus are established the nature of both the absence of misery and the fulfilment of desires (experienced by the knower of the Self). His other experiences, viz., the satisfaction of having done all that was to be done and of having achieved all that was to be achieved may be seen elsewhere.

units.label: Chapter 14 · Verse 39
units.deva:
उभयं तृप्तिदीपे हि सम्यगस्माभिरीरितम्।
त एवात्रानुसन्धेयाः श्लोका बुद्धिविशुद्धये॥
units.translation: Both the topics have properly been dealt with in Chapter 7 on the ‘Lamp of Perfect Satisfaction’. These verses quoted below should be meditated upon for the purification of the mind.

units.label: Chapter 14 · Verses 40–41
units.deva:
ऐहिकामुष्मिकव्रातसिद्ध्यै मुक्तेश्च सिद्धये।
बहु कृत्यं पुरास्याभूत्तत्सर्वमधुना कृतम्॥
तदेतत्कृतकृत्यत्वं प्रतियोगिपुरःसरम्।
अनुसन्दधदेवायमेवं तृप्यति नित्यशः॥
units.translation: Before realisation one has many duties to perform in order to acquire worldly and celestial advantages and also as an aid to ultimate release; but with the rise of knowledge of Brahman, they are as good as already done, for nothing further remains to be done. The Jīvan-mukta always feels supreme self-satisfaction by constantly keeping in view his former state and present state of freedom from wants and duties.

units.label: Chapter 14 · Verse 42
units.deva:
दुःखिनोऽज्ञाः संसरन्तु कामं पुत्राद्यपेक्षया।
परमानन्दपूर्णोऽहं संसरामि किमिच्छया॥
units.translation: Let the ignorant people of the world perform worldly actions and desire to possess wives, children and wealth. I am full of supreme bliss. For what purpose should I engage myself in worldly concerns?

units.label: Chapter 14 · Verse 43
units.deva:
अनुतिष्ठन्तु कर्माणि परलोकयियासवः।
सर्वलोकात्मकः कस्मादनुतिष्ठामि किं कथम्॥
units.translation: Let those desirous of joy in heaven perform the ordained rituals. I pervade all the worlds. How and wherefore should I undertake such actions?

units.label: Chapter 14 · Verse 44
units.deva:
व्याचक्षतां ते शास्त्राणि वेदानध्यापयन्तु वा।
येऽत्राधिकारिणो मे तु नाधिकारोऽक्रियत्वतः॥
units.translation: Let those who are entitled to it, explain the scriptures or teach the Vedas. I am not so entitled because all my actions have ceased.

units.label: Chapter 14 · Verse 45
units.deva:
निद्राभिक्षे स्नानशौचे नेच्छामि न करोमि च।
द्रष्टारश्चेत्कल्पयन्ति किं मे स्यादन्यकल्पनात्॥
units.translation: I have no desire to sleep or beg for alms, nor do I do so; nor do I perform the acts of bathing or ablution. The onlookers imagine these things in me. What have I to do with their imaginations?

units.label: Chapter 14 · Verse 46
units.deva:
गुञ्जापुञ्जादि दह्येत नान्यारोपितवह्निना।
नान्यारोपितसंसारधर्मानेवमहं भजे॥
units.translation: Seeing a bush of red guñjā berries from a distance one may suppose that there is a fire, but such as imaginary fire does not affect the bush. So the worldly duties and qualities attributed to me by others do not affect me.

units.label: Chapter 14 · Verse 47
units.deva:
शृण्वन्त्वज्ञाततत्त्वास्ते जानन्कस्माच्छृणोम्यहम्।
मन्यन्तां संशयापन्ना न मन्येऽहमसंशयः॥
units.translation: Let those ignorant of the nature of Brahman listen to the teachings of the Vedānta philosophy. I have Self-knowledge. Why again should I listen to them? Those who are in doubt reflect on the nature of Brahman. I have no doubts, so I do not do so.

units.label: Chapter 14 · Verse 48
units.deva:
विपर्यस्तो निदिध्यासेत्किं ध्यानमविपर्ययात्।
देहात्मत्वविपर्यासं न कदाचिद्भजाम्यहम्॥
units.translation: He who is subject to erroneous conviction may practise meditation. I do not confuse the Self for the body. So in the absence of such a delusion why should I meditate?

units.label: Chapter 14 · Verse 49
units.deva:
अहं मनुष्य इत्यादिव्यवहारो विनाप्यमुम्।
विपर्यासं चिराभ्यस्तवासनातोऽवकल्पते॥
units.translation: Even without being subject to this delusion, I behave like a human being through the impressions and habits gathered over a long period.

units.label: Chapter 14 · Verse 50
units.deva:
प्रारब्धकर्मणि क्षीणे व्यवहारो निवर्तते।
कर्माक्षये त्वसौ नैव शाम्येद्ध्यानसहस्रतः॥
units.translation: All worldly dealings will come to an end when the fructifying Karma wears out. If it does not wear out, thousands of meditational bouts will not stop the dealings.

units.label: Chapter 14 · Verse 51
units.deva:
विरलत्वं व्यवहृतेरिष्टं चेद्ध्यानमस्तु ते।
अबाधिकां व्यवहृतिं पश्यन्ध्यायाम्यहं कुतः॥
units.translation: To bring to an end your worldly dealings, you may practise contemplation as much as you like, but I know the worldly dealings to be perfectly harmless. Why should I then meditate?

units.label: Chapter 14 · Verse 52
units.deva:
विक्षेपो नास्ति यस्मान्मे न समाधिस्ततो मम।
विक्षेपो वा समाधिर्वा मनसः स्याद्विकारिणः॥
units.translation: There is no distraction for me, so for me there is no need of Samādhi too. Both distraction and absorption are states of the changeable mind.

units.label: Chapter 14 · Verse 53
units.deva:
नित्यानुभवरूपस्य को मे वाऽनुभवः पृथक्।
कृतं कृत्यं प्रापणीयं प्राप्तमित्येव निश्चयः॥
units.translation: I am the sum of all the experiences in the universe; where is the separate experience for me? I have obtained all that was to be obtained and have done all that was to be done. This is my unshakeable conviction.

units.label: Chapter 14 · Verse 54
units.deva:
व्यवहारो लौकिको वा शास्त्रीयो वाऽन्यथाऽपि वा।
ममाकर्तुरलेपस्य यथाऽऽरब्धं प्रवर्तताम्॥
units.translation: I am associationless, neither the doer nor the enjoyer. I am not concerned with what the past actions make me do, whether in accordance with or against the social or scriptural codes.

units.label: Chapter 14 · Verse 55
units.deva:
अथवा कृतकृत्योऽपि लोकानुग्रहकामया।
शास्त्रीयेणैव मार्गेण वर्तेऽहं का मम क्षतिः॥
units.translation: Or, there is no harm if I engage myself in doing good to the world following the scriptural injunctions even though I have obtained all that was to be obtained.

units.label: Chapter 14 · Verse 56
units.deva:
देवार्चनस्नानशौचभिक्षादौ वर्ततां वपुः।
तारं जपतु वाक्तद्वत्पठत्वाम्नायमस्तकम्॥
units.translation: Let my body worship God, take bath, preserve cleanliness or beg for alms. Let my mind recite ‘Om’ or study the Upaniṣads.

units.label: Chapter 14 · Verse 57
units.deva:
विष्णुं ध्यायतु धीर्यद्वा ब्रह्मानन्दे विलीयताम्।
साक्ष्यहं किञ्चिदप्यत्र न कुर्वे नापि कारये॥
units.translation: Let my intellect meditate on Viṣṇu or be merged in the bliss of Brahman, I am the witness of all. I do nothing nor cause anything to be done.

units.label: Chapter 14 · Verse 58
units.deva:
कृतकृत्यतया तृप्तः प्राप्तप्राप्यतया पुनः।
तृप्यन्नेवं स्वमनसा मन्यतेऽसौ निरन्तरम्॥
units.translation: As he has achieved all that was to be achieved and nothing else remains for him to do, he feels satisfied and always things thus:

units.label: Chapter 14 · Verse 59
units.deva:
धन्योऽहं धन्योऽहं नित्यं स्वात्मानमञ्जसा वेद्मि।
धन्योऽहं धन्योऽहं ब्रह्मानन्दो विभाति मे स्पष्टम्॥
units.translation: Blessed am I (dhanyo’ham), blessed, for I have the constant vision of my Self! Blessed am I, blessed, for the bliss of Brahman shines clearly to me!

units.label: Chapter 14 · Verse 60
units.deva:
धन्योऽहं धन्योऽहं दुःखं सांसारिकं न वीक्षेऽद्य।
धन्योऽहं धन्योऽहं स्वस्याज्ञानं पलायितं क्वापि॥
units.translation: Blessed am I, blessed, for I am free from the sufferings of the world. Blessed am I, blessed, for my ignorance has fled away, I know not where.

units.label: Chapter 14 · Verse 61
units.deva:
धन्योऽहं धन्योऽहं कर्तव्यं मे न विद्यते किञ्चित्।
धन्योऽहं धन्योऽहं प्राप्तव्यं सर्वमद्य सम्पन्नम्॥
units.translation: Blessed am I, blessed, for I have no further duty to perform. Blessed am I, blessed, for I have now achieved the highest that one can aspire to.

units.label: Chapter 14 · Verse 62
units.deva:
धन्योऽहं धन्योऽहं तृप्तेर्मे कोपमा भवेल्लोके।
धन्योऽहं धन्योऽहं धन्यो धन्यः पुनः पुनर्धन्यः॥
units.translation: Blessed am I, blessed, for there is nothing to compare with my great bliss! Blessed am I, blessed, blessed, blessed, again and again blessed!

units.label: Chapter 14 · Verse 63
units.deva:
अहो पुण्यमहो पुण्यं फलितं फलितं दृढम्।
अस्य पुण्यस्य सम्पत्तेरहो वयमहो वयम्॥
units.translation: O my merits, my merits, how enduringly they have borne fruit! Wonderful are we, the possessors of this great merit, wonderful!

units.label: Chapter 14 · Verse 64
units.deva:
अहो शास्त्रमहो शास्त्रमहो गुरुरहो गुरुः।
अहो ज्ञानमहो ज्ञानमहो सुखमहो सुखम्॥
units.translation: O how grand and true are the scriptures, the scriptures, O how grand and great is my teacher, my teacher! O how grand is this illumination, this illumination, O how grand is this bliss, this bliss!

units.label: Chapter 14 · Verse 65
units.deva:
ब्रह्मानन्दाभिधे ग्रन्थे चतुर्थोऽध्याय ईरितः।
विद्यानन्दस्तदुत्पत्तिपर्यन्तोऽभ्यास इष्यताम्॥
units.translation: This fourth chapter of the section called the ‘Bliss of Brahman’ describes the ‘Bliss of Knowledge’. Until that bliss is attained a man should engage himself in the practice of the contemplation of Brahman.

units.label: Chapter 15 · Verse 1
units.deva:
अथात्र विषयानन्दो ब्रह्मानन्दांशरूपभाक्।
निरूप्यते द्वारभूतस्तदंशत्वं श्रुतिर्जगौ॥
units.translation: Now, in this Chapter is described the bliss which is derived from (the contact of the mind with) external objects, which may be called a door to the bliss of Brahman and an aspect of it. The Śruti has established that it is an aspect of that bliss.

units.label: Chapter 15 · Verse 2
units.deva:
एषोऽस्य परमानन्दो योऽखण्डैकरसात्मकः।
अन्यानि भूतान्येतस्य मात्रामेवोपभुञ्जते॥
units.translation: The Śruti says that this is the supreme bliss which is indivisible and homogeneous, it is Brahman Himself and that other beings (individuated by Avidyā) enjoy only a fraction of it.

units.label: Chapter 15 · Verse 3
units.deva:
शान्ता घोरास्तथा मूढा मनसो वृत्तयस्त्रिधा।
वैराग्यं क्षान्तिरौदार्यमित्याद्याः शान्तवृत्तयः॥
units.translation: The mental modifications are of three kinds: serene (Sāttvikā, śāntā), agitated (Rājasikā, ghorā) and dull (Tāmasikā, mūḍhā). The Sāttvikā modifications are detachment, fortitude, liberality and so forth.

units.label: Chapter 15 · Verse 4
units.deva:
तृष्णा स्नेहो रागलोभावित्याद्या घोरवृत्तयः।
संमोहोभयमित्याद्याः कथिता मूढवृत्तयः॥
units.translation: The Rājasikā modifications are thirst and love for objects, attachment (to them as if they were real), greed and so forth. The Tāmasikā modifications are said to be delusion, fear and so forth.

units.label: Chapter 15 · Verse 5
units.deva:
वृत्तिष्वेतासु सर्वासु ब्रह्मणश्चित्स्वभावता।
प्रतिबिम्बति शान्तासु सुखं च प्रतिबिम्बति॥
units.translation: The consciousness aspect of Brahman is reflected in all these modifications, but in the Sāttvikā modifications alone joy also is reflected.

units.label: Chapter 15 · Verse 6
units.deva:
रूपं रूपं बभूवासौ प्रतिरूप इति श्रुतिः।
उपमा सूर्यकेत्वादि सूत्रयामास सूत्रकृत्॥
units.translation: The Śruti says that entering into different bodies the supreme Self assumes different forms. Vyāsa , the author of the Brahma-Sūtras, wrote the Sūtra which illustrates the entry of Brahman into the bodies by the example of the sun (taking different forms) when reflected in different water-vessels.

units.label: Chapter 15 · Verse 7
units.deva:
एक एव हि भूतात्मा भूते भूते व्यवस्थितः।
एकधा बहुधा चैव दृश्यते जलचन्द्रवत्॥
units.translation: (Another Śruti says): 'The supreme Self, though one only, exists in every object. Like the moon reflected in water, though one It appears as many'.

units.label: Chapter 15 · Verse 8
units.deva:
जले प्रविष्टश्चन्द्रोऽयमस्पष्टः कलुषे जले।
विस्पष्टो निर्मले तद्वद्द्वेधा ब्रह्मापि वृत्तिषु॥
units.translation: The moon which is reflected in water is faint in muddy water and clear in pure water. Similarly Brahman is two-fold according to the quality of the Vṛttis (modification) of the mind.

units.label: Chapter 15 · Verse 9
units.deva:
घोरमूढासु मालिन्यात्सुखांशस्य तिरस्कृतिः।
ईषन्नैर्मल्यतस्तत्र चिदंशप्रतिबिम्बनम्॥
units.translation: Because of the preponderance of impurities of the Rājasikā and Tāmasikā Vṛttis, the blissfulness of Brahman is obscured; but because of their slight purity the consciousness of Brahman is reflected.

units.label: Chapter 15 · Verse 10
units.deva:
यद्वापि निर्मले नीरे वह्नेरौष्ण्यस्य संक्रमः।
न प्रकाशस्य तद्वत्स्याच्चिन्मात्रोद्भूतिरत्र च॥
units.translation: Or as in pure water when heated there is the transmission of heat of the fire and not its light, similarly in the Vṛttis (in which Rajas and Tamas predominate) there is the manifestation of consciousness only (not the bliss).

units.label: Chapter 15 · Verse 11
units.deva:
काष्ठे त्वौष्ण्यप्रकाशौ द्वावुद्भवं गच्छतो यथा।
शान्तासु सुखचैतन्ये तथैवोद्भूतिमाप्नुतः॥
units.translation: But as in (a piece of burning) wood both heat and light are manifested, similarly in the Sāttvikā Vṛttis both consciousness and bliss are manifested.

units.label: Chapter 15 · Verse 12
units.deva:
वस्तुस्वरूपमाश्रित्य व्यवस्था तूभयोः समा।
अनुभूत्यनुसारेण कल्प्यते हि नियामकम्॥
units.translation: These two illustrations make it clear that it is the nature of things which determines what kind of manifestation they may give and it is by experience that these properties are established.

units.label: Chapter 15 · Verse 13
units.deva:
न घोरासु न मूढासु सुखानुभव ईक्ष्यते।
शान्तास्वपि क्वचित्कश्चित्सुखातिशय ईश्यताम्॥
units.translation: Neither in Rājasikā nor in Tāmasikā Vṛttis the experience of bliss is seen but in Sāttvikā Vṛttis experience of happiness is seen to a greater or lesser degree.

units.label: Chapter 15 · Verse 14
units.deva:
गृहक्षेत्रादिविषये यदा कामो भवेत्तदा।
राजसस्यास्य कामस्य घोरत्वात्तत्र नो सुखम्॥
units.translation: When a man has desires for houses, lands and other objects then because of the agitated quality of this desire which is an effect of Rajas, there is no happiness for him.

units.label: Chapter 15 · Verse 15
units.deva:
सिद्ध्येन्न वेत्यस्ति दुःखमसिद्धौ तद्विवर्धते।
प्रतिबन्धे भवेत्क्रोधो द्वेषो वा प्रतिबन्धकः॥
units.translation: There is misery in thinking whether it will succeed; in failure this misery increases; when there are obstacles to success, anger arises or if opposed, hatred.

units.label: Chapter 15 · Verse 16
units.deva:
अशक्यश्चेत्प्रतीकारो विषदः स्यात्स तानसः।
क्रोधादिषु महादुःखं सुखशङ्कापि दूरतः॥
units.translation: If the opposition is too formidable to be overcome, there is despair; that is born of Tamas. In anger etc., there is great misery; indeed even the chance of happiness is remote.

units.label: Chapter 15 · Verse 17
units.deva:
काम्यलाभे हर्षवृत्तिः शान्ता तत्र महत्सुखम्।
भोगे महत्तरं लाभप्रसक्तावीषदेव हि॥
units.translation: With the acquisition of the desired object the pleasing Vṛtti is calmed and there is great happiness; and in actual enjoyment, the happiness is greater. Even in the prospect of acquiring it, there is some happiness.

units.label: Chapter 15 · Verse 18
units.deva:
महत्तमं विरक्तौ तु विद्यानन्दे तदीरितम्।
एवं क्षान्तौ तथौदार्ये क्रोधलोभनिवारणात्॥
units.translation: But the greatest happiness is the outcome of detachment. This subject has been dealt with in the Chapter on the ‘Bliss of Knowledge’. Like this there is happiness in fortitude as well as in liberality, because there are no anger and greed.

units.label: Chapter 15 · Verse 19
units.deva:
यद्यत्सुखं भवेत्तत्तद्ब्रह्मैव प्रतिबिम्बनात्।
वृत्तिष्वन्तर्मुखा स्वस्य निर्विघ्नं प्रतिबिम्बनम्॥
units.translation: Whatever happiness is experienced it is Brahman alone because it is a reflection of the bliss of Brahman. When the Vṛtti is directed inward or is withdrawn, the reflection of bliss is unobstructed.

units.label: Chapter 15 · Verse 20
units.deva:
सत्ता चितिः सुखं चेति स्वभावा ब्रह्मणस्त्रयः।
मृच्छिलादिषु सत्तैव व्यज्यते नेतरद्द्वयम्॥
units.translation: Existence, consciousness and bliss – these are the threefold nature of Brahman. In objects like clay, stone and so forth, only existence is manifest, whereas the other two are not.

units.label: Chapter 15 · Verse 21
units.deva:
सत्ता चितिर्द्वयं व्यक्तं धीवृत्त्योर्घोरमूढयोः।
शान्तवृत्तौ त्रयं व्यक्तं मिश्रं ब्रह्मेत्थमीरितम्॥
units.translation: Both existence and consciousness are manifest in the Rājasikā and Tāmasikā Vṛttis of the intellect and all the three are manifest in the Sāttvikā Vṛttis. Brahman associated with the world including the Vṛttis is thus described.

units.label: Chapter 15 · Verse 22
units.deva:
अमिश्रं ज्ञानयोगाभ्यां तौ च पूर्वमुदीरितौ।
आद्येऽध्याये योगचिन्ता ज्ञानमध्यायोर्द्वयोः॥
units.translation: Brahman not associated with the world is comprehended by knowledge and Yoga. They have been spoken of earlier, the topic of Yoga in Chapter 11 and knowledge in the next two chapters.

units.label: Chapter 15 · Verse 23
units.deva:
असत्ता जाड्यदुःखे द्वे मायारूपं त्रयं त्विदम्।
असत्ता नरशृङ्गादौ जाड्यं काष्ठशिलादिषु॥
units.translation: The two, absence of consciousness and misery, and non-existence – these are the three forms of Māyā. Non-existence is illustrated by such expressions as ‘the horns of a man’; absence of consciousness is seen in such objects as wood, stone etc.

units.label: Chapter 15 · Verse 24
units.deva:
घोरमूढधियोर्दुःखमेवं माया विजृम्भिता।
शान्तादि बुद्धिवृत्त्यैक्यान्मिश्रं ब्रह्मेति कीर्तितम्॥
units.translation: There is misery in the Rājasikā and Tāmasikā Vṛttis. Thus Māyā is manifested. Because of His identification with the Vṛttis of the intellect, which are Sāttvikā, Rājasikā and Tāmasikā, Brahman is called ‘associated Brahman’ i.e., Brahman is associated with the world.

units.label: Chapter 15 · Verse 25
units.deva:
एवं स्थितेऽत्र यो ब्रह्म ध्यातुमिच्छेत्पुमानसौ।
नृशृङ्गादिमुपेक्षेत शिष्टं ध्यायेद्यथायथम्॥
units.translation: Such being the nature of Māyā and Brahman, the man who wishes to meditate on Brahman should ignore the objects which have no existence (such as the horns of a man) and concentrate properly on other objects.

units.label: Chapter 15 · Verse 26
units.deva:
शिलादौ नामरूपे द्वे त्यक्त्वा सन्मात्रचिन्तनम्।
त्यक्त्वा दुःखं घोरमूढधियोः सच्चिद्विचिन्तनम्॥
units.translation: In stone etc., he should reject both name and form and meditate on existence; in Rājasikā and Tāmasikā Vṛttis he should reject the misery (which is associated with them) and meditate on existence and consciousness.

units.label: Chapter 15 · Verse 27
units.deva:
शान्तासु सच्चिदानन्दांस्त्रीनप्येवं विचिन्तयेत्।
कनिष्ठमध्यमोत्कृष्टास्तिस्रश्चिन्ताः क्रमादिमाः॥
units.translation: And in the Sāttvikā Vṛttis he should contemplate on all the three – existence, consciousness and bliss. These three kinds of contemplation are successively called inferior, middling and superior contemplations.

units.label: Chapter 15 · Verse 28
units.deva:
मन्दस्य व्यवहारेऽपि मिश्रब्रह्मणि चिन्तनम्।
उत्कृष्टं व्यक्तुमेवात्र विषयानन्द ईरितः॥
units.translation: Even for a man of dull intellect meditation on the characteristics of Brahman is good. To tell this only ‘the Bliss of Objects’ is described here.

units.label: Chapter 15 · Verse 29
units.deva:
औदासीन्ये तु धीवृत्तेः शैथिल्यादुत्तमोत्तमम्।
चिन्तनं वासनानन्दे ध्यानमुक्तं चतुर्विधम्॥
units.translation: After having had enough of enjoyments, when the mental modifications become indifferent to objects and become detached, the contemplation regarding the bliss of impressions arise, which is the highest. Thus are the four kinds of contemplation on Brahman described.

units.label: Chapter 15 · Verse 30
units.deva:
न ध्यानं ज्ञानयोगाभ्यां ब्रह्मविद्यैव सा खलु।
ध्यानेनैकाग्र्यमापन्ने चित्ते विद्या स्थिरीभवेत्॥
units.translation: As in these four types of meditation there is an admixture of knowledge and Yoga they are not mere meditations; but should be considered as a (direct means of achieving) the knowledge of Brahman itself. The mind being concentrated by meditation, this knowledge of Brahman becomes steady.

units.label: Chapter 15 · Verse 31
units.deva:
विद्यायां सच्चिदानन्दा अखण्डैकरसात्मताम्।
प्राप्य भान्ति न भेदेन भेदकोपाधिवर्जनात्॥
units.translation: In steady knowledge, existence, consciousness and bliss shine as a single homogeneous entity and not as separate entities, their difference having disappeared with the disappearance of their Upādhis or adjuncts.

units.label: Chapter 15 · Verse 32
units.deva:
शान्ता घोराः शिलाद्याश्च भेदकोपाधयो मताः।
योगाद् विवेकतो वैषमुपाधीनामपाकृतिः॥
units.translation: It is said that the adjuncts creating difference are the Sāttvikā, Rājasikā and Tāmasikā Vṛttis. Through either Yoga or discrimination these disturbing Vṛttis are removed.

units.label: Chapter 15 · Verse 33
units.deva:
निरुपाधिब्रह्मतत्त्वे भासमाने स्वयंप्रभे।
अद्वैते त्रिपुटी नास्ति भूमानन्दोऽत उच्यते॥
units.translation: When the associationless, self-luminous and secondless Brahman is grasped or known, there is then no triad of knower, knowing and known. So it is called infinite bliss.

units.label: Chapter 15 · Verse 34
units.deva:
ब्रह्मानन्द अभिधे ग्रन्थे पञ्चमोऽध्याय ईरितः।
विषयानन्द एतेन द्वारेणान्तः प्रवेश्यताम्॥
units.translation: In this, the fifth chapter of the section called ‘the Bliss of Brahman’, ‘the Bliss of Objects’ has been dealt with. Through this door enter (i.e., into the bliss of Brahman).

units.label: Chapter 15 · Verse 35
units.deva:
प्रीयाद्धरिहरोऽनेन ब्रह्मानन्देन सर्वदा।
पायाच्च प्राणिनः सर्वान्स्वाश्रितां शुद्धमानसान्॥
units.translation: May the Lord who is both Hari (Viṣṇu) and Hara (Śiva) ever be pleased by this ‘Bliss of Brahman’ and may He protect all creatures who take refuge in Him and are pure in heart.
